# Levers: measured C idioms and blockers

Each lever is one measured finding about how this repo's compilers (gcc 2.6.0 / 2.7.2 with cc1 + maspsx) turn C into the retail bytes. Read them through `python3 tools/scripts/lever.py <keyword>...` (AND of keywords over heading, keywords and text; falls back to OR ranked by hits), `--index` for headings with counts and ids, `--symptoms` for the symptom table.

To add a lever: append a block under the heading that matches what the diff shows, in this exact shape, after you have MEASURED it (a closed match or a probe, with the round, unit and function):

    - id: <area>-<short-name> | keywords: three to eight, lowercase, comma separated
      **Lead sentence naming the construct.** What retail shows, the C spelling that produces it, where it was measured.

Headings are ordered by what a worker SEES in a diff. Each heading has a `symptoms:` line (what the diff looks like) and a `try:` line (words to pass to lever.py).

- id: a-pointer-local-assigned-before-a-volatile-store-keeps-the-base-live-across-it | keywords: regalloc, pointer, volatile, store, prologue, callee-saved, load, hoist
  **REPLACING TWO SEPARATE `g->field` READS AROUND A VOLATILE PRIM STORE WITH ONE POINTER LOCAL ASSIGNED BEFORE THE STORE IS WHAT PUTS RETAIL'S POINTER LOAD ABOVE THE STORE AND RESTORES THE THIRD CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER - the global's load is otherwise emitted after the store with a `nop` in front of it, i.e. one instruction more and a different saved set** (round 474, battle/main/misc2 func_80075938, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0; `pState = g_BattleDisplayState;` with `if (pState->primListsPending != 0) pState->unk82 = 1;` measured 93.40 -> 94.12% and 181 -> 159 differing lines, and the prologue became retail's exact `sw ra,0x2C / sw s2,0x28 / sw s1,0x24 / sw s0,0x20` with the constant 0xC in `$s2`). Retail reads that pointer into `$a1` between the two halves of the clut store's address calculation, so a body that names the pointer once gets the same scheduling window.

## register choice / allocator tie

symptoms: swapped registers, wrong s-reg, allocator tie
try: regalloc callee-saved swapped tie

- id: a-later-loops-index-loses-the-caller-saved-race-until-it-is-live-from-the-earlier-loop | keywords: regalloc, allocno, dg, dl, loop, index, caller-saved, permutation, quotient
  **A SECOND (SEQUENTIALLY LATER) LOOP'S INDEX THAT RETAIL KEEPS IN A CALLER-SAVED `$aN` CAN BE PUT BACK BY GIVING THAT INDEX AN EXTRA ASSIGNMENT INSIDE THE EARLIER LOOP, WHICH FLOATS IT PAST THE LOOP-CARRYING GIVS ON THE `-dg` QUOTIENT** (round 497, world_map/main/misc1 func_80071CDC, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, closed at retail's exact 532 bytes / 133 insns). The parked body was a 60-differing-line size-for-size permutation at 96.61%: sharing ONE `s32` id variable across both loops (it then crosses loop 1's `HeapAlloc` calls and takes `$s0`, where a per-loop `u8` id gives the same value in `$v1` and re-adds an `andi`) plus reusing loop 1's index as loop 2's ENTRY COUNT and giving loop 2 its own index took it to 98.98; the last step was `j = gearId;` inside loop 1's arm with an `nGearId = gearId;` copy beside it. Numbers from the 98.98 body (`<in>.i.greg`/`<in>.i.lreg`, dump recipe in the round-496 entry): processing order `96 72 76 134 181 182 74 75 ...`, the loop-2 index 75 at "11 times across 38 insns" = 0.868 against the pData cursor giv 181 at "14/34" = 1.235, so the index loses `$a0` to a giv that retail puts in `$a1`; the extra def extends the index's live range across a call and lifts it above the givs, and the two variables then hand out `$a0/$a1/$a2` exactly as retail has them. Deleting the `j =` line, or the copy, is 98.98 again - the 3-minute permuter found both, after hand spellings (separate index, three declaration orders) had stalled at 95.35-96.83. Companion measurement on the same closing body: what survives is only a RELOC NAME. Retail's operands read `%hi(g_WorldMapStreamQueueEntryData)`/`%lo(...)` at addend 0 where the C's `entries[i].pData` emits `g_WorldMapStreamQueue` + 4; both are 0x8009D3FC, `check_bin.sh world_map` prints OK, and objdiff stops at 99.85% because the symbol NAME differs rather than the addend - so diff_func prints MISMATCH where the SECOND EXCEPTION normally prints MATCH. Read the disassembly's `%hi` name as "the symbol sitting at that addend" before spending a lane on such a park.

- id: a-scratchpad-block-written-through-a-typed-svector-pointer-closes-the-constant-hoist | keywords: regalloc, hoist, constant, lui, scratchpad, svector, store, order, source-order
  **SIX RAW `*(s16 *)0x1F8000xx` STORES AND TWO RAW `(SVECTOR *)0x1F8000A0` CASTS REPRODUCE RETAIL'S SCHEDULE ONLY WHEN THE BLOCK IS WRITTEN AS A TYPED VECTOR ARRAY **AND** EACH VECTOR'S FIELDS ARE SET IN ONE RUN: `pRot = (SVECTOR *)0x1F8000A0; pRot[0].vz = 0; pRot[0].vx = 0; pRot[0].vy = pSlot->unk50; pRot[1].vz = 0; pRot[1].vx = 0; pRot[1].vy = pSlot->unk58;` TOOK A PARK THAT HAD SAT AT 97.59% FOR THREE ROUNDS TO MATCH / 100.00% IN TWO EDITS** (round 495, world_map/main/misc9 func_80088720, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 `--dont-expand-li`, retail's exact 1056 bytes / 264 insns). The pointer local is what fixed the register tie: with the casts, `RotMatrixYXZ`'s first `MATRIX` constant was hoisted into the prologue as `lui a1,0x1F80` and held `$a1` across the two angle sums, so both sums' second addend came out in `$a2` where retail has `$a1` (8 rows, 97.59); with the typed pointer the `lui a1` fell into the store block at retail's slot and the sums took `$a1` (4 rows left, 98.44). The remaining 4 rows are pure SOURCE ORDER, not the scheduler's: the two angle loads were hoisted to the top of the block while the park wrote all four zero-clears first, and writing each vector's `vy` inside its own run put `lw v0,0x50(s1)` two slots before its `sh` exactly as retail has it - so the earlier finding that "sched1 hoists the loads whatever the statement order" held only for the load reorderings that keep the clears contiguous. Companion measurement on the same body: `&((WorldMapEntry *)g_WorldMapGroups)[tileIndex]` instead of `tileIndex * sizeof(WorldMapEntry) + (u32)g_WorldMapGroups` mirrors the base/product pair (`addu v0,v0,v1` vs retail's `addu v1,v0,v1`) and costs 0.62%, i.e. the index-first sum is load-bearing there.

- id: a-three-way-rotation-is-closed-when-the-loser-needs-a-floor-log2-step | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, rotation, dg, dl, quotient, park
  **TWO ADJACENT SIBLING FUNCTIONS WHOSE ONLY RESIDUAL IS A ROTATED CALLEE-SAVED SET CAN BE CLOSED TOGETHER IN ONE `-da -dl -dg` READ, AND THE VERDICT IS USUALLY "PARK": the loser needs a `floor_log2` STEP (one more reference, i.e. one more instruction) or a live range 5-15 insns shorter, and retail's own instruction stream pins every one of those numbers** (round 496, slus_006.64/system/rendering_atfree func_8001EE88 parked 93.85% / 848 bytes against retail's 844 / 211 insns, and func_8001F1D4 91.34% / 860 = retail's exact 215, XenoRenderingAtfree = gcc-2.7.2-cdk `-O2 -G0`). Dump recipe for this preset (no per-unit script exists): copy the unit to a scratch file, `mips-linux-gnu-cpp -Iinclude -I build $unit_cpp_flags -DNON_MATCHING -DSKIP_ASM`, then `tools/gcc-2.7.2-cdk-psx/cc1 $cc_flags -O2 -G0 -da -dl -dg` in the container, and read `<in>.i.greg` ("N regs to allocate" is the priority order, "dispositions" the hand-out) with `<in>.i.lreg` ("used N times across M insns"). EE88: the trio sits at processing positions 18/19/20 as pSpriteData `11 times across 344` = 3837, i `7 / 153` = 3660, z `7 / 169` = 3314, and retail's map needs z first - z crosses the next step at 8 refs (5680) but that is the instruction the body is already one over; the two intermediate margins are 4.8% and 10%, i.e. 5-7 insns of a live range that the preheader `sllv`, the loop counter and the latch `lbu` fix. F1D4 is the same shape twice: (z, pSpriteData, i) plus height `30 / 87` = 55172 vs clip `22 / 53` = 66415 vs pPrim `46 / 144` = 63888, where retail's height/clip/pPrim order needs height's range 15 insns shorter and clip's 3 insns longer. Two spellings measured byte-identical on EE88 (declarations reordered to the .s's assignment order; `tileY <<= n;` moved above the spriteFlags read, so the flip block's `nop` in the `lw 0x3C` slot is a reorg branch-slot steal, dead in BOTH statement orders), and the preset is right (`try_flags.sh`: 2.7.2 88.77, 2.6.0 90.87, cdk -O3 91.34 for F1D4 against cdk -O2's 91.34 base). So when the residual is a rotation and the quotients are one step / a few insns apart, park on the arithmetic instead of running the permuter below 99%.

- id: a-default-parameter-copy-moved-into-the-other-arm-flips-a-mirrored-parameter-home | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, parameter, copy, live, length, mirror
  **AN `x = arg2;` DEFAULT AT THE TOP OF THE FUNCTION THAT THE OTHER ARM NEVER OVERWRITES IS PART OF THE ALLOCATOR'S PROBLEM: moving it INTO the arm that does not compute the value shortens the merged pseudo's live range and flips a mirrored pair of PARAMETER HOMES, which also restores the prologue's `sw sN / move sN,argN` save order** (round 496, field/main/misc11 func_80092894, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8; 91.82 -> 92.56%). Retail's homes are `s0=a2, s1=a3`; with `x = arg2;` before the entry block's work the two homes came out mirrored (a2=`$s1`, a3=`$s0`) and `sw s0,32(sp)` moved to the END of the prologue; with `x = arg2; z = arg3;` as the else arm's two statements (locals declared unitialised) the prologue became retail's exactly and the join copy `move a3,s1` reappeared. So before reading `-da`/`-dl` on a mirrored parameter pair, check whether one of the two values is a *default* assigned above the branch: that def is what makes its pseudo live from instruction 2 and it loses the contest.

- id: a-struct-field-re-read-around-a-call-is-a-source-local | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, reload, local, call, struct, field, hand-out
  **A FIELD THAT RETAIL LOADS ONCE INTO A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER AND READS AGAIN AFTER A CALL IS A SOURCE LOCAL, NOT A RE-READ OF THE PARENT STRUCT - and adding those locals can FLIP A PARK'S WHOLE CALLEE-SAVED HAND-OUT, because the extra long-lived values are exactly the pressure that makes global-alloc spill a parameter instead of a value the body was spilling** (round 494, battle/main/misc23 func_800A8BF0, XenoBattle260Div0 = gcc-2.6.0 -G0; 84.71 -> 89.73% and 2444 -> 2404 bytes against retail's 2384 in ONE edit). The park read `ResolveArchiveEntryPointers(pPartBuffer->ppParts); ResolveArchiveEntryPointers(pPartBuffer->ppParts[1]);` and `pPartBuffer->pSoundBank->pStartPixels` three times; retail keeps `ppParts` in `$s1` and `pSoundBank` in `$s0` ACROSS the resolve/SEDS calls, so the source had `u8 **ppParts = pPartBuffer->ppParts;` before the two calls and `Temp8 *pSoundBank = pPartBuffer->pSoundBank;` AFTER them (the second field is re-read once for the earlier resolve call, which is why the local is assigned after it, not at the top). The tell in the diff is a `lw t0,88(sp)` argument reload in retail where your body has `move a0,s8`, i.e. retail paid a memory reload to keep a field in a register. Effect on the rest of the prologue: retail's `sw a2,88(sp)` (the spilled struct pointer, six reloads) and `move s8,s0` with `andi v0,s8,...` tests came out exactly, replacing a body that spilled the flags halfword to 0x58 and kept the struct pointer in `$s8` - so a park note that proves a spill pair "unreachable" should be re-measured after adding any such local.

- id: raising-a-base-pointers-refs-across-a-floor-log2-step-flips-the-pair-and-costs-bytes | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, refs, pointer, copies, parameter, quotients
  **A CONTESTED CALLEE-SAVED PAIR THAT IS 3.5x APART ON THE `-dl` QUOTIENT CAN BE FLIPPED BY RAISING THE LONG-LIVED SIDE'S REF COUNT ACROSS A `floor_log2` STEP - spelling a run of struct copies off a pointer local instead of off array subscripts takes the base from 2 refs to 4, and the buy is retail's register map at the price of the absolute store forms** (round 493, battling/main/misc10 func_800868E0, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8, 337 retail insns). `-da`/`-dl`: pseudo 72 the parameter "3 times across 106 insns" (1132) took `$s2` and pseudo 74 the `pBar` base `&D_80095698[8]` "2 times across 244 insns" (327) took `$s3`, with retail the mirror. Writing the three tail copies `pBar[2] = pBar[0]; pBar[1] = pBar[0]; pBar[3] = pBar[2];` (field stores left as `&D_80095698[10]`) gives 74 four refs -> 1311 > 1132, so 74 takes `$s2` and the parameter `$s3`, and the body reads 0x58/0x5C/0x60 off `$s3` exactly as retail does - 86.35% / 1328 bytes / 332 insns. It is 5 insns short because every copy then derives BOTH addresses from the one base where retail re-forms a separate `lui` base per copy; spelling the field stores off the pointer too loses 8 (85.49% / 1316 / 329). So use this as the cheap pair-flip when the parameter/pointer mirror is the residual, then restore the retail `lui at` store shapes and count bytes - and read the two quotients first, because the flip needs the long-lived pseudo's `floor_log2` step (2 -> 4 refs) or its live range under `2*refs*4*10000/other_quotient` insns.

- id: a-short-temp-merged-into-a-reused-scratch-re-ranks-the-caller-saved-hand-out | keywords: regalloc, allocno, merge, local, count, scratch, caller-saved, permutation
  **ON A 747-INSN BODY WHOSE ONLY RESIDUAL WAS THREE SHORT-LIVED TEMPS IN THE WRONG CALLER-SAVED REGISTERS, FOLDING EACH TEMP INTO AN ALREADY-DEAD REUSED `s32` SCRATCH TOOK 99.69 -> 99.87 -> 99.99% AT RETAIL'S EXACT BYTE COUNT WITH EVERY INSTRUCTION ALREADY IDENTICAL - one allocno fewer moves the whole `$aN`/`$vN` hand-out** (round 491, world_map/main/misc11_c func_8008C844, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 `--dont-expand-li`, 2988 bytes / 747 insns). The park kept `s16 zone` (retail `$a2`, ours `$a0`), `s32 moved` (retail `$a2`, ours `$v1`) and a `pTrail` fill whose pointer and counter were swapped (retail `$a3`/`$a2`); the 3-minute permuter's winning edit was `zone` -> the function's existing `s32 j`, and applying the same merge to `moved` closed the second, which also pulled `pTrail` into `$a3` for free. The hint that the variables were the same allocno in retail is that retail used `$a2` for BOTH `zone` and `moved` at disjoint ranges. So on a same-size, same-instruction-stream register rotation, before any `-dl` work: list the locals whose live ranges do not overlap and try reusing one variable for them (this is the permuter's cheapest edit and it found it where two hand-attempts and a 3-min run on the earlier body had not). Different cause from `a-redundant-local-merged-away-re-ranks-the-whole-hand-out` only in that the merge target is a SCRATCH temp, not a copy of another local.

- id: a-two-table-pointer-load-order-decides-the-load-delay-slot | keywords: regalloc, load, delay, nop, pointer, source-order, base, dying
  **WHEN TWO INDEPENDENT POINTER LOADS FEED ONE ADDRESS AND A `nop` SITS IN THE FIRST LOAD'S DELAY SLOT, THE SOURCE ORDER OF THE TWO IS THE KNOB: assigning the SURVIVING base first and the dying one second lets the second load's result take the register the first had released, which fills the delay slot** (round 491, battling/main/misc6 func_8007F05C, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8). `count = *g_BattleEntries[idx]; pSprite = &g_BattleSpriteRects[count];` emits `lw v1,0(v0) / nop` (the entry word lands in `$v1`, the queue base's register, so the rects `lui`/`lw` cannot go in the slot) and 512 bytes / 128 insns; `pSprite = g_BattleSpriteRects; count = *g_BattleEntries[idx]; pSprite = &pSprite[count];` emits `lw v1,0(v0) / lui s1,%hi(rects)` with no `nop`, 508 bytes / 127 insns, +2.67%. Same instruction multiset otherwise, so read this before blaming the allocator on a one-`nop` residual.
- id: a-reassigned-parameter-written-as-an-explicit-sum-can-move-the-incoming-load-register | keywords: parameter, stack-argument, register, plus, compound-assign, head, lw, frame
  **ON A BODY WHOSE HEAD IS A WHOLE-FUNCTION REGISTER RENAME, THE PARAMETER'S FIRST UPDATE IS PART OF THE RESIDUAL: the winning 96.42% body spells it `x = x + 0xD3;` and its `lw` of the incoming stack argument, the compare, the branch's delay slot and every later use of `x` are in retail's registers, where the same body with `x += 0xD3;` had the argument in `$t1` against retail's `$t0`** (round 491, battling/main/misc6 func_8007F05C, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8; retail `lw t0,0x30(sp)` / `bne t0,v0` / `addiu t0,t0,0x40`, the `+=` body `lw t1,0x30(sp)` / `bne t1,v0` / `addiu t0,t1,0x40`). The two measurements differ in a second edit as well (`color = y0 + 0x38; y1 = color + grow;` for y1), so treat the explicit sum as a candidate spelling to retry first, not as a proven single knob.
- id: a-pointer-reassigned-per-copy-run-is-one-global-allocno-so-every-run-loses-v0 | keywords: regalloc, allocno, pointer, block, scope, movstr, caller-saved, copy
  **A POINTER LOCAL ASSIGNED ONCE PER RUN OF STRUCT COPIES MUST BE A SEPARATE *VARIABLE* PER RUN (one block scope each): written as one variable assigned four times, gcc merges the four defs into a single allocno that "dies in 4 places", global-alloc then pushes it out of the caller-saved set (into `$a3`), and every run's copy temps shift up by one register - the fix is four `{ WorldMapEntry *pEntries = ...; ... }` scopes, which gives four block-local pseudos that local-alloc hands `$v0` each** (round 490, world_map/main/misc4 func_800783E8, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 `--dont-expand-li`, parked 93.60% / 1376 bytes / 344 insns with an identical instruction multiset -> MATCH / 100.00%, first diff after the edit). Read it off `-dg`: the park's header is `1 regs to allocate: 74` with `74 conflicts: 74 2 3 4 5 6 29` - the whole chain base was the function's ONLY global allocno, and the `2 3 4 5 6` conflicts are the `(clobber (scratch:SI))` operands of the `movstrsi` insns (`-da` shows each 32-byte copy as `(set (mem:BLK (reg 121)) (mem:BLK (reg 122)))` plus four `(clobber (scratch:SI))`, with `(reg/v:SI 74)` feeding every `(plus 74 (const_int 284))` address). Reload resolves those scratches to the FIRST FREE of `$v0,$v1,$a0,$a1,$a2,$a3` at that point, so the base's register decides the whole hand-out: retail base `$v0`/src `$a2` gives temps `$v1/$a0/$a1`, ours base `$a3`/src `$a1` gives `$v0/$v1/$a0` and leaves `$a2` untouched. The 4-run 16-byte copies in the same chain follow the same rule (dest and src are the same base register, so 4 temps), and the last run's base takes `$v1` in retail because `$v0` then holds the returned `1`. Four *named* locals (or one reused local) measure 93.60; only the per-run scope moves it.

- id: a-displaced-argument-copy-is-a-combine_regs-symptom-not-a-scheduling-knob | keywords: regalloc, argument, copy, move, combine, tie, late, scheduler
  **WHEN THE ONLY DIFF IS THE CALL'S ARGUMENT COPY DISPLACED TO THE HEAD OF THE ARM AND THE MEMORY OPERANDS THROUGH THE ARGUMENT REGISTER, THE COPY's POSITION IS A CONSEQUENCE OF `combine_regs`, NOT A KNOB: SWAPPING THE ARM'S STATEMENTS OR USING A LITERAL IN PLACE OF A PRE-BLOCK CONSTANT CHANGES NOTHING (AND THE LITERAL CAN BE WORSE)** (round 490, battle/main/misc32 func_800BDC14, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0; parked 91.60% / 100 bytes = retail's 25 insns). Retail has `lui a1,%hi(fn) / addu a0,s0,zero / lbu v0,0x83(s0) / addiu a1 / sw v1,0x88(s0)`; the compile schedules the same `move a0,s0` three slots earlier, and that gives the copy two successors, so `priority()` ranks it with the `li` and it is emitted first instead of third - which is also why the two store addresses end up on `$a0`. Measured on the same body: writing the timer-reset literal `pTask->timer = 0x10;` inside the arm instead of a `s32 nextTimer = 0x10;` before the `if` drops it to 91.40 and folds the colour `lbu` into `$a0` too (the pre-if constant is rematerialised in the arm and keeps the load on `$s0`), and reversing the two arm statements is byte-identical to that. So on this shape: keep the constant in a pre-block local, do not reorder, and attack the copy's live range instead.

- id: a-masked-s32-local-is-free-when-the-qi-form-remasks-per-use | keywords: regalloc, tie, copy, parameter, qi, si, andi, preheader, local
  **WHEN A `u_char` PARAMETER'S TRUNCATION IS ALREADY RE-EMITTED AT EACH USE, WIDENING THE COPY TO AN `s32` LOCAL IS FREE AND MOVES THE TRUNCATION TO RETAIL'S PREHEADER, WHERE A `u_char` LOCAL IS COALESCED AWAY AND RE-MASKS INSIDE THE LOOP** (round 490, battle/main/misc11 func_80080C94, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8, 89.97 -> 90.08% and 305 -> 306 insns, i.e. retail's own count). The random-target loop's exit test compares a stored byte against `arg0`; `u8 target = arg0;` is coalesced into the parameter, so the loop body re-forms `andi v0,s2,0xff` per iteration (305 insns), while `s32 target;` + `target = arg0 & 0xFF;` before the loop gives retail's `andi s0,s3,0xff` in the preheader and a bare `beq v0,s0` - the same `andi` either way, so unlike `a-cross-mode-declaration-breaks-a-copy-tie-but-pays-an-andi` the widening cost nothing. A bare `arg0 & 0xFF` in the condition (`while (... == (arg0 & 0xFF))`) does NOT work: `arg0` is QI, so the mask folds to a plain truncation and the andi goes back inside the loop. Companion on the same body: the `s32` local also has to be defined in the LOOP PREHEADER (a definition above the preceding fill loop measures 305 insns again), because the preheader definition is what makes the range span the loop.

- id: a-one-arm-dead-local-moved-the-whole-hand-out | keywords: regalloc, allocno, count, dead, local, arm, inline, rotation
  **A LOCAL ASSIGNED IN ONE ARM OF AN IF/ELSE AND READ ONLY INSIDE THAT ARM'S OWN EXPRESSION IS NOT IN THE ORIGINAL: INLINING IT TOOK A 40-LINE REGISTER ROTATION FROM 95.08 TO 98.82% AT RETAIL'S EXACT BYTE COUNT** (round 487, menu/main/misc7_r2 func_801D7884, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, 238 insns / 952 bytes, still parked on the s4-s7 rotation). The row==0 arm and the row!=0 arm each began with `characterOffset = g_Menu->pManager->currentCharacterIDs[index] * sizeof(GameCharacter);`, but only the first arm reads it again; the permuter's winning edit was to delete the second arm's assignment and write the multiply inside that arm's `gears[...]` subscript (semantically identical, since the local dies there). The change moved the hand-out of every caller-saved temp in the prologue and the stat chain and closed both `nop`s, so when a park's prologue or load-delay nops differ together with a register rotation, look for a local that only ONE branch needs. Companion -dl reading for the residual: `15 regs to allocate: 170 165 233 83 266 270 82 84 71 80 81 194 190 73 75` with dispositions `83 in 16` (=$s0) upward, so the printed order IS the processing order and the highest-priority allocno takes the CHEAPEST ($s0) register; row (4 refs/117 insns/1 byte = 0.068) and tensDigit (2/76/2 = 0.053) therefore always land AFTER the two 3-ref/35-insn row*8 and row*24 temps (0.353/0.343), i.e. a QI parameter cannot be pushed to `$s7` while those exist.

- id: a-struct-array-subscript-derives-the-second-giv-from-the-first | keywords: regalloc, giv, loop, pointer, subscript, preheader, frame, cursor
  **TWO HAND-ROLLED POINTER CURSORS OVER AN 8-BYTE ENTRY ARRAY COST ONE EXTRA `lui/addiu` IN THE PREHEADER AND 8 BYTES OF FRAME; WRITING THE SUBSCRIPT (`entries[n]`) INSTEAD LETS `loop.c` BUILD ONE GIV FROM THE OTHER (`addiu aN,aX,-4`) AND THE FRAME FALLS TO RETAIL'S** (round 484, world_map/main/misc1 func_80071CDC, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 --dont-expand-li; parked 94.10 -> 96.61% at retail's exact 532 bytes / 133 insns, frame 0x38 -> 0x30, and it made loop 1 byte-identical besides). The body had `void** ppEntryData = &g_WorldMapStreamQueueEntryData;` and `u16* pArchiveIndex = &g_WorldMapStreamQueue.archiveIndex;` advanced by 2 and 4; retail's preheader is `lui a1,%hi(EntryData) / addiu a1,%lo / addiu a2,a1,-4` and its stores are `sh v0,0(a2)` and `sw v0,0(a1)`, i.e. two offset-0 bases one word apart - the signature of one base with two strength-reduced refs (offsets 0 and 4), not of two source pointers. Both members are then written through the same counter: `entries[nCount].archiveIndex = ...; entries[nCount].pData = ...;` with the counter advanced per entry, and the same subscript at the tail for the terminator entry. Byte-identical either way, so port the subscript form and keep the register lottery as the only residual.

- id: a-redundant-local-merged-away-re-ranks-the-whole-hand-out | keywords: regalloc, rotation, permutation, local, merge, pseudo, allocno, count
  **WHEN THE INSTRUCTION STREAM AND THE BYTE COUNT ARE ALREADY RETAIL'S AND ONLY THE REGISTER NAMES DIFFER, THE KNOB IS THE NUMBER OF LOCALS, NOT THEIR ORDER: MERGING ONE REDUNDANT LOCAL AWAY RE-RANKS EVERY REGISTER IN THE FUNCTION AT ONCE** (round 483, world_map/main/misc16 func_800981C8, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2 with --dont-expand-li, parked 96.44% / retail's exact 472 bytes / 118 insns with all 122 differing lines register names, four declaration orders measured identical and a `-da`/`-dl` read having concluded the order was pinned). The body kept `colCur` as a copy of `colBase` for the inner loop; writing `col = colBase;` and `col++` on the already-dead outer variable instead — one variable and one allocno fewer, no other edit, no byte change — took it to MATCH / 100.00% on the first diff. The permuter found it only after a useless first pass: its winning "edit" on the un-merged body was a semantically empty `w++; w--;`, i.e. it was buying the same thing by injecting a pseudo, which is the diagnostic that the hand-out is reacting to allocno COUNT. So on a pure-permutation park (`same size, same instruction stream, cyclic register rotation`), stop reordering declarations and instead look for a local that exists only to hold another local's value, a cast-only local, or a temp that a dead variable could own.

- id: a-pre-prologue-global-load-is-not-a-declaration-with-initialiser | keywords: regalloc, prologue, frame, load, declaration, initialiser, hoist, caller-saved
  **RETAIL'S `lui $vX,%hi(g) / lw $vX,%lo(g)` ABOVE THE `addiu $sp,-N` IS A SCHEDULER ARTEFACT OF THE UNIT'S OWN PRESET, NOT SOMETHING A DECLARATION-WITH-INITIALISER REPRODUCES: `s32 count = g_BattleTextPrimCount;` as the FIRST declaration compiles BYTE-IDENTICALLY to two direct global reads (load still after the frame setup) in a Default-preset unit** (round 480, battling/main/misc6 func_8007E964, parked 81.04% / 508 bytes / 127 insns against retail's 520 / 130). The tempting precedent is misc2/misc9 BattleEffectSetMatrix, whose retail does load `g_BattleEffectEntryCount` into `$a2` before its frame from exactly that spelling - so check the unit's preset before copying the shape: a unit WITH `-fschedule-insns`/`-fschedule-insns2` (XenoBattleTailCdk*) can hoist a load above the prologue, and a Default (2.7.2 `-O2 -G8`, no scheduler) unit cannot, which also pins the count's register (retail `$v1`, ours `$a0`) and therefore every other register in the body. Measured on the same body: gcc-2.7.2-cdk 81.31, so the preset is not the way out either.
- id: an-symbol-address-is-always-hoisted-above-the-load-in-the-preheader | keywords: regalloc, caller-saved, preheader, constant, la, lw, order, emission
  **WHEN TWO LOOP-INDUCTION POINTERS ARE INITIALISED IN THE PREHEADER AND ONE COMES FROM A SYMBOL ADDRESS (`la`) AND THE OTHER FROM A DEFERRED GLOBAL (`lw`), cc1 ALWAYS EMITS THE `la` FIRST AND HANDS THE PSEUDO CREATED FIRST `$a1`, THE SECOND `$a0` - SO RETAIL'S REVERSE PAIR (`$a0` = address, `$a1` = load) CANNOT BE TYPED, AND THE FIRST-IN-STREAM FACT ALSO DECIDES WHERE THE CALL RESULT'S COPY LANDS** (round 480, battling/main/misc6 func_8007EEE8, parked 90.10% / retail's exact 204 bytes / 51 insns). Insensitive to every source knob measured: which initialiser is written first, either declaration order, the address initialiser moved below the two global stores, and `g_BattleEntries = pQueue = HeapAlloc(...)` as one chained statement - all 90.10 / 204 / 51 with the identical stream (`move $6,$0 / la $5,D_80091964 / lw $4,D_80092874 / move $7,$2`). Retail's `move $7,$2` sitting in the entry block right after the call and its `lui $a1/lw $a1` before `lui $a0/addiu $a0` are the same hoisting of the constant. Free knob that IS worth knowing: `i = 0;` above a `HeapAlloc` call makes the counter live across the call, so it takes a callee-saved register and the body drops to 77.63% / 212 bytes - initialise loop counters after the call.
- id: a-two-statement-pointer-add-hoists-the-global-load-above-the-frame | keywords: regalloc, hoist, prologue, frame, load, pointer, index, preheader, emission
  **A GLOBAL LOAD CAN BE HOISTED ABOVE THE FRAME SETUP BY cc1, AND WHAT DECIDES IT IS WHETHER THE INDEXED POINTER IS BUILT IN ONE EXPRESSION OR TWO: `p = table[idx] + n;` KEEPS THE INDEX IN `$a0` AND EMITS `lw $a0,<global>` AFTER `addiu $sp` (with a `move $a0,<param>` before the next call), WHILE `p = table[idx]; p += n;` EMITS `lw $v1,<global>` BEFORE THE FRAME AND PUTS THE `addu p,p,n` IN THE CALL'S DELAY SLOT** (round 493, battling/main/misc6 func_8007E964, Default; 81.04% / 508 bytes in the one-expression spelling, 96.77% / 516 bytes in the two-statement one, same semantics and same instruction count ordering everywhere else). Two inline reads of the global CSE into the one-expression shape, so "no local at all" is not a way out either. Corollary worth checking before parking any body that is a few instructions short: the old park here was also MISSING A STORE (`setlen(p, 9)` = retail's `li $2,9 / sb $2,3(s0)`), 8 of its 12 missing bytes - count the stores in the `.s` against the C rather than believing a note that calls the gap "load-delay nops".
- id: a-cross-mode-declaration-breaks-a-copy-tie-but-pays-an-andi | keywords: regalloc, tie, coalesce, copy, parameter, mode, qi, si, andi, truncation
  **WHEN RETAIL KEEPS A `u_char` COPY IN ITS OWN REGISTER AND YOURS HAS COALESCED IT INTO THE SOURCE (the diff shows `andi s1,s1,0xff` where retail has `andi s3,s2,0xff`, one whole s-register rotation downstream), DECLARING THE DESTINATION `s32` IS WHAT BREAKS THE TIE - `combine_regs` refuses a cross-mode tie - BUT IT COSTS ONE `andi` PER u_char CALL ARGUMENT, AND THAT IS USUALLY EXACTLY THE INSTRUCTION YOU CANNOT AFFORD** (round 478, menu/main/misc9 func_801DD790, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0; parked body 95.96% / retail's exact 1940 bytes / 485 insns, all 188 differing lines register names). Read the seam off `-da`/`-dl`/`-dg` first: `23 regs to allocate: 89 189 76 452 88 84 166 77 90 195 80 79 182 181 83 73 85 78 71 197 74 87 86` with `80 used 23 times across 298 insns; 1 bytes -> $s1`, `79 18/251 -> $s2`, `182 16/233 -> $s3`, `181 16/234 -> $s4`, `83 7/75 -> $s5` - five QI loop-live values, quotients 3087/2868/2746/2735/1866, i.e. the hand-out IS the priority sort, so retail's map is not reachable by ref/live arithmetic at all when one of the five is missing. Pseudo 80 was `arg2` AND `group` merged; `s32 group` (same body, one edit) separates them - `andi $17,$16,0x00ff` appears in the block and the loop-live set becomes six values - and measures 95.70% / 1944 bytes / 486 insns, the extra instruction being the SImode qty's truncating `andi` before the first `u_char` argument (spelling the source `group = arg2 & 0xFF` changes nothing: `nonzero_bits` does not survive into the next block). The permutation also moved `arg0` out of `$s0`, so the tie was never the only residual. Diagnostic recipe that closes this class in one container run: `cc1 <unit cc_flags> -O2 -G8 -da -dl -dg` on a copy of `build/src/<unit>.c.i`, then `awk "/Function <func>/,0" m.i.greg` for the processing order and dispositions ('71 in 16' = `$s0`) and `m.i.lreg` for `used N times across M insns; Z bytes`.
- id: a-declaration-order-decides-the-callee-saved-pair-through-live-length | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, declaration, order, live, length, priority
  **A MIRRORED `$s0`/`$s1` PAIR CAN BE FLIPPED BY DECLARATION ORDER ALONE, BECAUSE THE PRIORITY QUOTIENT IS `floor_log2(refs) * refs / live_length` AND THE PSEUDO COMPUTED FIRST HAS THE LONGER LIVE RANGE - so the pointer that must lose `$s0` is the one whose address is expanded first** (round 477, battle/main/misc18 func_80098D2C, XenoBattle260, 91.79 -> 93.04% from reordering four local declarations, and 94.82 -> 99.98% from two more edits of the same kind). Measured with `-da`/`-dl` in the build container (`cc1 ... -da`, then `m.i.lreg`/`m.i.greg`): the losing pseudo read `used 52 times across 310 insns` (0.8387) against the winner's `49 / 296` (0.8277) - a 1.3% margin, one reference or five live instructions wide, the `a-a-near-miss-allocno-quotient` class. Two knobs moved it here and neither changes a byte of any other function's body: (1) declare the pointer that must take `$s0` last among the address computations, and (2) spell a second pointer off the ARRAY SUBSCRIPT (`&g_X[slot].state`) rather than off the first pointer (`&pSlot->state`) - the subscript form keeps the `slot * sizeof` temp alive and gives retail's `addu s4,v0,v1` off the sum, while the `pSlot` form folds to `addiu s4,s0,0xA4` and, more importantly, moves the whole hand-out. When retail's `lui/addiu` of the table base sits AFTER the index's `sll` chain and yours sits before it, the same ordering rule applies: the first expanded initialiser is what the block's schedule starts with.

- id: relaunching-a-dead-pointer-local-for-a-later-heapalloc-flips-a-mirrored-pair | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, dead, local, reuse, heapalloc, zero
  **REUSING A POINTER LOCAL THAT IS ALREADY DEAD FOR A LATER `HeapAlloc` RESULT, AND NAMING THE CALL'S ZERO ARGUMENT IN A LOCAL, CAN FLIP A MIRRORED CALLEE-SAVED PAIR WITH NO BYTE CHANGE - a 3-minute permuter run found it after two hand-attempts and a `-dg` read had not** (round 475, battle/main/misc23 func_800A9540, XenoBattle260Div0 = gcc-2.6.0 -G0, 98.98 -> 99.14% at retail's exact 372 bytes / 93 insns). The body's `pTable` dies at its one use (`base = pTable[index - 1]`), so `pTable = HeapAlloc(ArchiveDecodeAlignedSize(nameLen), 0)` with `pEntry->pBuffer2 = pTable;` and `zero = 0;` used at `HeapAlloc(..., zero)`/`if (count != zero)`/the two final zero stores replaced a dedicated `void *pBuffer2` temp; that handed the table address `$s0` and the index `$s1` (retail's map) where the temp version mirrored them. Read it with the quotient arithmetic of `a-global-allocno-priority-is`: the pair that SURVIVED (pEntry 7 refs / 32 insns = 1.75 against pTail 9 / 25 = 4.32) is 2.5x apart and did not move, so check the pair's -dl numbers before deciding whether a find like this is worth hunting - the remaining mirror here needs pEntry to reach 16 refs.

- id: a-two-use-symbol-address-rematerialises-under-g8-but-not-under-g0 | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, address, symbol, rematerialise, cse, fold, frame, g0
  **A `&g_Symbol` USED TWICE ACROSS A CALL IS FOLDED INTO EACH LOAD'S MEMORY OPERAND UNDER -G8 (no pseudo exists, so the frame is one callee-saved register short and EVERY other value rotates down one), AND THE SAME BODY UNDER `--gp -G0` MATERIALISES IT INTO A REGISTER - so a park whose only residual is `lui/addiu` of a global's address in retail's `$s0` against `lui/lw %lo(sym)` twice here is a PRESET question, not a spelling one** (round 475, field/main/misc func_8008C180, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, parked 92.49% / 428 bytes / 107 insns against retail's 436 / 109; `try_flags --gp -G0` measures 99.48). Retail keeps `lui s0,%hi(g_FieldActors)` / `addiu s0,s0,%lo(...)` once and does `lw v1,0(s0)` at both sites, with the constant 0xFF pushed from `$s6` to `$s7` and the frame from 0x40 to retail's 0x48 - i.e. all eight callee-saved registers in use, which is exactly what the source spelling `pActors = (FieldActor**)&g_FieldActors;` + two `(*pActors)[i]` uses gives in EVERY -G8 body (the cse pass deletes the copy at 2 uses; misc6's func_800A0524 keeps the same idiom because it has 8). The unit cannot switch to -G0 (FieldScriptSetRandomSkinParams 100.00 -> 91.67, 177 -> 176 functions at 100.00), so park it and report the -G0 number; do not spend runs on `&g_FieldActors[i]` twice, the initialiser, the assignment or `FieldActor* volatile*` (all 92.49). Companion reading of the same class: a park whose save/restore pair is missing exactly 2 instructions (4 bytes each end) is short ONE allocno, not two spellings.
  SOLVED, round 487, same function: the alias form of `a-an-asm-label-array-extern` fixes it under the unit's own -G8. `extern FieldActor* g_FieldActorsTable[] __asm__("g_FieldActors");` (an ARRAY of the same 4-byte element type, so the symbol is the same object) plus `pFieldActors = g_FieldActorsTable;` makes the address a real value: retail's `lui s0` / `addiu s0` / two `lw v1,0(s0)` come out verbatim, 92.49 -> 99.48% and 428 -> retail's exact 436 bytes / 109 insns. The residual then is a two-way hand-out swap (`$s5` = partyIndex*4 and `$s6` = &slots[partyIndex]); the array-alias lever also works on a POINTER global, not just a scalar. Do not park this class on the -G0 number.
- id: a-division-staged-through-the-variable-picks-the-sext-register | keywords: regalloc, division, sext, sra, sll, variable, stage, v1
  **A SHORT'S `/ 2` EMITS `lhu` + `sll 16`/`sra 16` AND THE REGISTER OF THAT SIGN-EXTENSION TEMP IS DECIDED BY WHICH VARIABLE STAGES THE LOAD, NOT BY THE DIVISION: staging it in the variable retail keeps in the target register reproduces retail's pair, and a fresh local or the inline `return p->x / 2;` mirrors it** (round 473, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_b func_80045C94, PSY-Q preset, 98.75 -> 99.77% at retail's exact 176 bytes / 44 insns; the two remaining rows are the div sum coalescing with the RETURN pseudo in `$v0` where retail reuses the dying sext in `$v1`). Measured on the same body: `v = p->x; return v / 2;` 99.77 (load `$v0`, sext `$v1` = retail), `x = p->x; return x / 2;` 99.55 (sext takes `$a0`, the register the other arms use for `x`), and `return p->x / 2;` or a fresh `h = p->x; return h / 2;` 98.75 (load `$v1`, sext `$v0`, four rows mirrored). The rule is that the extension temp inherits the register of the VARIABLE the value is assigned to, so pick the variable whose register retail's sext uses. Dead afterwards (all 99.77): `t = v / 2; return t;`, `return (v = p->x) / 2;`, a `do { } while (0);` between the load and the division, and a 3-minute permuter run (base=10 best=10) - the last two rows are the sum/return coalesce, which is allocator behaviour, not a spelling. ROUND 486 closed that last axis with a ~200-spelling census compiled in one `cc1_probe.sh` pass (standalone copies of the body: load target `v`/`t`/`x`/inline, result into `v`/`t`/`x`/`r`, `int`/`short`/`u_long` result, `do { } while (0)` before or after, a nested block, `v = v / 2;`/`v /= 2;`, per-arm `return` vs a result that crosses to the epilogue): the sum DOES reach retail's `addu $3,$3,$2` in several shapes (`return p->x / 2;`, `t = p->x / 2; return t;`, and any result variable that crosses a block), but in every one of them the final shift is 2-address (`sra $3,$3,1`). Retail's `addu $3,$3,$2` + `sra $2,$3,1` needs the div temp and the RETURN pseudo in DIFFERENT registers, and nothing spellable splits them; a third 4-minute run is `base=10 best=10`. The census method is the cheap way to close this class: one probe compile scores hundreds of spellings and you grep the emitted block for the register pair, instead of N 5-second diff runs.
- id: a-global-store-before-a-literal-init-lands-the-li-after-the-argument-mask | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, store, order, li, prologue, hoist, mirror
  **WHEN A FUNCTION OPENS WITH A GLOBAL STORE AND A ONE-LITERAL LOCAL INIT, THE ORDER OF THOSE TWO STATEMENTS DECIDES WHETHER RETAIL'S `ori aN,zero,LIT` SITS AFTER THE PARAMETER'S `andi 0xff`/`sll` PAIR OR IS HOISTED ABOVE IT - and with it which of the two surviving callee-saved allocnos takes the lower register** (round 469, menu/main/misc3 func_801C8D78, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, 97.10 -> 99.27% at retail's EXACT 368 bytes / 92 insns, 32 -> 30 differing lines, found by a 3-minute permuter run rather than by hand). Retail's prologue is `sw s2,0x48 / move s2,a0 / andi v0,s2,0xff / sll v1,v0,0x2 / ori a3,zero,0x5 / move a0,zero / ori t0,zero,0xff / sll a2,v0,0x4 ... sw zero,%lo(g_MenuCardSlotTotals)(at)`; with `retry = 5;` written BEFORE `g_MenuCardSlotTotals[a0] = 0;` the body emits `move s1,a0 / li a3,0x5 / andi v0,s1,0xff / sll v1,v0,0x2` instead, i.e. the literal init is scheduled above the parameter's mask and the whole saved-pair hand-out mirrors (retail keeps the `u_char` parameter in `$s2` and the shifted index in `$s1`; that body has them the other way). Swapping the two statements is the entire 2.2 points. The remaining residual is the documented `a-qiparam-size-one-pins-the-saved-pair` mirror, so this lever fixes the SCHEDULE and not the pair. Companion to `a-global-store-before-the-two-locals-pins-the-missing-li-and-the-s0-s1-roles`, which covers two `= 1` locals at the top; the general form is that a global store written first makes the compiler materialise that store's address operands before anything else at the top of the function, and a literal init written first lets reorg lift the `li` over the parameter's extension.
- id: a-parameter-home-register-is-abandoned-when-its-block-sets-it | keywords: regalloc, parameter, home-register, copy-propagation, in-place, addiu, cursor, abandons
  **RETAIL'S `move sN,aPARAM` FOLLOWED BY AN IN-PLACE `addiu sN,sN,0x18` (ONE PSEUDO FOR A COPIED PARAMETER AND ITS INCREMENT) IS NOT REACHABLE FROM SOURCE IN gcc 2.6.0: cc1 PROPAGATES THE PARAMETER INTO EVERY USE AND GIVES THE INCREMENTED VALUE A FRESH PSEUDO, SO THE COPY NEVER EXISTS AND THE PARAMETER'S HOME REGISTER IS FREE FOR ANOTHER VALUE** (round 462, lib_gear/main/main, XenoLibraryDiv = gcc-2.6.0, TWO functions blocked by the same tie - func_801DEF10 parked 96.81% and func_801DF0B4 95.40%, both at retail's exact size 420 / 1144 bytes with every other instruction identical). In the leaf func_801DEF10 retail has `lhu a2,4(a1)` (flags) then `bnez`/`addiu a1,a1,0x18` and the keyframe cursor in `$a1`; every body emits `addiu a2,a1,24` with flags in `$a1`, and the 12 downstream differences (x/y/z, the duplicated `andi` in the latch delay slot) follow from that one hand-out. In func_801DF0B4 the cursor crosses calls, so retail's version is the callee-saved form - `move s1,a2` hoisted into the prologue, the four header loads read THROUGH `s1` (`lhu t0,12(s1)` ... `lhu t0,4(s1)`) and `addiu s1,s1,0x18` - i.e. ONE pseudo that both reads the header and walks the keyframes; every body instead loads the header through `$a2` and emits `addiu s2,a2,24`, and the whole saved-set rotates (`$s8` taken, `x` in `$s1`). Measured dead on these two bodies, all byte-identical or the same percentage: `(s16*)(pBlock + 1)`, `pBlock->keyframes`, `pKeyframe = (s16*)pBlock; pKeyframe += 12;`, `pBlock++; pKeyframe = (s16*)pBlock;` (sets on the parameter: a fresh pseudo and `$a2` still live at the add), and `pHeader = pBlock;` + all four header loads through `pHeader` + `pHeader++; pKeyframe = (s16*)pHeader;` (the copy is substituted into the loads, so nothing is left to be callee-saved). Two companions: writing the cursor add LAST keeps it in the `bnez` delay slot exactly as retail only if the source's first load is not `type` (loading flags first measures 95.93 with the add in the slot but flags in `$a3`), and the same abandonment is why `arg1 += x` puts the sum in a new register (see a-two-use-sum-does-not-tie). Park this class; do not spell at it.
- id: a-pseudo-that-escapes-its-do-block-goes-to-global-alloc | keywords: regalloc, rotation, block, boundary, local-alloc, global-alloc, do-while, pointer
  **A POINTER THAT IS ASSIGNED BEFORE A `do { ... } while (0);` AND USED INSIDE IT CROSSES A BASIC-BLOCK BOUNDARY, SO IT IS ALLOCATED BY global-alloc AFTER THE LOCAL PASS AND GETS THE LEFTOVER REGISTER, NOT THE FIRST FREE ONE - while the same body with the pointer assigned INSIDE the block (or with no block at all) gets retail's registers** (round 4xx, world_map/main/misc6_b func_80080578, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2; the 94.71% park had `pActor` in `$a2` and the three position values in `$v1/$a0/$a1` where retail has `$v1` and `$a0/$a1/$a2`). Measured with `cc1_probe.sh` on a faithful replica: `pActor = &g_WorldMapSlots[index];` moved inside the do-block, or the do-block dropped, gives retail's exact `$v1/$a0/$a1/$a2` - a pure register swap that no declaration order, position-alias or `-G0`/2.6.0/cdk screen could reach. The catch, also measured: the do-block is what produces the *instruction order* retail has (a `li v0,1` hoisted six slots above the `sh` that reads it), and objdiff rates a displaced instruction block WORSE than a swapped register set (the same function: block-crossing body 94.71%, pointer-inside-block 84.71%, no-block-with-volatile-stores 88.24% with only 4 differing lines). So before spending a lane on a register rotation, count the basic blocks between a local's definition and its uses: if the local is the only thing crossing, the rotation is a block-structure decision, and the cheaper body may be the one objdiff likes more.
- id: a-a-constants-materialisation-point-picks-its-register | keywords: constant, li, lui, materialisation, order, store, register, source-order, v0, v1
  **THE REGISTER A SHARED `li`/`lui` CONSTANT LANDS IN IS DECIDED BY WHERE ITS FIRST USE SITS IN THE SOURCE, SO MOVING THE FIRST OF TWO CONSTANT STORES EARLIER IS A REGISTER LEVER FOR THE CONSTANT *AND* FOR EVERY POINTER ADDRESS BESIDE IT** (round 462, world_map/main/misc7 func_80081470, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2-psx, 89.94 -> 91.65%). Retail stores `0x980000` to a slot field with `$v1` held across the case-1 arm and uses the same `$v1` for the later global store, with the camera-rotation address in `$a0`; the park produced the MIRROR (`$v0` for the constant, `$v1` for the address) plus `lhu` + `sll 16`/`sra 4` on an unrelated read. Writing `pSlot->unk50 = 0x980000;` as the arm's FIRST assignment, i.e. before the two view-angle stores, materialises the constant where `$v0` still holds those stores' values, so it takes `$v1` and the address falls to `$a0` - the same body with the field store written after the angle stores is 89.94% and keeps the mirror. Nothing else moved: the source edit changed no statement, only the position of the first constant use. Two things measured on the same arm and dead: a `s32 nHeight = 0x980000;` local shared by the two stores is copy-propagated away (identical code), and the round-444 alias lever `extern s16 X[] __asm__("X")` for the reloaded halfword gives the wanted `lh` but a distinct C symbol lets sched2 hoist the load above the volatile store (the store then prints below its own load, 616 bytes / one instruction short), so check the ORDER of the result, not just the load's form, before adopting it. Round 475 measured the pair the other way round on the same arm: a PLAIN `g_X = -0x200;` store with the array-alias read scores 93.66% (the best number this park has ever printed) and does reproduce retail's rot chain - reload right after the constant store, the angle load after the rot stores - but the distinct symbol still lets the scheduler sink the store below its own load, so the two slot fields get the PRE-store angle: wrong code, and a permuter will offer it. Both spellings stay at 616 bytes / 154 insns against retail's 620 / 155; the missing instruction is retail's load-delay `nop` after the rot reload, which only a serial source-order schedule produces, and no correct spelling reached that schedule.
- id: a-duplicated-arm-tail-can-be-load-bearing-against-cross-jumping | keywords: cross-jump, shared-tail, duplicate, switch, arm, break, size, bulk
  **A TAIL STORE THE PARK DUPLICATES IN TWO OR THREE SWITCH ARMS CAN BE LOAD-BEARING: HOISTING IT TO ONE STORE AFTER THE SWITCH (WHICH IS WHAT RETAIL'S SHARED LABEL IMPLIES) LET dbr CROSS-JUMP THE NOW-IDENTICAL ARM BODIES AND COST 36 INSTRUCTIONS** (round 461, world_map/main/misc12 func_8008E76C, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2, a 2013-insn state machine whose 65.57% park had `D_8009BD04 = 0;` at the end of each of the three entry-switch arms; retail reaches that store through one shared label `.L8008EA90`). Measured on the same body: three copies = 2076 insns / 8304 bytes / 65.57%, one copy after the switch = 2040 / 8160 / 64.29%, i.e. -36 instructions because the case-1 and case-2 bodies differ only in the value stored to `g_WorldMapMode` and become mergeable. So retail's shared label is evidence of a shared tail in the SOURCE only when the arms it follows are not near-identical; when they are, retail's two full copies prove the store was written inside each arm. Read the arm count in retail's `.s` before de-duplicating any park.
  THE CONVERSE WAS MEASURED on battling/main/misc1 func_8007107C (Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, 426-insn battle-script interpreter): retail jumps four turn arms (12/13/15 and a falling-through 14) into ONE tail block at .L800712F8 holding only `sw v0,88(s0)`, `j`, `sh zero,206(s0)`, which reads as a `turn:` label in the source. Writing the shared label (`angle = <const>; goto turn; ... turn: pActor->targetAngle = angle; pActor->facingOffset = 0; return;`) parks at 94.01% and leaves a hop block, because cc1 merges the whole tail INCLUDING the per-arm `li` and case 12 threads through case 13's jump to reuse its constant. Writing each arm's own tail (`angle = <const>; pActor->distance = ...; pActor->targetAngle = angle; pActor->facingOffset = 0; return;`, keeping the `angle` local so the 0x28 frame survives) makes dbr cross-jump exactly the three instructions retail shares: 94.01 -> 95.40%, 422 -> 421 insns, and all four arms instruction-identical. So a retail shared tail whose arms differ only in a constant is dbr's merge, not a source label - keep the duplicated tails and let the compiler find them.
- id: a-a-volatile-store-stops-the-constant-displacement-biv | keywords: biv, giv, volatile, displacement, loop, pointer-walk, store, copy
  **A LOOP THAT STORES TWICE PER ITERATION TO `base + CONST` OFF A WALKING POINTER MAKES cc1 FOLD THE CONSTANT INTO A SECOND INDUCTION REGISTER (`addiu $a0,$v0,0x3B4` in the preheader, then `sh $v0,0($a0)` and `addiu $a0,$a0,2`); MARKING THE TWO STORES `volatile` KEEPS RETAIL'S `sh $v0,948($a1)` / `addiu $a1,$a1,2`, AND THE VOLATILE STORE'S ONE-EXTRA-`move` COST IS ONLY REMOVED BY GIVING THE STORED LOCAL A PROMOTED TYPE (`s32 value`, not `u16 value`)** (round 460, battle/main/misc1 func_80070F40, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0; closed 99.65 -> MATCH at retail's exact 1944 bytes / 486 insns, `check_bin.sh battle` OK). The park's two residuals were the mode-test `la` and this +1 insn. Measured on the same 486-insn body: a plain `pPoolFlags[0x1DA]` folds (+1 insn, 1948), a `u8 *` walking pointer adding 0x3B4 folds identically, and an index loop `pPoolFlags[0x1DA + i]` folds too; the FIRST index-loop spelling gives a `move` of the reloaded base instead (`move $a0,$v1`) because an index loop's base is strength-reduced. Two companions proved in the same function: (1) an arm that both reads and writes one byte global needs the same shared `la` retail has, and `extern u8 G[] __asm__("G"); p = G;` (array decay) supplies it where `&G` folds to a bare symbol store through `$at` - and a SECOND array-decay pointer variable for a later arm gets its own fresh `la` in a different register, matching retail, where one pointer variable shared by both arms stays live across the `switch` and takes the pool's `$a0`; (2) reading a flag global into a local BEFORE an unrelated store (`overlayFlags = D_800C3D44;` above `*(u16*)((u8*)pPool + 0x394) = 0xFF;`) is what fills the pool load's delay slot (`lw $a0` / `lui $v1,%hi(D_800C3D44)`), worth one instruction, and it also hands the pool the `$a0` retail keeps it in.

- id: a-shared-scratch-variable-is-what-pins-the-callee-saved-hand-out | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, shared, scratch, rotation, reuse, variable, s0
  **WHEN A PARK'S RESIDUAL IS A THREE-WAY CALLEE-SAVED ROTATION AROUND `$s0`, AND RETAIL USES `$s0` FOR MANY SHORT-LIVED VALUES IN DISJOINT RANGES (an interpolation temp at the top of one loop, an `abs` result in another block, the function's "amount" across a call, later a stack address), RETAIL'S `$s0` IS ONE SOURCE VARIABLE REUSED THROUGHOUT - a live range that crosses the calls puts it first in the saved hand-out - so MERGING THE PARK'S PER-VALUE LOCALS INTO THAT ONE SCRATCH VARIABLE is the fix, not a spelling of any single value** (round 460, battling/main/misc3 func_80075B50, 96.42 -> 98.38% at retail's EXACT 2124 bytes / 528 insns, 164 -> 20 differing lines, Default preset). The park had spent rounds on `-da`/`-dl` arithmetic proving that the slot offset, the slot pointer and the amount "cannot exchange `$s0`" - true for THAT allocno set, and irrelevant once the loop-1 interpolation temp, the `__builtin_abs` base distance, the percent/angle (with its in-place halving and doubling) and the loop-2 average became the same variable as the amount: retail's `s0` is then `mflo s0` at the loop-1 divide, `move s0,v0 / negu s0,s0` for the abs, the in-place `sra/sll` of the amount, `move s0,v0 / negu s0,s0` again, `mflo s0` at both loop-2 divides and `addiu s0,sp,64` for `&point` after them - six values in disjoint ranges of ONE pseudo. Read the FIRST use of the contested register in retail's `.s`: if it comes before the value the park believes owns that register is even defined, the park has the wrong variable count and no allocator evidence can save it. Four spelling residuals closed afterwards on the same body, each byte-neutral: the point interpolations are `amount * (base.X - center.X)` and not the other way round (retail's `mult s0,v0`), `hit = 1;` comes BEFORE `point = base;` / `point = center;` (retail's `li t0,0x1` in the arm's delay slot), `bestAmount = amount;` comes AFTER `p->moveEndTimer = amount / 3 + 12;` (which keeps the `/3` multiply on `$s0` in the `beqz amount` slot), and loop 2 adds to stateTimer before moveReentryTimer while loop 1 does the reverse - retail is genuinely inconsistent between the two loops, so read each site's load AND store order separately.
- id: a-promoted-local-keeps-its-allocno-size | keywords: regalloc, allocno, size, promotion, u16, counter, dg, dl
  **A LOCAL THAT IS ONLY EVER USED IN PROMOTED `int` CONTEXTS CANNOT BE GIVEN A SMALLER `allocno_size`, SO DECLARING A LOOP COUNTER `u16`/`u8` CHANGES NOTHING BUT ADDS THE EXTENSION** (round 459, slus_006.64/system/sound func_8003E900, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0, parked 98.51% at retail's exact 604 bytes / 151 insns with the loop's voice pointer and its `i` counter mirrored in `$t0`/`$t1`). The `-dl` numbers on the body are pVoice `8 refs / 96 insns` (0.25) against the counter `13 refs / 95` (0.41), so the lever `a-qiparam-size-one-pins-the-saved-pair` predicts a 2x drop for a HImode counter and a flip; measured, `u16 i` gives 96.36% / 608 bytes / 152 insns - one instruction MORE (the extension) and the SAME mirror, because `i = 0`, `i++`, `i < NUM_VOICES` and `1 << i` are all SImode contexts, so the pseudo never becomes HImode. Before planning a mode-size flip, look for the value's own QI/HI operations in the diff (an `andi 0xff`/`lbu`/`lhu` at every use): a mode size only survives from a parameter used at its own width or from a loaded object, never from a promoted local. The same body also measured, both worse: sharing one `pSpu` variable pre- and post-loop (97.85% / 608) costs the coalesce.
- id: a-call-argument-built-from-a-masked-flag-needs-its-partial-test-emitted-first | keywords: regalloc, argument, andi, sltiu, index, mask, allocno, order
  **WHEN RETAIL MAKES A FUNCTION'S THIRD ARGUMENT WITH `andi aN,sM,0xf` AND ALSO TESTS THE SAME BYTE WITH `andi s0,sM,0x10` + `sltiu`/`sll`, THE TWO ANDI STATEMENTS MUST BE SPLIT IN THE SOURCE WITH THE *PARTIAL* TEST FIRST (`rateMask = mode & 0x10;` then `index = mode & 0xF;` then `flags = (rateMask == 0) * 2;`) - writing `((mode & 0x10) == 0) * 2` inline after an early `index = mode & 0xF;` puts the index's andi in the wrong slot and shifts the jal delay-slot instruction** (round 472, slus_006.64/system/sound func_8003E04C, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0: 92.30 -> 93.66% at retail's exact 244 bytes / 61 insns, and the whole instruction STREAM becomes instruction-for-instruction identical - all 48 remaining differing lines are callee-saved register identities). Measured dead on the same body: the direct `pAudioElements->envelopes[2].field` spelling for every store plus `&pAudioElements->envelopes[2]` at the reset (90.46 - the extra refs do not change the allocno order, so the pointer local is kept), `mode & 0xF` inline at the call with `index = mode & 0xF;` assigned after it (90.54 - cse2 merges to one andi and places it just before the jal), and `s32 mode` for `u8 mode` (byte-identical). The residual is the global allocator's ORDER of the callee-saved allocnos (retail pAudioElements/volume/mode = s1/s2/s3, this body mode/pAudioElements/volume), which no spelling that keeps the stream intact has moved; park it rather than re-entering on register names alone.
- id: a-shared-read-local-barred-the-ternary-register | keywords: regalloc, ternary, caller-saved, volatile, local, split, live-range, store-shape
  **A TERNARY WHOSE VALUE GOES THROUGH ONE PSEUDO (BECAUSE THE STORE MUST HAPPEN ONCE) LANDS IN THE WRONG CALLER-SAVED REGISTER WHEN THAT PSEUDO'S LIVE RANGE COVERS A LOAD EARLIER IN THE BLOCK; SPLITTING THE SHARED READ LOCAL INTO TWO BLOCK-LOCALS MAKES cc1 EXPAND THE TERNARY INTO TWO ARM STORES (WHICH dbr THEN MERGES) AND HANDS BACK RETAIL'S REGISTER** (round 459, battling/main/misc8 func_80081A44, 99.70 -> 100.00 by `tools/scripts/check_bin.sh battling`, retail's exact 744 bytes / 186 insns, Default preset). Case 2 sets two text-list indices from bits 0 and 1 of `g_BattleSlotConfirmFlags`; with ONE `s32 flags` reused for both reads (`flags = *(volatile s32 *)&g_BattleSlotConfirmFlags;` twice, retail needs two loads because the first store may alias) the first ternary's value pseudo is `reg:HI 84`, defined in both arm blocks of the `if/else` but stored once at the join, so sched1 hoists the `li 5` above the branch and `m.i.greg` prints `84 conflicts: 84 2 3 29` -> `$a0`, three bytes off retail (`li v0,5`). Two block-locals (`flags`, `flags2`) make each ternary expand into a store per arm, dbr merges the pair into retail's single `sh` and BOTH arm constants get `$v0` on their own - 99.78% with only the `jtbl_` and typed-table reloc names left, and check_bin OK. Measurement detail that matters: the read must be a local, not inline (`(*(volatile s32 *)&g & 1)` inline in each store costs a frame and `s1`, 752 bytes / 93.11), the store must NOT be volatile (`*(volatile u16 *)&D_800916E2 = ...` forces the single-pseudo shape back: 99.70 / `$a0` again), and the typed target spelling `g_BattleTextLists[5].nextListIndex` re-materialises the base address (+1 insn, 748 / 95.22), so this unit keeps the `D_` global. Two more spellings measured on the same body: a single value local then a store (`u16 value = cond ? 4 : 5;` then store) is byte-identical to the park's 99.70, and a local for the first read alone is 748 / 98.60.
- id: a-ternary-in-a-call-argument-loses-the-arm-only-truncation | keywords: regalloc, ternary, argument, if-else, cross-jumping, truncation, andi, arm, call
  **A TERNARY PASSED AS A FUNCTION ARGUMENT WHOSE ONLY CONVERSION IS THE PARAMETER'S NARROWER TYPE CANNOT PRODUCE RETAIL'S `beq` + PER-ARM TRUNCATION, BECAUSE gcc TRUNCATES THE MERGED VALUE: WRITE THE TWO ARMS AS TWO *CALLS* IN AN if/else AND dbr CROSS-JUMPS THEM INTO RETAIL'S SHARED `jal`** (round 466, menu/main/misc6 func_801D2D38, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, 99.74% park at retail's exact 392 bytes / 98 insns -> 100.00 with the identical byte count). Retail loads a `u_char gearId`, keeps it in `$a0` and does `beq a0,0xFF` / `addiu a0,a0,0xB` in the branch delay slot / `j` with `andi a0,a0,0xff` in ITS delay slot / `li a0,0xFF` / shared `jal`. Every ternary spelling - cast on the whole ternary, cast on one arm, no cast - measures 99.74 with the value in `$v0` and a late `andi a0,v0,0xff` after the merge, and the four permuter runs the park already had could not move it. The shape that matches is `if (gearId != GEAR_ID_NONE) { MenuLoadCharacterNameTexture(gearId + 0xB, k); } else { MenuLoadCharacterNameTexture(GEAR_ID_NONE, k); }`: each arm converts its own value (the truncation is inside the else arm), cross-jumping merges the two identical tails into one call, and the load's pseudo stays in the argument register - 98 insns / 392 bytes / 100.00. THE CONDITION'S POLARITY IS PART OF THE MATCH: written `if (gearId == GEAR_ID_NONE) {...} else {...}` the same body is 97.35% at the same size with `bne` and the `li 0xff` in the `j` slot, i.e. the then-arm falls through; retail's `beq` means the NON-test-value arm is the `then` arm. So when a diff shows one inverted branch plus one displaced `andi` in the same merge block, rewrite the ternary as an if/else of the two calls before reaching for the allocator.
- id: a-loads-source-position-switches-the-whole-allocation-family | keywords: regalloc, local-alloc, load, order, position, source-order, family, sched2
  **IN A BRANCH-FREE BODY, MOVING ONE GLOBAL LOAD ONE STATEMENT IN THE SOURCE CAN MOVE THE *ENTIRE* LOCAL ALLOCATION INTO THE OTHER REGISTER FAMILY, SO A SCHEDULING RESIDUAL AND A REGISTER RESIDUAL CAN BE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE - measure both orders and read the whole diff before hunting either** (round 458, world_map/main/misc8 func_8008390C, parked 96.48% at retail's exact 61 insns / 244 bytes). Retail's tail is the natural source order (`sw v0,0x54` / `sw v0,0x3C` / `lui a0` / `lh a0` / ...), but written that way every position temporary moves from `$v0` to `$a1` (`lui a1` for each of the three player-position loads) and the `sll` loses `$a0`: 93.03%, same 61 insns / 244 bytes. Keeping the load BETWEEN the two stores gives retail's registers for the positions, both angle chains and both shifts, and leaves only the `0x960000` constant in `$a0` where retail has `$a1`: 96.48%, 8 differing lines. Splitting the angle-Y value into its own local, or keeping the `u32` temp plus a `v = angleZ` copy, changes nothing (93.44 / 93.03); dropping the body's `do { } while (0)` at the same time is 76.05. Two mechanisms follow, both measured dead on this body: (i) forcing the constant's range to OVERLAP the later angle chain (load the second angle before the global store that is the constant's last use) does not move the constant off `$a0` - 89.43%, still 61 insns / 244 bytes, cc1 puts the `lh` back after the store anyway; (ii) the preset screen leaves nothing (2.7.2-cdk 96.48, i.e. the identical allocation, but the unit's matched neighbours break under cdk: 99.43 / 97.46 / 85.56; -O3 96.48; -G0 86.46; 2.6.0 does not compile), so a `$a1` the source's own stream gives no conflict for is a hand-out, not a contest - the same verdict as `a-third-allocno-holds-the-contested-register`, reached from the local-alloc side.
- id: a-store-order-spelling-cannot-move-the-loads-allocno | keywords: regalloc, local-alloc, store, order, chained, mirrored, pseudo, family
  **WHEN RETAIL'S TAIL IS ONE LOAD WRITTEN AFTER TWO STORES AND EVERY SPELLING OF THOSE TWO STORES LANDS ON THE SAME SCORE WITH THE SAME ROTATION, THE DECIDER IS THE LOAD PSEUDO'S CREATION SLOT, NOT THE STORE WORDING - stop re-spelling the stores** (round 476, world_map/main/misc7 func_800827EC, XenoWorldMapDiv, re-parked 96.42% at retail's exact 240 bytes / 60 insns; its twin misc8 func_8008390C reaches the identical 8-line residual from a different body). Retail's tail is `sll v0 / sw v0,0x54 / sw v0,0x3C / lui a0,Z / lh a0 / ...`, so the natural source puts the second angle's load after BOTH stores, and every spelling of that order measures 93.33% with the SLOT POINTER rotating from `$v1` to `$a1`: the two stores written plainly (93.33 / 48 lines), as a chained assignment `*(s32 *)(p + 0x3C) = *(s32 *)(p + 0x54) = v << 12` (93.33), and as a mirrored store `*(s32 *)(p + 0x3C) = *(s32 *)(p + 0x54)` read back (cse forwards it to two `sw v0` as retail, byte-identical 93.33). Writing the load BETWEEN the two stores - one statement earlier than retail's own order - reproduces the whole register set except the shared constant and is the 96.42 park, so the only remaining trade is `$a0`/`$a1` on the constant (see a-loads-source-position-switches-the-whole-allocation-family). Also measured on this body and worse: one REUSED `s32 angle` local for both angles with the load after both stores, 94.58 / 24 lines (the first `lh` moves to `$a1` and the second chain to `$a1`/`$v0`, so the reuse costs more than the order buys).
- id: a-copy-of-a-local-in-an-entry-delay-slot-is-a-join-copy | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, copy, join, reorg, delay-slot, fold, second-local
  **A `move $sN,$sM` OF A LOCAL SITTING IN THE DELAY SLOT OF A BRANCH AT THE TOP OF A FUNCTION IS A COPY TAKEN AT THE *JOIN* OF THE BLOCK THAT CONDITIONALLY CHANGES THAT LOCAL - reorg steals it into the entry branch's slot, so the source statement belongs after the if/else, not before it; placing it before the assignment lets cc1 fold the copy away and delete the code that reads it** (round 454, menu/main/misc3 func_801C93A8, 95.40 -> 95.74%: retail's 7th callee-saved register (`move s6,s4` in the delay slot of the first card-status test) appears only when `rebuildWindow = waited;` is written at the join, between the first if-block's closing brace and the next statement, and read by the later `if (rebuildWindow) ...`; the same assignment in the ENTRY block measures 94.27% and loses 5 instructions because `waited` is a known 0 there, and reading `waited` directly at the use gives 95.40%). Read the copy's POSITION, not the register: an entry-position copy whose source is modified inside the following conditional block is a join copy, i.e. the source had a second local. Residual left on that body is a different problem: gcc's block ordering put the loop's shared break block inside the loop body instead of after its tail (+2 instructions, 523 against 521). **Round 467 CORRECTS where that +2 lives, from the objdiff JSON instruction streams of the same body (95.74 -> 95.78% at the same 2092 bytes, 118 -> 112 differing lines, by giving the Vsync countdown its own local `frames` instead of reusing `i`: retail's `li s0,0x3B` countdown is in `$s0` while `i` is `$s1`, so the reuse moved three rows).** The break-block ordering costs NO instructions: retail's six-instruction break2/break1/shared-tail block is present on both sides (the matcher reports a 6-instruction delete on retail and 2+4 inserts here, i.e. level), and the difference is only which block the reorderer placed where, which relabels every branch target after it. The two extra instructions are instead TWO `nop`s in the FIRST of the eight cursor-prim store groups - retail has `lw a1,0x428 / lw v0,0x32c / lbu a0,0x148 / lw v0,0x4f7c / sll / addu` (6 insns) where this body has `lw a1 / nop / lbu v0 / lw a0 / sll / addu / lw v0 / nop` (8) - and that group is the one the shared HImode `-6` constant disturbs: the body materialises `ori a2,zero,0xfffa` in the `beqz` delay slot that retail fills with the return copy `addu v0,s4,zero`, then loads `menuUnk2` late and needs both nops. So a size residual of exactly +2 insns can be a CONSTANT that got a register plus the load-hazard nops it forces in one group - read the group's schedule before blaming block layout, and note that the constant only gets `$a2` because `g_Menu` took `$a3` (retail: `$a2`), so the size and the register tie are one cause.
- id: a-volatile-local-forces-retails-slot-but-not-its-body | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, volatile, spill, slot, pressure, ninth
  **WHEN RETAIL SPILLS ONE LOCAL TO A `$sp` SLOT AND KEEPS ITS NEIGHBOUR IN A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER, `volatile` ON THAT LOCAL DOES LAND IT IN THE SLOT - AND STILL LOSES THE MATCH, BECAUSE cc1 THEN SPILLS SOMETHING ELSE AND SHRINKS THE FRAME.** Round 454, battle/main/misc29 func_800B7424 (275 insns): the innermost loop has ten live scalars for nine callee-saved registers and retail spills `radius` to 0x48(sp) while keeping the poly-loop counter `i` in `$s6`; the body keeps `radius` in `$s8`/fp and spills `i` plus the 0x10 constant. `volatile s32 radius` + a `rowNext` hoist local gave 73.97% but 1080 bytes / 270 insns against retail's 1100 / 275 (frame 0x98, 20 bytes short) where the same body without `volatile` is 72.39% / 1096 / 274 - i.e. the slot comes out right and the size gets worse, so a volatile is not a handle on which value an allocator spills. Also measured there: the choice between two values that BOTH have three refs in the inner loop is not steered by declaring the register-only locals in another order (moving `i` to the top of the declaration list is byte-identical); only the reload-spilled locals' declaration order matters (see j-declaration-order-sets-the-reload-slot-order).
- id: a-second-pointer-alias-carries-the-reads-retail-names | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, rotation, alias, pointer, copy-propagation, refs, dg
  **WHEN A PARKED BODY ALREADY HAS A SECOND POINTER VARIABLE ASSIGNED FROM THE FIRST (`pTween = pBlock;`, visible in retail as `move s6,s5`) AND THE CALLEE-SAVED HAND-OUT IS ROTATED, THE FIX IS OFTEN WHICH OF THE TWO NAMES CARRIES WHICH FIELD READS - retail's per-site base register in the `.s` (`lh 0xE(s6)` / `lh 0xC(s6)` next to `lh 0xA(s5)`) IS THAT PARTITION, AND MOVING ONE GROUP OF READS BETWEEN THE NAMES CHANGES THE FIRST POINTER'S REF COUNT, WHICH IS WHAT THE HAND-OUT TRACKS** (round 451, battle/main/misc25 func_800B026C, re-parked 95.81 -> 96.08% at retail's EXACT 2120 bytes, 236 -> 192 differing lines). Retail's second pointer carries the interpolation's `startX/Y/Z` group AND the midpoint's `targetZ` test plus both midpoint `targetY` subtractions; the park had put those three on the first pointer. Moving them onto `pTween` alone shifted the block pointer's hand-out from `$s1` to `$s3` (x and y then come out in retail's `$s1`/`$s2`) - a single group move, no byte change. Two limits measured on the same body: cc1 2.6.0 COPY PROPAGATION FOLDS MOST OTHER SPELLINGS BACK (reading the opcode, the absolute-target triple or the tag through the second name is byte-identical, so only a group that survives propagation is a handle - try a group, then check the register actually moved), and `-dg`/`-dl` on that body shows the "regs to allocate" order is NOT monotone in `floor_log2(refs)*refs*size/live` (a 66-ref/276-insn pointer was processed after a 48-ref/160-insn u16 and before a 48-ref/180 one), so the dump tells you where the contested value SITS but not which spelling moves it; measure the group instead. Also measured dead there: s32 x/y/z (95.53, 12 bytes short - the `lhu` loads say the locals are 2-byte), the curFrame/endFrame group moved to the second pointer (95.55), and presets 2.7.2 94.12 / cdk 82.19 / -O3 95.80 against the unit's 2.6.0.
- id: a-two-full-calls-in-if-else-land-the-value-in-a0 | keywords: a0, argument, call, cross-jump, size, select, if-else, ternary, xalloc
  **A VALUE THAT RETAIL COMPUTES STRAIGHT INTO A CALL'S ARGUMENT REGISTER IN BOTH ARMS OF A SELECT IS REACHED BY WRITING TWO COMPLETE IDENTICAL CALLS IN AN if/else, NOT BY ASSIGNING A LOCAL AND PASSING IT - the local lands each arm's result in `$v0` and costs the copy; two calls make gcc compute into `$a0` in each arm and cross-jump the `jal` block** (round 450, field/main/main func_80077884, 90.25 -> 96.38% at retail's exact 560 bytes / 140 insns; combined with the `nStreamSize` hoist the size-select region went from 14 differing lines to 0, which was the whole of residual 2 in a park that had been stuck for rounds). Retail is `bnez v0,<call arm>` / `lui v0,0xFFE2` (in the delay slot) / `lui a0,0xFF` / `ori a0,a0,0xFFFF` / `ori v0,v0,0x3FF8` / `and a0,v1,a0` / `j` / `addu a0,a0,v0` / [call arm] `jal ArchiveDecodeAlignedSize` / `li a0,0x6B9` / `addu a0,v0,zero` / [merge] `jal HeapAlloc` / `li a1,1`: one `jal HeapAlloc` reached by both arms with `$a0` already holding the size, i.e. cross-jumping plus argument-register allocation. Any single `nSize` local, in EITHER if/else order, is 90.25 and gives `and v0,...` / `addu v0,v0,v1` / a copy in the call arm. Two more load-bearing spellings in the same region, each measured: `nStreamSize = g_FieldStreamDataSize;` hoisted above the branch is required for retail's `lw v1,lo(g_FieldStreamDataSize)` above the `bnez` (read inline it sinks into the arm), and the guard/second operand spelling is not what was blocking it. Same mechanism as a-duplicated-guard-load-and-a, reached from the select side.
- id: a-reused-parameter-pseudo-rotates-a-later-loop | keywords: regalloc, rotation, parameter, home-register, counter, loop, fresh-pseudo, temp
  **A LOOP THAT REUSES ONE OF THE FUNCTION'S PARAMETERS AS ITS COUNTER KEEPS THAT PARAMETER'S HOME REGISTER (`$a3`) AND SO ROTATES EVERY OTHER TEMPORARY BY ONE - the fix is a COUNTER VARIABLE OF ITS OWN that dies before the first call, which gcc then hands the LAST temp register retail has it in** (round 449, shop_menu/main/misc ShopMenuSellMenu, 508 insns: a park at 99.73% / 2032 bytes = retail's exact size with the whole six-value hand-out {counter, i, iv1..iv3, pItemTypes} shifted one position, counter in `$a3` where retail has `i`, everything else in the next register up). The six values are allocated to `a3,t0..t4` in priority order, and a parameter pseudo is pinned to its home register while its live range lasts, so `itemType` (the parameter, `$a3` from entry) as the coalesce counter beats every other value and pushes them all up one. Retail's counter is a fresh pseudo in `$t4`, the LAST register, i.e. the LOWEST priority - and two spellings reach that: `coalescedCount` fresh + `itemCount = ++coalescedCount;` gives retail instruction for instruction (this closed the function); folding the two variables into one (`itemCount = 0; ... itemCount++`, or `itemCount` as the subscript index) is 95.95% / 2040 bytes because itemCount stays live across the menu loop's calls, so global-alloc lifts it out of its stack slot into `$s6`, evicting pItemSellQtys and adding 8 bytes of frame. So the rule: when retail holds a loop counter in the last temp register and your body has it in a parameter's home register, do not spell at the counter - split it into a short-lived counter plus the long-lived variable it feeds, and put the copy where retail's per-iteration `sw` is. Measured and dead on the same body (all 2032 bytes unless noted): the whole park note's 15 spellings, two 3-minute permuter runs (base=125 best=125 both), and try_flags 2.7.2 -O2 -G8 97.01 / 2.7.2-cdk 72.55 against the unit's 2.6.0.
- id: a-reset-loop-counter-that-is-a-later-live-variable-fixes-the-saved-map | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, loop, counter, reset, tie, cross-jumping
  **A SPRITE/ROW LOOP WHOSE `row` AND `i` LAND MIRRORED IN `$s3`/`$s4` IS USUALLY A RESET LOOP COUNTING WITH A LOCAL `j` INSTEAD OF WITH `row` ITSELF: giving the reset loop `row` makes that pseudo live across the sprite loops' calls, so global-alloc hands it `$s3` and the loop counter of `i` `$s4` - retail's map - and the reset loop's own counter/offset pair comes out in retail's `$s3`/`$v1` instead of a caller-saved `$v1`/`$a0`** (round 447, slus_006.64/system/system func_80034888, 96.83 -> 97.26%, 1564 bytes / 391 insns against retail's 1572 / 393). The reset loop is `for (row = 0; row < pString->maxChars; row++) pString->pChars[row].rowWidth = 0;` with `row = pString->scrollRow;` after it, which also explains retail's reload of scrollRow: the store through `pChars` may alias it. Same mechanism as `a-shared-counter-forces-the-callee-saved-register` (round 405), reached from the reset-loop side. Three measured non-fixes on that seam: a local `j` counter/`i` shared across the loops (96.72/96.83), declaration order of `row`/`i` and per-block scoping of each loop's locals (all byte-identical). The remaining 2-instruction gap on the same body is pure reorg: retail's merge block is `[sb, lhu, andi]` with the `lhu` owning an unfillable nop slot, our sched2 schedules the load first and reorg steals it into the preceding block's `lbu` delay slot, so a `flags = *(volatile u16*)&pString->flags;` local (byte-identical, 97.26) proves a volatile lvalue is NOT a scheduling barrier in 2.7.2. ROUND 460 CLOSED IT: an empty `do { } while (0);` between the store and the test is a block boundary that keeps the load out of the lbu slot - see `h-an-empty-do-while-is-a-load-hoist-barrier`.
- id: a-dead-if-else-block-flips-a-two-way-callee-saved-hand-out | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, dead, block, barrier, hand-out, priority
  **A TWO-WAY CALLEE-SAVED HAND-OUT SWAP THAT NO DECLARATION ORDER OR POINTER SPELLING MOVES CAN BE FLIPPED BY ADDING A BLOCK BOUNDARY WITH NO EMITTED CODE - and the shape a 1998 programmer would actually have typed for the same effect is a duplicated-tail EARLY RETURN** (round 487, field/main/misc func_8008C180, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, 99.48 -> 100.00% / 436 bytes / 109 insns). The residual was `$s5` vs `$s6` for `partyIndex * 4` and `&g_FieldPartyActorSlots[partyIndex]`. A `do { ... } while (0)` around the two tail stores reproduces retail exactly (permute.sh found the mechanism itself as a dead `if (g_FieldScriptVMCurActor) {X} else {X}`, 9-register body, PERMUTER_ZERO in 785 iterations), and so does the natural source shape: an early `if (slots[pi] == ACTOR_ID_INVALID) { <the two tail stores>; return; }` guard with the same two stores repeated after the body, which cross-jumps to retail's single shared tail block and lands the same allocation. So when a 2-register hand-out is the LAST 0.5%, the lever is a second basic block in the tail, not a spelling; a THREE-way rotation does not respond to it (func_8008B5D4: do-while around an argument read 96.59, dead if/else around the tail byte-identical at 98.06).
- id: a-scaled-index-local-buys-the-last-callee-saved-register | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, index, scaled, stride, rematerialise, cse, struct
  **WHEN RETAIL HOLDS AN `index * sizeof(struct)` BYTE OFFSET IN A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER ACROSS CALLS AND RE-ADDS IT TO A RELOADED GLOBAL BASE PER STATEMENT, NO PER-STATEMENT `table[i]` BODY CAN REACH IT - cse keeps that multiply in a CALLER-SAVED register (`$a1`) per extended basic block - BUT ONE SOURCE-LEVEL `s32 offset = i * sizeof(T)` LOCAL MAKES gcc USE THE SPARE CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER AND REPRODUCE RETAIL'S SAVED SET AND FRAME EXACTLY** (round 445, field/main/misc2 func_80076AC0, 73.82 -> 76.98%, 1764 -> 1736 bytes / 441 -> 434 insns against retail's 1776 / 444, XenoFieldNoGp). Retail saves s0..s7 + fp (10 words, frame 0x58); the per-statement body saves s0..s7 (9) with the offset in `$a1` and re-forms the `sll/addu/sll/subu/sll` chain per block, so all 423 diff lines are renames. With the offset local used over the whole body: 75.06%, 1692 bytes / 423 insns, gcc takes the 9th callee-saved (`$s1`) and `$fp` for the 7th parameter; with it used only up to the last call of the sprite-setup region (tail left per-statement): 76.98%, 434 insns, saved set and frame retail's, and the head's only register difference is a two-register hand-out (retail spriteId `$s1` / offset `$s2`, we get the mirror).
