Companion measurement on the same body: the last instruction, retail's base-first `addu v0,a3,t8` for `pGraphics[slot * 0x1E4 + 0x853D]`, wants the sum in a pointer local (`pSlotGraphics = pGraphics + slot * 0x1E4; pSlotGraphics[0x853D]`, the misc11_b func_800826CC lever) while KEEPING `pGraphics` as a local for the 28 prim stores - dropping that local instead (both sums off `g_BattleGraphicsWork`) reloads the global per store and costs 3 instructions / 2012 bytes / 98.63, and a front-end `off3 += 0x1E4` accumulator moves `move t8,zero` to the top of the function (99.45).
- id: a-call-arg-pool-reads-as-one-shot-expressions | keywords: regalloc, argument, a0, cse, one-shot, local, call, pool
  **A CALL WHOSE FIRST ARGUMENT IS `pool + K` AND WHOSE OTHER ARGUMENTS ARE FIELDS OF THAT SAME POOL PUTS THE POOL IN `$a0` ONLY WHEN ALL THREE USES ARE ONE-SHOT CSE'D EXPRESSIONS - a named `p` local loads it into `$v1` and costs a register, 0.07% and a `MATCH`** (round 436, battle/main/misc2 func_800745EC, 99.90 -> 99.97% at retail's exact 1228 bytes / 307 insns, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0, the switch's own jtbl operand the only residual, `check_bin.sh battle` OK). Retail is `lw a0,-0x5DD0(at) / nop / lbu a1,0x66E(a0) / lbu a2,0x66A(a0) / jal / addiu a0,a0,0x190`, i.e. the pool load lands in the ARGUMENT register and the `+K` reuses it in the delay slot; with `p = ((Work *)g_Work)->pPacketPrims; BattleAddPrimListToOT((u8 *)p + 0x190, p->digitCount, p->pairPrimIndex)` the load goes to `$v1` and the arg becomes `addiu a0,v1,0x190` - same instruction count, same bytes. Spelling all three uses as the full `((BattlePacketPrims *)((Work *)g_Work)->pPacketPrims)->field` expression (cse merges them into one load) gives retail's `$a0` for free. This is `a-inline-field-reads-beat-locals` at a CALL site rather than a two-field difference, and the same function's earlier gain was the same lever on a `labelDrawn` test, so on a one-register residual at a call whose args all come off one loaded pointer, replace the pointer local with the inline expression at every use before permuting. Measured dead on the same call site at 99.90 / 1228: a `u8 *pDest` local, a second `BattlePacketPrims *q` local, `(u8 *)&p->prims[10]`, reading the two bytes before forming the pointer, and a three-copies-of-the-field-expression form that keeps `p` for the argument - and the permuter cannot run on the body at all (its randomizer rewrites the `(u8 *)` argument casts into a non-scalar cast and gcc rejects base.c; log in permuter/func_800745EC/).

- id: a-shift-written-in-place-is-retails-in-place-sra | keywords: regalloc, in-place, shift, sra, mask, constant, tie, source shape
  **RETAIL'S `sra rd,rd,0x8` IS AN IN-PLACE C UPDATE (`x = x >> 8`), NOT A SEPARATE RESULT REGISTER, AND WRITING IT THAT WAY FLIPS THE WHOLE PROLOGUE'S REGISTER CONTEST - a 99.00% park went to a match on two `>>=` statements after six declaration/order permutations and two permuter runs measured nothing** (round 437, battling/main/misc9 func_80082488, 99.00 -> 99.92%, XenoBattlingNoGp = gcc-2.7.2 -G0; residual afterwards is reloc spelling only, `check_bin.sh battling` OK). The body takes `x = pPos->vx; z = pPos->vz;`, masks both to cell corners (`mx = x & 0xFFFFFF00`) and shifts both to cell indices. With named results (`col = x >> 8; row = z >> 8;`) retail's prologue was 6 instructions off: mask `$a3` for `$a0`, x `$v0` for `$t2`, z `$a0` for `$t1`, mx/mz mirrored, because each shift's output was a fresh pseudo. Reusing the variable (`z = z >> 8;` for row, then `x = x >> 8;` for col, with the index written `(z << 7) + x`) gives retail's in-place `sra t2,t2,0x8` / `sra t1,t1,0x8` and the mask falls into `$a0` (the register the dying source released) with no other change; the first of the two was found by a 3-minute permuter run (base 255 best 100), the second by applying the same shape to the other shift. So when retail's diff shows an operation DESTROYING its source register, look for the C form that updates in place before running the allocator diagnostics: the -dl/-dg quotient argument this park had accumulated was measuring the fresh pseudos, not the original's shape. Measured dead on the same body: a `VECTOR` local for the 12-byte dot-product view at the dead fourth corner (frame 0x70 -> 0x80) and dropping the three unused `SVECTOR` locals (frame -> 0x58), so those pads are load-bearing.

- id: an-unbounded-array-extern-keeps-a-register-busy | keywords: regalloc, tie, array, extern, scalar, value, temp, delay-slot, phase, lw
  **AN UNBOUNDED ARRAY EXTERN, WHICH HOLDS THE GLOBAL'S ADDRESS IN ONE REGISTER FOR THE WHOLE BODY, ALSO DECIDES WHICH REGISTER THE STORED VALUE TAKES - AND THAT IS WHERE RETAIL'S UNFILLED LOAD-DELAY `nop` COMES FROM** (round 440, field/main/misc8 func_80081C54, 69.69 stale -> 92.75% on the re-measure, 768 bytes / 192 insns against retail's 776 / 194, Default preset). Retail's 17 singleton stores are `lui v1,%hi(idx) / lw v1,%lo(idx)(v1) / nop / sll / addu / lw v1,<field>(p) / sll / lui at / addu at / sw`: the index and the VALUE share `$v1`, so the index load's delay slot cannot be filled (the value load would clobber the address) and stays a `nop`. With the unit's `extern volatile s32 g_FieldSpriteUpdateIndex[]` the body instead holds `&g_FieldSpriteUpdateIndex` in `$a0` for the whole function, loads with `lw v1,0(a0)` (one instruction, retail pays two), and because `$a0` is busy the value takes `$v1` - retail's phase, so every `nop` and every store position matches, but the body ends up 2 instructions SHORT (the two delay slots retail fills from elsewhere and the 8 extra `lui`s it pays). Declaring a scalar alias `extern volatile s32 g_FieldSpriteUpdateCursor __asm__("g_FieldSpriteUpdateIndex")` restores retail's absolute `lui`+`lw` pair per store and the body comes out at retail's EXACT 194 insns / 776 bytes - and scores 71.21 (74.34 with a permuter `i = value` hint) because with the index in `$v1` and `$a0` free the value loads hoist into the delay slot (`lw a0,12(a2)` where retail has `nop`) and every store lands one instruction early. So: when a retail group is `index and value in the same register with a nop between`, both halves of the tie are decided by whether the global's ADDRESS is live - the array extern (register-busy, phase right, one instruction per load short) and the scalar (retail's instruction stream, phase wrong) are two different bodies, not two spellings, and a TU that needs both declaration forms for other functions cannot reach 100. `k-unbounded-array-extern-global` is the same effect read as an address-shape difference.
- id: a-retail-j-after-an-arm-truncation-is-a-ternary-not-a-store-back | keywords: regalloc, a0, ternary, narrow, trunc, select, store-back, caller-saved
  **WHEN RETAIL SHOWS `beq` / `addiu` / `j` / `andi` IN PLACE ON THE ARGUMENT REGISTER, THE BODY IS A TERNARY PASSED AS THE CALL ARGUMENT AND ITS RESULT REGISTER CANNOT BE MOVED TO `$a0` FROM SOURCE - and the spellings that DO reach `$a0` are one instruction short, because gcc then sinks the single narrow conversion past the branch and the whole thing becomes a select** (round 439, menu/main/misc6 func_801D2D38, re-parked 99.74% at retail's exact 392 bytes / 98 insns, XenoMenu260). Retail: `lbu a0,780(at)` (a `u_char` gear id out of a table), `beq a0,s2` / `addiu a0,a0,11` in the delay slot / `j join` / `andi a0,a0,0xff` in the delay slot / else arm `li a0,0xff` / `join: jal`. Every 98-insn spelling (ternary as the argument, arm casts, `& 0xFF`, inverted `!=` form, both arms cast, `gearId` declared in the inner block) is instruction-identical with the value in `$v0` and `andi a0,v0,0xff` at the join; every spelling that assigns the narrow value back to the local (`u_char gearId = cond ? ... : ...;` or if/else with casts per arm, 97.76 / 388 / 97 insns) gives retail's `lbu a0` + in-place `addiu`/`andi` but replaces the `j` with `bne` + one shared `andi` after the `li`, i.e. jump-optimisation merged the two conversions into a select. So the a0 chain and the `j`-with-arm-truncation are mutually exclusive; the reachable part of such a park is the shape (98 insns) and the register is closed - four permuter runs (1650, 991, 1217, 1360 iterations) all base==best, and the two load-bearing neighbours of this body are `characterIndex * 2` with a `u_char` counter (which yields `sll a1,s0,1` + `andi a1,a1,0xFE`) rather than `j * 2` (93.87 / 404), and `6 + (j << 1)` for the second one (94.28 / 400).

- id: a-two-unit-mirror-with-a-25-to-35-percent-quotient-gap-is-closed | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, mirror, quotient, refs, live, dg, dl, park
  **BEFORE SPENDING A LANE ON A MIRRORED CALLEE-SAVED PAIR IN A FUNCTION THAT IS ALREADY INSTRUCTION-IDENTICAL, COMPUTE THE TWO QUOTIENTS FROM ONE `-da`/`-dg` COMPILE: a 25-35% gap is not the 4%-margin class `a-a-near-miss-allocno-quotient` closes, it is a park** (round 442, world_map/main/misc9, two parks re-measured and quantified: func_800863E0 93.98% at retail's exact 392 bytes and func_80087C6C 97.30% at retail's exact 756 bytes, both XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, both with the whole instruction multiset identical and the only delta one mirrored `$s2`/`$s3`). In func_800863E0 the processed order is `133 138 79 75 130 72 76 73 77 74` = `floor_log2(refs)*refs/live*4`, with 79 = pVertex "16 times across 34 insns" (1.88) ahead of 75 = x "14 times across 28" (1.50), so pVertex takes `$s2` and x is pushed to `$s3`; closing it needs x at 16 refs (a floor_log2 step, i.e. two instructions retail does not have) or 8 fewer live insns. In func_80087C6C the order is `150 79 142 78 73 108 139 147 80 75 74` with 73 -> `$s0` (34/114 = 5.96), 139 = the `g_WorldMapWaypointTileX` symbol_ref -> `$s1` (5/13 = 3.08), 147 = `g_WorldMapWaypointTileZ` -> `$s2` (5/20 = 2.00) and 75 = the `0x1F800000` scratchpad pointer -> `$s3` (17/182 = 1.49); retail has the scratchpad in `$s2`, so the pointer would need live <= 136 insns although its def is in the entry block in BOTH bodies (retail's `lui $s2,0x1f80` sits in the same slot), which no spelling reaches. Two things make this cheap rather than a session: `-dg` prints the process order and the dispositions as `<pseudo> in <hard reg>`, `-dl` prints `<refs> times across <live> insns` per pseudo, and `m.i.cse2` names the pseudos by their RTL (`(set (reg:SI 139) (symbol_ref:SI ("g_WorldMapWaypointTileZ")))`), so the identity of each contested allocno is one grep. Presets screened on both bodies: func_800863E0 gcc-2.6.0 93.78 / cdk 81.80, func_80087C6C 2.6.0 94.81 / -O3 97.30.
- id: a-qiparam-size-one-pins-the-saved-pair | keywords: regalloc, swapped, callee-saved, parameter, qi, size, dg, dl
  **A SWAPPED CALLEE-SAVED PAIR WHOSE LOWER-PRIORITY SIDE IS A `u_char` PARAMETER CANNOT BE FLIPPED: the parameter pseudo is QI, so `allocno_size` is 1 and it carries a 4x handicap in `floor_log2(refs)*refs*10000/(live*size)` that the shifted/temp value on the other side can never make up - read `-dl`'s "N bytes" per pseudo and park in one compile** (round 443, menu/main/misc3 func_801C8D78, re-measured 90.05 -> 97.10% at retail's EXACT 368 bytes / 92 insns, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, whole body instruction-identical with retail holding the parameter in `$s2` and `a0 * 0x10` in `$s1` where the build mirrors them). `-da`/`-dl` on the body: `8 regs to allocate: 75 141 87 73 74 71 115 92`, dispositions `73 in 16` (count, QI), `71 in 17` (parameter, "1 bytes"), `115 in 18` (`a0 * 0x10`, SI) give 4655 / 1818 / 394, so retail's arrangement needs 394 to clear 1818 - 4.6x - and every term is pinned by retail's own instruction stream (the parameter stays QI, which is exactly why retail re-does its `andi 0xff` at four separate sites; `a0 * 0x10` spans the `strcpy` loop, live 19). So when a diff shows an input parameter swapped against a computed temporary, dump `-dl` FIRST: a "1 bytes" line on the parameter side ends the lane. On this body, re-ordering declarations and both operand orders of the compares are byte-identical at 97.10.
- id: a-one-iteration-do-while-splits-the-block-and-flips-a-qiparam-pair | keywords: regalloc, swapped, callee-saved, parameter, qi, barrier, do-while, label
  **A SWAPPED CALLEE-SAVED PAIR WHOSE `-dl` QUOTIENTS SAY "CLOSED" CAN STILL FLIP FROM SOURCE: ONE ONE-ITERATION `do { ... } while (0);` AROUND THE STATEMENTS AFTER THE LOSER'S LAST USE INSERTS A LABEL, WHICH SPLITS THE TRAILING BASIC BLOCK, AND THE PAIR COMES OUT RETAIL'S WAY** (round 482, menu/main/misc3 func_801C8D78, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, 99.27 -> 99.78% at retail's exact 368 bytes / 92 insns, leaving only the `D_801C50AC`-vs-`g_MenuCardPathPrefix0 + 4` reloc, `check_bin.sh menu` OK). The body was the one `a-qiparam-size-one-pins-the-saved-pair` calls unreachable (parameter QI at 1818 against `a0 * 0x10` at 394, needing 394 to clear 1818), so the flip is NOT the quota: the `do`/`while (0)` leaves a CODE_LABEL between the directory scan and the following `cardSlotCounts` store, and the extra block changes which pseudos each allocator pass sees. A permuter run found it (base 65 -> best 20 differing lines); porting it by hand measured 30 -> 12 differing lines with the `$s1`/`$s2` mirror gone and every other instruction unchanged. Measured dead on the same body: a bare `{ }` compound block is byte-identical to no barrier at all (99.27, so it is the label and not the scope), `s32 offset = a0 * 0x10` used by both loops merges the two products and costs a frame word (90.77, 93 insns), moving `struct DIRENTRY dir;` inside the guarded block is 86.90 / 380 bytes, `-O3` 99.27, and gcc-2.7.2-cdk 78.58. Read this as: the residual is a block-structure question and not a quota one, and the shipped body carries the one-iteration `do`/`while (0)` itself (the natural 99.27% body without it is the fallback if a reviewer rejects the construct).
- id: a-sched2-hoisted-global-address-has-no-source-order | keywords: regalloc, live-length, sched2, hoist, preheader, address, swapped, unreachable
  **WHEN THE LIVE-LENGTH TERM IS THE ONLY THING BETWEEN YOU AND A SWAPPED PAIR, CHECK WHERE THE COMPILER ACTUALLY PUTS THE INIT: a dependency-free `lui/addiu` of a global is hoisted by sched2 to the HEAD of its block, so the source position of the initialising statement does not change the pseudo's live range by one instruction and the `live_length <= N` window is not walkable** (round 443, menu/main/misc3 func_801CBA4C, re-measured 96.29% at retail's exact 836 bytes / 209 insns, XenoMenu260). Retail forms the text walker's `lui/addiu g_GameState` in the FIFTH slot of the loop preheader and this build in the FIRST, so the walker's live range is 36 where retail's own position gives 32, and 32 is inside the `<= 34` window that would flip the pair (see a-a-near-miss-allocno-quotient for that function's 2393-vs-2291 numbers). Moving `pText = (u8*)g_GameState.strings;` from after the three header stores to before them measures the same 96.29 with a byte-identical emission - the preheader order is a CONSEQUENCE of the allocation (sched2's register-pressure model), not a lever on it. So a park note that reads "the address formation happened one statement earlier here" is describing the symptom of the mirror, not a second residual; do not spend a lane re-ordering the preheader.
- id: a-block-split-flips-a-caller-saved-pair | keywords: regalloc, caller-saved, swap, block, do-while, barrier, local-alloc, scheduler
  **A MIRRORED PAIR OF CALLER-SAVED TEMPS (`$v0`/`$v1`) IN A STRAIGHT-LINE BLOCK IS DECIDED BY WHICH BLOCK THE TWO PSEUDOS ARE ALLOCATED IN, NOT ONLY BY THE REFS QUOTIENT: an empty `do { } while (0);` between the two definitions makes local-alloc allocate the first one alone, so it takes `$v0` and the second falls to `$v1` exactly as retail has it - the test costs 15 s and proves in one diff whether the mirror is a wall or a block artefact** (round 452, field/main/misc5 func_800A6E70, still parked 99.56% at retail's exact 500 bytes / 125 insns). Retail holds `j*16`, truncated in place by the `andi`, in `$v0` and that mask + 0x10 in `$v1`; the body compiles the mirror, 18 differing lines, and the seven `-dl`/`-dg` readings and permuter runs in the park note all failed to move it. A `do { } while (0);` between `nU = nX & 0x3F;` and `nU1 = nU + 0x10;` flips it: 98.40%, same 500 bytes / 125 insns, TWO differing lines - the pair is retail's and the cost is the second line, `move a2,s2` (the GetTPage division's dividend copy, which sched2 hoists to the block head right after the SetPolyGT4 delay slot) landing after the `addiu` because sched2 can then only hoist it to the new block. Barrier placements measured on the same body: before the `andi` keeps the pair mirrored and moves the copy below the `andi` (97.96%), a second barrier at the loop-body head changes nothing, and the copy is attached to the LAST barrier - so recovering the copy needs the barrier at the head while the flip needs it after the `andi`, i.e. the two residuals are provably exclusive and no legitimate statement puts a block boundary between the two definitions. Read this as a cheap diagnostic (does the pair flip? then the residual is a block structure question, and any earlier "unreachable quotient wall" verdict in a park note is wrong) and remember the barrier itself is not shippable source, so it can only be used to learn, never to match.


- id: a-second-assignment-to-the-loser-promotes-it-to-a-global-allocno | keywords: regalloc, caller-saved, block-local, global-alloc, second-assignment, mask, refs, pair
  **A MIRRORED BLOCK-LOCAL CALLER-SAVED PAIR CAN BE BROKEN FROM SOURCE BY GIVING ONE OF THE TWO VALUES A SECOND ASSIGNMENT LATER IN THE SAME BODY: cc1 then allocates the two assignments as ONE pseudo (its refs are the two values' refs SUMMED), that pseudo's live range leaves the basic block, it becomes a global allocno, and the block-local pass allocates the surviving value alone - so it takes the first free register unconditionally** (round 465, field/main/misc5 func_800A6E70, MATCHED 99.56 -> 100.00% at retail's exact 500 bytes / 125 insns, Default preset, `check_bin.sh field` OK). The u mask and the mask + 0x10 mirrored `$v0`/`$v1` for four rounds and seven permuter runs (base=55 each); the winning edit is that the loop's `pPoly->tpage = GetTPage(...)` writes its result into the SAME variable that holds the mask + 0x10 (`nU1 = GetTPage(0x2, 0x1, j / 4 * 0x40 + 0x2C0, 0x100); pPoly->tpage = nU1;` or the chained form, both byte-identical), which is semantically free because that value is already dead after its last store. The `-dl`/`-dg` dumps name the mechanism: before, pseudo 79 = `used 9 times across 6 insns IN BLOCK 2` and the block-local pass gave it `$v0` ahead of the 12-ref mask; after, the same pseudo reads `used 15 times across 6 insns` with no block 2 tag and appears in the `N regs to allocate` list (3rd of 14) as a global allocno, while the mask keeps 12 refs / 7 insns in block 2 and takes `$v0` - retail's arrangement. Also measured on the same body: a dedicated `int nTpage` receiving the call changes NOTHING (99.56, fresh pseudo, the mirror returns), a `u_short nTpage` is 99.56 too, storing the result into the MASK's variable (`nU`) scores 96.52, and into `nX` 91.94 (123 insns) - so the receiving variable has to be the exact one that lost the contest. Cheap test to run before parking any `$v0`/`$v1` mirror whose two values are both dead before a later call in the same body: route the call's result through the loser. This supersedes the "provably exclusive residual" verdict of a-block-split-flips-a-caller-saved-pair on that function: the barrier was the diagnostic, the second assignment is the shippable form.

- id: a-global-store-before-the-two-locals-pins-the-missing-li-and-the-s0-s1-roles | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, constant, store, order, prologue, hoist
  **WHEN TWO `= 1` LOCALS AND ONE `g = 1` STORE SIT AT THE TOP OF A FUNCTION, THE ORDER OF THOSE THREE STATEMENTS DECIDES BOTH WHICH LOCAL TAKES `$s0`/`$s1` AND WHETHER THE STORE PAYS ITS OWN `li` - and it also decides whether the switch operand's global load gets hoisted above the frame setup** (round 451, menu/main/misc1 func_801C531C, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, 161 insns / 644 bytes, matched instruction for instruction with the jtbl operand as the only difference, `check_bin.sh menu` OK). Retail is `ori s1,zero,1` at entry, `lui v1,%hi(g_Menu)` / `lw v1` / `li v0,1` / `sw ra` / `sb v0,g` / `lbu v1,0x336(v1)`, with `ori s0,zero,1` in the `beqz` delay slot; s1 is the returned flag and s0 the per-arm result. Measured on the same body, three orders only: (a) `result = 1; shouldContinue = 1; g = 1;` -> 96.66% / 640 bytes, one instruction short, because the store reused the register already holding 1 (`sb s1,0(at)`), the `g_Menu` load was hoisted ABOVE `addiu sp,sp,-0x20`, and the two locals took the mirrored registers; (b) `g = 1; result = 1; shouldContinue = 1;` -> retail's prologue and the fresh `li v0,1` restored, but the locals still mirrored (`$s0`=returned flag); (c) `g = 1; shouldContinue = 1; result = 1;` -> exact, 644 bytes. So put the global store FIRST and initialise the locals in an order such that the first one gets the HIGHER callee-saved register, and read a store that reuses a saved 1 (`sb s1,<global>`) where retail has `li v0,1` / `sb v0` as this ordering tell rather than as an allocator tie - one reordering, no permuter run needed.

- id: a-retail-recomputes-a-shift-the-sum-also-needs | keywords: regalloc, sll, cse, recompute, duplicate, shift, subu, allocator
  **"RETAIL HAS TWO SHIFT INSTRUCTIONS YOUR BODY DOES NOT" IS A cc1 CSE GAP WHEN THE RECOMPUTED VALUES ARE THE SECOND OPERANDS OF THE SUBTRACTIONS: the `subu` result takes that operand's register, which kills the cse entry the sum needs, and no source spelling reaches it** (round 453, `field/main/misc5` `FieldInitializeParticlePrimitive`, re-measured and re-parked at 96.58% / 512 bytes / 128 insns against retail's 520 / 130). The body writes four values - `x1s-x0s`, `y1s-y0s`, `x0s+x1s`, `y0s+y1s`, `xs = x << 4` - to eight `SVECTOR` halves, i.e. four distinct shifts, and every compile gives four `sll`. Retail has six: `sll a3,a3,4` (x1s) and `sll a1,a1,4` (y1s) are shared with the sums, but in `sll a0,a1,4 / subu a0,a3,a0` the subu's destination IS the second operand's register, so x0s dies there and the sum re-forms it as `sll a1,a1,4`; same for y0s. Ten spellings probed with `cc1_probe.sh` on this unit's own cc1 (all four int locals; `u_short` locals; the four x stores then the four y stores; the shifted extremes in their own locals; a `SVECTOR*` vertex pointer local; a `ParticleShape*` local with inline field reads; no locals with the table read inline at all 16 sites; `x * 16 + y * 16` for the sums; `(x << 4) - -(y << 4)` for the sums): four `sll` every time, except the pointer-local form (the shift lands AFTER the subu) and the inline-read forms (16 `lhu` - the stores invalidate the load entries). -O3 also four, -O1 73.08, cdk 71.36, 2.6.0 identical to Default. Second tell that retail had one more live pseudo at the loads: its four `lhu` start at `a1` with `a0` left free, every spelling here starts at `a0`. Read this with the companion fact of c-a-minus-chain-reassociates-the-subtract (one copy plus one recompute per axis is a cse difference to park) - do not spend a lane probing spellings here, park on the sll count.
  Round 466 addendum (re-un-parked, identical 96.58 / 512 / 128): the blocker can be stated as a QUANTITY argument instead of a spelling list, which is what makes it terminal. Retail's `subu a0,a3,a0` puts the result in the SECOND OPERAND's register, and local-alloc only ties a result to an operand whose qty DIES at that insn - so in retail the shifted `x0 << 4` has exactly one use there and the sum's `sll a1,a1,4` rematerialises it from the still-live raw `x0`. A source with one `x0 << 4` occurrence per axis gives cse ONE qty with two uses, which can never die at the subu, so every spelling either keeps it (four `sll`, our 128 insns) or loses the entry another way. Reaching six `sll` therefore needs two source occurrences cse must NOT merge, and a call, a label or an aliasing store between them is the only thing that blocks cse - none of the three is in retail's body. Corollary for the frame: retail's 0x98 is 0x24 of o32 stack args + 0x18 of saves at 0x80.. + 0x5C of locals at 0x24..0x80 that NO instruction in the `.s` references, so the original had dead local aggregates whose stores cse deleted; for the code to stay as it is, such a local must fold away completely, so it is not a handle on the allocation - keep the `_pad` and do not try to name the dead local.

- id: a-value-live-across-a-call-that-retail-reloads-displaces-a-parameter | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, reload, live-across-call, parameter, mirror, array
  **WHEN RETAIL RE-LOADS AN ARRAY ELEMENT AFTER A CALL INSTEAD OF REUSING THE LOCAL IT PASSED IN, THE SOURCE HAD THE ARRAY SUBSCRIPT AT THE STORE, NOT THE LOCAL - AND KEEPING THE LOCAL LIVE ACROSS THE CALL IS WHAT PUTS IT IN A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER AND PUSHES A PARAMETER DOWN ONE, SO A WHOLE-FUNCTION REGISTER MIRROR IN THE PROLOGUE CAN HAVE ITS CAUSE IN ONE STORE NINE HUNDRED INSTRUCTIONS LATER** (round 459, world_map/main/misc14 func_80095414, 71.12 -> 71.73%, parked at 2156 bytes / 539 insns against retail's 2240 / 576, XenoWorldMapDiv). Retail's search loop is `lh v1,0x0(s0)` (the candidate index), `move t0,v1` for the callee's argument, and then, after the `WorldMapProjectTriangleNormal` call, `lh v1,0x0(s0)` AGAIN feeding `sw v1,%lo(g_WorldMapStepTriangleIndex)` - i.e. `g_WorldMapStepTriangleIndex = D_8009D718[i];`, not `= next;`. With `= next;` the local `next` is live across the call, gcc hands it a callee-saved register (`$s6`) and pDelta falls to `$s7`; with the reload the prologue is retail's exactly (`sw s6,0xA8(sp)` then `addu s6,a1,zero`) and the -1/base/pOut hand-outs shift with it, +0.61% for one line. Diagnostic rule: when a parameter is one register lower in retail than in the body and the function is long, look for a LOCAL THAT RETAIL RE-LOADS FROM ITS ARRAY OR GLOBAL AFTER A CALL rather than reusing; the tell is a `move tN,<local>` before the `jal` followed by a fresh load of the same address after it. The remaining ties on that body (base vs -1 for `$s7`/`$s8`, pOut vs count for `$s3`/`$s4`, `state` in `$v1` against retail's `$s1`) did not move under any spelling, and cdk measures 69.74 against the unit's 2.7.2.

- id: a-multiply-cse-across-a-call-costs-the-parameters-register | keywords: regalloc, cse, spill, parameter, multiply, delay-slot, s8, frame
  **A MULTIPLY SHARED BY TWO CALL ARGUMENTS IN ONE ARM (`BattleDrawSpritePackage(8,..,i*0x10+0x54,..)` then `..(7,..,i*0x10+0x64,..)`) IS CSEd ACROSS THE FIRST CALL, AND THE PSEUDO THAT HOLDS IT TAKES ONE OF THE TEN CALLEE-SAVED REGISTERS - WHICH IS THE REGISTER THE FUNCTION'S `u8` PARAMETER NEEDED, SO THE PARAMETER IS SPILLED AND THE WHOLE FRAME GROWS; SPELLING THE SECOND ARGUMENT AS A DIFFERENT TREE (`(i + 1) * 0x10 + 0x54`) BREAKS THE CSE AND HANDS THE REGISTER BACK** (round 460, battle/main/misc13 func_800861D0, 95.22 -> 98.56%, 2504 -> 2496 bytes / 626 -> 624 insns against retail 2488 / 622; the frame went 96 -> retail's 88, `move s8,a1` came back, and every one of the six `andi X,fp,0xff` re-masks replaced an `lbu X,24(sp)` reload). Retail re-forms the multiply after each call (`sll a2,s2,0x4` in the `jal` delay slot), which is the signature: retail's register set only exists if the CSE does not. Two limits measured on the same body: `(i << 4) + 0x64` is NOT a different tree - cc1 canonicalises the multiply to the shift at RTL, so the object is byte-identical (95.22, unchanged) - and the shift of the OTHER argument changes nothing either; the rewrite has to add or remove an operation, not respell one. Diagnostic that found it: dump both objects and diff the sequences with the register names normalised (`sed` every `$sN/$aN/$vN` to `R`), then count instructions between consecutive `jal`s - the surplus appears exactly in the arm that carries the CSE.
- id: a-flag-word-rmw-mask-follows-the-other-two | keywords: regalloc, flag, rmw, mask, word, shift, rotation, local-alloc
  **IN A FLAG-WORD READ-MODIFY-WRITE WHOSE THREE PSEUDOS (MASK CONSTANT, LOADED WORD, SHIFTED VALUE) EACH HAVE ONE REF, MOVING ONE OF THEM ROTATES ALL THREE - the mask is NOT independently pinnable, so there is only one degree of freedom to steer (word versus shift) and a spelling that wins it hands the mask a different register** (round 460, battle/main/misc31 func_800BB350, XenoBattleTailCdk0, re-parked 98.10% at retail's exact 496 bytes / 124 insns). Retail's tail is `lw a0,0xA8(s0)` / `sll v0,s5,0x1e` / `sw zero,0x4C` / `sw zero,0x48` / `sb s4,<global>` / `and a0,a0,v1` / `or a0,a0,v0` / `srl v0,s5,0x2` / `lw v1,0xAC(s0)` / `andi v0,v0,0x3` / `sw a0,0xA8(s0)` - mask $v1, word $a0, shift $v0, and its store sinks past the 0xAC load because $a0 is untouched by the `srl`. Measured on the same body, all at 124 insns: the one-expression form keeps mask $v1 / word $v0 / shift $a0 (98.10); reading the load as its OWN statement at retail's `lw` position (the a-in-place-chain-on-a-named-local shape) is BYTE-IDENTICAL (98.10), so pinning the word first is not what moves it; creating the shift in a local above the load gives mask $a0 / word $v0 / shift $v1 (97.78), a three-way rotation rather than one moved register. Cross-check that makes the class parkable: system/temp1's MATCHED func_80023B84 holds the same one-expression statement under the same 2.7.2-cdk with retail's mask in $v0, word in $a1 and shift in $a0 - i.e. the mask keeps the lowest register only when its live range is long, so the pick follows block coverage of the 0x8CB8 address temp rather than any source order. Do not spend a lane re-spelling this family; park on the mask/word/shift triple.

- id: a-a-value-live-across-a-call-costs-a-saved-reg-where-a-reload-does-not | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, reload, lh, live-range, call, s8, struct-field
  **A LOCAL THAT MUST SURVIVE A CALL TAKES A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER, AND READING THE SAME VALUE BACK OUT OF THE STRUCT FIELD IT WAS STORED TO TRADES THAT REGISTER FOR EXACTLY ONE RELOAD - so when a body is one saved word and two instructions over retail, try the memory read before hunting allocator ties** (round 461, field/main/misc8 func_80082620, 95.34 -> 96.26% at 1436 bytes / 359 insns against retail's 1424 / 358, Default preset). The body computed a `s16 dyAngle = pTracked[i].rotation.y - track->rotationY;`, stored it to `delta.vy`, and used the local after `FieldGetActorDistance2D` and `ratan2`; that value needed a 9th callee-saved register, so `actorIndex` was pushed to `$s8` (10 saved words, 362 insns). Writing `delta.vy = <the difference>;` and using `delta.vy` in the angle expression replaces the register with `lh v0,0x52(sp)` and restores retail's 9-word saved set (359 insns, one over). Measured on the same body, all 1448 bytes / 362 insns: `s16 dyAngle` 95.34 (+`$s8`), `s32 dyAngle = (s16)(...)` 95.19, the chained `delta.vy = dyAngle = ...` 95.34. The gap the two shapes leave is retail's own middle route - it truncates into a register early (`sll a0,a0,16` after the delta stores, `sra s0,a0,16` in the `bnez` delay slot) and REUSES `$s0`, which is dead `stepX` in that arm - so the register only costs a save when the value is not a single-arm reuse.
- id: a-two-init-near-tie-flips-one-pair-not-the-other | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, tie, init, li, prologue, delay-slot, order
  **TWO `= 1` LOCALS AT THE TOP OF A FUNCTION PIN BOTH THE PROLOGUE HOIST AND THE REGISTER PAIR, AND WHICH ONE IS HOISTED IS ALSO WHICH ONE *FIRST* IN THE SOURCE - so a diff whose delay slot holds the wrong `li` AND whose saved pair is mirrored is ONE statement-order question, and the answer is visible before any dump: write the init order that puts retail's hoisted value first** (round 468, menu/main/misc9 func_801DB920, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, 267 insns / 1068 bytes, re-parked 98.45%). Retail hoists `active = 1` into the prologue (`sw s5,0x54(sp)` / `ori s5,zero,1`, s5 = active) and leaves `refresh = 1` for the `andi 0x80`/`beqz` delay slot (s1 = refresh); the park's `result = 0; refresh = 1; active = 1;` measures 98.45% / 1068 / 267 with the hoist and the slot MIRRORED (refresh hoisted, active in the slot) but active = `$s5` and the shared const-1 = `$s6`, both retail's, while `result = 0; active = 1; refresh = 1;` (the flags load before or after the refresh init measures identically) gives retail's exact hoist/slot pattern but swaps that pair (active = `$s6`, const-1 = `$s5`) - 98.19%, 64 differing lines. So the (active, const-1) contest is a genuine tie that a reorder breaks on allocno number, and the (refresh, pItemId) mirror it exposes does not move in either order (6 QI refs over ~210 insns against 2 SI refs over ~20, the quotient gap `a-global-allocno-priority-is` calls unreachable). Read this as: when a reorder flips a pair, that pair is a tie and the remaining mirror is not - take the order that wins the hoist/slot, then park on the pair and say which one is the tie.
  Round 481 put `-da`/`-dg`/`-dl` on that body, which replaces the estimate in the last sentence with the quotient itself and closes the (refresh, pItemId) mirror by arithmetic: `20 regs to allocate: 76 74 123 179 87 82 81 77 83 73 84 131 80 75 ...` with 87 (pItemId) `used 5 times across 18 insns; pointer` = 2.22 and 81 (refresh) `used 17 times across 144 insns; 1 bytes` = 0.47. Retail's hand-out needs refresh to be processed BEFORE pItemId, i.e. 0.47 to clear 2.22 - refs >= 32, or a live range of <= 30 insns on a QI pseudo whose `andi 0xff` retail emits - or pItemId to fall under 0.47, i.e. a live range >= 85 insns for a 2-ref pointer retail forms in the case-4 preheader. Neither is a spelling, so read this pair as closed and do not brief it again. Also measured there, worse and reverted: `result = 0` moved OUT of `if (refresh)` to the top of the loop body (retail's zeroing does run unconditionally, in the `beqz` delay slot) measures 98.22% / 1068 / 267 with 54 differing lines, because the store is then hoisted into the prologue and the pair ROTATES to result=`$s2`, refresh=`$s3` - an unconditional store's slot fill is not the same insn as retail's, so the delay-slot residual in this body is not explained by statement scope.

- id: a-pluss-result-and-a-loads-dest-both-take-the-dying-base-register | keywords: regalloc, coalesce, load, dest, base, addu, pointer, chain
  **TWO HAND-OUTS THIS cc1 WILL NOT GIVE UP, BOTH "THE RESULT REUSES THE DYING BASE PSEUDO'S REGISTER": a pointer chain `p = *(u16*)(p + K) + p;` puts the `addu`'s destination on the BASE in every spelling, and `pFrameData = pBase->pCurRenderFramesData;` puts the load's destination on the DEAD `pBase` register -- so a retail body whose offset pseudo / a freed earlier register owns those values is unreachable from source** (round 468, slus_006.64/system/rendering_b, XenoRendering = gcc-2.7.2, two parks re-measured and left: `func_8001F5BC` 97.95% / 244 bytes / 61 insns and `func_8001F6B0` 97.38% / 160 bytes / 40 insns, both at retail's exact size with an identical instruction multiset). `func_8001F5BC`: retail's 5th insn is `addu v1,v1,v0` (dest = the just-loaded u16 OFFSET pseudo) and ours is `addu v0,v0,v1` (dest = the BASE); measured dead on that body - the single expression, `(u8*)((mem_addr)*(u16*)(pAnimations + 2) + (mem_addr)pAnimations)`, the in-place `pAnimations += *(u16*)(pAnimations + 2);` (the `b-in-place-...` lever, which does not apply to a memory-loaded offset), a chain through a separate `u8* pAnimation` local, and a named `u32 offset` temp (94.75 / one insn SHORT, so the temp is strictly worse). Everything downstream rotates from that one coalesce (pFrame a1 instead of retail's in-place `addu a0,v0,a0`, the parameter t0 instead of a1, the second division's v0/v1 mirror), which is why the park reads 38 differing lines on a body of retail's exact size. `func_8001F6B0`: ours emits `lw v1,32(t1)` (pBase) then `lw v1,48(v1)` (the load dest coalesced onto the dead base) so pFrameData is v1 and the freed a0 goes to the loop counter; retail keeps that load dest in a0 and gives v1 to the `sll`. A named `SpriteDataI1* pBase` local is byte-identical, and moving the pFrameData statement above the colour load moves the colour word into a0 instead (97.12). Judge these parks by the FIRST hand-out in the diff: if the first differing register is a coalesce of this kind, the rest of the rotation is downstream and no spelling of the later sites will fix it.

- id: a-the-pointer-registers-hands-out-the-macro-scratch-registers | keywords: maspsx, scratch, macro, lhu, lui, pointer, loop, bias, base, absolute-symbol
  **A `lhu GLOBAL` / `lui+lw GLOBAL` MACRO INSIDE A LOOP IS EXPANDED BY MASPSX INTO THE FIRST FREE REGISTER OF {a1, v1, a0}, SO THE REGISTER THE LOOP'S BIASED POINTER OCCUPIES DECIDES EVERY ABSOLUTE-SYMBOL LOAD IN THE BODY - a diff that looks like "every register one place off" can be ONE allocator hand-out, and the assembler, not cc1, produces the shift.** Round 469, battling/main/misc9 func_80082C4C (XenoBattlingNoGp = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G0, 133 insns, parked 94.35%): cc1's own `.s` there is `lhu $5,D_800927A0` macros; retail holds the biased sprite pointer `p+0x25` in `$a1` and maspsx expands the two macros into `$v1`/`$a0`, this body coalesces the pointer into `$v1` (its own `.s` reads `addu $3,$3,37`, retail has `addiu a1,v1,0x25` - a separate pseudo) and maspsx then picks `$a1`/`$a0`, which is all 63 differing lines plus one unfilled load-delay slot (134 insns / 0x218 against retail's 133 / 0x214). Two usable readings: (1) count the diff as ONE residual and look at what register the pointer *came from* - retail keeping a separate `addiu` instead of an in-place add means its pointer pseudo did not coalesce with the base load, which no source spelling reached here (for-init comma assignment, declaration order, a shared statement order for both halves, `-O3` all identical; cdk 71.26 and 2.6.0 85.30, so not a compiler question); (2) THE BIAS OFFSET IS A FINGERPRINT OF THE SOURCE FORM, so read it before choosing one: a fill loop over N records written `p`/`p++` biases the base to a MIDDLE offset (here `p+0x25`, the last field of the first record - retail's) while the same body written `p[0]`/`p[1]` with `p += 2` biases to the END of the block (`p+0x4D`) at the very same 133 insns / 0x214 bytes. So objdiff can prefer the wrong source form: the `p[0]`/`p[1]` body measures 93.62% at retail's exact size while the `p`/`p++` body measures 94.35% four bytes over, and the size match is the coincidence.
- id: a-one-pointer-local-per-copy-base-splits-the-copy-registers | keywords: regalloc, base, pointer, local, table, copy, split, addu
  **WHEN SEVERAL STRUCT-ASSIGNMENT COPIES THROUGH ONE COMPUTED TABLE BASE (`index * sizeof(T) + g_Table`) ALL SHARE ONE POINTER LOCAL, gcc GIVES EVERY OCCURRENCE THE SAME REGISTER (and the same reuse: a re-formed base lands in the SAME register the first copy used); GIVING EACH COPY-GROUP ITS OWN POINTER LOCAL MAKES EACH BASE A SEPARATE PSEUDO AND HANDS THEM RETAIL'S REGISTERS IN TURN** (round 470, world_map/main/misc9 func_80088720, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2-psx, 90.69 -> 97.59% at retail's EXACT 264 insns / 1056 bytes, 222 -> 16 differing lines). Retail copies a 0x20-byte matrix into `g_WorldMapGroups[tileIndex].matrix` five times, using `$v1` for the entry-5 copy and `$v0` for the entry-3 copy and the 3->2->1->0 chain, and re-reads `g_WorldMapGroups` between them; with ONE `pEntries` variable the compile put every base in `$t0` (all ~110 copy rows differ by that one name, which is why such a body reads 91% with an identical instruction multiset), with `pParent` for the chain the second base came out `$v0` (94.23), and with a third local `pEntry` for the trailing quad copy that base did too (97.59), after which the first base fell out as `$v1` with retail's `$a0/$a1/$a2` copy temps. So a "not a spelling" verdict on a copy-base register split is worth one re-test with per-copy variables: the register split follows the SOURCE VARIABLES, not the number of reloads. Companion, same function: a struct copy whose source is written as a LITERAL address (`*(WorldMapPos4*)0x1F800000`) re-materialises the address (`la t7,0x1F800000`) and splits the block move 3 words + 1 word with a nop (+2 instructions, 1064 bytes), where copying through the pointer whose register already holds that address (`*(WorldMapPos4*)pPos`) reuses it and gives retail's 4 x `lw` / 4 x `sw` at retail's exact size.


- id: a-a-do-while-parity-knob-does-not-stack | keywords: regalloc, do-while, parity, reorg, dispatch, andi, duplicate, callee-saved
  **A `do { } while (0)` THAT BUYS RETAIL'S DUPLICATED DISPATCH `andi` CAN COST THE CALLEE-SAVED PAIR IN THE SAME BODY, AND A SECOND ONE DOES NOT STACK - the knob is reorg block numbering PARITY, so measure the pair and the byte count together and accept whichever trade is larger** (round 470, menu/main/misc9 func_801DBE54, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, parked 94.26% / 892 bytes / 223 insns against retail's 896 / 224). The body is a 10-case input switch whose loop test is `andi v0,sX,0xff`; with an empty statement at the end of case 2's arm, reorg duplicates that `andi` into the out-of-range dispatch's `beqz` delay slot exactly as retail has it (888 -> 892 bytes, 93.91 -> 94.17%) - but the same edit mirrors `(active, needsOpen)` between `$s5`/`$s6`. The same empty statement at the end of case 9's arm measures the same 892 / 94.17 with the same mirror, and BOTH do-whiles together measure 892 / 94.17 again, so it is parity of the block count, not an accumulating barrier. A companion measurement on the same body: the two `= 1` local inits move only the PROLOGUE SAVE ORDER (`needsOpen = 1; active = 1;` saves `$s6` first like retail, 94.26; the other order saves `$s5` first, 94.17) and never the register pair - read the init order as a save-order lever only, per a-two-init-near-tie-flips-one-pair-not-the-other. The other residual is a cross-jump one: retail keeps a separate `j` into the `selectedSlot = 0xFF` block it shares with case 5, the body merges the two blocks and threads case 5's `bne` onto the merged block's `j`.

- id: a-a-field-type-change-recolors-the-neighbouring-loop | keywords: regalloc, type, u8, s32, andi, two-loops, shared-local, recolor, objdiff
  **IN A FUNCTION WITH TWO LOOPS OVER THE SAME FIELD, TYPING THE SHARED LOAD LOCAL `s32` KILLS RETAIL'S ABSENT `andi 0xff` IN LOOP 2 BUT MOVES LOOP 1'S OTHER `u8` LOAD OFF ITS REGISTER - and the two spellings disagree with objdiff's score, which PREFERS the body with one instruction MORE** (round 472, world_map/main/misc1 func_80071CDC, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2-psx, parked 94.10% / 540 bytes / 135 insns against retail's 133; progress from 84.51). Retail loads the party id with `lbu s0` and compares it with no mask in both loops, but loop 1's `lbu` result and the gearId load that follows have one type that satisfies both loops only by accident: with ONE `s32 nCharacterId` loop 2 is mask-free and the id lands in `$s0` as retail has it, at the cost of loop 1's gearId moving from `$a0` to `$v0` plus one extra `addu` (94.10% / 135 insns); with `u8 nCharacterId` for loop 1 plus a second `s32` local for loop 2, loop 1 is byte-identical and the body is 134 insns / 536 bytes but scores 92.21%, because loop 2's id then sits in `$v1` instead of `$s0`. So measure BOTH, park the higher objdiff number, and write the trade in the park note; do not assume the byte-exact loop is the better park. Two dead spellings measured on the same body: a fresh loop-2 index variable (so the saved register the first loop's `i` frees can go to the entry counter, retail's `i` is `$a0`/`nCount` `$s1`) rotates loop 1's entire s-set and drops to 91.23%; u8 byte cursors with `*(s16 *)pCursor` stores are byte-identical to typed `u16*`/`void**` cursors.

- id: a-block-boundary-gives-the-base-its-register-and-takes-the-latency-fill | keywords: regalloc, do-while, block, boundary, hoist, mult, latency, base
  **A `do { ... } while (0)` AROUND A DELAYED STORE GROUP HANDS THE GROUP'S BASE POINTER RETAIL'S REGISTER (the highest free arg reg) BUT ALSO STOPS sched2 FILLING THE PRECEDING `mult` LATENCY WINDOW WITH THAT GROUP'S CONSTANT AND ADDRESS, SO THE TWO HALVES OF THE FIX CANCEL** (round 473, slus_006.64/system/system func_80034888, Default preset, parked 98.99% / 1572 bytes / 393 insns = retail's exact size). The clear-tile tail is `setXY0Fast / setWHFast / SystemLinkPrim(pOt, &pString->clearTile[context])`; without a block the body reaches 98.03 with the base in `$a2` and retail has `$a3`, and the window holds `lui 0xff00` where retail holds the tag load. Wrapping only the link in a do-while gives the base `$a3` (retail) and blocks the mask `lui/ori` and the address out of the window, so a load-delay `nop` appears: 394 insns / 1576 bytes / 96.87%. Wrapping all three statements: base back in `$a2`, 393 / 1572 / 98.31%. Three realistic spellings of the link (the file's own AddPrim-inline macro, the same with `.tag`, and two statements with a `u_long tag` local) all measure 98.03 with the tag load at base+offset as retail has it, so the surviving 0.96% lives in WHICH instruction fills the window, not in the spelling - and when a boundary fixes the register and breaks the window fill, the two are one trade-off, not two residuals.

- id: a-an-identical-arm-branch-is-a-refs-probe | keywords: regalloc, refs, allocno, probe, permuter, identical, arms, diagnostic
  **A PERMUTER CANDIDATE THAT WRAPS ONE ARM IN `if (p) { A } else { A }` IS A REFS PROBE, NOT WRONG CODE: gcc MERGES THE TWO IDENTICAL ARMS so the instruction stream is unchanged, and the only thing that moved is the pointer's allocno ref count - so port it for 30 seconds to read whether a wrong register is refs-driven, then find a NATURAL extra reference or park** (round 474, world_map/main/misc16 func_80099708, XenoWorldMapDiv, 65 insns / 260 bytes = retail's exact size, parked 97.74% with three wrong registers and one increment two slots late). The 3-minute run came back `base=155 best=140` whose single edit was that branch on `pPkt`; ported, it measures 97.97% and `pPkt` takes retail's `$t0` while the other three keep cycling - i.e. one extra reference is exactly what that allocno was missing, and the body itself has no fourth natural use of `pPkt` to write, so the honest body parks. Use the ported candidate as the diagnostic (does the hand-out flip? then it is refs, and `a-second-assignment-to-the-losers-promotes-it-to-a-global-allocno` is the shippable form), and never ship the identical-arm branch: it is a spelling nobody wrote in 1998.


- id: a-caller-saved-rotation-can-depend-on-the-blocks-after-it | keywords: regalloc, rotation, caller-saved, blocks, truncate, probe, v0, v1, a1
  **A CALL BLOCK'S CALLER-SAVED ROTATION (`$v0`/`$v1`/`$a1` handed the count, the chain and the base in the "wrong" order) IS DECIDED BY THE WHOLE FUNCTION'S BLOCK ORDER, SO MEASURE IT WITH A TRUNCATION PROBE BEFORE SPELLING AT IT: replacing everything after the block with a `return;` and re-diffing tells you in one run whether the block's own body is what is wrong** (round 474, battle/main/misc14 func_800898F0, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0, 91.38 -> 97.23% at retail's EXACT 520 bytes / 130 insns). Retail's three identical `x += BattleDrawSpritePackage(id, (s32)(off + (s32)g_BattleSpriteColumnWork), pitch >> 16, 0xCC)` sites have base `$v1` / count `$v0` / chain `$a1`; every body of the correct shape (statement-separated `off`, the re-tested `while (i < 4) { s32 slot = ids[i++]; ... }` of the matched neighbours) emits base `$a1` / count `$v1` / chain `$v0`, same instructions. Truncating the function after the first loop made that loop allocate exactly retail's way, so the body was already right and the residual is the block/allocno context: removing loop 2, the tail call, the resets, either store, or pitch's second init individually changes nothing, i.e. it is not one statement. Same-block spellings measured byte-identical: `off` as u32, a named count local, a named base local, both operand orders of the arg sum, `for` vs `while`, the pitch increment inside vs outside the `if`. Do not park this class as "allocator tie" without the probe: the probe is what separates "my body is wrong" from "the rest of the function decides".

- id: a-a-surviving-copy-of-a-live-pointer-re-allocates-the-whole-function | keywords: regalloc, copy, pseudo, arm, mirror, s0, s1, callee-saved, instruction count
  **A RESIDUAL THAT IS "RETAIL HAS ONE EXTRA `addu aN,sN,zero` COPY OF A LIVE POINTER AND READS THE ARM THROUGH IT" CANNOT BE SOURCED: ANY COPY THAT SURVIVES THE COALESCER COSTS A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER AND MIRRORS EVERY REGISTER IN THE FUNCTION** (round 478, lib_gear/main/main func_801E5D44, parked 97.61% at retail's exact 1512 bytes / 378 insns; retail's case-2 arm reads `pCmd->...` through `$a1` after `addu a1,s0,zero` in the `beqz` delay slot, while every body reads through `$s0`). Measured on one 378-instruction body: `pCommand = pCmd;` written inside the `index < 2` sub-block with the merged reads through `pCommand` DOES survive, but costs 4 instructions (382 insns / 1528 bytes, 95.71%) and moves case 9's pointer from `$a0` to `$s2`; the same copy at the top of the arm is 96.74% / 1512 / 378 with `$s0`/`$s1` swapped at every one of the body's ~100 sites, because the extra pseudo takes a callee-saved register and local-alloc hands out the rest differently. So judge such a park closed rather than one edit away, and do not spend runs on copy positions: this is the `a-a-parameter-home-register-is-abandoned-when-its-block-sets-it` class seen from the other side (there the copy never exists, here it exists only at the price of the whole allocation).


- id: a-split-loop-local-frees-the-callee-saved-set | keywords: regalloc, loop, local, split, shared, callee-saved, rotation, quotient
  **A LOCAL SHARED BY TWO CONSECUTIVE LOOPS WHEN ONLY THE FIRST ONE NEEDS IT PERSISTENT IS A WHOLE-CALLEE-SAVED ROTATION: giving the second loop its own variable moves the shared one back to a caller-saved register and restores the first loop's `$s0/$s1/$s2` roles with no instruction-count change** (round 479, battling/main/misc17 func_8008E120, Default = gcc-2.7.2: one `s32 value` used as loop 1's persistent switch value AND as loop 2's per-iteration quotient scored 91.16% / 400 bytes / 100 insns with loop 1's registers mirrored; a second local `s32 avg` for loop 2's quotient measured 89.31% / 392 bytes / 98 insns but made all 40 instructions of loop 1 retail's, including the `move s2/v0` structure - so judge the split by the instruction stream, not by the fuzzy percentage, which fell because the rest of loop 2 re-allocated). The reason is the `floor_log2(refs)*refs/live_length` quotient: the shared pseudo's live range spans BOTH loops, so its priority drops below the loop-1 counter's and it takes the highest s-register; two variables give it a short range in loop 2 and a caller-saved register there, which is what retail's `subu v1,v1,v0` shows.
- id: i-a-two-symbol-preheader-hoist-order | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, preheader, lui, addiu, base, offset, order, adjacency
  **WHEN A LOOP PREHEADER HOISTS TWO SYMBOL ADDRESS GROUPS AND ONE OF THEM APPEARS IN TWO FORMS (base AND base+offset), THE GROUP EMITTED FIRST IS THE ONE WHOSE TWO FORMS ARE ADJACENT IN THE SOURCE, AND THE FORM WRITTEN FIRST BECOMES THE PRIMARY (the other is derived with a NEGATIVE addiu)** (round 479, battle/main/misc19_r1 func_8009BE0C, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0, 97.23 -> 100.00% at retail's EXACT 580 bytes / 145 insns, `check_bin.sh battle` OK). Retail's prologue is `lui t5,%hi(g_BattleWorkBlock)` / `addiu t5,%lo` / `addiu t7,t5,0xA4` then `lui t4,%hi(g_GameState+0x26C)` / `addiu t4` / `addiu t6,t4,0x70C`: the slot-table group first, base primary, the +0xA4 state base derived positively. Three spellings of the same otherwise-exact body: (a) `p = &g_BattleWorkBlock[i];` then `pChar`/`pGear`, with `pState = (BattleSlotState*)((u8*)&g_BattleWorkBlock[i] + 0xA4);` written LAST - the intra-group shape is retail's (+164) but gcc emits the g_GameState group FIRST, 99.71%, 22 differing lines, all register names; (b) the same `pState` written FIRST and `p` second - the +0xA4 form becomes the primary (`addiu t5,%lo+164` then `addiu t7,t5,-164`), so the group order becomes retail's but the stream gains an addiu retail does not have, 99.82%; (c) `p` first and that same `pState` line as the NEXT statement, 100.00%. So make the base and its +offset partner consecutive with the base first, and order the two symbols by which group retail emits first. Measured dead on the same body: `pState = &p->state` (the typed member; the +0xA4 hoist vanishes and g_GameState takes `$t5`), and `pState = (BattleSlotState*)((u8*)p + 0xA4)` (the whole slot-table address stays inside the loop). Two park-hygiene notes from the same close: an unused `u32 frame[2]` IS load-bearing for retail's empty 8-byte frame (deleting it deletes `addiu sp,sp,-8`), and the park's two `*(volatile u16*)&p->hp` / `*(volatile u32*)&pGear->hp` casts were NOT needed once the body's shape was right - plain stores are 100.00%.

- id: a-six-argument-call-head-cannot-be-moved-off-v0-v1 | keywords: regalloc, argument, delay-slot, sll, addu, jal, head, li
  **A SIX-ARGUMENT `SpriteAllocFromAnimFile` HEAD WHOSE INDEX SHIFT AND GLOBAL BASE SIT IN `$v0`/`$v1` HERE AND IN `$v1`/`$a2` IN RETAIL IS CLOSED, NOT ONE SPELLING AWAY: the retail shape only exists because the third-argument register is free early there, and NOTHING IN THE SOURCE REACHES IT - the whole head is a consequence of the register set, and the register set is decided by the rest of the function, not by the call** (round 481, world_map/main/misc10 func_8008A5B8 92.63% / 372 bytes / 93 insns and func_8008A2C8 95.46% / 612 / 153, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2-psx; both bodies compile INSTRUCTION-FOR-INSTRUCTION identical from `move a0,v0` on, so the residual is one 12-line head repeated in three functions of the unit). Retail: `addiu a1,0,0x100 / sll a2,a0,0x7 / li v0,0x100 / sw v0,0x10(sp) / li v0,0x40 / lui a0(anim) / lw a0 / lui v1(g_Slots) / lw v1 / li a3,0x140 / sw ra / sw s0 / sw v0,0x14(sp) / addu s0,v1,a2 / jal / li a2,0x1E0`. Ours: shift `$v1`, base `$v0`, `addu s0,v0,v1` in the `jal` slot and `li a2,0x1E0` at insn 8. The TRUNCATION PROBE (see `a-call-blocks-caller-saved-rotation-...`) says the head is body-dependent - cutting the body to the alloc call gives base `$s0` coalesced into the sum and shift `$v0` - but there is no handle because the body itself is exact. Measured identical at 92.63 this round, all on the same body: `pActor = g_WorldMapSlots + arg0;` (pointer arithmetic, no subscript); a `void* pAnimFile` local placed AFTER the pointer; a named `s32 size` local for the sixth argument's 0x40 (copy-propagated back to the literal, which also disproves "retail's base is `$v1` because `$v0` still holds the 0x40"); and rounds 452/468 measured the subscript, `(u8*)base + index * 0x80`, a separate `s32` offset local, a declaration-with-initialiser, and `(WorldMapPlayer*)((u8*)... + (arg0 << 7))`. Presets are dead too (2.6.0 76.09, 2.7.2-cdk 76.69 on the sibling, cdk -O2 71.79 / -O3 95.46 on A2C8) and so is `-fschedule-insns` in cc1's own output. The neighbouring retail functions disagree with each other on this head (misc11_c WorldMapInitPartyActorSprite0/1 and matched misc11_b WorldMapInitPartyActorSprite2 all shift into `$v1` with the base straight into `$s0`), which is the tell that it is an allocator outcome per function. Park this class; a head fix would convert all three.
- id: a-qI-value-derived-from-a-live-local-should-be-masked-in-place | keywords: regalloc, rotation, callee-saved, block-local, andi, index, in-place, local-alloc
  **A BYTE MASKED OFF A LOCAL THAT IS LIVE ACROSS A CALL SHOULD BE THE SAME VARIABLE, MASKED IN PLACE: A SEPARATE `s32 index = mode & 0xF;` IS A PSEUDO WHOSE WHOLE LIFE IS ONE BASIC BLOCK, SO LOCAL-ALLOC (NOT GLOBAL-ALLOC) HANDS IT THE FIRST FREE CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER AND PUSHES EVERY OTHER VALUE UP ONE, ROTATING THE WHOLE FUNCTION'S SAVED MAP** (round 491, slus_006.64/system/sound func_8003D9A4, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0, 268 bytes / 67 insns either way: the twin-port body with `index = mode & 0xF;` is 91.13% and `mode &= 0xF;` at the same site is 90.52% WITH retail's exact prologue save order and the element pointer in retail's `$s1`). `-dl` on the first body is explicit about the cause: `index` is `used 4 times across 17 insns in block 7` - the "in block N" suffix is the block-local signature - while element/velocity/mode/pScript are live from block 0, and retail's own map (`flags $s0, element $s1, velocity $s2, mode $s3` with the index reusing `$s3` after the mask kills mode) can only be produced by a body with one fewer block-local candidate. So read `-dl` for "in block N" before reordering declarations on a rotation, and prefer the in-place mask when the derived value is only ever fed by that one variable. What the in-place form does NOT fix on this function is the mask's own register: retail computes it into `$a2` (the call's argument register) and copies with `move s3,a2`, so the `sra` of the third argument lands in the `jal` slot, while the in-place body masks into its home and then needs `move a2,sN` in the slot - that residual is a copy suggestion on the argument, not an allocation question.
- id: a-biased-iv-reuses-or-keeps-the-dying-pointer-register | keywords: regalloc, caller-saved, iv, bias, coalesce, addiu, in-place, pointer
  **A LOOP THAT FILLS A STRUCT ARRAY THROUGH ONE POINTER GETS ITS BASE BIASED TO THE HIGHEST FIELD IT STORES (`addiu p,0x25` for a 0x28-byte POLY_FT4), AND WHETHER THAT BIASED IV KEEPS ITS OWN CALLER-SAVED REGISTER OR RUNS IN PLACE ON THE JUST-LOADED POINTER IS NOT A SPELLABLE KNOB - retail's `lw v1,%lo(g) / addiu a1,v1,0x25` is a FRESH pseudo (so the freed `$v1` then takes the first per-quad `lhu`), ours is the in-place `addiu v1,v1,37` (so the `lhu` takes `$a1`), and the same flip also costs 4 bytes because retail fills an `lbu` delay slot with a store that ours hoists one slot earlier, leaving a `nop`** (round 482, battling/main/misc9 func_80082C4C, parked 94.35% / 536 bytes / 134 insns against retail's 532 / 133; every other instruction, the frame, both HeapAlloc calls and the CLUT loop are identical, all 63 differing lines are that one register). Measured dead on the same body: the two per-quad `clut`/`tpage` loads moved above the two `setPolyFT4` tag stores (87.92%, the tag stores must stay first), `clut`/`tpage` declared before the `POLY_FT4 *p` (byte-identical 94.35%, so this hand-out is not declaration-order sensitive), quad 2 written in quad 1's store order (94.10%), `p[0]`/`p[1]` with `p += 2` (93.62% but the bias moves to +0x4D, so the `p`/`p++` form is the right source), 2.7.2 `-O3` (94.35), preset screen cdk 71.26 / 2.6.0 85.30, and a 3-minute permuter run (base=935 best=905). The tell is the disassembly of the bias itself: `addiu rX,rX,N` in place means gcc folded the loaded pointer (dead at that insn) into the IV, so the register the first global load takes afterwards is forced; park the body and say which register is mirrored.

- id: a-two-literal-inits-only-move-the-prologue-save-order | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, swapped, init, order, prologue, mirror, qi
  **TWO `u8` LOCALS BOTH INITIALISED `= 1` KEEP THE SAME REGISTER EACH WHATEVER ORDER THE TWO INIT STATEMENTS ARE WRITTEN IN; ONLY THE PROLOGUE'S SAVE ORDER FOLLOWS THE SOURCE - so a mirrored pair of them is not a statement-order question, and reordering the inits only costs percentage** (round 483, menu/main/misc9 func_801DBE54, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, parked 94.26% / 892 bytes / 223 insns against retail's 896 / 224). Retail has `active = $s6` (its `= 1` first, `move s6,zero` in the case-5 arm) and `needsOpen = $s5` (the `andi 0xff` loop test). With `needsOpen = 1; active = 1;` the body emits retail's prologue ORDER (`sw s6 / li s6,1 / sw s5 / li s5,1`) but with the pair mirrored: 94.26%, 109 differing lines. With `active = 1; needsOpen = 1;` it emits `sw s5 / li s5,1 / sw s6 / li s6,1` and active is STILL `$s5`: 94.17%, 113 lines. So the init order decides only which `sw` comes first; flipping the mapping needs the two allocnos' quotient or processing ORDER changed (`a-global-allocno-priority-is`), never the statements. Same verdict as `a-declaration-order-decides-the-callee-saved-pair-through-live-length`'s negative half: do not re-brief a two-literal-init mirror as an init-order knob.

- id: a-guard-through-the-array-and-the-walk-through-a-second-pointer | keywords: regalloc, loop, preheader, guard, pointer, walk, coalesce, callee-saved, delay-slot
  **A `-1`-TERMINATED ID LOOP WHOSE GUARD AND WALK BOTH READ ONE `pIds` VARIABLE IS COALESCED BY cse INTO A SINGLE PSEUDO AND THE LOOP POINTER THEN TAKES THE CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER ITSELF, WHICH IS WHAT MIRRORS THE WHOLE HEAD; WRITING THE GUARD THROUGH THE ARRAY (`g_Ids[0] != END`) AND THE WALK THROUGH A SEPARATELY-INITIALISED POINTER MAKES THE ADDRESS A VALUE cse KEEPS IN A CALLER-SAVED REGISTER AND THE WALK A COPY OF IT (`move s0,a0`) IN THE BRANCH DELAY SLOT - retail's shape, 89.25 -> 95.56% in one edit** (round 485, world_map/main/misc10 func_80088B40, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2 with --dont-expand-li; 84 insns / 336 bytes = retail's exact, and the loop body has a `jal` so the walk must be callee-saved). The compact form `pIds = g_WorldMapSpriteSetIds; if (*pIds != END) { do { WorldMapSetSpriteSetParent(0x45, *pIds++); } while (*pIds != END); }` gives `sw s0,0x10(sp) / lui s0 / addiu s0 / lh v1,0(s0)` and a nop in the loop's backedge delay slot; the two-expression form `if (g_WorldMapSpriteSetIds[0] != END) { pWalk = g_WorldMapSpriteSetIds; do { WorldMapSetSpriteSetParent(0x45, *pWalk++); } while (*pWalk != END); }` gives retail's `lui a0 / addiu a0 / lh v1,0(a0) / ... / move s0,a0` and its duplicated `sll v0,s2,0x7` in both delay slots. It is also how the already-matched neighbour WorldMapHideSpriteSetGroups in the same file is spelled, so check the unit's matched neighbours for the second expression before re-spelling a loop head. The same file's second id loop (whose walk crosses no call) then matches with the two-expression form and stays in `$a0`, minus one `move`.

- id: a-truncating-copy-in-the-rtl-names-which-register-is-the-user-variable | keywords: regalloc, caller-saved, subreg, hImode, s16, dl, dg, tie, copy
  **ON A CALLER-SAVED TIE, THE DUMP THAT NAMES THE LOSING PSEUDO IS `<in>.i.lreg`'s `(set (reg/v:HI N) (subreg:HI (reg:SI M) 0))` RECORD: THE `reg/v` IS THE SOURCE VARIABLE AND `reg:SI M` IS THE RETURN-VALUE COPY, SO IT TELLS YOU WHICH `move` IN RETAIL BELONGS TO THE VARIABLE AND WHICH IS THE COALESCED CALL RESULT - WITHOUT IT YOU CANNOT TELL WHICH OF TWO IDENTICAL-LOOKING COPIES IS THE ONE TO MOVE** (round 497, world_map/main/misc11 func_8008A72C, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 `--dont-expand-li`; 740 insns / 2960 bytes = retail's exact size, parked 99.48% with only the s16 `zone` variable's register differing: retail `addu a2,v0,zero`, body `move v1,v0`). The RTL is `(set (reg:SI 151) (reg:SI 2 v0))` then `(set (reg/v:HI 81) (subreg:HI (reg:SI 151) 0))` plus `(set (reg:SI 153) (ashift:SI (reg:SI 151) 16))`, and 151 coalesces back into `$v0` - which is why retail's stream shows BOTH `addu a2,v0,zero` (the variable) and `sll v0,v0,16` (the shift of the coalesced return), and why the register to chase is 81's, not the copy's. `.lreg` gives its ranking input (`Register 81 used 6 times across 13 insns; dies in 2 places`) and `.greg`'s `18 regs to allocate: 75 79 80 90 431 81 ...` gives the hand-out position. Note the direction: the body already holds `$v1`, EARLIER in `reg_alloc_order` than retail's `$a2`, so raising 81's priority cannot produce it - retail's `$3/$4/$5` must be in conflict with 81 where this body's are not, i.e. the knob is how many disjoint ranges ONE variable spans, not the statement order. Recipe (no `-da` file dumps on this preset's cc1 unless the output file is in the working tree): run `tools/gcc-2.7.2-psx/cc1 <cc_flags> -O2 -G8 -dl -dg build/src/<unit>.c.i -o build/src/<unit>.c.s` in the ethos container; the dumps land beside the INPUT as `<unit>.c.i.lreg` / `.i.greg`. Measured dead on the same body before parking: moving the `s16` declaration up one slot (99.48, the same 245 differing lines), splitting the proximity-index into its own `s16` (99.34, 2956 bytes / 739 insns, so the shared scratch is load-bearing), and a 1081-iteration permuter run (base=225 best=225, NONE).
## delay slot

symptoms: nop vs instruction in a delay or load slot
try: delay-slot nop jal slot
- id: c-a-pointer-local-for-the-store-base-blocks-the-load-slot-fill | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load, pointer, local, array-extern, asm-label, store, base
  **A POINTER LOCAL THAT HOLDS ONE GLOBAL'S STORE BASE IS WHAT LEAVES `nop` IN A LOAD-DELAY SLOT RETAIL FILLS: write the store (and the same global as a call argument) straight off the asm-label array extern with NO local, and reorg fills the slot with the neighbouring load's `lui`** (round 470, world_map/main/misc3 func_800776E0, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2-psx, 97.71 -> MATCH at retail's exact 628 bytes / 157 insns, `check_bin.sh world_map` OK). Retail is `lw $2,0x38($5) / lui $6,%hi(g_WorldMapCameraHeight) / lw $6 / sra` - the `lui` of the next load pair fills the delay slot - while a body holding `s16 *pRot = g_WorldMapCameraRotTable;` and storing `*pRot = ...` (needed, with the same array form, to get retail's `sh $2,0($a3)` and the `move a0,s0` jal slot) emits `nop` there and pushes the whole `lui/lw` pair four slots later. Spelling it `*g_WorldMapCameraRotTable = ... >> 12;` and `func_80096F18(pName, pTarget, g_WorldMapCameraHeight, (u16 *)g_WorldMapCameraRotTable);` closes the function; the SCALAR form (`g_WorldMapCameraRot = ...` / `(u16 *)&g_WorldMapCameraRot`) re-forms the address per use and loses the instruction again (99.01, 632 bytes). A permuter run found the same body by replacing the local with a `>> new_var` temp, so treat a `PERMUTER_ZERO` diff that removes a pointer local as "the local was the defect", and check that the shift temp is not load-bearing (`>> 12` inline measured identical here).
- id: c-a-hoisted-compare-local-fills-the-branch-slot | keywords: delay-slot, slt, compare, local, hoist, bne, beq, exact-size
  **A `slt` THAT RETAIL PUTS IN A `bne` DELAY SLOT COMES FROM A COMPARISON NAMED IN A LOCAL ABOVE THE `if`, NOT FROM THE `if` CONDITION ITSELF**: `less = x < pSlot->x;` on the statement before `if (x != pSlot->x || z != pSlot->z)`, with `less` used as the arm's test, is what makes reorg fill the `bne` slot and lands retail's exact size; writing `if (x < pSlot->x)` inside the arm instead leaves nops in both delay slots and one extra `slt` later (round 439, battle/main/misc30 func_800B905C, XenoBattleTailCdk0: 96.61% / 512 bytes -> 97.48% / retail's exact 508). Reading the field twice to force retail's two x pseudos (`less = t.xWhole < slot->x; x = t.xWhole;`) costs 8 bytes and 3 points (94.28 / 516). Note retail's second copy of the same `slt` in the FOLLOWING branch's slot is not a source duplicate: the slot-z load clobbers `$v0`, so that recompute is forced once the slt result lives in `$v0` - if yours lands in `$a2` the slot stays a nop and the size is still right.
- id: c-storing-a-call-result-through-a-temp-moves-the-reorg-slot | keywords: delay-slot, beq, reorg, call-result, temp, store, pointer-advance, source-order
  **WHEN RETAIL HAS `addiu pTail,..` BEFORE A `beqz` AND THE CALL'S RESULT STORE IN THE SLOT, THE C STORED THE RESULT THROUGH A TEMP WITH THE POINTER ADVANCE IN BETWEEN - reorg fills a delay slot with the LAST INSTRUCTION BEFORE THE BRANCH, so the slot tells you which statement came last** (round 462, battle/main/misc23 func_800A9540, XenoBattle260Div0 = gcc-2.6.0, 94.73 -> 98.98% at retail's exact 372 bytes / 93 insns). `pEntry->pBuffer2 = HeapAlloc(ArchiveDecodeAlignedSize(nameLen), 0); pTail = &pEntry->fileIndex3;` makes the RTL [call, a1=0, sw v0,0xC(s2), addiu pTail, beqz] and reorg puts the pTail addiu in the slot; `pBuffer2 = HeapAlloc(...); pTail = &pEntry->fileIndex3; pEntry->pBuffer2 = pBuffer2;` gives [call, a1=0, addiu pTail, sw v0,0xC(s2), beqz] and reorg then puts the store in the slot, which is retail's - one edit, no byte change, and it closed the ONLY residual that was not register naming. Generalisation: a call's result store normally sits immediately after the call in the RTL, so retail's store appearing AFTER a later statement's instruction means the source had an intermediate assignment; check the same shape whenever the park's note blames reorg for a swapped delay slot.
- id: c-a-store-in-a-jal-delay-slot-proves-source-order | keywords: delay-slot, jal, store, statement-order, reorg, store-before-call
  **AN INSTRUCTION IN A `jal` DELAY SLOT EXECUTES BEFORE THE CALLEE, so a store that sits there in retail proves the source wrote that store BEFORE the call - read the slot before you trust your own statement order, because gcc's reorg does not move a store forward past a call** (round 432, field/main/misc2 func_80076AC0, 73.94 -> 73.82% but 1728 -> 1764 bytes: 9 of the park's 12 missing instructions). Retail is `move a0,s0 / lui v0 / lw v0 / ori a1,0x20 / addu v0,s2,v0 / jal SpriteReallocFramesData / sw s0,4(v0)` - the address chain is formed before the call because the STORE is before the call, i.e. `pActorData->pSpriteData = pSpriteData; SpriteReallocFramesData(pSpriteData, 0x20);`. Written call-then-store (the natural reading of the listing) the store address cannot be computed before the call at all - the base is a volatile `lw` - so the whole 5-instruction `sll/addu/sll/subu/sll` index chain is re-formed after the call. In the same body, the sibling path that does NOT end in a call (`j .L80076DC4 / sw s0,4(v1)`) keeps the store AFTER its SpriteAllocFromAnimFile, so the two paths really do differ in order and one statement order cannot serve both.
- id: c-goto-past-a-post-loop-label | keywords: delay-slot, reorg, duplicate, goto, label, block-order, j, short
  **A BODY ONE INSTRUCTION SHORT BECAUSE RETAIL HAS A `j`-OVER-A-BLOCK WHOSE DELAY SLOT DUPLICATES THE NEXT BLOCK'S FIRST INSTRUCTION WANTS AN EXPLICIT `goto` TO A LABEL PLACED AFTER THE LOOP, NOT A BETTER SPELLING OF THE ARM** (round 423, world_map/main/misc10 func_80089748, 97.08 -> 99.89% at retail's exact 332 insns / 1328 bytes, XenoWorldMapDiv). Retail's tail is `[scan exit][sb flags ^= 0x80][store: sll/or/sw]`, i.e. the clear's block sits between the scan exit and the shared store, so the scan exit needs `j store` and reorg fills that slot with a COPY of the store's `sll`. Writing the arm as `else { pSprite->flags ^= 0x80; goto store; }` puts the sb inline in the arm (in the goto's delay slot) and is exactly 4 bytes / 1 insn short. The fix is a second label: `else { goto clearFlags; }` with `clearFlags: pSprite->flags ^= 0x80;` placed AFTER the scan loop and immediately before `store:`, plus an explicit `goto store;` after the scan's if-block so the scan-exit stops falling into the clear (without that goto the body compiles to the right size but CLEARS THE FLAGS ON THE SCAN-EXHAUSTED PATH - wrong code that scores 97.55%). Two companion findings from the same function: `low = p.field; high = low >> 16; low = (s16)low;` (ONE variable for the packed pair) is what puts retail's `lw s5` + `sra s8,s5,16` shape together and fixed the leftover `$s5`/`$s6` mirror; and the residual 0.11% left afterwards is only the scratchpad address form (`%lo(D_1F8000xx)` vs a folded +0xF0 immediate over `s3 = 0x1F800000`), which links identically - do not "fix" it with an extern, misc14 measured that a named D_1F8000xx makes cc1 form a fresh lui+addiu.
- id: c-a-bare-j-tail-call-thunk | keywords: delay-slot, tail, sibcall, j, jal, thunk, frame, noreturn
  **A RETAIL 8-BYTE `j Callee` + `nop` IS A SIBLING CALL, AND NO COMPILER IN tools/ EMITS ONE ON MIPS - so a C wrapper around a variadic callee can never be matched here** (round 406, slus_006.64/system/archive_b func_800379C8, parked 0%, 8 bytes retail). Retail is opcode-2 `j FontPrintf` with a0 untouched: a variadic passthrough that forwards the caller's arguments, which is exactly why the original could not have been an ordinary `f(char* p) { FontPrintf(p); }`. Probed with cc1_probe.sh under the unit's own flags: the call gives `subu sp / sw ra / jal / lw ra / addu sp / j ra` (32 bytes), unchanged by `-foptimize-sibling-calls` and unchanged when the callee is declared `__attribute__((noreturn))` (2.7.2 accepts the attribute and still keeps the frame). The honest variadic signature is worse (48 bytes: the a1-a3 save area). gcc 2.6.0 and 2.7.2-cdk are 0% too, 2.8.1 also frames + jals, and mips.md gets sibcall patterns only in 3.x. So a lone `j`-first glabel is a hand-written thunk: report SIBLING_CALL and do not spend runs on it. (splat prints such a word byte-swapped - 0x0800DC03 shows as `03DC0008` - so verify against disc/ before doubting the disassembly.)
- id: c-a-loop-label-lands-after | keywords: delay-slot, nop, label, mflo, maspsx, branch, displacement, bnez
  **A BACK EDGE WHOSE DISPLACEMENT IS ONE INSTRUCTION SHORT IS maspsx'S HAZARD-NOP PLACEMENT, NOT A SOURCE SHAPE: `_handle_mflo_mfhi` emits the follower and its nop as one unit and only then replays the loop label, so the label lands AFTER the nop where retail's assembler put it BEFORE** (round 404, slus_006.64/system/archive_b func_80037878, parked 99.94% at retail's exact 316 bytes / 79 insns: the whole stream is identical and only `bnez v0,+0x74` vs `+0x78` differs, 2 differing lines). cc1's line order is `mult / mflo / addu / $L8: / mult`; in maspsx's next_next-is-mult branch (tools/maspsx/maspsx/__init__.py) the generic `elif not inst.startswith("#")` path appends the follower, then `res.extend([expand_move(inst), "nop"])` puts the nop after it, and the label line is replayed last - so the three reachable label positions are after the nop (99.94), at the addu (label line moved before the follower, 4 bytes the other way) and before the nops (the next-is-mult branch, which emits TWO nops, +8 bytes). maspsx does use label-then-nop in its OTHER handler (`_handle_nop_before_next_instruction`), so this is one convention apart and only a maspsx edit closes it. Preset screened the same round: -O3 99.94, -G0 99.94, cdk 95.59, 2.6.0 93.54. Diagnose by comparing the branch TARGET against the loop-head nop before re-shaping the loop: several loop spellings (for(;;)+break, for(j=i;...), an empty do/while at the head) all measure the same number with this same single difference.
- id: c-a-call-argument-constant-beats | keywords: delay-slot, li, constant, reorg, jal, priority, scheduling
  **A CALL-ARGUMENT CONSTANT OUTRANKS A STORE-ONLY CONSTANT FOR A BRANCH DELAY SLOT, and no source order reaches it** (round 391, slus_006.64/system/archive func_8002B5D0, stuck at 97.47% / 736 bytes). Retail's `beq` after `CdPosToInt` carries `li $v0,1` (the value stored immediately after the target) where our compile carries `li $a1,0x200` (the following `jal`'s size argument). reorg fills the slot eagerly from the target block when that block is the branch's only successor, taking its FIRST scheduled insn - and sched2's rank_for_schedule compares INSN_PRIORITY first, so the constant that feeds the `jal` (on the block's critical path) is scheduled ahead of the constant that only feeds a `sh`. Statement order, a volatile state store (96.67), a live-in u16 id local (97.47) and a pointer local for the second call argument (97.47) all left the slot unchanged. Symptom to look for: your delay slot holds the arg constant of the FIRST call in the target arm while retail's holds a constant used later in that arm.
  Round 403 re-measured it on func_8002B2F0 (the instruction-identical sibling): still 97.47 / 736 bytes with the exact instruction multiset. New data points on the same body: the two-statement queue index (`entryIndex = g_ArchiveStreamQueueIndex; g_ArchiveStreamQueueIndex = entryIndex + 1;`) scores 97.93 but is 732 bytes / 183 insns - local_alloc loads straight into the callee-saved register and the `move` disappears, so it can never link; a `pCurrent = NULL` initialiser breaks the duplicated tail's cross-jump (92.50 / 740 / 185). permute.sh cannot run the body at all: its parser reports 'conversion to non-scalar type requested' on the write-pointer read line for all three spellings tried (inline `s8* volatile*` cast, `s8* volatile*` local, `volatile u32*` local), so this park is hand-only.
  Round 431 on the same body: the DOUBLE NEGATION on the destination sum (`entryIndex * CD_SECTOR_SIZE - (-(mem_addr)*(s8* volatile*)&writePointer)`, the c-double-negation mechanism) keeps the score at 97.47 / 736 but lands the `sll` in `$a0` as retail does and removes the maspsx load-delay `nop`, so the residual becomes a PURE REORDER - identical multiset, identical registers, and the only moved positions are this section's `li` pair and the `sll`'s slot. That is the closest shape measured on this pair and is what both parks now carry. Also re-measured on it: both id reads plain CSE to one `lhu` (96.40 / 732 / 183, so the volatile cast is load-bearing); permuting the four found-block statements in source (id read hoisted into a `u16` local, state store after it) compiles BYTE-IDENTICALLY, which is the proof that these two rows are scheduler priorities and not statement order; gcc-2.7.2-cdk 95.67.
  Round 473 measured the sibling direction: a LOOP INIT that retail keeps in a BRANCH delay slot is not reachable by moving the source statement either - cc1 always emits the counter's `move $16,$0` immediately after the preceding call and reorg then takes it for that call's delay slot, where retail keeps the store of the last statement before the call (`sb v0,0xA8(v1)`), and the `beqz` above it keeps a SECOND copy of the switch bound (`sltu $2,$19,9`, required because reorg redirected that branch past the sltu) where retail's branch targets the sltiu itself (battle/main/misc13 func_800861D0, Default = gcc-2.7.2, parked 98.56% / 2496 bytes / 624 insns against retail's 2488 / 622). Proof that position is not the lever: writing `o = 0;` as the FIRST statement of the if body, and separately between the two neighbouring global stores (retail's exact slot), each compiles BYTE-IDENTICALLY - cc1's own `.s` still reads `jal BattleUpdateFrame / move $16,$0`. So when a park's only residual is a `move <callee-saved>,zero` loop init in the wrong slot plus the bound's duplicate, the lever is a different loop SHAPE (do-while moves the test to the bottom) and not the init's statement position.
- id: c-twin-source-shape-beats-a-park | keywords: delay-slot, twin, park, load-slot, addiu, pointer, increment
  **A PARKED BODY THAT DIFFERS FROM RETAIL ONLY IN "PLACEMENT" IS A DIFFERENT SOURCE SHAPE, AND A MATCHING TWIN IN THE SAME UNIT HANDS YOU THE SHAPE - port it verbatim before re-deriving it** (round 417, menu/main/misc7_r2 func_801D6338, 309 insns under XenoMenu260: the park stood at 95.53% at retail's exact 1236 bytes with two delay-slot residuals, and a wholesale port of the matching twin func_801D680C's body reached 100.00 / 1236 bytes on the FIRST diff run - the two residuals disappeared without being separately diagnosed, so this lever is the method, not a bisected attribution).
