The three shape differences the park had, all of them exactly the kind that produces a slot difference: (1) the digit scan was `for (i = 0; i < count; ) { u8 digit = digits[digitOffset + i++]; if (digit != NONE) ... }` where the twin has `for (i = 0; i < count; i++) { if (digits[digitOffset + i] != NONE) ... }` and uses the same subexpression as the call's index - the post-increment in the index makes gcc put a `nop` in the `lw $a2,%lo(g_Menu)` load-delay slot where retail fills it with `addu v0,digitOffset,i`; (2) the prim-address argument was an integer sum with the base added FIRST (`count * (2*sizeof(POLY_FT4)) + 0x1630 + (u32)base`), which emits `addiu t0,t0,0x1630` on the base and a plain `addu a2,a2,t1`, where the twin's pointer form `(POLY_FT4*)((u8*)base + (count * (2*sizeof(POLY_FT4)) + 0x1630))` keeps 0x1630 in the scaled-count chain and puts the base add in the `jal` delay slot - retail's shape, with the base/count temps also swapping registers (t1/t0) as a consequence; (3) the x cursor was `x - characterId * 24` with `x += MENU_DIGIT_SPACING` at the loop end, where the twin keeps `x + i * MENU_DIGIT_SPACING - characterId * 24` and gcc strength-reduces it into the back-edge `addiu s1,s1,8`. So when a park's note reads "same instruction multiset, only the placement differs", run twin_for.py and diff the twin's body against the park before trying spellings by hand.
- id: c-there-source-ordering-lever | keywords: delay-slot, nop, li, delay, goto, jr, reorg
  **There is no source ordering lever for delay-slot fill** (round 311, ten micro probes): reorg always steals the instruction immediately preceding `jr` in RTL, so a ternary, a comma expression, a goto, an if/else and a scoped block all measure identical. What moves is the RTL position of a `li v0,K` return against trailing constant-zero stores, and with TWO constant-zero stores before `return 1` the `li` is still the one stolen. If a park's only residual is which instruction fills a slot, park it with that number and say so instead of spending the batch.
- id: c-load-load-sub-against | keywords: delay-slot, nop, delay
  **`load/load/sub` against retail's `load/nop/sub` is a DECLARATION-ORDER question, not a scheduling one.** round 370, battling/misc5 func_8007B270 (85.17 -> 100.00): dbr_schedule fills a load-delay slot from a LATER independent insn, so the order in which the channel locals are assigned decides which load gets stolen - the natural ascending `r = p0[0] - 0x80; g = p0[1] - 0x80; b = p0[2] - 0x80;` produced retail's shape where reordering the STORES never moved the tie.
- id: c-every-missing-insn-is-a-hazard-nop | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load, byte-count, regalloc, reuse, hazard, maspsx
  **WHEN A PARK'S BYTE DEFICIT EQUALS ITS COUNT OF MISSING INSNs AND EVERY ONE IS A maspsx LOAD-DELAY `nop`, THE DEFICIT IS AN ALLOCATOR CONSEQUENCE, NOT A MISSING STATEMENT: each retail nop exists only because retail's loaded value lands in the register the immediately following instruction writes, so reorg cannot steal a later insn into the gap - and no spelling adds the instruction back** (round 487, world_map/main/misc12 func_800925A0, XenoWorldMap, re-parked 93.72% / 1592 bytes / 398 insns against retail 1604 / 401). Both arms have `lw a0,112(a1)` (ordering-table node) immediately followed by `lw v0,0(a0)`, and the tail has `lhu v0,34(s0)` followed by `addiu v0,v0,1`; our body fills the arm gap with the tpage address (its own register `$t0`, so nothing conflicts) and the tail gap with `move v0,s1` (our load took `$v1`). Diagnose it in one pass: diff the two instruction lists and check that the count difference is exactly the `nop`s, then read which register retail REUSES (here `$a0` for the tpage address and `$v0` for the return copy) - that reuse is the same hand-out tie as the mask registers, so report the pair and park instead of writing statement variants. Measured byte-identical on the same body: moving the `pTpage = g_WorldMapFadeTpageArr;` statement above `pPrim = ...`, swapping the pTpage/pPrim declaration order, and `x = x + 1` for `x++` on the timer.
- id: c-original-keeps-li-a0 | keywords: delay-slot, nop, li, delay, jal, move, reorg
  The original keeps `li a0,N` in a `jal`'s delay slot while yours hoists it: gcc has no scheduler here, so the `li` is stolen into the slot by reorg only when it is the last insn before the call and no register conflict blocks it. Move other argument setup earlier, or make the constant argument the last one evaluated.
  THE MIRROR CASE IS A LOCAL_ALLOC LOCK-IN, NOT A STATEMENT ORDER: when retail HOISTS `li a0,N` to the head of a long block that also contains a small-struct copy, the constant's liveness is what bars `$a0` from the copy and pushes the copy's loads into `$a2`/`$a3` - and in our build the constant sinks to the `jal` slot, `$a0` goes to a copy load, and sched2 can then never move the constant above that load (WAW). Symptom: retail's block head reads `li a0,N / addiu a1,base,K` while yours has only the `addiu a1`, the copy's loads land in `$a0`, and the function is ONE instruction short (retail's load-delay `nop` disappears because the pData-style pointer bump fills it). Measured on field/main/misc3 func_8006FDEC (round 479, 98.45% / 668 bytes against retail's 672, Default preset): cc1's own `.s` already splits the same way at -O2 - blocks 1 and 2 of the same three-block unroll emit their `li $4` at the head and block 3 does not, while block 3's `addu $5,$17,352` IS hoisted, so the hoister works on the second argument's computation and not on the constant. Dead on that body, all byte-identical at 668 / 167 insns: a named `s32 lightIndex = 2;` passed to the call (copy-propagated before sched1 ever sees a pseudo), and one do-while barrier wrapping the copies AND the call. permute.sh: PERMUTER_NONE base=260 best=260 over 1624 iterations in 3 minutes, so it cannot reach a scheduling/allocation tie like this - do not spend a second run on it.
- id: c-a-call-argument-constant-folds-early-when-the-compare-load-sinks | keywords: delay-slot, li, constant, jal, nop, load, compare
  **A CALL WHOSE RESULT IS COMPARED AGAINST A LONE NARROW LOAD FIRES ITS ARGUMENT CONSTANT ~9 INSTRUCTIONS EARLY AND NO SPELLING MOVES IT, so retail's `jal; ori a0,N` slot is unreachable on that shape while the identical shape one function away matches** (round 443, field/main/misc11 func_80095CC4, parked 96.19% / 172 bytes / 43 insns against retail's 168 / 42 - the whole body, the registers and the branch layout are exact, the only extra insn is the `nop` that takes the slot the argument constant should have filled). `FieldScriptVMGetArgument(2)`'s `li $4,2` comes out right after the previous call in cc1's OWN output (`build/src/<unit>.c.s`, so this is not the assembler), before the array-index sll chain, and reorg then fills the call's slot with a nop. Measured, all 172 bytes: plain `arg = F(2); if (arg == p->field)` 96.19; an `int wm = p->field;` local hoisted above the call compiles BYTE-IDENTICALLY (copy-propagated) so the load's statement order is not the lever, 96.19; negated test with the arms swapped byte-identical, 96.19; operands swapped (`p->field == arg`) puts the load BEFORE the call and drops to 94.76; gcc-2.7.2-cdk `-O2 -G8` 96.19. The MATCHED neighbour FieldScriptCheckActorWalkmeshMaterial has retail's exact `jal; ori a0,2` slot, and the one difference is that its compared value is an `lbu` reached through the triangle table (so it is emitted before the call) where this one is a lone `lh 0x10(s0)`. Park this class rather than permuting below 99%. Round 470 added three negatives on the same body: the call written inline in the compare (no `arg` local) is 96.19 again, gcc-2.6.0 `-O2 -G8` is 96.19 (and the unit's matched neighbour func_800925A0 drops to 93.53 under it, so this is not a preset split), and the two-operand order with the load first is 94.76.
- id: c-only-difference-hoisted-li | keywords: delay-slot, nop, delay, jal, li
  Only difference is a hoisted `li a0,N` where the original keeps it in the jal delay slot: put the argument in an `int` local before the call, or pass a variable instead of a literal.
- id: c-stolen-delay-slot-retail | keywords: delay-slot, nop, addiu, andi, delay, reorg, sll
  A stolen delay slot (retail has a `nop` where yours has an `andi`/`sll`/`addiu`): the cheapest lever found is the function's RETURN TYPE - `void` lets gcc 2.7.2/2.6.0 reorg steal the instruction into the slot, a non-void type (`int`, `char`, even unused) keeps retail's `nop` (rounds 64-65 closed three functions this way, one of them 99.36% -> 100.00% with no other change). Try that before any statement reordering, and say in a comment why the unused return type is there.
  MEASURED NEGATIVE, round 472, battle/main/misc21 func_800A1B50 (97.90% / 420 bytes / 105 insns, XenoBattle260Div = gcc-2.6.0): the body is `void` because an `s32` return costs a `move v0,zero` after the latch (96.95 / 424 / 106) and retail has no such move - yet reorg still emits `nop` where retail duplicates a dead `andi v0,t3,0xffff` into the backward branch's slot, so this lever's direction does not fire when the only candidate before the branch is the `andi` that feeds that branch's own `slt`. Do not re-brief the return type on a body whose return value is never read.
- id: c-make-gcc-put-return | keywords: delay-slot, nop, jr, addu, delay, move
  To make gcc put a return-value copy in the jr $31 delay slot (retail's jr $31 / addu $2,$5,$0 instead of move $2,$5 hoisted to the top), put "$2" in the asm block's clobber list; without it the copy floats above the block (+4 bytes, 98.x%). maspsx also REJECTS hex immediates inside an inline-asm body (invalid literal for int() with base 10: '0x6') - write them decimal, as the matched ScaleMatrix/SetMulMatrix blocks do.
- id: c-two-stores-same-value | keywords: delay-slot, nop, delay, lw, sw
  Two stores of the same value class: SOURCE ORDER decides which one gets the load-delay slot. Retail `lw v0,112(s1); sw v1,4(s2)` (constant store in the delay slot) needs the non-constant store written FIRST (round 47, world_map/misc8 func_80082F64: 98.71 -> 100%).
- id: c-wrong-parameter-type-callee | keywords: delay-slot, nop, addiu, andi, delay, jal, reorg, s32
  A WRONG PARAMETER TYPE ON THE CALLEE COSTS A DELAY SLOT: declaring a callee's first parameter s32 instead of u_char removes an andi a0,a0,0xff at every call site, which is what lets reorg put the following addiu in the jal slot (menu/misc12's func_801E8B4C). Before blaming your caller, check the callee's prototype against its own .s.
- id: c-dead-constant-delay-slot | keywords: delay-slot, nop, delay, cse, reorg, missing, arm, eager
  **FALSIFIED IN ROUND 404 - READ THIS BEFORE BELIEVING THAT A CONSTANT IN A DELAY SLOT IS "DEAD".** The 99.87% park of field/dialogue/text_box func_8009C5A8 (round 304, "a dead ori $s0,zero,0x94 that this build declines to place") was a MISSING LIVE ASSIGNMENT, not a reorg fill: the below-actor arm's outer `else { width = 0x48; height = 4; x = 0xA0; }` never set `y`, so a `y = 0x94;` spelled first in that block closes the function at 100.00% (1872 bytes, 468 insns) - retail's ori sits in the bne delay slot because reorg's EAGER fill moves the FIRST instruction of a branch target that the branch is the only reference to. The tell that round 304 missed: the value is READ on the taken path (the else arm falls through to the layout clamps, which consume `y`), so it was never dead; and the sibling arm's else had its own `y = 0x10;` in the same position, which is the shape to compare against. When a one-instruction delay-slot residual is a constant store/li, first check whether every arm of the corresponding if/else sets that variable in your C, and whether the arms are symmetric; only call it dead after proving no path reads it.
- id: c-eager-fill-steals-the-targets-arg0-copy | keywords: delay-slot, nop, missing, move, argument, eager, reorg, if-else
  **WHEN BOTH ARMS OF AN `if`/`else` CALL THE SAME FUNCTION, gcc EXPANDS `arg0 = pSpriteData` BEFORE THE OTHER ARM'S LOAD, SO THE ELSE BLOCK'S RTL STARTS WITH THE COPY AND reorg's EAGER FILL HOISTS IT INTO THE `bnez` AT THE TOP - retail's block starts with the `lw`, which eager fill cannot take, so retail keeps the `nop` and re-forms the copy at the arm; the function then compiles ONE INSTRUCTION SHORT and can never link** (round 443, `slus_006.64/system/temp1` func_80022B2C, parked 96.25% / 376 bytes against retail's 380 / 96 insns, XenoGraphics). Retail's else arm is `lw a1,16(s0)` / `addu a0,s0` / `jal` / `sra a1,a1,4`; every body emits `addu a0,s0` first, reorg moves it to the `bnez` delay slot, and the arm loses the copy. Measured dead for reaching the load-first order: hoisting `speed = pSpriteData->step.y;` as the else body's first statement (`... SpriteScaleValue(pSpriteData, speed >> 4)`) compiles BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the inline form - gcc folds the local back into the argument expansion - and so does declaring the else's load in its own function-scope local. The second residual on the same body is reorg's other direction: a `speed = -step.y * flags / 256; step.y = speed;` whose quotient retail keeps in the mflo register (`sra v1,v1,8`) gets a fresh register here (`sra a1,v1,8`) and reorg then moves the following `sw` into the `bgez` delay slot where retail has a `nop` (a separate `bounce` local instead of reusing `speed` scores 95.99 with the value in `$v0` and gravity in `$a0`, retail: bounce `$v1`, gravity `$v0`). Preset is settled by an earlier 2.6.0/2.7.2/-O1..-O3/-G4..-G8 sweep; park this class with the two mechanisms named rather than re-briefing spellings.
- id: c-per-arm-identical-stores-let-cross-jump-keep-the-nop | keywords: delay-slot, nop, eager, reorg, if-else, cross-jump, shared, store, local, arm, phi
  **A `bnez` WHOSE DELAY SLOT RETAIL LEAVES AS `nop` BUT YOURS FILLS WITH THE ELSE ARM'S FIRST `li` IS NOT A REORG WALL: WRITE THE SHARED STORE INTO EACH ARM (identical statements, no local) AND gcc's CROSS_JUMP MERGES THE TWO TWIN TAILS INTO RETAIL'S ONE STORE, WHICH ALSO REMOVES THE PHI THAT MADE THE DELAY-SLOT STEAL POSSIBLE - 89.15 -> 100.00 in one edit** (round 486, battling/main/misc1 func_8007191C, Default = gcc-2.7.2-psx, retail's exact 212 bytes / 53 insns). Retail is `sltiu v0,s0,1 / sb` ... `bnez s0,else / nop` / `jal BattlePlaySoundEffectById / ori a0,0x37` / `ori v0,2` / `sh v0,%lo(D_80098698)` / `j .L8007196C / ori v0,0xB4` and the else arm `ori v0,4 / sh / ori v0,0x9A`, both falling into ONE `lui at / sh v0,%lo(D_80098692)` - i.e. retail's shared store IS a cross-jumped tail, never a join phi. The parked spelling (`s32 value;` assigned 0xB4/0x9A in the arms, `D_80098692 = value;` after the if) reads 89.15% at 208 bytes: reorg's eager fill takes the else arm's `ori v0,4` into the `bnez` slot (retail has a `nop`), the value pseudo then gets `$v1` instead of `$v0`, and the shared store is scheduled after the following `sll/lui/addu/lw` chain - one cause, three rows. Measured dead on it: `s32` on the (otherwise void) return, the lever above, is byte-identical here. The tell is the `j` out of one arm INTO the shared store block: cross-jump produced it, so write the store in both arms and let cc1 merge. Applies to any if/else whose arms end in the same store and whose shared store block retail reaches with a `j` from the non-fall-through arm.

- id: c-a-displaced-pointer-load-pair | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load, hoist, deferred, base, schedule-insns, pair
  **TWO ADJACENT POINTER LOADS IN RETAIL WHERE YOUR BUILD DEFERS ONE OF THEM IS OUTSIDE BOTH SCHEDULING FLAGS, SO PROBE cc1 ONCE (5 s) BEFORE SPENDING DIFF RUNS ON OPERAND ORDERS** (round 408, field/main/misc12 func_80099AC0, parked 97.96% at 1076 bytes against retail's 1080 - one load-delay `nop` short). Retail's case-2 arm is `subu; sll v1,v1,2; lui a0,%hi(Base); lw a0; lui a1,%hi(Cur); lw a1; addu v1,v1,a0; lw s0,0x4C(v1); nop; lhu v0,0x1E(s0); lhu a0,0x1E(a1)`: the base pointer load is deferred BELOW the index's last `sll` and the second pointer load sits adjacent to it, so gas has nothing to pad after `lw s0`. Every body measured loads the base BEFORE that `sll` and the second pointer AFTER `lw s0`, which fills the slot. The probe that closes the question without editing the unit: run the unit's own cc1 on the already-built `build/src/<unit>.c.i` with the unit's `cc_flags` plus `-fno-schedule-insns -fno-schedule-insns2` inside the build container - the non-scheduled stream is byte-for-byte the same order, so it is not sched1 or sched2, and the preset screen agrees (2.6.0 95.27, cdk 96.74 with the same deferred load, -O3 fails to compile). Report it parked with the cc1 probe in the note instead of permuting: three earlier permuter runs found nothing and the target-first operand order only re-ranks objdiff's fuzzy score (97.72) while the byte count stays 4 short.
    - round 429 on the same function, two spellings the 408 note did not cover: (1) target-first written as `(FIELD_ACTORS + FieldScriptVMGetActorIndex(1))->pActorData` with `pTargetActor->solidRange + g_FieldScriptVMCurActor->solidRange` DOES reach retail's `lhu` pair order and `addu a0,v0,a0` (97.72, still 1076 bytes, the pointer loads stay displaced), so target-first is the right operand order and the byte loss is the pointer placement alone; (2) reading the second pointer through a `volatile` cast (`(*(ActorData* volatile*)&g_FieldScriptVMCurActor)->solidRange`) does NOT stop cc1 sinking that load into the `lw s0` load-delay slot, so the placement is not source-order-reachable even with a volatile barrier - do not retry volatile here.
    - round 452 (slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu MoveImage, PSY-Q preset, parked 95.69% / 196 bytes / 49 insns = retail's exactly): the SAME probe answers the opposite way here, so run it before parking a one-slot-moved load. Retail keeps the call's arg0 load (`lw a0,0x18(v1)`) AFTER the last packet store; cc1 hoists it four slots to just below `sw a0,0(a1)`. Compiling the body's own `.i` with the unit cc1 plus `-fno-schedule-insns -fno-schedule-insns2` moves BOTH vtable loads to the end in RTL order (`lw 8(v1)` then `lw 24(v1)`, where retail has 24 then 8) and reorders the prologue saves, so here the hoist IS sched1's and no flag or preset reproduces retail - the two states bracket retail and neither is reachable. Also measured: reversing the source store order (`D_80056984` before `*pPacket`) keeps the same hoist and drops to 87.33, so the store order in the diff is sched-chosen and reordering statements only loses the store block retail already matches.
- id: c-call-arg-setup-swapped | keywords: delay-slot, jal, addiu, move, argument, statement, hoist
  **A TWO-INSTRUCTION ARGUMENT-SETUP SWAP BEFORE A `jal` CLOSES WHEN THE COMPUTED ARGUMENT BECOMES A STATEMENT ABOVE ITS `if`** (round 389, battle/misc7 func_8007C040, 97.53 -> 99.78 at retail's exact 356 bytes). Retail had `beqz s2,L` / `addiu a1,s2,-1` in the slot / `move a0,zero` / `jal` / `andi a1,a1,0xff`; the body `BattleSlotBitMask(buf[GameRandomByteRange(0, count - 1)])` inside `if (count != 0)` gave `move a0,zero` in the branch slot and the addiu after it, because gcc expands call arguments left to right. Moving the bound out - `lastIndex = count - 1;` as a statement BEFORE the `if`, then `GameRandomByteRange(0, lastIndex)` - puts the addiu first and matches. A `s32 last = count - 1;` DECLARATION inside the if (or inside a nested block) does not; the permuter found it in 1274 iterations after two hand spellings measured identical.
- id: c-s32-return-type-otherwise | keywords: delay-slot, nop, s32, addiu, callee-saved, delay, li, reorg
  AN s32 RETURN TYPE ON AN OTHERWISE VOID FUNCTION can be the last instruction (round 305): with void, reorg steals the branch target's addiu into the final beqz slot where retail has a nop; declaring the function s32 (and not using the value) puts the nop back. Also from the same body: a && with the else arm as the fall-through is what lets gcc delay-slot-fill a li and drop a j where the || spelling costs an extra jump; and a type = 0; STATEMENT after a store beats a declaration initialiser, which keeps the variable live across the first call and costs a callee-saved register.
- id: c-select-copy-in-branch | keywords: delay-slot, select, polarity, beqz, reorg, return, permuter
  **RETAIL'S SELECT WITH THE VALUE COPY IN THE BRANCH'S OWN DELAY SLOT NEEDS THE `-1` ARM AS THE FALL-THROUGH, AND WHAT PINS IT IS A DEAD `do { } while` LOOP** (round 392, slus_006.64/psyq/libsn PCcreate and _SN_read, both 100.00 at retail's exact 32 and 24 bytes, after both had been parked at 84-99% for rounds). Retail is `beqz v0,L; addu v0,v1,zero; addiu v0,zero,-1; L: jr ra`: branch on the status the break syscall left in $v0, the value copy speculated into that branch's delay slot, the -1 arm in the fall-through. Two returns alone (`if (status == 0) return value; return -1;`) give the MIRROR image - `bnez v0,L; li v0,-1` in the slot, `move v0,v1` in the fall-through, same six words, 56.67%. What flips it is comparing the status against a LOCAL holding 0 and leaving a dead loop in the -1 arm: `noError = 0; if (status != noError) { return -1; do { } while (noError); } else return value;`. The loop is load-bearing (delete it and the mirror comes back) and a literal `if (status != 0)` does not substitute for the local. permute.sh found it in 21 iterations from the mirror body after ~30 hand shapes (if/else both ways, ternary, goto join, hard-bound registers, 2.6.0/cdk/-O2) had failed; every break-syscall wrapper in that unit is the same six words.
- id: c-two-loads-hoist-the | keywords: delay-slot, li, constant, hoist, load, lbu, block
  **A BLOCK WITH TWO LOADS GETS ITS FIRST CONSTANT ASSIGNMENT HOISTED TO THE BLOCK TOP AND ITS SECOND DROPPED INTO THE FIRST LOAD'S DELAY SLOT, whatever the statement order** (round 393, menu/main/misc4_260 func_801CDC6C, parked 99.17 at retail's exact 1120 bytes / 280 insns). Retail's `if`/`else` prologue is `andi/sll chain, lbu gearId, li count, sll chain, lw hp, li base` - each constant in the delay slot of the load above it and NOTHING at the block top - and six source orders all gave the same 1-at-top/1-after-the-lbu shape: (value,base,count) 99.17, (value,count,base) 99.15, `u8 gearId` declaration first 99.15, and a `do { ... } while (0)` around the arm 98.75 (it also reshuffles s4/s6/s7/s5). A `cc1_probe.sh` replica (a byte load feeding a word load, plus two constant assignments) isolates the trigger: with ONE load in the block both `li`s stay after it in source order, with the second load present the first `li` moves to the block top. So when a park's only residual is which side of a load two `li`s sit on, probe the block with one load removed before spending more orders on it - the placement is reorg's, not the C's. permute.sh 3 minutes: base=90 best=90.
  Round 407 named the pass: it is the PRE-RELOAD scheduler, not reorg. Compiling the same `.i` with the unit's own cc1 and `-fno-schedule-insns2` keeps the first `li` at the block top, `-fno-schedule-insns` moves it to just before the byte load, and with BOTH off the block ends `lw, li base, li count` (retail's stream order) and reorg fills the two load-delay slots. So a park of this shape is a cc1 SCHEDULING artifact that no statement order reaches - it is not worth a second permutation round, and it is not evidence that the preset is wrong (the same function's other residual, a `sw s5/move s5,a3` + `sw s8/move s8,a1` parameter-copy pair that retail emits in NON-parm order, behaves the same way under all four flag sets). Round 447 saw the same class in battle/main/misc15 func_8008BED8 (parked 99.42% / 1156 against retail 1160): retail's `sw s4,88(sp); li s4,1` pair sits right after `li s6,2` only when the `pagePending = 1;` statement is in the init block, and EVERY position after the two `BattleInitSlotGraphics` calls (between them, after both, after the next call) collapses to one body that puts the pair five slots late, after `li a3,0x118` - so when one post-call position has been measured, the others are the same body and statement order is exhausted. ROUND 460 re-confirmed from a fresh unpark on that function: init-block body 99.42% / 1156 bytes (one `li s0,1` short), post-call body 98.52% / 1160 bytes = retail's exact size with that pair displaced 5 slots past `li a3,0x118` and every other line identical - the size-exact end can never be improved by moving the assignment, so park the higher-scoring one and record both.
- id: c-an-empty-do-while-does-not-pin-a-li-below-a-load | keywords: delay-slot, li, constant, hoist, load, do-while, barrier
  **THE ROUND-433 EMPTY `do { } while (0)` BARRIER PINS A `li` BELOW A STORE (and orders two memory refs against each other, see `c-a-per-site-do-while-restores-the-load-delay`) BUT NOT A `li` AGAINST A LOAD: a block whose only residual is a constant that sched1 hoists to the block top is byte-identical with the barrier inserted** (round 436, menu/main/misc4_260 func_801CDC6C, re-parked 99.29% at retail's exact 1120 bytes / 280 insns, XenoMenu260). Two spellings measured on that body: the empty `do { } while (0)` between the value load and the base assignment changes nothing, and writing the else arm as its own `gearId` statement, then `glyphCount`, then `value`, then `glyphBase` - retail's exact STREAM order, the order that reproduces retail instruction for instruction once sched1 is off - measures 99.26 with FOUR differing lines, because sched1 hoists the first `li` (count) to the block top and drops the second (base) into the `lbu` delay slot. So `c-two-loads-hoist-the`'s "whatever the statement order" holds even when the order is provably retail's, and `-O1` (the only preset-visible way to turn sched1 off) is 69.74 on the same body: park, do not re-permute.
- id: c-moved-constant-merges-then-sinks | keywords: delay-slot, nop, li, constant, cse, sink, load
  **MOVING A CONSTANT ASSIGNMENT UP OUT OF A LOAD-DELAY SINK MERGES IT WITH THE SAME CONSTANT'S STORE AND COSTS AN INSTRUCTION** (round 396, menu/main/misc9 func_801E05D0, parked 98.88% / 2468 bytes against retail 2472 - 4 bytes short). Retail's inner-switch tail has `lui v0,g_Menu / lw v0,0(v0) / nop / lw v0,0x33C(v0)` plus a separate `li s0,1` for `closeList` ten insns earlier, right after the `MenuCopyEquipmentToPanel` call; the natural body (`shouldRender[0] = 1;` then `closeList = 1;`) keeps BOTH `li 1`s but reorg drops closeList's into that load slot, so nothing is left for the assembler to pad and the function is one insn short. Every order that puts `closeList = 1;` before the store makes cse merge the two QI constants (615 insns / 2464 bytes / 98.39 - the store becomes `sb s0,0x140`), and before the call itself breaks the arm (620 insns / 93.26); this is the `c-two-loads-hoist-the` class seen from the other side, so park it rather than permute. Round 432 re-measured the function (the note's 98.88 / 2468 / 617 is current under gcc-2.6.0) and added one spelling: `closeList = 1;` FIRST, then the cursor-prim call, then the `shouldRender` store - moving the store below the call does stop the merge (both `li 1`s survive) but cc1 then sinks the store below the call (`jal` / `lw g_Menu` / `#nop` / `lw 0x33C` / `li s0` / `sb s0,0x140`), so the arm loses retail's shape and the body is still 617 / 2468 / 98.00. The lead for a next attempt is that the SAME function's BACK arm already reproduces retail exactly - cc1 hoists its `li s0,1` above the cursor-prim argument setup and keeps both `li 1`s - so the hoist is reachable in this unit and only the CONFIRM arm's cse merge stands in the way.

- id: c-call-result-copy-needs | keywords: delay-slot, jal, move, copy, callee-saved, temp, statement
  **A CALL RESULT'S COPY INTO A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER LANDS IN THE NEXT CALL'S `jal` DELAY SLOT ONLY WHEN THE `+ K` THAT CONSUMES IT IS A SEPARATE ASSIGNMENT THROUGH A SECOND LOCAL** (round 396, field/main/misc func_8008A2E8, 98.33 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 504 bytes / 126 insns). Retail is `jal FieldScriptArgument1 / li a0,5` then `li a0,4 / move a1,zero / jal ArchiveSetIndex / move s0,v0 / addiu s0,s0,2043`: reorg fills the slot from the insn immediately preceding the jump in RTL, which is the result copy only if the copy is the LAST thing before the argument setup. Three probe spellings of `x = f(); g(); ...` separate it: `x += 0x7FB;` after the call puts the copy right after `f` and `move a1,zero` in the slot (98.33, our shape); `x = f() + 0x7FB;` folds to one `addu s0,v0,2043` (4 bytes short); `t = f(); g(); x = t + 0x7FB;` with a SECOND local keeps the separate `move s0,v0` in the slot plus the separate `addiu` and matches. The second local must be its own variable: reusing one that another arm of the same `if` writes widens its live range, moves the copy out of the slot AND flips that other arm's register (97.38 / 508 bytes).

- id: c-displaced-li-inside | keywords: li, constant, hoist, store, group, sched2, priority, preset, sweep
  **A SINGLE `li` AT THE WRONG DISTANCE INSIDE A STRAIGHT-LINE CONSTANT-STORE GROUP IS A SCHEDULING TIE NO SPELLING REACHES - SWEEP THE PRESETS AND PARK** (round 397, field/main/misc9 func_800AC3AC, parked 97.89% at retail's exact 1520 bytes / 380 instructions: every other instruction, the frame and the saved set identical). Retail keeps `ori $v1,zero,0x280` at the head of the 56-store group (60 insns before its first `sh`); the body emits it 18 before, right after the `0x18` def. The other three defs (0xFF, 0x18, 0xC8) land exactly where retail has them in BOTH builds, so the hoisting is register-/priority-driven and only this one lost its slot. Measured dead: every local spelling of the constant (declaration initialiser, statement assignment at the group head, s16/u16 casts, store-to-load-forwarded reuse), `do {} while (0)` around the group (94.64) or around the zero stores (75.68), moving the stores up (93.73 - sched2 does not re-sort stores), -O3, gcc 2.6.0 (97.82), 2.7.2-cdk (70.15), and `try_flags.sh --sweep` (2.7.2 -O2/-O3 x -G4/-G8 x mcpu 3000/r8000), which reads 97.89 in every cell. A `cc1_probe.sh` replica reproduces the body's shape, so retail's def was RTL-positioned at the block head - its source had a statement there that cse folds in this build. Park, do not permute. CONFIRMED on a 39-insn pure-initialiser (round 441, battle/main/misc24 func_800AA898, XenoBattle260Div, parked 74.36% at retail's exact 156 bytes / 39 insns): retail's `addiu v1,zero,-1` is insn 1, ahead of a 0xFFFF/0xFF/0x6B `li`+store triplet, and every body emits it at slot 5 inside the triplet, all 39 instructions otherwise in retail's order - so objdiff's 74.36 is ONE displaced load, not a structural distance. A local cannot hoist it: `s32 negOne = -1;` used by all three -1 stores (cse rematerialises a constant home at its first use) and `s16 n = -1;` both leave it at slot 5, and `try_flags.sh --sweep` over THIS body reads -O1 94.87 / -O2,-O3 74.36 in all 24 cells of 2.6.0 / 2.7.2 / 2.7.2-cdk x -G4/-G8 x 3000/r8000. The identical function in lib_gear (func_801E3534) is parked for the same residual. One clue for a future round: drop the triplet and the same body hoists both homes to slots 0 (-1) and 1 (1), so the retail -1 home was created at the block head by a statement cse folds away. Round 483 measured the `volatile` door on a TWO-displaced-store body and it is a trap: world_map/main/misc3 func_8007756C (parked 93.22% at retail's exact 93 insns / 372 bytes, XenoWorldMap) has retail's `sh zero,g_WorldMapViewRotationZ` and its `sw v0,0(a1)` camera-target store each one sched slot from where the body puts them; a `*(volatile s32 *)` pin on one of the two stores DOES give the target triple retail's relative order, but it stops sched for the whole block and sinks an unrelated `la` (pathFrame) and `lw` (camera height) below it - 83.28%, ten points down at the same 372 bytes. On this class a volatile pin is a rewrite of the schedule, not a partial fix; reordering the three stores was also cyclic (source x,Y,Z 93.22, x,Z,Y 92.89, Z,Y,x 87.68, locals then x,Z,Y 92.57 - the pointer-based store always sinks exactly one position past the first macro store).

- id: a-split-the-if-arm-at-the-product | keywords: delay slot, mult, mflo, sll, sra, split, statement, permuter
  **A `mult`/`mflo` PAIR THAT RETAIL FILLS WITH TWO SHIFT INSTRUCTIONS COMES FROM A SPLIT STATEMENT, NOT FROM ONE NESTED EXPRESSION** (round 400, world_map/misc16 func_80099708, 81.95 -> 91.34 and then 94.82 at retail's exact 260 bytes / 65 insns). Retail is `mult v0,t5 / sll v1,v1,0x18 / sra v1,v1,0x15 / mflo s1 / sra v0,s1,0x14 / addu`; written as one expression (`c = (((pTbl[i].sin * iCol) >> 20) + ((s8)v << 3)) << 16;`) cc1 keeps the mult and the shifts adjacent and leaves the latency unfilled, which costs a whole different body. Two statements - `c = (s8)v << 3;` then `c = ((prod >> 20) + c) << 16;` with `prod` its own local - emit the shifts between `mult` and `mflo` and everything else falls into place. The permuter found the split; it is a normal thing a programmer writes, so port it.

- id: c-a-strength-reduced-index-bump | keywords: delay-slot, nop, addiu, loop, biv, conditional, increment, x
  **AN `addiu sN,sN,8` RETAIL KEEPS INSIDE THE LOOP BODY WHILE ITS LOOP-BACK SLOT HOLDS A `nop` MEANS THE ORIGINAL BUMPED THE COORDINATE ITSELF, CONDITIONALLY - the `x + i * 8` call argument that reproduces the sibling loop cannot produce it, because loop.c turns `i * 8` into an unconditional biv increment and reorg then drops it into the back-edge delay slot** (round 410, menu/main/misc7_r2 func_801D680C, park 99.62 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 1256 bytes / 314 insns). The function draws two number rows with the same `for (i = 0; i < count; i++) if (digits[...] != NONE) primCount += func(..., x + i * 8, y, 0x1000);` shape; row 1 matches with that spelling (its bump is in the `bnez` slot, exactly as retail has it) and row 2 does not: retail row 2 is `lbu <count> / addiu s1,s1,8 / addu / sb` inside the `if` with a `nop` in the back-edge slot. Writing row 2 as `func(..., x - characterId * 24, y, 0x1000); x += MENU_DIGIT_SPACING;` with the bump as the LAST statement of the `if` block makes sched2 place the addiu between the count's reload and its add and leaves the back-edge slot empty - the whole 4-line residual vanished in one edit. The two rows really do differ in the source (row 1's bump executes on every iteration, row 2's only on a drawn digit), so do not 'clean up' the asymmetry; it is invisible in behaviour because `x` is dead after the loop. Symptom: a lone `nop`/`addiu` swap in a loop-back slot where the same function has a second loop that matches.

- id: c-a-per-site-do-while-restores-the-load-delay | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load-delay, do-while, store, order, block, barrier
  **A `do { pActor = g_FieldScriptVMCurActor; read; } while (0)` BARRIER BLOCK AROUND EACH CONTINUATION READ - with the store of the previous result left OUTSIDE it - RESTORES RETAIL'S MISSING BASE-LOAD `nop` AND ITS EXACT INSTRUCTION COUNT, BUT THE STORE STILL LANDS BEFORE THE ACTOR LOAD AND ANY STRAIGHT-LINE TAIL AFTER THE BLOCKS SCRAMBLES** (round 411, field/main/misc func_8008EA58, 114 -> 118 insns at retail's exact 118 / 472 bytes, 74.57 -> 65.84 because the tail reorders, so measure both ends). Five script-argument reads: retail emits per site `[lui/lw v1 actor][sh store of the previous result][lhu v0,0xCC(v1)][lui/lw v1 scriptData][nop][addu v0,v0,v1][lbu]`, i.e. the store sits between the actor load and the ip read and the base load's delay slot has nothing left to fill. The natural spelling (`pActor = g_FieldScriptVMCurActor;` then the store, then the next read) makes cc1 load scriptData BEFORE the ip lhu and fill that lw's slot with the `sh`, so every site is one instruction short (114 insns, 74.57%) and can never link. Wrapping each continuation read together with its `pActor` assignment in its own `do {...} while (0)` gives every site the base-load nop and the exact byte count (each row then reads `[sh store][lw actor][lw base][lhu][nop][addu][lbu]`, still one swap from retail's actor-load-first order); the matched twin FieldScriptSetGameState17FC30 gets the same order for free because its store is a struct field and loading `g_pGameState` pins it. Reach for this when a park is N instructions short with exactly one missing load-delay nop per repeated read/store pair.
Round 425 settled the split: wrap ONLY the read, keep `pActor = g_FieldScriptVMCurActor;` and the store of the previous result OUTSIDE the block (`pActor = ...; store; do { value = call(n, SCRIPT_READ_U8(pActor->ip + 0xB)); } while (0);`) - then every site is retail's `[lw actor][sh store][lhu ip][lw base][nop][addu][lbu]` and the function reaches retail's exact 118 insns / 472 bytes, 74.57 -> 83.85. So the block boundary is what pins the order (cc1 keeps it; the base load cannot be hoisted across it), and the head of this class of function is solvable even though the do-while is not shippable C - report it ROUGH. Same function, same round: statement POSITION inside a single straight-line tail block is not a lever at all (a read-modify-write moved to the first, middle and last position of a store group measures byte-identical, as does an explicit early `u16 t = G;` read with a late `G = t & 0xF;`), so when a tail's remaining diff is three instruction positions, the cause is the register one constant got, and the permuter's own score is not objdiff's: two runs improved the permuter objective 2165 -> 1175 -> 985 while objdiff went 83.85 -> 82.92 -> 74.41 on the same 472 bytes.
Round 474 (slus_006.64/psyq/libc_sprintf Sprintf, PSY-Q preset, 98.87 -> 99.78% and 531 -> 535 insns at retail's exact 2140 bytes) is the same barrier curing the two-hoisted-loads class of `c-a-second-loads-position-inside-a-block-is-not-source-order` when one of the loads is a `va_arg` fetch: wrap ONLY the fetch (`do { value = va_arg(*((va_list*)&ap), s32); } while (0);`) and sched1 can no longer hoist the following `lw flags` above it, so retail's load order and the load-delay `nop` it pays come back in all four arms at once. The block must hold the fetch and nothing else - moving the `if (fmt.u.flags & SPRINTF_FLAG_SHORT)` line inside it puts the flags load back in the same block and loses all four instructions again (measured, 531). Residual left is a local_alloc register tie (retail loads ap into `$v1`, this build into `$v0`), which permute.sh cannot move (base=110 best=110 over 1194 iterations).
Round 471 measured the PER-STATEMENT block on a plain straight-line run with no volatile and no pointer local, and on a pair of struct assignments (field/main/misc3 func_8006FDEC, Default preset, parked 93.66 -> 98.45% / 668 bytes against retail's 672): three consecutive `D_800AFB04 = (u_short)pData[0] << 4;`-style stores are a 6-instruction body against retail's 8 because sched1 hoists the third `lhu` into the second one's load-delay slot into a fresh `$v1`; one `do { color = (u_short)pData[i] << 4; D_800AFB0X = color; } while (0);` per index gives retail's serial `lhu / nop / sll / sh` chain verbatim (93.66 -> 95.24, and that whole block then matches). The same wrapper around `pLights[1] = pLights[0]; pLights[2] = pLights[0];` stops sched1 floating that 22-instruction copy block into the preceding light's `lhu` slot (95.24 -> 98.45). It is not free: the two blocks together leave the function ONE instruction short, because the barrier also hands the following `jal`'s argument setup (`li a0,0x2`, `addiu a1,s1,352`) the slots the retail code gives a `pData++` skip and a load-delay `nop`, and every reordering of that skip measured 97.26 or 95.24 at the same 668 bytes. `build/src/<unit>.c.i` compiled with the unit cc1 plus `-fno-schedule-insns` is retail's exact stream here, INCLUDING the load-delay nops, so diagnose with that probe before spending runs on the skip's position.
- id: c-both-sides-of-the-store-get-the-block | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load-delay, do-while, volatile, pointer, chain, block
  **THE `do { } while (0)` BLOCK AROUND A REPEATED READ OF A `T* volatile` GLOBAL HAS TO CONTAIN THE STORE TOO, AND IT IS PER-STATEMENT: four consecutive `pActor->f = g_FieldActors[i].g << 16;` statements are 8 INSTRUCTIONS SHORT (retail emits each as its own serial `lui/lw/nop/addu/lw/nop/sll/sw` chain) until each one gets its own block** (round 428, field/main/misc8 func_80080A74, 77.88 -> 82.88%, 1200 -> 1228 bytes of retail's 1232, 300 -> 307 of 308 insns, Default preset). A wrapper holding only the read side measures nothing; blocks that are too big also lose: one block around the neighbouring curTriNormal triple is +2 insns (1240, 82.80, it re-reads walkmeshId once more) and one block around the flags12C/flags130 mask statements drops to 70.81 because the hoisted mask constants lose their registers. Wrap exactly one read-plus-store statement per block, and expect the same recipe NOT to transfer to the adjacent straight-line code - measure each block boundary.
- id: c-an-empty-do-while-in-a-case | keywords: delay-slot, reorg, duplicate, andi, switch, dispatch, block, do-while, barrier
  **AN EMPTY `do { } while (0);` AT THE END OF ONE `switch` ARM SHIFTS REORG'S BLOCK NUMBERING SO REORG DUPLICATES A LOOP-TEST `andi` INTO THE DISPATCH `beqz` DELAY SLOT - +1 INSTRUCTION, AND IT IS WHAT RETAIL SHOWS WHEN THE DISPATCHER IS ONE INSTRUCTION LONGER THAN YOURS** (round 420, menu/main/misc9 func_801DBE54, 93.91 -> 94.17% and 888 -> 892 bytes against retail's 896). Retail's do-while menu dispatcher is `sltiu v0,v1,11 / beqz v0,<loop test+4> / andi v0,s6,0xFF` (the loop test's FIRST instruction duplicated into the slot) with `sll v0,v1,2` as an ordinary instruction after the branch; every spelling of the switch gave reorg `sll v0,v1,2` for that slot instead, one instruction short, which three earlier rounds had recorded as an unreachable reorg decision. Adding `do { } while (0);` after the last statement of ONE arm (`prevCol = 0xFF;` then the empty loop) makes reorg emit retail's duplicated `andi` with no other change to the body. It is a permutation guard, not semantics: it also swapped the two loop flags between $s5 and $s6, so check the rest of the prologue afterwards. A second empty do-while at the one remaining site (case 4's tail, where retail keeps an extra `j`) measured identical (94.17 / 892), so the barrier is per-site. The permuter found this in 3 minutes (base 1337 best 1103) among otherwise wrong edits - when a park is one instruction short in a DELAY SLOT, run the permuter on it even if the note says the residual is reorg, then port only the do-while half.


- id: c-flipped-operand-fills-the-load-nop | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load, operand, commuted, and, block, layout, branch
  **A COMMUTATIVE `&`/`|`'s OPERAND ORDER DECIDES WHICH SIDE IS LOADED FIRST, SO A `nop` IN A GLOBAL LOAD'S DELAY SLOT (PLUS A MISPLACED SHARED TAIL BLOCK) IS CURED BY PUTTING THE GLOBAL FIRST** (round 426, field/main/misc2 func_800726E8, 93.36 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 212 insns / 848 bytes, XenoFieldNoGp). Retail tests `dollyStop & g_FieldDirectionMasks[dir]` with the dolly byte loaded right after `lh sceneAngle.vy` (that load's delay slot) and the mask byte emitted after the index chain; the park's `g_FieldDirectionMasks[dir] & dollyStop` emits `lh / nop / ... / lbu mask / lui+lbu dolly`, one instruction more in each of the two button blocks (214 vs 212 bytes) and the shared `frames == 0` tail laid out at +0x168 instead of retail's +0x2b0. gcc's expand_operands evaluates the LEFT operand first and lets the result reuse the RIGHT operand's register, so retail's `and v0,v0,a0` (mask in the result register) means the mask was the source's RIGHT operand. Measured on the same body: swapping the four `&` operands alone gave 99.93 at 212 insns with only three branch targets left, and nesting the two button blocks INSIDE the outer dolly `if` (so the shared tail is the function's last block, which is what those targets encode) closed it. So when a diff is one extra instruction plus a `nop` per repeated block and the branch targets are all shifted while the instruction multiset matches, suspect a commutative operand you spelled the other way round before touching the allocator or the block order.

- id: c-a-call-second-argument-is-emitted-last | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load, jal, argument, expand_call, maspsx, unreachable
  **A CALL'S SECOND ARGUMENT LOAD IS EMITTED AFTER THE FIRST ARGUMENT'S WHOLE ADDRESS CHAIN, SO WHEN RETAIL HAS IT IN THE FIRST ARGUMENT'S TABLE-LOAD DELAY SLOT NO SOURCE ORDER REACHES IT** (round 432, field/main/misc8 func_8008110C, parked 98.13% at 1260 bytes / 315 insns against retail's 1252 / 313). Retail's `SpritePlayAnimation(g_FieldActors[i].pSpriteData, pActor->animationOverride)` site is `lui v0,%hi(g_FieldActors) / lw v0,%lo()(v0) / lh a1,0xEA(s0) / addu v0,s3,v0 / lw a0,4(v0) / jal`, i.e. the second argument's load sits between the table load and the index addu. Reading cc1's own output for the same call (build/src/<unit>.c.s, right above the `jal`) shows `lw $2,g_FieldActors / #nop / addu $2,$19,$2 / lw $4,4($2) / lh $5,234($16)`: expand_call's load_register_parameters walks the arguments a0-first, so the a1 load is emitted LAST and cc1 marks the load-delay hole with a bare `#nop` that maspsx expands; reorg does not steal past the insn that consumes the load. A pre-call local (`s16 anim = pActor->animationOverride;`) moves the lh BEFORE the `lui %hi(g_FieldActors)` that opens the call (source order is contiguous), and the two-statement `pSprite = g_FieldActors[i].pSpriteData; SpritePlayAnimation(pSprite, ...)` folds back to the identical 98.13 / 315 - so this residue is retail's assembler filling the slot, not C. Diagnose by reading cc1's `.s` for a `#nop` between the load and its use before trying spellings.

- id: c-a-volatile-store-blocks-the-branch-slot-only | keywords: delay-slot, load-delay, reorg, volatile, store, increment, latch, hoist
  **A `volatile` STORE STOPS REORG SINKING THE STORE INTO A `bnez` DELAY SLOT BUT DOES NOT STOP IT HOISTING THE LOOP INCREMENT INTO THE PRECEDING GLOBAL LOAD'S DELAY SLOT, so a 4-byte-short body whose last body statement is that store reaches retail's exact size (352) with the store in the WRONG place (95.17%)** (round 442, battle/main/misc1 func_80072938, XenoBattle260 gcc 2.6.0, see also g-source-local-holding-the-doubled-index for the same body at 95.62 / 348). Spelling measured: `*(volatile u8 *)&pPrim[g_BattlePrimStartIndex + prim].b0 = 0;` as the loop's last statement - the non-volatile park gives `lw v0,symbol / addiu s2,s2,1 (stolen) / ...chain... / slt / bnez / sb zero,6(v1) (stolen)`, the volatile one gives `... / slt / sb zero,6(v1) / bnez / nop` (retail's branch-slot nop and its size) but the increment is STILL in the load slot and the store is after the `slt` where retail has it before the increment. So the volatile lever buys the delay slot it is aimed at and nothing else: it is worth one run on a one-instruction-short park, and the load-delay-slot hoist is a separate wall. cc1's own `.s` (build/src/<unit>.c.s) shows the `addiu` already in the load slot before the assembler, so maspsx is not involved.

- id: c-a-second-loads-position-inside-a-block-is-not-source-order | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load, order, va_arg, flags, cse, local-alloc
  **WHEN THE ONLY RESIDUAL IS A `nop` IN ONE LOAD'S DELAY SLOT BECAUSE RETAIL PUTS TWO INDEPENDENT LOADS IN THE OTHER ORDER, FIVE SOURCE SPELLINGS COMPILE BYTE-IDENTICALLY: the order comes from sched1, whose `rank_for_schedule` ranks INSN_PRIORITY first, so plan the spelling hunt around a SHAPE change (an in-block dependent), not statement order** (round 448, slus_006.64/psyq/libc_sprintf Sprintf, parked 98.87% / 2124 bytes / 531 insns against retail 2140 / 535 - the whole body, both digit loops, all three pad loops and the copyOut tail are instruction-identical, and the missing four instructions are exactly the four arms whose vararg lands in `value`). Retail's 'd'/'i' arm is `lw v1,0x220(sp) / addiu v0,v1,4 / sw v0,0x220(sp) / lw a0,0(v1) / lw v1,0x210(sp) / nop / andi v0,v1,0x20`; this compile swaps the last two loads (`lw v1,0x210(sp)` before `lw a0,0(v0)`), so the andi's source is not the freshly loaded register and the nop disappears. The 'n' and 's' arms load the flags FIRST in retail too, so it is not a rule about the arm. Measured byte-identical (five scored runs, `build/src/<unit>.c.s` compared each time): `fmt.u.flags` copied into a `u32` local after the fetch; the same local read BEFORE the fetch; `va_arg` split by hand into `pArg = ap; ap = pArg + 4; value = *(s32*)pArg;`; a `(u32)` cast around `va_arg`; and `value` declared first among the locals. `permute.sh --minutes 4` returns PERMUTER_BETTER base=674 best=522 on a candidate that wraps the fetch in a redundant `if (fmt.u.flags)` and duplicates it - wrong-shaped, not ported. Compare the two loads' positions in cc1's `.s` before spending more than one spelling on this class.

  - round 461 (same function, same 98.87% / 2124 / 531 park) finally named the mover, and it is NOT expand/local_alloc/reorg as the 448 note guessed: compile the unit's own `.i` with `-da` and read the pass dumps - `.rtl`/`.cse`/`.cse2`/`.loop`/`.flow`/`.combine` all hold retail's order (the va_arg value load 503 before the flags load 506) and `.sched` holds the swap, which then survives `.lreg`/`.greg`/`.sched2`/`.dbr`. `schedule_insns` (sched1) runs BEFORE `local_alloc` in toplev.c, and sched.c's priority is `max over in-block successors of (prio + insn_cost - 1)`: with the mips 2-cycle load latency the flags load scores 2 (it feeds `andi` -> `beqz`, both in this block) while the value load scores 1 (its only consumer is the `sll` of the `(s16)` cast, which lives in the beqz delay slot, i.e. the next block), so sched1 emits flags first and the priority tie that would let LUID keep retail's order never happens. A reachable spelling therefore has to give the VALUE load an in-block successor. Two measurement traps this round, both worth more than the match: (1) `-fno-schedule-insns` CANNOT test sched1 in this gcc - toplev.c assigns `flag_schedule_insns = 1` in its `if (optimize >= 2)` block AFTER option processing, so `-O3 -fno-schedule-insns` still schedules (the earlier note's 'cc1 has no -fschedule-insns' was that red herring), and only the `.sched` dump or a `-O1` build shows the difference; (2) read the dump's own pass order out of toplev.c before attributing a move to a pass.
- id: a-pointer-local-dead-in-a-region-must-go | keywords: regalloc, local-alloc, pointer, temp, dead, inline, base, permuter
  **A POINTER LOCAL THAT IS ASSIGNED THE BARE BASE AND THEN USED BY A LATER CLUSTER OF STORES KEEPS THAT BASE PSEUDO LIVE ACROSS THE CLUSTER AND COSTS A REGISTER: delete the assignment and write the base inline in each store's address and local-alloc reuses the register, for free** (round 448, battle/main/misc18 func_80097D5C, 99.52 -> 99.56%, instruction and byte count unchanged at retail's exact 752 / 3024, differing lines 86 -> 76). Here `pDst = (u8*)g_BattleCurWorkBlock;` fed four stores at 0x3F4/0x3F5/0x800/0x801 and then nothing, while two arms set `pDst` again for their own store; rewriting the four as `((u32*)((u8*)g_BattleCurWorkBlock + (snapOffset = i * 8)))[0x3F4] = ...` closed one whole mirror pair (the base was in `$v0` where retail has `$v1`). Permuter-found (run 2 of 3, 1049 iterations, base 330 -> 330-internal-365->330); the companion edit it found on run 1 is the opposite shape on ONE arm only - `pDst = (u8*)(pWorkBlock = g_BattleCurWorkBlock) + i * 8` in the characterId != 4 arm while the == 4 arm keeps the plain form - worth 99.51 -> 99.52. So when a park's diff has several store clusters off the same global base and one intermediate pointer serves more than one of them, split it per cluster before hunting priority quotients; three mirror pairs of the allocno class remained after this and a third permuter run (1021 iterations) was base=best.

- id: c-a-nosched-probe-says-whether-sched2-moved-it | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load, hoist, sched2, schedule-insns2, probe, barrier
  **BEFORE PARKING "THE SCHEDULER MOVED IT", COMPILE THE UNIT'S OWN `build/src/<unit>.c.i` WITH THE UNIT cc1 PLUS `-fno-schedule-insns -fno-schedule-insns2` INSIDE THE BUILD CONTAINER: if that stream is retail's statement order, sched2 is the mover and the remaining levers are the two that re-rank the scheduled stream - an empty-statement barrier after a STORE PAIR, and moving an UNRELATED GLOBAL STORE between two statements of the pair** (round 459, world_map/main/misc7 func_800828DC, 75.62 -> 80.07%, 1676 bytes / 419 insns against retail's 1672 / 418, XenoWorldMapDiv). Retail's five big switch arms run `sw unk50 / sw unk38 / lh ViewRotationY / nop / sll / sw unk54 / sw unk3C / sw CameraHeight / lh ViewRotationZ / nop / ...`; the scheduled build hoists the first `lh` above the two stores and fills the load slot, and the nosched probe prints retail's order exactly (with the load-delay `#nop` marker), which is what the source already says. Two measured spellings moved the SCHEDULED stream: (1) `do { } while (0);` after the unk50/unk38 pair restored the store-then-load order and the load-delay nop, 75.62 -> 77.56 (1684 bytes); (2) writing the CameraHeight store BETWEEN `pSlot->unk58 = ...` and `pSlot->unk40 = ...` instead of before unk58, 77.56 -> 80.07, i.e. the sibling store's position is what lets sched2 rank the constant materialisation into the load delay slot. Measured worse on the same body: a barrier between unk58 and the CameraHeight store 77.14 / 1728; a barrier after unk40 in cases 5/7/9 77.16 / 1744; a shared `s32 angle` local 79.97 / 1676. The probe is 2 docker runs (~10 s) and needs no edit to the unit, so run it before spending diff runs on statement order in any body with a load-delay `nop` residual.

- id: c-a-fresh-local-plus-no-do-while-fills-three-load-slots | keywords: delay-slot, scheduler, do-while, fresh, reuse, materialise, local, scratchpad
  **THREE ARG-SETUP INSTRUCTIONS ROTATED ACROSS THREE LOAD-DELAY SLOTS ARE TWO COUPLED SOURCE FACTS: the pointer whose `addiu` retail materialises first must be a FRESH local (reusing an earlier phase's pointer variable hands it that pseudo's register and one slot later), and a `do { ... } while (0)` wrapped round the constant stores before the call must GO** (round 460, world_map/main/misc4 func_80079778, 2292 bytes = retail's EXACT size, 573 insns, matched with `check_bin.sh world_map` OK; only residual is the scratchpad `%lo(D_1F8000F0)` reloc of `c-goto-past-a-post-loop-label`). Retail's post-switch block fills its three load-delay slots with `[addiu s0=scratch+0xF0, move a1,s0, ori a0=scratch+0xA0]`; the parked body had `[ori a0, addiu s2, move a1]` at 99.74 because the 0xF0 MATRIX pointer was assigned to the switch's own `g_WorldMapGroups` pointer (`pEntries = scratch + 0xF0`), whose pseudo lives in `$s2` from the prologue. Giving it a fresh `MATRIX *pMtx` local used by the first and the last `RotMatrixYXZ` puts it in retail's `$s0` but materialises it one slot later (99.66), and DELETING the `do { } while (0)` around the six constant halfword stores then rotates all three into retail's slots (99.97, the reloc-only residual). The two edits interact, which is why the park's note ("dropping the do/while is 99.26") was measured on the `pEntries` body: one 3-minute permuter run on the clean body returned PERMUTER_BETTER base=325 best=10 with exactly those two edits. Measured and worse on the same body: assigning pMtx before the store cluster (99.55 - the addiu is then stolen into an earlier slot in the preceding block's load delay).

- id: c-one-decrement-is-copied-into-both-jal-slots | keywords: delay-slot, jal, reorg, duplicate, decrement, counter, if-else, arm
  **ONE `i--` IN THE SOURCE IS DUPLICATED BY REORG INTO THE `jal` DELAY SLOT OF BOTH ARMS OF AN `if/else`, SO AN `addiu sN,sN,-1` IN EACH ARM'S SLOT IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE ORIGINAL PROGRAMMER WROTE A DECREMENT IN EACH ARM** (round 471, battling/main/misc15 func_8008BD70, Default preset; four bodies measured IDENTICAL at 93.67% / 228 bytes: `i--` inside both arms, one `i--` after the `if/else`, `for (; i != -1; i--)`, and a guarded `do {} while`, all with `jal func_8008C620` / `jal func_8008C4B0` as the two arms). The parked note had claimed the two-arm spelling was load-bearing; it is not, so do not keep an unnatural per-arm decrement to "protect" a delay slot, and read a decrement in both slots as "one statement, before or after the if/else". What did NOT move in the same four bodies: the loop ENTRY shape (see g-rotated-entry-j-to-bottom-test) and the frame (`vars=8` / frame 40 against retail's `vars=0` / 32), both of which follow from cc1 duplicating the loop exit test.

- id: c-a-load-both-arms-perform-was-hoisted-above-the-test | keywords: delay-slot, nop, load, both-arms, if-else, hoist, merge, texheight
  **WHEN RETAIL'S TWO ARMS OF AN IF/ELSE EACH HOLD THE SAME `lbu` AND ONLY ONE OF THEM DOES ARITHMETIC ON IT, THE LOAD WAS HOISTED ABOVE THE TEST AND THE ARITHMETIC LEFT AFTER THE MERGE - writing the whole `x = field - clip` expression after the if/else instead puts the load directly in front of its only use on the else path and forces a `nop` in the load slot, i.e. exactly one instruction too many** (round 483, slus_006.64/system/rendering_atfree func_8001F1D4, XenoRenderingAtfree = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0): `texHeight = pFrameData[i].height;` above the texY test with `texHeight -= clip;` after it measures 91.34% at retail's EXACT 860 bytes / 215 insns, against 91.22 / 864 / 216 for the one-statement `texHeight = pFrameData[i].height - clip;` below the if/else. Retail is `blez s0,L / srav s1,s1,v0 / lbu a1,5(s3) / lbu t0,7(s3) / j L2 / addu a1,a1,s1`, then `L: lbu a1,5(s3) / lbu t0,7(s3) / subu a1,a1,s1`, with the surviving `subu t0,t0,s1` landing in the following `beqz` delay slot; the second load fills the first load's slot in both arms. Generalisation: a load that both arms perform is hoisted and only the arm-specific arithmetic is duplicated, so count the loads per arm in retail before reading the arms as two independent statements.

- id: c-two-subtraction-args-as-statements-second-arg-first | keywords: delay-slot, nop, jal, subu, arguments, load order, subtraction, scheduler, call
  **A CALL WHOSE TWO ARGUMENTS ARE EACH `field - field` OF THE SAME STRUCT GETS RETAIL'S LOAD ORDER AND ITS `subu` IN THE JAL SLOT ONLY WHEN THE TWO SUBTRACTIONS ARE SEPARATE STATEMENTS AND THE SECOND ARGUMENT'S IS WRITTEN FIRST - inline in the call, the first argument's loads come first, its `subu` sits in the last load's delay slot with a `nop`, and the second argument's `subu` takes the jal slot** (round 484, battle/main/misc27 func_800B51B0, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0: 84.19 -> 84.73% and one instruction, 992 -> 988 bytes / 247 insns against retail's 246). Retail is `lh v1,0xC(s1) / lh v0,0xE(s1) / lh a0,0xA(s1) / lh a1,0x8(s1) / subu a0,v0,a0 / jal ratan2 / subu a1,v1,a1`, i.e. the x1/y1 loads come before y0/x0 and the y-difference is the one computed before the call; `angle = ratan2(pLine->y1 - pLine->y0, pLine->x1 - pLine->x0) + 0x400;` instead gives `lh v1,0xE / lh a0,0xA / lh v0,0xC / lh a1,0x8 / nop / subu a1,v0,a1 / jal / subu a0,v1,a0`. With `dx = pLine->x1 - pLine->x0; dy = pLine->y1 - pLine->y0; angle = ratan2(dy, dx) + 0x400;` every row of that region is retail's. dy-first and dx-first as statements are byte-identical to each other (measured), so the load order is the scheduler's once the subtractions are out of the call; the WIN comes from taking them out, and the `nop` disappears with it. Generalisation: when a diff's residual is one `nop` in a load-delay slot plus two `subu`s swapped between the pre-call stream and the jal slot, check whether the call's arguments are expressions of more than one load each - hoisting them into named locals is the source shape that lets reorg place them, and the extra instruction is the observable.

- id: a-volatile-global-pointer-blocks-the-jal-store-slot | keywords: delay-slot, jal, store, volatile, reorg, extern, qualifier, probe
  **A `volatile` QUALIFIER ON THE GLOBAL POINTER A STORE GOES THROUGH IS WHAT LEAVES A `jal` DELAY SLOT WITH SOMETHING OTHER THAN RETAIL'S STORE: cc1 wraps the store in `.set volatile`, reorg then may not move it, and the slot is filled from the next block instead - which also displaces a loop init and can duplicate the following bound test (2 instructions / 8 bytes)** (round 486, battle/main/misc13 func_800861D0, Default = gcc-2.7.2 `-O2 -G8`; 98.70 -> 99.41% and 2496 -> retail's exact 2488 bytes / 622 insns). Retail's tail is `li v0,1 / jal BattleUpdateFrame / sb v0,0xA8(v1)`; with `extern volatile u8 *g_BattleDisplayState;` the identical body emits `sb` BEFORE the jal and the jal slot takes the free-loop init, so the `beqz s7` guard slot fills from the target (`sltiu`) and the test appears twice. Proved without touching the unit with `tools/scripts/cc1_probe.sh battle/main/misc13` on a two-function snippet that differs only in the qualifier: `volatile u8 *` -> `.set volatile / sb / .set novolatile` then a bare `jal`; plain `u8 *` -> `jal / sb` in the slot. WHERE THE QUALIFIER IS GENUINELY NEEDED it is per-STORE, not per-file: same unit's BattleDrawCommandRowSprites needs its last store NOT to fall into the `jr $ra` slot (that store without the qualifier is 96.05 / 316 bytes against 100.00 / 324), and a local `volatile u8 *pState = g_BattleDisplayState;` used for THAT ONE store keeps it while the file keeps the plain `extern u8 *` every other battle unit uses. So when a park's note blames reorg for a swapped/duplicated delay slot, grep the qualifier on the pointer before re-spelling the C.

- id: a-retail-nop-in-a-jalr-slot-is-a-volatile-store | keywords: delay-slot, jalr, nop, volatile, store, callback, reorg, function-pointer
  **A `nop` IN RETAIL'S `jalr` DELAY SLOT WHERE YOUR COMPILE PUTS THE PRECEDING STORE IS EVIDENCE THAT THE STORE'S LVALUE IS VOLATILE IN THE SOURCE: a plain store is slottable and reorg moves it after the `jalr`, a volatile one is not, so the slot keeps retail's `nop` - and that is also what lands retail's exact size** (round 491, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_c func_8004696C, PSY-Q = gcc-2.7.2-psx `-O3 -G0`: 186 -> 187 insns and 744 -> 748 bytes = retail's exact, 94.44 -> 95.27%). Retail's DrawSync-callback arm ends `sw zero,0(v1) / jalr v0 / nop`; with `u_long *pPending = &g_DrawSyncCallbackPending;` the store lands in the jalr slot and the body is one instruction short, and `volatile u_long *pPending` reproduces retail. The flag is set from the DMA-callback context, so the qualifier is honest rather than a hack. Check the whole arm's rows, not just the slot: the same qualifier is on the flag's READ and retail's read shape (`lw v0,0(v1)` off an address held in one register) is unchanged by it. This is the inverse of `a-volatile-global-pointer-blocks-the-jal-store-slot` - there a volatile store was the defect, here retail's own nop proves it is load-bearing, so read the slot first and blame the qualifier second.

- id: a-merged-tail-duplicated-into-the-previous-unconditional-jumps-slot | keywords: delay-slot, reorg, duplicate, merge, tail, call, mask, jump
  **REORG CAN FILL THE DELAY SLOT OF AN UNCONDITIONAL JUMP BY *DUPLICATING* THE FIRST INSN OF THE JUMP'S TARGET WHEN THE TARGET BLOCK HAS ANOTHER PREDECESSOR, WHICH COSTS ONE INSTRUCTION AND DISPLACES THE INSN RETAIL PUTS IN THAT SLOT** (round 494, battle/main/misc2 func_8007500C, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0, parked 89.74% / 352 bytes / 88 insns against retail's 344 / 87, the single surplus instruction being exactly this copy). The body makes TWO identical calls of a six-argument function, one per if/else arm, so each arm carries its own `u16` truncation of one argument; cc1 merges the two call tails into one block (`andi a1,a1,0xffff` / `jal` / `sw v0,0x14(sp)`) and reorg then copies that block's FIRST insn into the if arm's `j` slot, where retail's slot holds the arm's own `addu a0,a0,s2` (which this body emits two instructions earlier, before the arm's last volatile load). Measured on the same body, all worse, so the mask count cannot be steered: a single call after the if/else with the per-arm argument values in locals collapses the whole argument setup into the shared block (78 insns / 312 bytes / 59.66); `extern void F();` (K&R, no caller-side truncation anywhere) removes both masks but re-orders the arm and the prim-index load (77 differing lines / 68.99); a `u16` temp assigned before each call moves the mask onto the wrong register (84.16). So when a surplus `andi`/`lbu` shows up at the end of ONE arm and nowhere else, check whether it is the first insn of the merged target block before hunting a declaration - and note that a park whose surplus is this copy is one instruction over retail and can never link.

- id: c-a-do-while-label-before-the-dead-stores-restores-the-arrival-block-order | keywords: delay-slot, nop, reorg, do-while, label, block, arrival, call-argument, load-slot
  **A ONE-ITERATION `do { } while (0)` AROUND THE DEAD STORES THAT PRECEDE A CALL IS WHAT MAKES A SHARED TAIL BLOCK START WITH ITS LOAD, SO REORG CANNOT STEAL THE CALL'S ARGUMENT COPY INTO THE PRECEDING BRANCH'S DELAY SLOT - the label is the whole knob, and it buys retail's block order AND retail's `nop` in one edit** (round 496, field/main/misc11 func_80092894, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8; 92.56 -> 96.68%, 912 bytes / 228 insns against retail's 908 / 227). The tail is reached by a `bnez` (fall-through) and two later branches; retail's block opens `lhu v0,0x106(s2)` and its slot is `nop`, while the park emitted `move a0,s7 / move a1,zero` first and reorg filled the slot with the `move a0` (one instruction short, block order scrambled). Wrapping just `pSpriteData->moveSpeed = 0; pActorData->curAnimationId = 0;` in `do { } while (0);` (96.42) and then leaving the call OUTSIDE the wrapper so its argument copies start a second block (96.68) reproduces retail's `lhu / (slot) / ori / sh / sh / sw / sh / lui / lw / move a1,zero / index chain / jal / addu` exactly. Both ends worth knowing: the label does NOT have to be semantically meaningful (a bare `{ }` is not enough here, the label is), and the residual it leaves was the per-block copy of the pointer into `$a0` (ours coalesced it, so the load-delay slot after the `lhu` took a `nop` - the 4 surplus bytes). Read with `a-dead-if-else-block-flips-a-two-way-callee-saved-hand-out` and `n-a-do-while-0-is-a-barrier`.

## operand order of addu and arithmetic spelling

- id: c-offset-first-cast-sum-does-not-flip-an-array-symbol-base | keywords: addu, operand, index-first, base-first, cast, symbol, array, sizeof, limit
  **THE OFFSET-FIRST CAST SUM OF `c-cast-sum-with-the-offset-term-first-flips-a-global-pointer-base` DOES NOT TRANSFER TO AN ARRAY SYMBOL BASE WHOSE ADDRESS NEEDS ITS OWN `lui`/`addiu` (no load): there the scaled index and the base register are decided by whether the STORE of the index value is emitted before or after the address sum, and no spelling moves it** (round 483, world_map/main/misc4 func_80077E68, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2 with --dont-expand-li, parked 92.97% / retail's exact 1060 bytes / 265 insns). Retail is `sra v0,index / sll v1,v0,3 / addu a0,v1,a0 / sw v0,84(s0)` (index survives the sum in `$v0`, base pre-loaded into `$a0`, index-first `addu`); `pPoint = &g_WorldMapCameraPathPoints[grid]; p->unk54 = grid;` and `pPoint = (WorldMapPathPoint *)(grid * sizeof(WorldMapPathPoint) + (u32)g_WorldMapCameraPathPoints);` are BYTE-IDENTICAL to each other (92.97 / 1060 / 265) and both emit `sw, sll, addu` with the scale reusing `$v0`, i.e. base-last `addu` with the index destroyed. Also byte-identical on that body: the tail's six scratchpad word stores written as a typed `WorldMapPos4` pair (`pDst[0].x/.y/.z`, `pDst[1].x/.y/.z`) instead of `((s32 *)pScratch)[0..6]`, so a 0x10-stride struct view buys nothing when the fields are written one per statement - and a permuter find of the shape `pVec->f = g_X; pVec->f = (pVec->f >> 12) + 0x32;` DOES buy retail's load position (95.26%) but emits the intermediate store the retail object does not have (1064 bytes / 266 insns), so it is a false better for any park whose byte count was already retail's.

- id: c-cast-sum-with-the-offset-term-first-flips-a-global-pointer-base | keywords: addu, operand, index-first, base-first, cast, u32, pointer, global, sizeof
  **FOR A GLOBAL POINTER BASE (`FieldActor* volatile g_FieldActors`) LOADED ONCE AND INDEXED BY A SCALED `int`, cc1 WRITES RETAIL'S INDEX-FIRST `addu` (`addu v1,v0,v1`, base destroyed in place) ONLY WHEN THE OFFSET TERM IS WRITTEN FIRST IN A CAST SUM** (round 475, field/main/misc12 func_8009AEE0, Default preset, 97.42 -> 97.48% at retail's exact 636 bytes / 159 insns; the function stays parked at 97.48 for an unrelated tail-order residual). Retail is `sll v0,index,1 / addu v0,v0,index / sll v0,v0,3 / subu v0,v0,index / [lw v1,g_FieldActors] / sll v0,v0,2 / addu v1,v0,v1`; `(FieldActor*)(actorIndex * sizeof(FieldActor) + (u32)g_FieldActors)` reproduces it, while `actorIndex + g_FieldActors`, `&g_FieldActors[actorIndex]`, `&FIELD_ACTORS[actorIndex]`, `(FieldActor*)((u32)g_FieldActors + actorIndex * sizeof(FieldActor))` and a plain `g_FieldActors[actorIndex]` subscript all emit the mirrored `addu v1,v1,v0`. Same family as `c-context-term-written-first-flips-a-row-subscript-addu` (offset term first) and the opposite of `c-pointer-from-memory-paren-sum-is-base-first` only in that the base here is a symbol, not a struct member: measure the two orders before believing either. COMPANION from the same function, a load-grouping lever worth 3.8 points: when retail keeps two narrow field loads adjacent (`lh a0,0x22(s2)` / `lh a1,0x2A(s2)`) and this cc1 splits them around an intervening store and `addiu`, READ THE TWO FIELDS INTO LOCALS BEFORE THE ARITHMETIC - `positionX = CONV_TO_GTE(pActor->position.vx); positionZ = CONV_TO_GTE(pActor->position.vz);` then `delta.x = x - positionX; delta.y = 0; delta.z = z - positionZ;` gives retail's `lh,lh,addiu,sw-zero,subu,subu,sw,jal,sw` exactly (93.65 -> 97.42 with the byte count already correct), where `delta.x = x - CONV_TO_GTE(...)` written inline, the same three statements in dx,dz,dy order, and dy first all split the loads.

  COMPANION (field/main/misc8 func_80080F44, Default preset, 99.12 -> 100.00% at retail's exact 456 bytes / 114 insns, MATCH): a body with TWO volatile reads of `g_FieldActors` needs TWO pointer locals before the cast sum can help, and each local's read must be pinned - `pFieldActor = (FieldActor*)(actorIndex * sizeof(FieldActor) + (u32)g_FieldActors); pFieldActor->spriteFlags = 0; do { } while (0); pSlot = <same cast sum>; actorStatus = pSlot->status; pActor = pFieldActor->pActorData;` reproduces retail's split (first read's base does the store and the `pActorData` load, second read's base does the status `lhu` and the model-data load). Three of those lines are separately load-bearing, each measured on the otherwise-identical body: the typed `&g_FieldActors[actorIndex]` mirrors the `addu` and scores 99.82, deleting the empty `do { } while (0)` between the store and the second read scores 92.98 (cc1 then reloads both bases up front and the store sinks), and dropping the `actorStatus` local in favour of `pSlot->status` in the `if` scores 98.51 (the `lhu` moves after the `pActorData` load). So on a 99%+ park whose only residual is WHICH read a field load goes through, count the source reads first: the fix is usually a second pointer plus a barrier, not a register-order spelling.
- id: c-narrow-type-as-the-left-add-operand-flips-a-halfword-corner-addu | keywords: addu, operand, index-first, base-first, u16, halfword, narrow, corner, declaration, in-place
  **FOR A HALFWORD-ONLY SUM (`u16` result from two `u16` operands) THE LEFT OPERAND IN THE C IS THE `addu`'s FIRST SOURCE, SO RETAIL'S `addu v1,s2,v0` FOR A CORNER IS REACHED BY WRITING THE DISPLACEMENT FIRST (`x1 = nWidth + x0;`); THE SAME SWAP DOES NOTHING WHEN ONE OPERAND IS `s32`, BECAUSE THE WIDENED ADD IS LEGALISED THROUGH A `zero_extend` AND cc1 COMMUTES IT BACK** (round 473, slus_006.64/system/temp2 func_8002675C, XenoGraphicsDiv = gcc-2.7.2-cdk, park 92.96 -> 97.55% at retail's exact 688 bytes / 172 insns). Four corner adds in one texture-quad builder: retail has `addu v1,s2,v0` (the scaled width first, the origin second) and `addu v0,s5,v0` (scaled height first) at both the flipped and unflipped arms. The park's natural `y1 = y0 + nHeight;` emits the mirror; `y1 = nHeight + y0;` (both operands `u16`) gives retail's order at all four y sites. The x pair is `s32 nWidth` and stays mirrored whichever way the sum is written (measured: `nWidth + x0` byte-identical to `x0 + nWidth`), so read the type of each operand before spending an attempt. Companion lever from the same function, worth 2 instructions: an `s16` FIELD decremented into a local (`v = pData->v - 1;`) re-issues the load (`lhu` for the earlier `u16` use, then a second `lhu` for the `s16` read) where the in-place `v--;` on the already-loaded `u16` local emits retail's single `addiu`, so prefer the in-place form whenever a park is 2 instructions over with one duplicated load.
- id: c-struct-member-displacement-flips-a-reloaded-global-base | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, struct, member, displacement, reload, global, store
  **ON A STORE THROUGH A GLOBAL POINTER THAT MUST BE RELOADED PER STATEMENT, THE BASE-FIRST `addu` IS REACHED BY PUTTING THE CONSTANT IN A STRUCT MEMBER'S DISPLACEMENT - a cast that folds the constant into the pointer keeps the index-first order, which is why six cast spellings measured dead** (round 472, battle/main/misc23 func_800A64E4, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0 -G0, 98.71 -> MATCH at retail's exact 928 bytes / 232 insns, `objdiff 100.00%`). This CORRECTS the "not reachable from C" verdict of `a-addu-index-first-is-the-legitimiser` and `c-no-index-spelling-flips-a-store-side-addu-under-a-reloaded-global`: those probed `g[i * 0x24 + K]`, `*(u8 *)(g + i * 0x24 + K)`, `((ProbeSlot *)(g + 0x1740))[i].c0[k]`, an `off` local, both embedded assignments and a `Row` view - every one of them either writes the index first or FOLDS THE CONSTANT INTO THE POINTER, and a folded pointer is a `PLUS` the legitimiser may commute. Declare the view struct with the constant as a real member offset (`BattleSpriteColorView { u8 unk0[0x16E0]; BattleColorSlot unk16E0[4]; BattleColorBlock unk1740[4]; }`) and write `((BattleSpriteColorView *)g_BattleSpriteRenderData)->unk1740[i].colours[0].red = pSrc[0];`: that is `MEM(base = the reloaded global, index = i, scale = 0x24, disp = 0x1740)`, and cc1 emits retail's `addu $2,$2,$5` (base first, the running `i * 0x24` second) with the reloaded pointer in `$2` and the `lbu` result in `$3` - retail's `$v0`/`$v1` pair AND its operand order, at all 30 sites, with each site still reloading the global through its own bare `lw $2,sym`. A 2-D `u8 member[4][0x24]` flips identically, so the element's internal typing is free. Measured with `tools/scripts/cc1_probe.sh battle/main/misc23` on both bases of that body (the `u8 *` global and the `void *[2]` array's element 0, which needs a separate view struct for its 0x284/0x2E4 offsets); the guard spelling is unaffected (`g[0] != NULL` still tests a POINTER, which is what keeps retail's 928 bytes - the scalar extern tests a byte and costs 8).

- id: c-context-term-written-first-flips-a-row-subscript-addu | keywords: addu, operand, index-first, base-first, subscript, sum, array, row, per-site
  **WHERE THE PLAIN TYPED SUBSCRIPT CANONICALISES A ROW ADDRESS INDEX-FIRST, WRITING THE CONTEXT/OFFSET SUM FIRST IN THE SOURCE (through a cast view of the row) EMITS RETAIL'S OPPOSITE OPERAND ORDER AT THAT SITE ONLY - and the function can want BOTH orders, because retail's own body has them** (round 460, slus_006.64/system/system func_80034888, 97.93 -> 98.03, retail's exact 1572 bytes / 393 insns). Four `code |= 1` / `code &= ~1` flag writes into `pString->pChars[row].sprt[context][1].code` were the only `addu`s wrong: retail has `addu v1,s2,v1` (the `context * 0x28` pseudo first) at 0x34AA0-0x34B2C's flag arms but `addu v1,v1,s2` (same pseudo second) for the sprite stores two instructions later, for the SAME address. The typed subscript always gives the second form. Spelling the flag writes as `((SystemStringChar *)(context * sizeof(pString->pChars[0].sprt[0]) + (u32)&pString->pChars[row]))->sprt[0][1].code |= 1;` - the context term written FIRST in the sum - gives retail's first form at those four sites and leaves every other address in the body alone, so the flip is per-site and the row's `* sizeof` giv survives. Two companions: a `u16`-poisoned spelling of the same address silently widens the access (`lhu`/`sh` and `andi 0xfffe` where retail has `lbu`/`sb`, 97.11), and the double-negation lever does not apply here (the destination is already the row register, so there is nothing to move it off).

- id: c-offset-first-sum-cast-flips-a-local-array-slot | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, cast, local, array, stack
  **FOR A STACK-LOCAL ARRAY SLOT the plain subscript puts the BASE in the `addu`'s destination (`normals[idx].vx` -> `addu v1,a0,v1`) and a cast over an offset-first sum puts the OFFSET there (`((VECTOR*)(idx * sizeof(VECTOR) + (u32)normals))->vx` -> retail's `addu v1,v1,a0`)** (round 441, field/main/misc8 func_80080A74, Default preset, still parked: 83.17 -> 83.39 but 1228 -> 1224 bytes, i.e. it buys the operand order and loses an instruction elsewhere). Same family as `c-p-tag-cast-flips-a-u8-store-index-first`: the cast-with-the-offset-written-first is the spelling that moves the base off the destination, and for a LOCAL array it is the only one measured. Judge it on the byte count: on that body the +0.22% came with a shorter body, so the operand fix alone is not a win.
- id: c-p-tag-cast-flips-a-u8-store-index-first | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, cast, p_tag, byte, store, memory-base
  **FOR A BYTE STORE THROUGH `polys[renderContext]` WITH A BASE THAT COMES FROM MEMORY, WRITING THE STORE THROUGH A `P_TAG*` CAST IS WHAT PUTS THE OFFSET FIRST - the typed `POLY_FT4` field write gives base-first plus a load-delay `nop` per store** (round 422, menu/main/misc8_r2 func_801DA9A8, parked 98.08%; 12 such stores in one function, `-0.6%` and 3 nops from the spelling alone). Retail is `addu v0,v0,v1` (destination = the `renderContext * 0x28` temp, base second) with `sb s0,0x1004(v0)`; `g_Menu->pItemRows->primGroupStrings[0].polys[g_Menu->renderContext].r0 = 0x80;` emits the mirror `addu v1,v1,v0` and, for the `g_Menu->itemRowStrings[row]` group, `addu v0,v0,a2` + `addu a0,a0,v0` (g_Menu added last) with a `nop` in every load-delay slot. `((P_TAG*)&....polys[g_Menu->renderContext])->r0 = 0x80;` (the misc9 func_801DCE60 spelling) gives retail's `addu a0,s1,a0` (base+row<<7 formed right after the `lw g_Menu`, filling the delay slot) then `addu v0,v0,a0`, and keeps the per-statement `lui/lw g_Menu` reloads. Measured with `cc1_probe.sh menu/main/misc8_r2` on six spellings in one snippet: the typed field write, the flat `((POLY_FT4*)primGroupStrings)[ctx]` cast, `((u8*)base)[0x1004 + ctx*0x28]` and its `*(...)` twin are all offset-first; only the typed struct-field write is base-first. The `SetSemiTrans(&....polys[ctx], 0)` argument (a pointer, not a byte store) was already offset-first in both.
- id: c-pointer-from-memory-paren-sum-is-base-first | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, pointer, field, paren, volatile
