  **`((u8*)ptrField + i)[K]` IS THE BASE-FIRST SPELLING WHEN THE BASE POINTER COMES FROM MEMORY (`g_Menu->unk35C`), where `((u8*)ptrField)[K + i]` is index-first - and a `volatile`-QUALIFIED POINTER LOCAL is what puts such a base pair in retail's stack slots** (round 421, menu/main/misc8 func_801D8644, parked 88.01% under XenoMenu260 at 1964 bytes / 491 insns against retail 1952 / 488; whole 488-instruction body written from the assembly, no twin). Probed with `tools/scripts/cc1_probe.sh menu/main/misc8` on a four-spelling snippet: `pos[0x32C0 + i] = v`, `(pos + i)[0x32C0] = v`, `pos[i + 0x32C0] = v` and an in-place `p += i; p[0x32C0] = v` - only `(pos + i)[0x32C0]` emits retail's `addu $2,$2,$4` (base first, destination = the base register); the other three emit `addu $2,$4,$2`. That is the opposite verdict to `a-addu-index-first-is-the-legitimiser`, which measured the same parenthesised form as index-first for a PLAIN `u8 *` GLOBAL, so the pointer-from-memory base is the distinguishing case (same class as the round-419 `g_BattleGraphicsWork->pPacketPrims` finding, one edit per site, 85.02 -> 85.69 here from ten sites). Companion: declaring the two stat pointers `u16* volatile pStat;` / `u16* volatile pSaved;` forces both into 8-byte stack slots that are RELOADED at every use, which is exactly retail's `sw v0,64(sp)` then `lw a2,64(sp)` per row, and buying that one allocation change moved the whole body 85.69 -> 88.01 with no other edit (a plain `u16* pStat` kept them in `$s0`/`$s1` and cost the function two accumulator registers). Do not ship the volatile - it is a measurement tool here - but it identifies "spilled pointer pair" as the allocation retail had.
- id: c-double-negation-works-on-a-mem-field-base-and-then-decides-the-switch | keywords: addu, operand, negate, base-first, in-place, switch, case, order
  **THE DOUBLE NEGATION IS NOT ONLY FOR A POINTER VARIABLE: `MEMFIELD - (-(idx * 0x28))` PUTS A STRUCT/POINTER-FIELD SUM IN PLACE TOO, AND WHAT REGISTER IT LANDS IN THEN DECIDES WHICH `switch` CASE ORDER THE BODY NEEDS** (round 419, battle/main/misc17, gcc 2.6.0/XenoBattle260). func_80093578 matched 100.00 first try and func_8009187C went 98.22 -> 99.89 at retail's exact 700 bytes from one edit in each: retail forms every `g_BattleGraphicsWork->pPacketPrims + idx * 0x28` row address in place (`addu v1,v1,v0`, base first, destination = the base register), and `pRec = g_BattleGraphicsWork->pPacketPrims - (-(((s32 *)g_BattlePrimStartIndex)[0] * 0x28));` reproduces it where the plain `prims + idx * 0x28` gives the mirrored `addu v0,v0,v1` (pRec $v0, palette value $v1). It is the same sum at the two palette stores only; the call argument keeps the inline `prims + (idx * 0x28 + 0x320)` form. Two companion facts from the same pair: (1) once pRec is in place, 9187C's `switch` wants its cases listed 0, 1, 2, default -- the 0, 2, default, 1 order its old park note demanded (98.22, switch instruction-identical but a `nop` in the first `beq` slot) becomes wrong, so a case order is not a property of the switch, it is a property of the body's register state; (2) the double negation does NOTHING on a sum of two INTEGER offsets (`off = (..) * 0x28 + arg0 * 0x5F0`): it folds away and compiles identical, so 9187C's remaining residual (that sum's destination is the slot-offset register, `addu v0,v1,v0`, against retail's `addu v1,v1,v0`) is not reachable this way, and a fourth permuter round on the 99.89 body is PERMUTER_NONE base=20 best=20 over 1435 iterations. Round 426 (battle/main/misc16_r2 func_800904A0, same preset/tables, 91.97 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 620 bytes / 155 insns) adds two companion facts. (1) THE INLINE `g_BattlePrimStartIndex[0]` IN THE CALL IS WHAT PUTS `li a1,K` / `li a2,K` BEFORE THE `la` OF THE PRIM INDEX: with a `s32 *pMode = &g_BattlePrimStartIndex;` statement the `lui/addiu` pair is emitted there, the join block starts with it, reorg cannot split the pair, so the two `beqz` and one `beq` delay slots stay `nop` and the body is 4 bytes long (91.97, 624) - writing the index inline in the call argument lets right-to-left argument expansion emit the constant args first and leaves the address pseudo for the pointer argument, giving retail's order and the three filled slots. (2) IT ALSO DECIDES `default:`: 800904A0's retail switch is the same three cases with the case-0 block separate and a `j`-to-join fall-through for values over 2, so it wants NO default, where 9187C's identical-looking switch wanted one - the case list follows the body's register state here too.
- id: c-a-folding-constant-needs-its-own-local | keywords: reassociate, constant, fold, addiu, subtract, clamp, operand, local
  **A CLAMP WHOSE CONSTANT gcc CAN FOLD INTO THE SURROUNDING SUM NEEDS THAT CONSTANT IN A LOCAL, and the sibling statements come back one per variable** (round 404, field/dialogue/text_box func_8009C5A8, the last 0.3% of a 468-instruction body). Retail's box clamp is `left = x - 8 - width * 2` / `left + 16 + width * 4` / `y + 8 + height * 14`; written with the literals cc1 reassociates them into `x - (width * 2 + 8)` and `y + (height * 14 + 8)` (97.10, five instructions off each clamp), and `i = 8; left = x - i - width * 2;` / `i = 0x10; ...` / `i = 8; ...` (the `i` local reused for the two margins) reproduces retail's separate `addiu` chain. Two further statement-splitting facts measured on the same body and worth reaching for before a park: `y = screenY - height * 14 - 0x24;` in one expression computes `height * 14` BEFORE loading `screenY`, so the load has to be its own statement (`projectedY = screenY; projectedY = projectedY - height * 14; y = projectedY - 0x24;`); and an "already open, bail out" tail written inline lands at the head of the function while the same statements behind a `goto` to a label at the very end land where retail has them, moving every branch target in the body.

- id: c-a-prim-offset-constant-in-a-local-adds-to-the-offset-not-the-base | keywords: addu, addiu, operand, constant, fold, prim, offset, local
  **A PRIM ADDRESS OF THE FORM `count * 80 + 0x1C70 + base` NEEDS THE CONSTANT HIDDEN BEHIND A LOCAL, OR cc1 FOLDS IT INTO THE BASE POINTER AND THE `addu`'s ORDER FLIPS** (round 474, menu/main/misc7_r2 func_801D7884, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, park 93.14 -> 95.08, 2 of the 3 residual instruction sites). Retail is `sll a2,t0,2 / addu a2,a2,t0 / sll a2,a2,4 / addiu a2,a2,0x1C70 / jal / addu a2,a2,t1`, i.e. the constant is added to the OFFSET side and the unmodified base goes in the call's delay slot. The natural `(POLY_FT4*)(count * (2 * sizeof(POLY_FT4)) + 0x1C70 + (u32)base)` measures `addiu t0,t0,0x1C70` (the base pointer local gets the constant) and `addu a2,a2,t0`; hoisting the sum to `u32 primOffset = count * (2 * sizeof(POLY_FT4)) + 0x1C70;` and passing `(POLY_FT4*)(primOffset + (u32)base)` reproduces retail's order at both such calls. The same edit in a loop that folds the constant into the `lhu` displacements (`pPrim = base + i * 40 + 0x1C70`, loads at 0x1C78/0x1C80/0x1C92) is WRONG - there the plain `base + offset + 0x1C70` is already retail apart from a commuted `addu`, so apply it per site, judged by whether retail's displacement carries the constant. Same family as `c-a-folding-constant-needs-its-own-local`.
- id: c-a-double-negated-offset-flips | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, negate, subtract, address, tie
  **A DOUBLE-NEGATED OFFSET (`p - -(i * sizeof(T))`) MAKES cc1 PUT THE BASE IN THE `addu`'s DESTINATION, WHICH IS THE ONE SPELLING THAT FLIPPED THIS PARK'S FOUR MIRRORED ADDRESSES** (round 405, menu/main/misc7_r2 func_801D5ED4, 99.32 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 704 bytes / 176 insns, XenoMenu260 = gcc 2.6.0). Retail forms every `primBase + renderContext * 0x28` row address as `addu v1,v1,v0` - base FIRST, destination = the base register - where `(u8*)base + ctx * 0x28`, the `[ctx]` subscript, a named pointer local, `base + ctx` pointer arithmetic, the `pBase = base; pBase += ctx * sizeof;` in-place form and a pointer-arithmetic cast ALL emit the mirrored `addu v0,v0,a1` (offset first, destination = the offset temp) with the base and context registers swapped as well, at all four sites. Writing the offset with a double negation (`*(u16*)((u8*)g_Menu->pGearWindowPrims - -(g_Menu->renderContext * sizeof(POLY_FT4)) + 0x66) = ...`) closed one site per edit and each edit is exactly one site, so the four were measured independently: 99.43 (the 0x66 store), 99.72 (both palette arms), 100.00 (the `x0`/`y0` pair). The pointer-arithmetic form `((POLY_FT4*)base + ctx)` measures the same 99.32 as the subscript, so it is the negation that carries the fix, and `sizeof(POLY_FT4)` at all four sites is code-identical to the literal 0x28. Do not reach for this on a body that is otherwise fine - the in-place `pBase +=` form is still the one to try for a `pBase + CONST` store - but for a base/offset pair that mirrors at EVERY site of one function, the negated offset is one edit per site, and the permuter does find it (this park's note recorded a 1392-iteration run with no find on the same body; a 1324-iteration run found exactly this edit, base 120 -> 100).

- id: c-the-negation-closes-a-window-prim-tail-and-a-typed-view-loses-it | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, negate, tail, store, poly_ft4, struct, block
  **THE DOUBLE NEGATION CONFIRMED ON THE SAME UNIT'S GEAR-WINDOW TAIL, AND THE MEASURED PROOF THAT A TYPED `POLY_FT4` / BLOCK VIEW OF THE SAME BYTES IS NOT THE FIX** (round 430, menu/main/misc8 func_801D7CFC, 97.08 -> MATCH at retail's exact 596 bytes / 149 insns under XenoMenu260). The body was parked at 97.08 with a whole-tail instruction-order residual (retail loads `pGearWindowPrims` two slots earlier and forms `addu a0,a0,v1` base-first for the `tpage |= 0x20` read-modify-write, index-first for the three `r0`/`g0`/`b0` byte stores); ONE edit - `*(u16*)((u8*)g_Menu->pGearWindowPrims - -((g_Menu->renderContext + selected * 2) * sizeof(POLY_FT4)) + 0x1E16) |= 0x20;` - closed the whole tail at once (the three byte stores kept their plain index-first casts; they already matched). The natural-looking typed spelling of the SAME statements (`typedef struct { u8 unk0[0x1E00]; POLY_FT4 windowPrims[2][2]; SVECTOR windowQuadVertices[2][4]; ... }` with `pBlock->windowPrims[sel][ctx].tpage |= 0x20` / `->r0 = 0x20` / `->x0`) measures 64.37% at 592 bytes / 148 insns, because the block pointer becomes a loop-invariant local that cc1 hoists and the whole tail then shares one register. So: when the loop already matches through `pBase`/`pEntry` offset locals, do not "clean up" the tail into a struct view to match the identical bytes - measure it, expect ~64%, and keep the negated cast.

- id: c-the-negation-does-not-survive-a-loop-index | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, negate, giv, loop, accumulator, tie
  **THE DOUBLE NEGATION FLIPS AN OFFSET THAT IS A MULTIPLY OF A NON-LOOP REGISTER ONLY: WHEN THE OFFSET IS THE LOOP'S OWN `i * STRIDE`, loop.c STRENGTH-REDUCES THE NEGATED FORM INTO A NEW ACCUMULATOR WITH A NEGATIVE STEP AND THE BODY COSTS AN EXTRA INSTRUCTION** (round 406, menu/main/misc9 func_801DD5E8, still parked 99.72% at retail's exact 424 bytes / 106 insns, gcc 2.6.0). The two residuals are the addresses of two `lbu renderContext` loads, `panel + i * 0x80` with `panel = g_Menu->unk430` loaded at the use site; retail writes both base-first (`addu v0,v1,s0`, `addu v0,v0,v1`) and cc1 2.6.0 offset-first (`addu v0,s0,v1`, `addu v1,v1,v0`), same operand pair, same instruction multiset. The round-405 win's spelling applied here (`(u8*)g_Menu->unk430 - -(i * sizeof(MenuString)) + 0xF7D`) does put the base first, but as `subu v0,v1,s3` off a fresh negative accumulator (`addiu s3,s3,-128` in the latch), so it is 92.78% at the same 424 bytes with the register set rotated. `cc1_probe.sh` on a standalone copy of the loop (base-first cast, offset written first, a base pointer local assigned inside the loop, an embedded assignment temp `(pBase = (u8*)g_Menu->unk430)`, an index-first struct view, a u16 index) emits `addu $2,$2,$3` - offset first - for every one, and a fourth `permute.sh -j 2` run (1189 iterations, base=30 best=30) ends at the same body. So a park whose only residual is a base/offset `addu` order where the offset is a loop index's own multiply is the legitimiser, not the source: park it, do not respell.

- id: c-struct-member-array-subscript-flips-a-loop-index-addu | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, struct, member, array, loop, subscript
  **AN `addu` WHOSE OFFSET IS THE LOOP'S OWN `i * STRIDE` DOES FLIP TO RETAIL'S BASE-FIRST ORDER WHEN THE ARRAY IS A STRUCT MEMBER AND THE INDEX IS THE BARE LOOP VARIABLE - what cannot flip it is any cast spellings of the same address, including `(T*)field[i + K]`, `((u8*)field + i * N)[K]` and the paren sum, which all cse to index-first** (round 443, menu/main/misc9 func_801DD5E8, 99.72 -> MATCH at retail's exact 424 bytes / 106 insns, XenoMenu260 = gcc 2.6.0; this CORRECTS `c-the-negation-does-not-survive-a-loop-index`, which ends "park it, do not respell"). The two residuals were the `lbu renderContext` addresses of the 0x430 panel's two shifted sprite groups: retail `addu v0,v1,s0` / `addu v0,v0,v1` (base first, displacement 0x77D / 0xF7D), every cast spelling `addu v0,s0,v1`. The panel is a `void*` (`g_Menu->unk430`) so the twin's own spelling was unavailable as written. Fix: declare a file-local view struct with the two record arrays as members at their real offsets (`u8 unk0[0x700]; MenuString shadedRowStrings[0xE]; MenuString columnStrings[2]; MenuString headingStrings[2];`, the same idiom as this file's existing `MenuUnk430ValueStrings`) and write `->shadedRowStrings[i].renderContext`. The struct-member form gives the address the MEM(base, index=i, scale=0x80, disp=0x77D) shape whose index is the biv, so cc1 emits `sll vN,i,0x7` + base-first `addu`; the cast form folds the constant into the pointer and the legitimiser then prefers index-first. Two companion measurements on the same body: (a) `->valueStrings[i]` (the neighbouring 0x700 array of the existing view struct) works identically, and (b) an index that is a SUM (`->valueStrings[0x10 + i]`) does NOT - loop.c strength-reduces it into a second running accumulator (`li s3,0x800` / `addiu s3,s3,0x80`) and the whole body rotates to 94.14% at the same 424 bytes, so the constant base must be the member's, not the index's. Also measured dead here: taking the row entry as a typed `MenuString* pString` used for BOTH the `polys[rc].r0` gate and the call address (97.74% / 416 bytes - retail forms the gate's address as `base + (i*0x80 + rc*0x28)` and the call's as `(base + i*0x80) + rc*0x28`, two different trees, so the gate must stay a separate expression).
- id: c-a-minus-chain-reassociates-the-subtract | keywords: reassociate, subtract, subu, operand, order, crossjump, tail, local, clamp
  **`(C - a) - b` IS REASSOCIATED TO `(C - b) - a`, WHICH SWAPS WHICH VALUE GOES IN WHICH REGISTER AND - WHEN TWO ARMS SHARE THE TAIL - COSTS THE CROSS-JUMP; a `v = C - a; return v - b;` LOCAL PUTS RETAIL'S ORDER BACK, BUT gcc THEN MERGES ONLY THE LAST `subu`** (round 411, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_b func_80045C94, parked 92.73% at 184 bytes against retail's 176 / 44 insns). Retail holds `0x400 - w - p->x` in two arms and executes it once: case 2 jumps INTO case 1's tail at +0x40 with `li v0,1024` in the delay slot. Five spellings measured: the plain `return 0x400 - p->w - p->x` in both arms 88.02 (v1 = **x**, a0 = w - the loads come out `lh v1,0` / `lh a0,4`, mirrored, and no merge); the same with `w = p->w / 2;` in case 2 92.68; `v = 0x400 - p->w; return v - p->x;` in both arms 87.16 (retail's operand order and load order, 45 insns, but both arms jump to a THIRD block holding `subu v0,v0,a0` instead of case 2 jumping into case 1); the v-form in case 1 plus the w-local in case 2 92.73 - the park. A 4-minute permuter run (base 457 -> 317) found only the un-parenthesised case-2 arm, which is 88.07 on objdiff, so its metric and objdiff disagree here: judge this class by the block layout, not the score. Companion fact from the sibling clamp in the same unit (func_80045A34, 79.12% at 188 bytes against retail's 204): retail spends TWO extra instructions per axis on a `move a2,v0` that copies the loaded `g_GpuScreenWidth` plus a `addiu v0,a2,-1` that RECOMPUTES `G - 1` in the clamp block, i.e. its build did not cse that expression across the branch, while cc1 here computes `addiu v1,v0,-1` once and moves it into the merge; the if/else clamp-block spelling that should separate the two uses scores 65.59, so an "extra instructions retail has" gap of exactly `1 copy + 1 recompute` per bounded axis is a cse difference to park, not a source shape to find.

- id: d-array-extern-hoists-its-address-scalar-extern-does-not | keywords: addu, operand, in-place, array, scalar, extern, hoist, cse
  **THE OBSTACLE TO THE IN-PLACE `+=` FORM FOR AN ARRAY-BASED GLOBAL IS THE ARRAY, NOT THE CONSTANT ADDRESS: with `extern u8 *g[2]` cc1 hoists `la t0,g` out of the loop and reloads through it, while the SAME global declared as the SCALAR `extern u8 *g` keeps the per-site symbolic `lw v0,g` and then gives retail's base-first `addu`** (round 418, battle/main/misc23 func_800A5EB4, 92.95 -> 99.16 at 1412 bytes / 353 insns against retail's 1424 / 356; the previous park's 99.58 body had retail's exact size but all 15 `g_BattlePartPrimBuffers` operand orders mirrored). The probe (`cc1_probe.sh battle/main/misc23`) settles it in 10 s: the identical loop body over `extern void *gArr[]` emits `la $7,gArr` once + `lw $2,0($7)` per site, over `extern void *gScalar` it emits `lw $2,gScalar` per site - and both give base-first `addu $2,$2,$3` for the two-statement form (`p = g; p += i * 0x18; pDst[0] = p[0x284];`). So when a TU uses only element 0 of a global that another unit declares as an array (`extern u8 *g[2]` in misc22), declaring it scalar in this TU is what puts the address back inside the MEM. Casts do not substitute: `*(u8 **)&g` re-creates the array address (hoist), and `*(u8 * volatile *)&g` forces an INDIRECT address (`lui/addiu/lw`, one instruction more than retail's `lui/lw`).

- id: c-two-or-terms-need-a-local | keywords: or, operand, order, reassociate, fold, constant, local, pack
  **A WORD THAT IS `(value << N) | CONST | (mem & mask)` NEEDS THE `(value << N) | CONST` HALF IN ITS OWN LOCAL, or cc1 moves the constant next to the memory operand and the final `or`'s destination swaps** (round 421, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_b func_80045E44, 98.51 -> MATCH at retail's exact 151 insns / 604 bytes, PSY-Q preset). Retail builds the E1 draw-mode word as `srl/sll` (color >> 31 << 10) / `or v0,v0,v1` (0xE1000000) / ... / `andi a0,a0,0x7ff` / `or a0,a0,v0` - the result in the register the *status* read was in. Written inline as `(color >> 31 << 10 | 0xE1000000) | (*g_GpuGp1Port & 0x7FF)` cc1's fold reassociates the constant onto the memory term and emits `or a0,a0,v1` then `or v0,v0,a0` (96.03%); moving the whole `(color >> 31 << 10) | 0xE1000000` subexpression *out of the arms* to one local before the `if` is worse still (87.70, the result wanted `$t2` across both arms and the body lost 4 instructions). The closed form is a local declared at the TOP of each arm (`u_long drawMode; drawMode = (color >> 31 << 10) | 0xE1000000;`) - one per arm, not shared, because retail reloads the `lui 0xE1000000` in each arm - plus the memory term FIRST in the final `or` (`(*g_GpuGp1Port & 0x7FF) | drawMode`); the operand order there is what makes the destination retail's register rather than a mirror. Companion fact: `limitRange(x, 0, W - 1)` from libgpu.h is the exact clamp retail has on both axes of this body, but its `move a2,v0` + recomputed `addiu v0,a2,-1` per axis is the same cse gap already recorded under c-a-minus-chain-reassociates-the-subtract - here gcc cse'd it and the prologue still matched, so do not chase it.

- id: i-if-else-inside-a-loop-canonicalises | keywords: if, else, block, order, layout, arm, break, continue, canonicalise, loop
  **AN IF/ELSE WHOSE TWO ARMS BOTH END IN `break`/`continue` INSIDE ONE LOOP IS CANONICALISED BY cc1 2.6.0, SO THE ARM ORDER YOU WRITE CANNOT MOVE THE BLOCK LAYOUT - measure it once, then park** (round 430, menu/main/misc8 func_801D9704, 84.26% at retail's exact 260 bytes / 65 insns under XenoMenu260). Retail is `bnez a2 -> gear block` with the `currentCharacterIDs` arm as the fall-through and the gear block placed after it, just before the return; cc1 emits the mirror (`beqz a2 -> characterIDs`, gear arm fall-through) and, worse, `addiu a0,a0,1` before the case's `andi a2,a2,0xff`/`lui g_Menu` group where retail has it last. Four spellings measured and all byte-identical to each other: the if/else-if, an else-less then-arm ending in an explicit `continue` (the shape retail's duplicated `addiu a0,a0,1` in BOTH back-edge delay slots suggests), the same with the arms swapped, and `if (!arg2)`. Earlier rounds on the same body also measured `while (1)` + trailing `arg0++`, a `pManager` local (66.43), and `goto` labels (right arm order, 62.38 - the loop stops being recognised and `g_Menu`/the 0xFF constant stop being hoisted) plus an explicit `arg0++; continue;` with a second `arg0++` at the bottom (85.62, cross-jumped increments, +8 bytes). Block order is not a source shape when the arms are symmetric: park it.

- id: c-base-plus-field-offset-is-canonicalised | keywords: addu, operand, offset, field, pointer, local, subscript, canonicalise, probe
  **`(u8*)pBase + pBase->fieldOffset` IS CANONICALISED BASE-FIRST BY gcc 2.7.2 FOR ALL SIX SPELLINGS, INCLUDING A DECLARED `s32` OFFSET LOCAL - the operand order follows the pseudo numbering of base vs load temp, not the source, so a park whose only residual is the mirror of retail's `addu v0,v0,v1` is closed** (round 441, battling/main/misc10 func_80084C88, parked 97.37% at retail's exact 840 bytes / 210 insns; retail has the offset as the addu's first operand AND destination where the body emits base-first with the same destination). Probed with `cc1_probe.sh` on a snippet reproducing the function's real six-statement context (`pScript` / `pPartTimings` / `pModelScriptOffsets` / `pActions` stores around the one in question): the plain sum, the offset written first (`pHeader->offset + (u8*)pHeader`), an `(s32)` cast, the subscript form `&((u8*)pHeader)[off]`, and a named `s32` offset declared before AND after `pHeader` all emit the identical `lw $2,48($3)` / `addu $3,$3,$2` (base first, destination = the first operand, i.e. the base; the load temp folds into the sum so the declared local changes nothing). Read this with `b-commutative-sum-will-canonicalise`, where a copy of a PARAMETER does move the pair: that trick needs the copied value to stay a live pseudo, and a memory load's result cannot. The 2.6.0 route is also measured dead here - that compiler keeps source order, so the offset-first spelling was scored on the whole body: 96.13, the same number as the plain spelling, i.e. the addu leg buys a 2.6.0 switch nothing (cdk 94.04, Default 97.37).

- id: c-a-base-pointer-local-expands-the-address-before-the-index | keywords: addu, address, order, prologue, lui, addiu, sll, base, index, local
  **WHEN RETAIL'S PROLOGUE EXPANDS THE BASE ADDRESS (`lui`/`addiu`) BEFORE THE INDEX MULTIPLY AND EVERY SINGLE-EXPRESSION SPELLING EMITS THE INDEX FIRST, ONE `T* p = base;` STATEMENT ABOVE THE SUBSCRIPT SWAPS THE TWO GROUPS AND IS BYTE-NEUTRAL** (round 448, menu/main/misc8_r2 func_801DA9A8, 99.04 -> MATCH at retail's exact 1668 bytes / 417 insns, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0). For `pItemId = &g_GameState.itemIDs[arg1 * 2 + arg0];` retail is `lui v0,%hi(g_GameState+0x2026)` / `addiu v0,v0,%lo(...)` then `sll a1,a1,0x1` / `addu a1,a1,s1` / `addu s3,a1,v0`; the subscript, the `g_GameState.itemIDs + idx` pointer form and the swapped index order all emit the `sll`/`addu` pair first (99.04, 99.48, 99.04, each 4 differing lines and retail's byte count), and `pItemIds = g_GameState.itemIDs; pItemId = &pItemIds[arg1 * 2 + arg0];` gives retail's order exactly. The pointer base survives as its own pseudo because it is a declared local, so expand_expr has an already-materialised base to emit before the index; a cast or a folded symbol does not (same mechanism as several `cast` levers above). Count it as a spelling, not a scope change: the local is dead after the one statement, costs no register and no instruction.

- id: c-the-negation-unmerges-a-cross-jumped-switch-tail | keywords: addu, cross-jump, merge, switch, tail, negate, destination, instruction-count
  **A SWITCH WHOSE ARMS RETAIL DOES NOT MERGE AND YOURS DOES (your body SHORT by the size of one arm's shared tail) CAN BE UNMERGED BY PUTTING THE ELEMENT ADDRESS'S BASE IN THE `addu` DESTINATION WITH THE DOUBLE NEGATION - and what is then left is the operand ORDER, because retail's own two forms in that function differ in it** (round 456, gear_shop_menu/main/render func_801D2B74, 96.75 -> 97.64%, 2508 -> 2528 bytes / 627 -> 632 insns against retail's 2532 / 633, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0). Three gear-table arms (stride 0x14 / 0x8 / 0x10) each compute `&table[shopItemIDs[id]]` with two uses (price and equipFlags) and a copy of the load/`j`/store tail; retail keeps ONE tail shared by the armor and frame arms and a SECOND inline copy for the engine arm (`addu v1,v0,v1` there, `addu a0,v0,v1` in armor/frame), and cross_jump merges all three into one copy when every site lands in `$v0`. `pEngine = (T*)((u8*)pGearEngines - -(id * sizeof(T)));` was the single edit that unmerged it: dest becomes the BASE (`addu v1,v1,v0`). The subscript and `pGearEngines + id` both measure 2508 (dest = index). NOT closable on the same body, measured: the double-negated form is base-FIRST where retail's engine sites are index-first with the base as destination, and armor/frame want a third register (`addu a0,v0,v1`) that coalesces with neither dying operand; the 1 remaining instruction is retail's `places[]` base rebased onto a spilled frame pointer (`lw t1,0x78(sp); addiu a1,t1,0x10`) where ours folds to `addiu a1,sp,48`. Related dead ends there: writing the divisor through the frame pointer (`((s32*)((u8*)pRect + 0x28))[j]`, 2544 / 636 - the displacement is materialised per use), a single work struct holding rect+digits+decoded+places (88.24), and `pRect` for every `&rect` use (88.86). Judge a merge-shortfall park by `addu` DESTINATION first, order second.

  Round 469 added the cheap half of the same body: **a `RECT` that is both the target of a `setRECT` macro and the argument of a pointer call (`LoadImage`) wants the MACRO sites spelled `&rect` (cc1 folds them to stack stores, retail `sh s1,0x20(sp)`) and the CALL sites spelled through the pointer variable (`LoadImage(pRect, ...)`, so the spilled pointer is reloaded as retail's `lw a0,0x78(sp)`) - one spelling for all of them is two different errors.** `LoadImage(&rect, ...)` folds to `addiu a0,sp,0x20` and costs 1.27% (97.64 -> 98.91 here, 109 -> 101 differing lines, same 632 insns / 2528 bytes); `setRECT(pRect, ...)` as well as `LoadImage(pRect, ...)` and `LoadImage(&rect, ...)` both reload the pointer, which adds the frame slot the function did not have (98.56% at 0xE0 frame / 635 insns). The matched neighbour is the reference: `GearShopMenuRenderSellItemRows` in the same file is `setRECT(&sp20, ...)` + `LoadImage(pRect, ...)`, and it also shows the `places[j]`-rebased-onto-pRect shape this park is one instruction short of (`addiu a1,fp,0x10` / `lw v0,0x28(a1)` with pRect in a register; the same body with pRect spilled has to spend retail's extra `lw t1,0x78(sp)` first, which is why the 4 bytes are not reachable while pRect has no live register).

- id: c-paren-sum-does-not-flip-a-pointer-globals-base-loaded-once | keywords: addu, operand, base-first, index-first, paren, cast, pointer, global, negate
  **THE PAREN-SUM / CAST SPELLING (AND SO THE DOUBLE NEGATION) DOES NOT FLIP `addu` ORDER WHEN THE BASE IS A POINTER GLOBAL LOADED ONCE INTO A REGISTER - it measures byte-identical to the plain subscript, so that park's residual is the legitimiser's per-use choice and not a spelling question this unit can reach** (round 478, lib_gear/main/main func_801E5D44, parked 97.61% at retail's exact 1512 bytes / 378 insns, XenoLibraryDiv = gcc-2.6.0). The body has three `D_801E8644[index + K]` stores (`extern s16 *D_801E8644`, one `lw` of the pointer into `$a0` for all three); retail is index-first at `+1` (`addu v1,v1,a0`) and base-first at `+4` and `+7` (`addu v1,a0,v1`, `addu a0,a0,v0`), i.e. one expression, three uses, two orders. `((s16 *)((u8 *)D_801E8644 + pCmd->index * 2))[4]` and `[7]` - the `c-pointer-from-memory-paren-sum-is-base-first` shape, and the only spelling that corresponds to the double negation when the base is a MEM rather than a declared pointer local - measured the same 97.61 / 1512 / 378 with the same 156 differing lines. Companion verdict in the same function for the same reason: `c-a-double-negated-offset-flips` needs the base to be a pointer VARIABLE (`pBase`, `g_Menu->pField`), and the unit's own park note had recommended the negation for this body without measuring it.


- id: f-a-half-hoisted-operand-in-its-own-local-gives-retail-or-destination | keywords: or, operand, order, dest, hoist, local, index, flags
  **WHEN RETAIL'S `or` PUTS THE SECOND-COMPUTED VALUE IN THE DESTINATION AND THE FIRST IN THE SECOND SOURCE (`or v0,v0,v1` WITH `v1` = `a->flags_0xA8 >> 30` AND `v0` = `(a->flags_0xAC & 3) << 2`), NEITHER OPERAND ORDER OF THE ONE-EXPRESSION SPELLING REPRODUCES IT: A8-LEFT GIVES RETAIL'S LOAD AND OP ORDER (BOTH `lw`s, THEN `srl`, THEN `andi`/`sll`) WITH THE TWO REGISTERS MIRRORED, AND AC-LEFT GIVES RETAIL'S REGISTERS WITH THE A8 CHAIN EMITTED LAST (94.42 MEASURED). ASSIGNING THE A8 HALF TO ITS OWN LOCAL FIRST AND WRITING THE `|` AC-LEFT REPRODUCES BOTH** (round 484, battle/main/misc30 func_800B9F78, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0, 95.94 -> 99.97% and retail's exact 1384 bytes / 346 insns). The three sites of the idiom sit in three different scopes, and each needs its OWN local: `s32 partHigh; partHigh = a->flags_0xA8 >> 30; index = ((a->flags_0xAC.flags & 3) << 2) | partHigh;` closed the head site and the `case 5` site with the local declared inside each `{}` block, and the same edit at the `case 4` site (whose `or` was the only residual there, operand order alone) closed the last one - one function-scope `partHigh` shared by two arms instead re-mirrors them.

- id: a-redundant-reload-and-a-per-access-at-form-are-two-separate-holes | keywords: addu, reload, volatile, la, at, per-access, display-value, tail
  **A RETAIl/RECOMPILE INSTRUCTION-COUNT HOLE IN A GLOBAL-ARRAY READ-MODIFY-WRITE IS TWO INDEPENDENT REQUIREMENTS - a redundant RELOAD (a `volatile`-free spelling never emits it) and a PER-ACCESS `lui $at,%hi` + `addu $at,$at,idx` + `lbu %lo($at)` address (every 2+-ref spelling here CSEs one `la` base into a register) - and no probed spelling gives both: `+=`, `A[i] = A[i] + x`, aggregate, 2-ref and 4-ref all give the hoisted `la` + `andi 0xff`, while `extern volatile` gives retail's reload but STILL hoists the `la`** (round 488, battle/main/misc11 func_80080160, still parked 95.01% / 2424 bytes / 606 insns against retail's 2436 / 609; retail's `if (q[0x2E3])` display-value block is 23 insns against the body's 16 with exactly these two differences). Measured with `tools/scripts/cc1_probe.sh battle/main/misc11`. Companion facts from the same round: the struct-member-displacement lever above does NOT transfer to a `u8 *` GLOBAL POINTER indexed by `g + idx * 0x40` - spelling the 0x3C sites as `((BattleCommandRow *)(g_BattleCommandQueue + arg0 * 0x40))->targetSlotId` is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the raw `((u8 *)(...))[0x3C]` cast and keeps the index-first `addu` (that lever needs a MEM-with-constant-base, not a pointer variable); and the preset leg for this unit is closed - gcc-2.6.0 scores this function 96.34 but drops BattleFindMinValueOtherSlot to 99.69 and BattleSetActorFlag34 to 97.00, and cdk scores 85.02 and breaks four, so `battle/main/misc11` stays Default and the mixed unit cannot be switched.

## extra or missing move

symptoms: one extra or missing move / second copy of a value
try: move copy missing extra
- id: a-table-load-through-its-own-local-produces-retails-two-copies | keywords: move, copy, extra, local, load, table, global, callee-saved, nop
  **WHEN RETAIL COPIES A TABLE LOAD INTO A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER TWICE (`lw a1,0(at)` then `move s5,a1` in the `beqz` delay slot then `move s6,s5`) AND YOURS LOADS STRAIGHT INTO THE SAVED REGISTER AND LEAVES A `nop` WHERE THE SECOND MOVE SHOULD BE, THE FIX IS TO GIVE THE LOAD ITS OWN LOCAL: `pSlot = g_Table[i]; if (pSlot == NULL) continue; pEntity = pSlot;`** (round 479, battle/main/misc25 func_800B026C, XenoBattle260Div = gcc-2.6.0, 96.08 -> 96.36% at retail's exact 2120 bytes, 190 -> 166 differing lines, and the load/test/copy group became instruction-identical). One variable (`pEntity = g_Table[i];`) lets reload put the load's destination in the saved register directly and the copy chain collapses to one `move` plus a hole; naming the load's result makes the copy into `pEntity` a real pseudo, so gcc emits retail's two moves and fills the delay slot. The extra pseudo also perturbs the whole callee-saved hand-out (here it also swapped `z` back into retail's `$s3`), so re-measure the pair after adopting it even when the instructions line up.
- id: e-a-second-copy-between-two-callee-saved-pseudos-cannot-exist | keywords: move, copy, cast, combine-regs, callee-saved, pseudo, parameter, addu
  **A `(T *)parameter` CAST IS *NOT* FREE IN cc1 2.7.2 - IT MAKES A SECOND PSEUDO AND A REAL `move` - BUT `combine_regs` KEEPS THAT COPY ONLY BECAUSE ITS SOURCE IS THE CALL-CLOBBERED `$a0`; A *THIRD* COPY BETWEEN TWO CALLEE-SAVED PSEUDOS (`addu s1,s0,zero`, a second local initialised from the first after the allocations) IS ALWAYS MERGED, so a body that is exactly one `move` short for that reason cannot be fixed by spelling it** (round 455, battling/main/misc14 func_8008B13C, parked 97.42% / 588 bytes against retail's 592 / 148 insns). Retail is `move t1,a0` at entry, `move s0,t1` before the first call, and `move s1,s0` right after the HeapAlloc; our body has the first two as `move s1,a0` / `move s0,s1` and no third, which is the whole 4-byte gap (every other instruction, both jump tables and the frame are exact). Three spellings measured, all byte-identical to the park: the copy `pBase = (u8 *)pCfg;` placed BETWEEN the HeapAlloc and the next store (retail's exact emission slot), the two loop-2 sums written value-first (`pSpec->value + pBase`) to chase retail's `addu v1,v1,s1` (gcc normalises to `addu v1,s1,v1` regardless of operand order), and the same sums as `&pScript[pSpec->value]`. So read the register of the copy's SOURCE before spending a lane: a copy whose source is a parameter's `$aN` is reachable, one whose source is an already-saved pseudo is not.
- id: a-preheader-copy-needs-the-earlier-loop-scratch | keywords: move, copy, coalesce, preheader, callee-saved, loop, counter, scratch
  **A `move dst,src` AT A LOOP PREHEADER THAT A SECOND LOCAL LOSES (cc1 coalesces the src/dst pair because src dies there) IS REACHED BY MAKING THE DESTINATION THE *SAME* VARIABLE AN EARLIER LOOP ALREADY USED AS ITS COUNTER - one variable, two roles, and the whole callee-saved hand-out follows** (round 438, world_map/main/misc1 func_80072DB4, 96.65 -> 97.81 -> 99.94% at retail's exact 1356 bytes / 339 insns, XenoWorldMap). Retail is `move s5,a1` (colour param) then `addu s2,s5,zero` in the entry test's delay slot, and `s2` is ALSO the FT4 column-init loop's counter at the top of the function - so the colour's pseudo is one whose live range already crosses the four HeapAlloc/GetTPage calls, which is exactly why it is callee-saved and why the copy survives; a separate `nColor` gets `$s3` (the freed param register), coalesces with `color` into one pseudo and the copy disappears, 1352 bytes and unlinkable. Two more load-bearing shapes on the same body, each worth its own instructions: the count-down loop is written `count--; for (; count != -1; count--)` (a single pre-decrement statement, so loop.c cannot fold it to `beqz count`, and the parameter register is reused IN PLACE as `addiu s7,s7,-1` - `for (i = count - 1; i != -1; i--)` and a `nEnd = -1` local both cost a register and 4-8 bytes of frame), and retail's third-column `setUV4` has u3 = u1 = the column width (0x40), not the first column's 0x80 - that one value error alone kept 12 store rows permuted AND was a wrong byte in the overlay, so read every setUV4 argument off the `sb` list before blaming sched2 for a store-order diff. Residual after all three: only the two `PutDispEnv`/`PutDrawEnv` pair relocations name `D_8009BC9C` in retail where the typed `g_WorldMapGfxEnvs[1].dispEnv` gives base+0xD4 (same address, check_bin OK) - and the `(DRAWENV*)((u8*)pDispEnv - 0x5C)` cast is load-bearing: `pEnv = &g_WorldMapGfxEnvs[1]; PutDispEnv(&pEnv->dispEnv); PutDrawEnv(&pEnv->drawEnv);` is 98.76%.
- id: b-cse-reuses-a-limit-behind-a-branch | keywords: move, copy, cse, limit, addiu, clamp, regenerate, branch
  **A CLAMP LIMIT RETAIL COMPUTES TWICE FROM A PRESERVED COPY OF THE LOADED BASE (`addu a2,v0,zero` / `addiu v0,v0,-1` for the compare, `addiu v0,a2,-1` in the arm) IS NOT REACHABLE FROM SOURCE WHEN IT IS A CHEAP reg+const EXPRESSION: gcc 2.7.2 cse1 keeps ONE pseudo and copies it into the arm (`addiu v1,v0,-1` / `move a0,v1`), and 14 spellings that name the limit twice still merge** (round 424, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_b func_80045A34, parked 79.12% at 188 bytes against retail's 204 - 4 instructions, 2 per axis, so it cannot link; the sibling func_80045B00 is the same body plus an opcode word and parks the same way at 79.80%). Measured with `cc1_probe.sh` on this unit's flags, every one giving a single `-1` and a move into the arm: ternary on the parameter, if/else-if with and without an else arm, a limitRange-style macro on a local, the same macro with the limit textually duplicated, an s16 mirror local, `int`/`u_short` locals holding W-1, comparing against `>= g_GpuScreenWidth` (which instead computes the limit AFTER the slt and costs the same 1), `int w = g_GpuScreenWidth;` with `w - 1` written twice, sequential ifs, and m2c's hoisted-limit shape. Presets ruled out: 2.7.2-cdk 75.78, 2.6.0 79.12. Load-bearing in the parked body: `u_long t[4]` reproduces retail's 0x10 frame with no store anywhere (`.frame $sp,16`, so it goes in the bltz delay slot), and the mode test spelled `!= 1 && != 2` gives retail's `sltiu` + bnez.
- id: b-increment-hoisted-above-a-call-pair | keywords: move, copy, increment, addiu, delay, reorg, loop, counter
  **A LOOP COUNTER RETAIL INCREMENTS IN TWO INSTRUCTIONS (`addiu $vN,counter,1` then `move counter,$vN`) IS INCREMENTED WITH THE SUM HOISTED ABOVE THE PRECEDING CALL PAIR AND THE COPY BELOW IT - the one-instruction spellings all coalesce and reorg then steals the `addiu` into the previous `jal`'s delay slot, where retail has a `nop`** (round 409, field/main/misc3 FieldFree, 98.66% at 652 bytes against retail's 656 -> 100.00 / 656). Retail is `jal GfxFlushImageList / nop / jal DrawSync / move a0,zero / addiu v0,s1,1 / lui+lw g_FieldCurRenderContextIndex / move s1,v0 / addu a0,a0,s1` with the loop test at the bottom. What reproduces it is `do { next = i + 1; GfxFlushImageList(); DrawSync(0); i = next; GfxSetRenderContext((g_FieldCurRenderContextIndex + i) & 1); ... } while (i < 2);` - the sum lands in `$v0` before the two calls, the copy into the counter `$s1` after them, and the pair is then too far from any branch to be target-filled. Measured dead ends, all 98.66 / 652: `i++`, `++i`, `i += 1`, `i = i + 1`, `(i = i + 1)` in the argument and `next = i + 1; i = next;` AT the increment site (after `DrawSync`, before the context call) - every one coalesces to a single `addiu`; `i++` at the loop top; using `next` instead of `i` in the context argument; gcc-2.7.2-cdk 90.87 and -O3 98.66. A permuter run found it from a two-temp body (`new_var = i + 1` at the top, `next = new_var; i = next;`) in 67 iterations; the single temp with the copy after the call pair is the tidy equivalent and also scores 0.
- id: d-mult-by-2-emits-a-copy | keywords: move, copy, sll, mult, shift, expand_binop, park
  **`x * 2` whose result has to live in a callee-saved register costs an extra `move`; `x << 1` does not** (round 394, battle/misc23 func_800A9540, 376 -> retail's 372 bytes, 94.49 -> 94.73). cc1's expand of `index = slotTextIndex * 2;` emits a TEMP plus a copy (`sll v1,v1,1` / `move s0,v1`, confirmed in the -dg dump as a `(set (reg 100) (ashift (reg 74) 1))` followed by `(set (reg 76) (reg 100))` in the pre-alloc .combine dump, i.e. it is in the RTL, not the allocator), while `index = slotTextIndex << 1;` expands the shift straight into index's allocno (`sll s0,v1,1`) and reaches retail's byte count. When a body is exactly one `move` too long and the value is a multiply by two, write the shift.
- id: d-repeated-base-i-stride | keywords: move, copy, loop, addu, cc1, delay, permuter, pointer
  **A repeated `base + i * stride` sum that retail COPIES into a second register is source-controllable: give the LOOP its own pointer local.** round 370, battle/misc9 (a permuter find, base 974 -> 263): `pRow = (u16 *)((arg1 & 0xFF) * 0x40 + (s32)g_BattleSlotWordRegs); pRow[idx] = 0; pField = pRow;` and then the loop reads `pField` - the sum pseudo stays live past the copy, so cc1 emits retail's `addu v1,v1,v0` + `move s5,v1` instead of coalescing both uses into `addu s5,v1,a0`. The same body then parked ONE instruction short (93.64%, 344 vs retail's 348) because retail has the `i++` in the beqz delay slot after a call while reorg target-fills the loop test there; that residual is not reachable from source, so park it with the number.
- id: d-live-value-costs-nothing | keywords: move, copy, s32, addiu, addu, li, loop, lw
  **A live-in value that costs nothing is a PARAMETER** (round 335): retail's `lw v0,sym / addu a1,v0,zero / addiu v1,a1,1` copy appears when the local is LIVE AT THE LOAD, and the free spelling is that the value IS one of the function's parameters (the caller already cleared that register). A local initialised to -1 gives the same loop but costs `li a1,-1` (404 vs retail's 400 bytes). system/archive func_8002B8B0 matched at 100.00 as `f(s32 param0, s32 nQueueIndex)`.
  Round 418 counter-measurement in the same unit, for the case where the index has to SURVIVE A CALL: func_8002B5D0/func_8002B2F0 want retail's `move s2,v0 / addiu v1,s2,1` in a scan loop whose index is live across `CdGetSector`. Making it the second parameter produces the copy in the right order but MIRRORS the callee-saved pair (the index takes `$s1`, the in-loop pointer `$s2`, retail has the opposite) and grows the prologue by one `sw` - 96.71% / 740 bytes / 185 insns against the local's 97.47 / retail's exact 736. So the trick pays when the parameter's register is the one retail uses (a caller-saved `$aN`); when the variable is callee-saved, its cold pseudo at function entry wins the FIRST free saved register and every other pointer in the function shifts.
- id: d-sltiu-copy-idiom-retail | keywords: move, copy, sltiu, u8, addu, delay, s32
  THE SLTIU-COPY IDIOM: when retail does 'sltiu v0,<x>,1' then 'addu t0,v0,zero' in the 'j' delay slot instead of 'sltiu t0,<x>,1', the boolean local must be u8, not u32/s32 - a u8 return makes gcc compute the compare into v0 and copy it into the return register (two functions first try in battle/misc12 after the u32 versions sat at 95.5%).
- id: d-leftover-a1-a2-jal | keywords: move, copy, delay, jal
  A leftover `$a1`/`$a2` at a `jal` usually means the source passes a COMPUTED value there and the parked C replaced it with a literal: check every call site's delay slot before blaming register allocation (round 47, battling/misc10 func_80084B48: 95.98 -> 100%).
- id: d-two-0xff-immediates-cse | keywords: move, copy, cse, s32
  Two 0xFF immediates are CSE'd into one register unless they differ in mode: give one of them an 's32 v = 0xFF;' local.
- id: d-clamp-copy-shape-round | keywords: move, copy, slti, u8, addu, s32
  THE CLAMP-COPY SHAPE (round 35, took two stubs from 93.3/94.5 to 100.00 first try): when retail COPIES the result to a second register before the compare ('addu v1,v0,zero; slti v1,v1,0x100'), it had a separate narrow variable - write 's32 value = <sum>; u8 result = value; if (value > 0xFF) result = 0xFF; pTbl[k] = result;'. A single variable gives a test-in-place; the 'u8' copy pseudo is what reproduces retail's extra move. Try this before calling any 'retail copies X to $vN before bgez/slti' diff an allocator tie.
- id: d-second-walker-must-be | keywords: move, copy, pointer, loop, param, regalloc, twin
  **A SECOND WALKER must be a local initialised at ENTRY from the parameter, and the first loop walks the PARAMETER** (round 389, battle/misc21 func_8009F1C4 96.45 -> 100.00). Retail keeps two copies of the array base across the whole function (`move s3,a0` for the first loop's walker, `move s6,s3` for the copy the LAST loop restarts from); writing `pSprite = pSprites;` as a re-assignment before the last loop instead of `BattleSprite* pSprite = pSprites;` at the top costs an extra `move` at that point, puts the wrong copy in `$s6` and permutes every register in the function (249 vs 251 insns, 94.26). Read the twin's own source for which name walks which loop: src/battle/main/misc21's matched neighbour BattleUpdateSpriteTransforms has the same pair.
- id: d-one-instruction-short-park | keywords: move, copy, loop, lhu, u16, volatile, lbu, lui
  AN "ONE INSTRUCTION SHORT" PARK IS A MISSING LOAD, NOT AN ALLOCATOR PROBLEM (round 299, battle/misc15 func_8008ADD0: 98.54 percent at 820 bytes against retail's 824 - it could never link). The missing instruction was a reload: retail re-forms lui %hi + lhu %lo(sym) on EVERY loop iteration while any spelling that also keeps the symbol's address in a register reads through the saved register. What restores it is *(volatile u16 *)&g_Sym inside the loop body, and the saved register the same change frees comes from new_var = &g_Sym; placed BEFORE the branch with pMask = new_var; at the use. That body is now 99.90 percent at retail's exact 824 bytes. So when you are 4 bytes short, look for the load retail has that you do not - a lbu/lhu/lw of a global inside a loop is the usual one - and try the volatile-u16 read before anything else.

- id: d-loop-bottom-accumulator-copy | keywords: move, copy, loop, or, delay, coalesce, park
  **An accumulator update at a loop bottom whose retail body copies THROUGH A TEMP is not reachable by spelling: cc1 coalesces the two live-out variables into one register** (round 392, battle/main/misc10 func_8007F8C0, parked 99.30% at 684 bytes against retail's 688, one instruction short and so never linkable). Retail's tail is `or v1,s3,s0` / `move s3,v1` (in the beqz delay slot) / `move s0,s3` / `andi v0,s0,0xff`, i.e. the OR lands in a scratch that is copied to the accumulator, and the accumulator then to the returned variable; every source shape that writes `next = acc | ret; acc = next; ret = acc;` compiles to `or s0,s3,s0` / `move s3,s0` because acc and ret hold equal values and gcc gives them one register. Measured dead ends: the copies after the loop instead of inside it (93.49, `or s3,s3,s0` in the beqz slot, 684), `ret = next` with the exit reading the other variable (99.30, byte-identical to the coalesced body), chained assignment, u8 opcode local, for(;;)+break, two inline returns, and three permuter runs from the 99.30 body (1479/1225/995 iterations, all RESULT PERMUTER_NONE). Round 405 adds two more: the temp kept in the loop with the copy moved BELOW it (`next = acc | ret; acc = next;` then `ret = acc;` after the loop) is 93.49% / 684 bytes - cc1 folds next into acc (`or s3,s3,s0`) AND folds the exit copy into the return (`andi v0,s3,0xff`), losing two copies; and a fourth permuter run from the 99.30 body (1502 iterations, base=111 best=111, PERMUTER_NONE). Preset-independent: 99.3 under every 2.7.2 -G4/-G8 combination, 94.59 under 2.7.2-cdk -O2.  Round 419 improves the park to **99.80% at retail's exact 688 bytes / 172 insns** (was 99.30 / 684, one short): the two loop-bottom copies DO come back once the temp is LIVE AT A MERGE - `if (!(cont & 0xFF)) goto out;` ... `next = ret; next = acc | next; acc = next;` ... `ret = next;` `out:` `return ret & 0xFF;` - and only `char ret` (or `u8 ret`) keeps cc1 from folding it, which is also what buys retail's schedule (the OR stays after the `lw`, reorg fills the beqz slot from the exit block). Residual then is 3 rows of one cause: the OR's second operand is the zero-extended copy of `ret` in a scratch (`or v1,v1,s3`, exit `move s0,v1`, delay-slot andi in v1) instead of ret's own register (`or v1,s3,s0`, `move s0,s3`). A plain `s32 ret` with the same goto merge keeps the temp but reorg steals the OR into the beqz delay slot (99.30 / 684). Do not re-brief this residual as a hand job. Round 431 measured the shape that drops the shared label entirely - `if (!(cont & 0xFF)) return ret & 0xFF;` inside the loop plus `return ret & 0xFF;` after it - and it DOES give retail's exit-block `andi` in the cont beqz delay slot with the OR after the `lw`, so that half of the residual is reachable and the label is not needed: `char ret` 99.16 / 684, `s32 ret` 99.30 / 684 (there the OR is raw, `or v1,s3,s0` exactly as retail, and the missing instruction is the folded acc/ret pair: `or s0,s3,s0` + `move s3,s0`), `next = acc|ret / acc = next / ret = next` with the temp 96.95 / 684 (reorg moves the OR into the delay slot and sinks the early `andi` to the shared exit). An empty `do { } while (0);` after case 0x99's `cont = 1` on the two-return body measures identical to 96.95 / 684, so the c-an-empty-do-while-in-a-case barrier does not shift reorg in a 28-case dispatcher; a sixth permuter run from the 99.80 body (1773 iterations, base 21 best 21, 3 minutes) finds nothing.
- id: d-shift-through-a-temp-read-after-the-loop | keywords: move, copy, sll, shift, accumulator, loop, temp, live-out
  **A LOOP-BOTTOM `acc = acc * 2` THAT RETAIL EMITS AS `sll a1,s0,1` + `move s0,a1` MATCHES WHEN THE DOUBLED VALUE GOES THROUGH A TEMP THAT THE CODE AFTER THE LOOP READS**: write `next = acc * 2; acc = next;` in the body and read `next` after the loop (round 458, battle/main/misc9_260 func_8007E334 95.31 -> 100.00% / 260 bytes and func_8007E554 89.08 -> 100.00% / 288 bytes, both at retail's exact instruction and byte count, gcc-2.6.0 XenoBattle260). The temp stays a separate pseudo because it is LIVE OUT of the loop, so cc1 cannot coalesce it into the loop-carried accumulator; retail then keeps the shift result in a caller-saved register with the `move s0,a1` back-edge copy, and reorg duplicates the one shift into all three branches' delay slots. `acc *= 2`, `acc <<= 1`, `acc = acc * 2`, and a temp whose value the tail does NOT read all coalesce to an in-place `sll s0,s0,1` and stay one instruction short. Two companion spellings measured in the same unit: `pRow = g_BattleSlotWordRegs[arg1]; pRow[operand1] = next << 2;` gives retail's tail order (`andi/sll/lw/lui/addiu/lbu/addu/.../sh`) where the inline array-index form hoists the symbol address, and `s32 i = 0xA;` + `for (; i >= 3; i--)` puts the counter's `li s0,0xa` in retail's prologue slot where `for (i = 0xA; ...)` emits it two instructions later (94.11% before, 100.00% after, that difference being only the save/initialise order). Round 459 closed the THIRD member of the family, battle/main/misc9_260 func_8007E438 (94.01 -> 100.00% / 284 bytes), and it measures the two boundaries of this lever. (1) Its retail body is the IN-PLACE `sll s1,s1,1` (one shift at the join, no `move` back), so the temp spelling of the two functions above is WRONG here and `acc <<= 1;` is exact - read the loop tail's shift/`move` pair in the `.s` before porting a sibling's doubling. (2) The tail there is `andi v0,s1,0xffff` / `srl v0,v0,1`, i.e. `acc >> 1` on a `u16 acc`; `(u16)acc >> 1` on an `s32 acc` folds the mask into the shift and emits `andi v0,s1,0xfffe` instead, 94.01% with the body otherwise exact. The narrow accumulator also leaves the loop's `acc |= 1` as a plain `ori s1,s1,1` (no mask per update) because the high bits are don't-care until that read-back, so `u16 acc` is the honest declaration - a `u16` accumulator is not readable from the loop body, only from the final truncation.
- id: d-select-two-assignments-if-else | keywords: move, copy, j, bgez, diamond, select, ternary, branch
  **A CLAMP-TO-ZERO SELECT WHOSE RETAIL ARM IS `j merge` IS AN IF/ELSE WITH TWO ASSIGNMENTS, NOT A TERNARY, AND NOT A `y = 0;` HOIST.** (round 394, slus_006.64/system/temp2 func_800273C4 - parked at 99.02%, 12 bytes / 3 instructions short, for two rounds; the if/else closes it to 100.00 at retail's exact 1332 bytes / 333 instructions). Retail's diamond is `lh v0,0x22(sp); nop; bgez v0,Lelse; move v1,v0; [then] move a0,zero; j Lmerge; [Lelse] move a0,v1; Lmerge: sll v0,a0,16; sra v0,v0,16` - branch on the negated condition, the value SPECULATED into that branch's delay slot, two separate assignments to the same destination, and a `j` over the taken arm. Writing `y = (proj2.vy < 0) ? 0 : proj2.vy;` gives a REGISTER-ONLY select (`bgez; move a0,v0; move v0,zero; move a0,v0`) with no `j` and drops the destination's stack slot; and the park's original `y = 0; if (cond) { ...; y = proj2.vy; } if (!cond) y = 0;` gives the right `sll/sra` narrowing but a second `lhu` reload and no `j`. What produces all three of retail's instructions is `if (proj2.vy < 0) { y = 0; } else { y = proj2.vy; }` - both arms assign, so cc1 has to materialise two blocks and join them. The `sll/sra` pair that follows is just the destination being `s16` at its single use, so do not chase that separately. Measured only under gcc-2.6.0-psx (the preset that function's tail needs); the 2.7.2-cdk spellings of the same three shapes were not re-measured. Round 454 applies it to a second function in that unit, system/temp2_r1 func_800278F8 (parked 74.87 -> 75.62%, 265 -> 267 insns against retail's 274): converting its rows diamond (`if (top < 0 || top > unk32C+0xF0) { rows = 0; rowStart = 0; } else { rows = (unk32C << 8) / (span + 0x100); rowStart = 0; }`, the divisor limit written twice in both arms) reproduces retail's `j` over the taken arm with `move t0,zero` in its delay slot and the `mflo v0 / nop / move t2,v0` copy. COUNTER-MEASUREMENT: applying the same if/else to a SECOND diamond in the same function (the `col = remainder` sign fixup, 8 instructions earlier) restores none of it and MIRRORS the function's callee-saved pair (col/pPrim swap $s3/$s4, 74.36%): one diamond per function, on the one whose retail arm carries the `j`.
Round 493 CORRECTS the func_800278F8 half of that paragraph: the if/else with BOTH arms assigning `rowStart` is one instruction short (270 insns / 1076 bytes), and retail's `mflo v0 / nop / move t2,v0 / move t0,zero` comes from writing `rowStart = 0` ONCE AFTER the if/else (`if (top < 0 || top > unk32C+0xF0) { rows = 0; } else { rows = (unk32C << 8) / (span + 0x100); }` then `rowStart = 0;`): jump optimisation duplicates the single store into both arms - giving retail's two `move t0,zero`, one in the `j` delay slot and one after the quotient copy - and only then does the else arm end with the mips1 mflo hazard `nop` instead of the scheduler filling that slot with `move t0,zero`. 87.77% / 1084 bytes / 271 insns at that point. Companion on the same body: `u16 rows` (not `s32`) is what keeps the quotient in `$v0` and copies it to `$t2` - with an s32 local cc1 coalesces them into `mflo t2` and retail's move disappears. So read a duplicated store's ARMS before choosing the if/else shape: a copy in each arm plus a `j` can be ONE statement written after the diamond, and the difference is not visible in the source shape alone.

- id: d-crossjump-tail-merge-stops | keywords: move, extra, cross-jump, tail-merge, duplicate, argument, block, order
  **A TAIL DUPLICATED IN BOTH ARMS OF AN IF/ELSE-IF IS WHAT PRODUCES RETAIL'S OUT-OF-LINE SHARED BLOCK, BUT gcc's CROSS-JUMP ONLY MERGES THE SUFFIX THE SCHEDULER PLACED AT THE SAME DISTANCE FROM THE END IN BOTH COPIES, so a call's argument setup that sched2 hoisted in one arm stays behind as a second copy** (round 397, battling/main/misc8 func_80080C48, parked 95.60% at 204 bytes against retail's 200 - 2 instructions, so it cannot link). Retail's block order is `[test1][arm A][j tail][test2][arm B][tail][else]` with the tail reached by fall-through from B and by a `j` (plain `nop` slot) from A; writing the 8-statement tail ONCE after the chain puts the else before it instead (79.80%, that is RTL emission order, no block reordering in 2.7.2). Duplicating the tail in both arms reproduces retail's block order exactly - the merged block sits where the second copy was - and the only residual is its first instruction: retail's merged block begins with `addu a0,zero,zero` (the BattleSetScreenMode argument, reorg then drops it into the jal slot) and arm A only has `j`+`nop`, while ours carries `move a0,zero` in A's j slot and hoisted the same move above the store in B, so cross-jump merges from the jal onward and the setup is emitted twice. Measured dead ends on that exact body: tail written once with the else returning first 79.80, a local variable for the argument, else with and without `return`, a 3-minute permuter run (base=221 best=221 - the merge boundary is not reachable by source edits), -O3 0.0, 2.7.2-cdk 85.36.
- id: d-crossjump-survivor-is-the-last | keywords: cross-jump, tail, duplicate, block, order, merge, arm, park
  **gcc 2.6.0's CROSS-JUMP MERGE TARGET IS THE FUNCTION'S LAST BLOCK WITH THAT SUFFIX, so a tail written in every arm merges into the arm the front end emitted last; retail that instead shows a STANDALONE shared tail (two arms merged into a block placed where the second arm's copy was, a third arm keeping its own) was not reachable from six source shapes** (round 403, lib_gear/main/main func_801E5CD8, parked 71.67% at 88 bytes against retail's 108, 22 insns of 27). Retail is `[test0 bnez][arm 0][test1 beq arm1][test2 bne exit][arm 2][shared tail: lhu/sll, reached by arm 0's j and arm 2's fall-through][arm 1, its own full lw/lw/lhu/sll copy][jr ra]`, with a `nop` in the `bnez` delay slot; every spelling merged arms 0 and 2 into arm 1's copy instead (5 insns short) and put the next test's `li v0,1` in the `bnez` slot. Measured, all 88 bytes unless noted: three separate `return`s in an 0,1,2 `if` chain 61.93; one local + one return in 0,2,1 order 64.59; `if (type != 0) {nested} else {...}` 0.00 at 96 (arm 0 ends up last behind a `beqz`); the nested 0,1,2 form 54.41 at 96; `if (t == 0) A; else if (t != 1) {...} else B` 71.67 - the only shape that reproduces retail's test ORDER and POLARITY (`beq` for type==1, `bne` for type==2, arm 1 emitted last), and what the residual is measured on; duplicating the tail into each arm as well 71.67. A `switch` on the parameter was 19.74. Identical under gcc-2.7.2-cdk, so the split is not a preset. Round 415 re-measured the other direction with `cc1_probe.sh` - trying to make arm 1's tail rtx-DIFFERENT so jump.c would leave it alone: `& 0xFFFF` on the loaded field, `* 0x10000`, `(x << 8) << 8`, a `u32 id = pTexture->unk14; return id << 16;` local, a `u16* pId = &pTexture->unk14; return *pId << 16;` alias, and a `goto` label placed INSIDE arm 2's then-body that arm 0 jumps to (with and without a separate `goto arm1`). All seven compile to the same 20 insns / one merged tail with the survivor at arm 1's copy: cse2 and combine fold every spelling before the cross-jump runs, so the second copy cannot be spelled from source and this stub is BLOCKED at 71.67 - do not reopen it without a new compiler.
- id: d-a-shared-tail-store-needs-both-threads-identical | keywords: cross-jump, tail, store, delay-slot, duplicate, j, fall-through, arms
  **jump.c WILL NOT CROSS-JUMP A STORE FROM ONE ARM ONTO THE OTHER ARM'S COPY WHEN THE TWO THREADS END DIFFERENTLY (one arm jumps to the epilogue, the other falls into it), AND ADDING `return;` TO BOTH ARMS TO MAKE THEM SYMMETRIC IS CANONICALISED AWAY BEFORE jump.c RUNS** (round 450, field/main/misc10 func_8009635C, parked 96.70% at retail's exact 176 bytes / 44 insns, Default preset, every register retail's: nItemId `$s1`, nIndex `$s0`, pIds `$s2`, the `-1` `$s3`, pQuantities `$s4`, byte `$a0`, address `$v1`, value `$v0`). Retail ends `beqz` (>= 99 -> epilogue, `nop` in the slot) / `j` to the `sb` that closes the else arm (`addiu v0,a0,1` in the slot): ONE store, reached by the jump and by the else arm's fall-through. Every body emits the store in the `j` delay slot and jumps past the shared block instead (three `sb` against retail's two, paid for by retail's nop), i.e. reorg copies it because the target block has no second label use. Measured on the same body: two `pQuantities[nIndex]` stores (96.70), both arms storing `pQuantity[0]` (96.59, pIds/pQuantities mirror), both arms storing a shared `nQuantity` (86.70 - value and address roles flip: address `$a0`, value `$v1`), the same plus `return;` at the end of both arms (byte-identical to 86.70), the pointer assigned before vs after the ids store (byte-identical), one store after the join (90.41, 92.16 with a pointer local). Presets: 2.6.0 96.93, cdk 96.70, -O3 does not compile. Companion, useful on its own: **a `u_char *p = &p[i]` POINTER LOCAL is what fixes a mirrored callee-saved pair here** - the subscript form puts nItemId in `$s0`/nIndex in `$s1`, the pointer form gives retail's `$s1`/`$s0` - so try the address-into-a-pointer spelling before the allocator levers on a two-arm byte writer.
- id: d-combine-folds-mask-eq-zero | keywords: move, copy, andi, sltiu, combine, bit-test, block, delay, mask
  **gcc 2.6.0's COMBINE FOLDS `(x & K) == 0` INTO `srl/xori/andi` ONLY WHEN THE ANDI AND THE COMPARE SHARE A BASIC BLOCK - put the mask in the PRE-BRANCH block and retail's `andi/sltiu/move` shape comes back** (round 397, menu/main/misc9 func_801DCE60, parked 97.64%: the plain `if (flags & 0x4000) row = 2; else row = (flags & 0x1000) == 0;` folds the else to `srl v1,12; xori; andi` where retail has `andi v0,v1,0x1000` IN THE beqz DELAY SLOT, then `sltiu v0,v0,1; move v1,v0`). Two spellings defeat the fold: `masked = flags & 0x1000;` as a statement BEFORE the `if` (blocks the combine, 96.69% - but the andi then precedes the condition's andi, so reorg fills the delay slot with the else's one remaining sltiu and the branch INVERTS, 480 insns), and the one that reproduces retail's whole shape at 97.28%: `cond = flags & 0x4000; masked = flags & 0x1000;` (both u_int statements, in that order) then `if (cond) row = 2; else row = masked == 0;` - the mask is the LAST insn before the branch, so reorg hoists the `andi 0x1000` into the beqz delay slot exactly like retail, and the sltiu stays in the else block. Residual there: ours loads flags into $v0 and cond into $v1 (retail: flags $v1, cond+masked $v0) and lacks the `move v1,v0` (a `tmp = masked == 0; row = tmp;` split is UNTRIED). u16 cond/masked reorder the andis and invert the branch again (96.69%). Preset ruled out: 2.7.2 96.93, cdk compile-fails, -G0/-O3 no change.
  Round 424 closed the fold with a spelling that also KEEPS every register retail has, found by permuter (base 1605 -> 1112) and confirmed by hand: compare against the destination variable itself - `row = 1; row = (flags & 0x1000) < row;` (same value, `row = (flags & 0x1000) == 0`). The compare's operand is now a variable, so combine cannot turn the AND into a shift; retail's `andi 0x1000` lands IN the beqz delay slot and the else keeps a lone `sltiu v0,v0,1` - 97.81% at 1924 bytes / 481 insns against retail's 1928 / 482, i.e. everything is retail's except the `move v1,v0` (retail keeps the compare result in `$v0` and copies it into row's `$v1`; ours coalesces them, and the same body then wants `$s1/$s2/$s0` where retail has `$s0/$s1/$s2` in the two call setups). Measured on the same block and dead: `< 1` for `== 0` (folds identically, 97.66 at retail's exact 482/1928), `!(...)`, a u_char/u_int boolean temp assigned then copied to row (the truncation of a proven-0/1 value is deleted, 97.81/97.52), and `row` declared u8 (483 insns). So on this shape: block the fold with a self-referential compare, then count the missing instruction - if it is the boolean copy, the park is one allocator tie from a match.

- id: d-nested-else-keeps-a-case-copy | keywords: duplicate, store, cross-jump, merge, nested, else, arm, polarity
  **ONE DUPLICATED `x = 0` IN A SWITCH ARM SURVIVES retail's CROSS-JUMP ONLY WHEN THE ARM IS SPELLED AS `if (A) { if (B) S; } else { S; }` - the test's POLARITY, not the statement set, is the load-bearing part** (round 404, menu/main/misc9 func_801DC3D8, 99.81 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 2696 bytes / 674 insns, gcc-2.6.0/XenoMenu260). The residue was 3 instructions in one spot: retail's case-0 shade test is `bnez v0,<shared test> / nop / j <join> / move s2,zero` (its OWN copy of the store, in the `j` delay slot) and every other spelling gives `beqz v0,<shared store> / nop / j <shared test> / nop` - same insn count, one store block merged instead of kept. Measured on the same body, all 99.81 / 674 insns: `if (mask == 0 || available < value) S;`, `if (mask == 0) { S; break; } if (available < value) S;` (two statements, so cross-jump merges both copies), `if (mask == 0) { S; } else if (available < value) { S; }`, AND the mirror `if (mask == 0) { S; } else { if (available < value) { S; } }`. What matched is the negated test with the nested second test in its TRUE arm and the plain store as the else: `if (mask != 0) { if (available < value) { shade = 0; } } else { shade = 0; }` - the same shape retail's `bnez` shows. So when a diff's only residue is "retail keeps a second copy of one store, ours merged it", write the arm so the branch retail's `bnez`/`beqz` implies is the one holding the nested test; equal-statement spellings are not equal.
- id: a-duplicated-guard-load-and-a | keywords: cross-jump, duplicate, copy, if-else, ternary, jal, arm, g_menu
  **A TERNARY FED TO A CALL AS "TWO FULL IDENTICAL CALLS IN AN if/else" IS CROSS-JUMPED BY gcc 2.6.0 INTO ONE jal, AND THAT IS what PUTS THE GUARD'S GLOBAL LOAD IN BOTH ARMS** (round 400, menu/main/misc4_260 func_801CF8D8, 79.94 -> 91.32 at 612 of retail's 620 bytes). Retail shows ONE `jal`, yet loads `lui/lw g_Menu` + `lw a2,0x32C(v0)` in BOTH arms of the index test, stores one stack arg in both arms, sets `li a1,0x115` in the `beqz` delay slot and merges the shared tail at the arm's own `j`. Every single-call spelling (`cond ? A : B` as one argument) hoists that load and the whole prologue into one block, 4-5 instructions short - no amount of type or order tweaking recovers it. Writing the if/else around two complete, identical calls (only the differing argument changes) reproduces it in one edit. Try this on any diff where retail has one `jal` for two near-identical call sites; the residual after it is then a pure allocator tie.
- id: d-entry-param-copy-survives | keywords: move, copy, parameter, entry, prologue, copy-propagation, reassign
  **A `move <arg-reg>,<param-reg>` AT ENTRY (retail copies a parameter out and then reuses the parameter's own register for a value derived from it, `sll a1,a1,16 / sra / addiu` IN PLACE) IS PRODUCED BY A LOCAL INITIALISED FROM THE PARAMETER THAT IS REASSIGNED IN A LATER ARM - and only then, because the reassignment is what stops copy-propagation coalescing the two.** (round 400, slus_006.64/system/animation_scripts func_800223B0, parked 74.09% at 668 bytes / 167 insns against retail's 688 / 172). Writing `s32 index = animId;` at the top and letting cases 1/2 overwrite `index` with the group index gives the entry copy (`move a0,a1`, 74.09%); a named parity local `s32 parity = ((s16)animId + 0x400) & 1` is worth the same +0.55 over the inline test (73.54 -> 74.09, same 668 bytes); but writing the case-1/2 casts off `index` instead of `animId` makes the copy's initial value dead on those paths, gcc coalesces it away and the copy disappears entirely (73.54%, 664 bytes). Which register the copy takes is then not source-controllable on that body: declaration order moved it between `$a0` and `$a2` (both 74.09) and never to retail's `$a3`, so the arms' temporaries all shift and the park is 5 `move`s short - park that residual, do not permute it.

- id: d-sign-known-ternary-folds | keywords: abs, negu, move, ternary, bgez, fold, builtin, instruction
  **AN ABS WRITTEN AS A TERNARY INSIDE AN ARM THAT ALREADY ESTABLISHED THE SIGN FOLDS TO A BARE `negu` AND DROPS RETAIL'S `addu v1,s1,zero`, LEAVING THE BODY ONE INSTRUCTION SHORT; `__builtin_abs(x)` KEEPS THE PAIR** (round 404, battling/main/misc3 func_80076884, 97.34 -> 99.43 at retail's exact 1972 bytes / 491 instructions). Retail's analog-stick clamp is the two-step `bgez s1,L` / `addu v1,s1,zero` (delay slot) / `negu v1,v1`; inside `if (stickY2 < 0 && enabled)` cc1 knows the sign, so `limit = stickY2 < 0 ? -stickY2 : stickY2;` compiles to the single `negu v1,s1` and the function cannot link even at 99.x. The extra `negative = stickY2 < 0;` local *does* defeat the range knowledge (bgez/addu/negu) but raises the register pressure enough to flip two other variables (+8 bytes), and applying it to both clamp arms lands 8 bytes over. `limit = __builtin_abs(stickY2);` is the same source-level intent, compiles the two-step form, and costs nothing elsewhere - so any abs whose retail body has a `bgez` plus a move-plus-negu pair wants the builtin, not the ternary.

- id: d-an-abs-needs-one-local-per-site | keywords: abs, builtin, negu, move, bgez, local, per-site, coalesce
  **A REPEATED `__builtin_abs` PATTERN NEEDS ONE ABS LOCAL PER SITE, NOT ONE SHARED ONE: the wins are nested** (round 405, world_map/main/misc12 func_80090FB4, 98.03 -> 98.52 with `__builtin_abs` and 98.52 -> 98.71 with a second local, retail's exact 1148 bytes / 287 insns all the way). Retail shows `bgez v0,L / move a1,v0 / negu a1,a1 / L: slt v0,a1,t0` in two different ramp blocks, and cc1 gives that pair ONLY for `__builtin_abs(x)` - the ternaries and if/else spellings of the same abs are coalesced to one pseudo before allocation (a `-dc` dump of the unit shows `(reg 87) = 107 - 82` then `(reg 87) = -(reg 87)`), so reorg target-fills the bgez slot with a duplicate `slt` and the body is one instruction short. With `nAbs = __builtin_abs(nDelta);` shared by both blocks the two sites get the SAME register (`v1` twice) where retail uses `a1` then `a0`; splitting it into `nAbs` and `nAbsVel` gives `a1` then `a0` and makes the second ramp block instruction-identical. Measured dead ends on the same body: `if (d >= 0) { a = d; } else { a = -d; }` DOES keep a copy (`bgez / move rd,rs / negu rd,rs`, the right shape) but costs 5 instructions elsewhere (95.78%, 292 insns), and an if/else of either polarity without the builtin, `u32 nPad`, reading the pad global inline at all five tests, and block-scoped locals all leave the residual register rotation alone.
- id: d-builtin-abs-shape-but-one-shot-short | keywords: abs, builtin, negu, move, bgez, scheduling, rotated, short
  **`__builtin_abs` DOES buy retail's `bgez rd,Rn` / `move Rw,Rn` / `negu Rw,Rw` shape, but on a scheduled cdk unit it also moves the `sll` of an unrelated constant past the `bgez` and leaves the body one instruction short - so an abs-shaped residual can be right in shape and still unlinkable** (round 419, battle/main/misc28 func_800B65B0, XenoBattleTailCdk0, re-parked once measured). Retail's two angle-clamp blocks are `sll a1,v0,0x2 / bgez v1,L / move v0,v1 / negu v0,v0 / slt v0,a1,v0`; the do-while magnitude body that matches the 600 bytes / 150 insns gives `move v0,v1 / negu v0,v1` (negate of the SOURCE), and `mag = __builtin_abs(delta);` gives retail's pair but 596 bytes / 149 insns with rate's `sll` after the branch, scored 95.50. Per-site locals (`deltaY/deltaZ/magY/magZ/turnY/turnZ`) with the builtin: 604 / 151 and both abs shapes right, but rate takes `$a0` where retail has `$a1` and sched1 inserts two load nops. Plain `turn = delta; mag = delta;` in both blocks: 604 / 151 (one pseudo for both blocks' delta gets copied twice). Read this as: the builtin is the right spelling for the SHAPE and the wrong one for the SIZE whenever the unit has `-fschedule-insns`.
- id: d-value-both-arms-compute | keywords: move, copy, join, if-else, phi, temp, shared, sized
  **A VALUE BOTH ARMS OF AN IF/ELSE COMPUTE BECOMES ONE COPY AT THE JOIN ONLY WHEN IT GOES THROUGH A WIDER TEMP: give a `u16` local an `s32` temp that both arms assign and one `local = temp;` after the if/else** (round 405, battle/main/misc25 func_800B026C, 2124 -> retail's exact 2120 bytes / 530 insns, parked 95.81%). Retail's first actor/table block computes `y` per arm (`subu` in the jal delay slot on one path, late on the other) yet copies it ONCE at the merge (`addu s2,v1,zero` at 0xF8); assigning the `u16 y` directly in both arms makes cc1 emit one copy in EACH arm, exactly 4 bytes too many. With `s32 dy;` assigned in both arms and `y = dy;` after the if/else the copies collapse to retail's single join copy and the size is exact. Both operands need their `(u16)` casts or the loads come out `lh` where retail has `lhu`. The same body's remaining residual is the callee-saved rotation, which is a wall: `-dg`/`-dl` show the block pointer at 75 refs over 276 insns against 48/160, 39/135 and 48/180 for the three `u16` components, so it takes `$s1` where retail has `$s5` and no spelling moves it.

- id: a-register-arg-constant-la-is-deferred | keywords: la, move, constant, argument, expand, call, placement, park
  **A REGISTER-PASSED CONSTANT ARGUMENT'S `la` IS EMITTED IN load_register_parameters, i.e. AFTER every memory argument's load - so retail materialising the address FIRST means that argument was not a compile-time constant, and no single-use local can say so** (round 408, movie/main/misc1 func_800704E8, parked 99.04% and then 99.28% at retail's exact 2276 bytes / 569 insns once the preheader `li` was fixed - see g-front-end-statement-places-a-preheader; residual below is the `la` row plus that trade). The function has eighteen `FontPrintf(fmt, ...)` calls whose `la a0,fmt` sits LAST among the argument loads in both retail and our build; at one site retail has it FIRST and ours last (`lui a0,%hi(D_8006FC40)/addiu` before `lw a1..a3` instead of after). Reading cc1's own output (`build/src/<unit>.c.s`) shows ours is `lw $5/$6/$7/$2` then `la $4`, and `la $4` first at the one call retail agrees with; the mechanism is that expand_expr emits nothing for a SYMBOL_REF argument, so the move surfaces late, while a non-constant argument is materialised at its own statement - which is where retail's early `la` sits. A single-use pointer local is folded back into the constant (measured twice, 99.04 and identical rows), so the only surviving route is to make the argument a real value, which changes the instruction count. Two more negatives on the same body: moving `pCounters = ...; pBase = ...;` from before the loop into the loop's first two statements is hoisted straight back to the identical preheader slot (cc1 emits `la s4 / move s2 / li s3` either way), and declaring those two locals first changes nothing - Round 423 closed it with `cc1_probe.sh` on a standalone copy of that block: six spellings of the
call (bare symbol, `char* pFormat = D_8006FC40;` as the block's first statement, a `(char*)` cast,
`&D_8006FC40[0]`, `D_8006FC40 + 0`, and the pointer assigned ABOVE the branch) emit
`lw a1 / lw a2 / lw a3 / lw v0 / la a0` under BOTH gcc-2.6.0 and gcc-2.7.2; the only spelling that
hoists the `la` is the pre-branch assignment, which puts it above the `slt`/`beqz` instead of
inside the block - so retail's in-block la-first order is unreachable from any call spelling, while
the preheader `li sN,K` at that function did move (see g-front-end-statement-places-a-preheader),
so a preheader whose hoisted `li` sits LAST where retail has it FIRST is a front-end-statement
question first, and only then the same class: park after reading the cc1 .s rather than permuting (a 4-minute run from this identical body: base 460 = best 460, because the reloc-name rows dominate its score).

- id: a-statement-between-the-test-and-the-call-reorders-the-format-argument | keywords: la, argument, call, constant, placement, statement, order, block
  **A CONSTANT-ADDRESS ARGUMENT'S `la` IS EMITTED FIRST, NOT LAST, WHEN THE CALL IS THE FIRST STATEMENT OF ITS BLOCK - so a retail `la a0,fmt` above the other argument loads means a statement that used to sit between the `if` test and the call has to move INSIDE the block after it, and the previous entry's "unreachable from any call spelling" was really a statement-position problem** (round 436, movie/main/misc1 func_800704E8, 99.28 -> 99.66 -> 100.00 with `check_bin.sh movie` OK at retail's exact 2276 bytes / 569 insns, XenoBattle260Div = gcc-2.6.0). Retail's stream-status `FontPrintf(D_8006FC40, g_MovieDebugCounters, g_MovieStreamBlock, g_MovieStreamWritePtr, g_MovieStreamBytesLeft)` emits `lui/addiu a0` before `lw a1..a3`, and every body with `i = 0;` immediately before the `if (g_MovieStreamCommand >= 0xB || ...)` puts it after them; moving that one statement to the top of the if-body (its value cannot be observed before the loop below it) puts the `la` first and is worth the row, with `move s0,zero`/`addu s0,zero,zero` no longer in the `beqz` delay slot. Six call spellings (bare symbol, pointer local, cast, `&arr[0]`, `+ 0`, pre-branch assignment) measured identical before that, so when a diff shows one `la` of a constant argument in the wrong slot, look at the STATEMENTS AROUND the call before the call's own spelling.

- id: b-assignment-used-as-the-while | keywords: move, copy, delay, while, condition, loop, mask, reload
  **A `move sN,v0` IN THE BRANCH DELAY SLOT BEFORE A LOOP BODY MEANS THE VALUE IS THE `while` CONDITION'S OWN ASSIGNMENT (`while ((x = expr) != 0)`): cc1 tests the temp and copies it into `x`'s home register in the delay slot, where a separate `x = expr;` statement assigns straight into the home register and leaves a `nop`** (round 415, slus_006.64/psyq/libetc/intr trapIntr, 96.06 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 488 bytes / 122 insns, PSY-Q preset). Retail re-reads `enabledInterruptsMask` at BOTH copies of the condition (`and v1,v1,a0` / `and v0,v0,v1` / `beqz v0` / `move s0,v0` at the entry and again at the loop bottom, rotating the loop over the body), which a hoisted `mask = enabled & ...;` before the loop cannot produce: the load has to be inside the condition so it reappears per iteration. Spelling it `mask = enabled & *g_pI_STAT; inInterrupt = 1; mask &= *g_pI_MASK; while (mask) { body; mask = ...; }` scores 96.06 with the SAME 122 insns and frame, differing only in the missing delay-slot copy and which register the final `and` lands in - so when a park's residual is exactly "one move in the delay slot plus a mirrored `and` operand", check whether the source's loop condition recomputes the value instead of a statement before the loop.

- id: d-copy-then-mask-in-place-is-a-combine-miss | keywords: move, copy, andi, mask, store, combine, park, one-short
