  **AN `sll r,r,0x10` / `sra r,r,0xf` PAIR SCALING AN ARRAY INDEX IS `2 * (s16)x` AND PROVES THE INDEX'S SIGNED 16-BIT RANGE WAS *UNKNOWN* TO cc1 - WHICH A VALUE LOADED WITH `lbu` NEVER IS, so no spelling of the s16/u16/s32 local reproduces it and the pair is not a declaration to hunt** (round 472, world_map/main/misc11 func_8008A72C, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, parked 98.29% / 2952 bytes against retail's 2960, this being one of its two 4-byte residuals). Retail's cell index is an if/else join - `lbu` twice, one load per arm of the `g_WorldMapZoneId == 7` test, `addiu a2,v0,3` on one side - and the shared `lbu a2,%lo(g_WorldMapZoneProximity)` result is still widened with the sign-extend. `cc1_probe.sh world_map/main/misc11` over that exact join measured `sll $2,$2,1` (no widening) for `s16 zone`, `s32 zone`, `s32 zone` with `(s16)` at the subscript, `u16 zone` with `(s16)` at the subscript, and the `zone = prox; ... zone += 3;` form, because the zero-extended `lbu` range survives the merge; the pair appears only when the same if/else is fed by an `s16` *parameter* (`sll $2,$2,16` / `sra $2,$2,15`), i.e. a value of unknown sign. Same diagnostic as `e-a-sign-extend-pair-implied-by-casts` and `a-lbu-then-andi-0xff-then-andi-0xffff-is-unreachable`: when retail sign-extends something your compile knows is non-negative, the original value did NOT come straight from that load (a wider load, a return value, or a store/reload), and re-declaring the local cannot reach it. Also measured on the same body: `zone = prox; if (..) zone += 3;` 2936, a named `s16` angle local 2944 and a named `s32` one 2952, gcc-2.6.0 97.95, gcc-2.7.2-cdk 86.82.

- id: e-a-s16-cast-does-not-buy-lh-when-the-value-feeds-an-identical-himode-store | keywords: lh, lhu, s16, cast, halfword, store, movhi, narrow, identical-width
  **A `(s16*)` CAST ON A HALFWORD READ DOES NOT FORCE `lh`: WHEN THE LOADED VALUE ONLY FEEDS ANOTHER HALFWORD STORE, cc1 2.7.2 IS FREE TO PICK `lhu` BECAUSE THE SIGNEDNESS OF THE MODE IS UNOBSERVABLE, SO A RETAIL `lh` AGAINST YOUR `lhu` AT THE SAME OFFSET HAS TO BE EXPLAINED BY THE VALUE'S TYPE, NOT BY THE CAST** (round 473, field/main/misc8 func_80081C54, parked 92.75% / 768 bytes against retail's 776). Retail reads the actor position's high halves with `lh v1,0x22(t0)` / `0x26` / `0x2A` and stores each into a `s16` field of the ring entry; the park's `D_800B14F0[idx].positionX = ((s16*)&pActor->position)[1];` (a `s16*` into a `VECTOR`, whose members are `long`) assembles to `lhu $3,34($8)` plus `sh $3,...` in all three, so the cast is not the lever - the original read a genuinely signed field, and the wide struct member has to be re-read as a named `s16` field (or through an `extern s16` alias, per `a-a-16-bit-unsigned-count-gives-sltu-pick-and-keeps-div-signed`) before the load width changes. Judge this one by the load opcode in the instruction diff, not by objdiff: the three pair up at the same size.

- id: e-only-a-cast-around-the-shift-keeps-the-lbu | keywords: lbu, lb, sll, sra, sign-extend, cast, shift, fold
  **A SIGN-EXTENDED BYTE THAT IS THEN SHIFTED (`lbu` / `sll 24` / `sra 18`) IS NOT REACHABLE AS `(s8)byte << 6`: THAT SPELLING FOLDS TO `lb` + `sll 6`, AND SO DOES EVERY INTERMEDIATE-LOCAL FORM OF IT; ONLY THE CAST AROUND THE SHIFT (`(s8)(byte << 6)`) KEEPS THE `lbu`, AND IT EMITS A DIFFERENT PAIR (`sll 30` / `sra 24`)** (round 482, battling/main/misc14 func_8008B730, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, parked 93.45% at retail's exact 764 bytes / 191 insns; the arm is `bits |= (s8)pScript[1] << 6;` over a `u8 *pScript`, and retail has `lbu $v0,1($a1)` / `sll $v0,$v0,0x18` / `sra $v0,$v0,0x12`). `cc1_probe.sh` over seven spellings of that expression: `(s8)(pScript[1] << 6)` = `lbu` + `sll 30` + `sra 24`; `(s8)pScript[1] << 6`, `u8 b; b = pScript[1]; (s8)b << 6`, `s8 n; n = pScript[1]; n << 6`, `s32 e; e = (s8)pScript[1]; e << 6`, a `u16 op` in the middle, and a `s8 *` script pointer ALL = `lb` + `sll 6` (one instruction shorter, so it cannot link). Retail's `lbu` with extend-then-shift-6 therefore needs combine to SKIP the extend-into-load fold, which no spelling reaches - park it instead of re-deriving it from the `.s`.

- id: f-a-half-hoisted-operand-in-its-own-block-scoped-local-keeps-the-schedule | keywords: lh, lhu, s32, intermediate, block, scope, delay, slot, readback
  **THE `s32` INTERMEDIATE THAT BUYS RETAIL'S `lh` MUST BE BLOCK-SCOPED TO THE ARM THAT USES IT: DECLARED AT FUNCTION SCOPE AND SHARED BY TWO SWITCH ARMS IT ALSO MOVES THE STRUCT'S HALFWORD READ-BACK INTO THE NEXT LOAD'S DELAY SLOT, WHICH IS TWO INSTRUCTIONS SHORT OF RETAIL AND CANNOT LINK** (round 484, battle/main/misc30 func_800B9F78, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0, 99.28 -> 99.97% and 1384 bytes). Retail's two distance arms each do `lh v0,2(s1)` / `nop` / `sh v0,16(sp)` / `lhu a1,16(sp)` / `lh v0,10(s1)` / `nop` / `sh v0,18(sp)`; the direct spelling `vec0.vx = pSprite->position.parts.xWhole;` narrows both position loads to `lhu` (the store truncates, per `e-a-s16-cast-does-not-buy-lh...`) and measures 99.28 at the exact size, a function-scope `s32 x; s32 z;` gives the `lh`s but fills the `lh v0,10(s1)` delay slot with the read-back for 1376 bytes / 99.05, and `case 2: { s32 x; s32 z; x = pSprite->position.parts.xWhole; vec0.vx = x; z = ...; vec0.vy = z; ... }` inside each arm's own block gives retail's `lh`s AND retail's placement. Hoisting both halves above both stores (`x = ...; z = ...; vec0.vx = x; vec0.vy = z;`) instead flips the two stores and measures 98.15 / 1380.

## division mfhi/mflo

symptoms: div/mfhi/mflo or mult/srl sequence differs
try: div mfhi mflo mult
- id: a-staged-multiply-then-divide-puts-mflo-in-the-variables-register | keywords: div, mfhi, mflo, mult, sra, staged, in-place, expression, callee-saved
  **`x = A * f() / 4096;` AS ONE EXPRESSION MAKES cc1 2.6.0 PUT THE `mflo` IN A SCRATCH REGISTER AND SHIFT OUT OF IT (`mflo v0` / `sra s0,v0,0xC`); SPLITTING IT INTO `x = A * f(); x = x / 4096;` PUTS THE `mflo` IN `x`'s OWN REGISTER AND SHIFTS IN PLACE (`mflo s0` / `sra s0,s0,0xC`), which is what retail has for a value it later negates in place** (round 479, battle/main/misc25 func_800B026C, XenoBattle260Div = gcc-2.6.0, 96.36 -> 96.55% at retail's exact 2120 bytes, 166 -> 164 differing lines). Read which form retail wants per value before applying it to both: on the same body the SECOND sibling is retail's single-expression form (`mflo v0` / `sra s4,v0,0xC`), so the two are deliberately spelled differently, and staging both would move the wrong one.

- id: a-u8-local-staging-a-division-keeps-the-unmasked-quotient | keywords: div, mfhi, mflo, quotient, u8, qi, andi, narrow, regalloc
  **A DIVISION STAGED IN A `u8` LOCAL IS WHAT PRODUCES RETAIL'S "`andi` BEFORE THE BRANCH BUT THE RAW QUOTIENT IN THE STORE VALUE" PAIR - a QI pseudo may hold the unmasked shift result in its register and is masked only at each SImode use (gcc cse's that into ONE `andi`), and widening the same local to `s32` costs an instruction and rotates every caller-saved register by one** (round 477, battle/main/misc11 func_8007FF14, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8; `u8 n; n = v / 100;` gives 117 insns / 468 bytes with v=`$a1`, offset=`$a2`, digits=`$a0`, n=`$a3`, both masked copies in `$v1` - retail's map - where `s32 n` gives 118 / 472 and v=`$a2`, offset=`$a3`, n=`$v0`, digits=`$a1`). Read the tell first: if the branch tests an `andi`-masked copy while the arithmetic on the same value uses the register raw (`addiu v0,a3,131` after `andi v1,a3,0xff`), the variable is QI and NOT an `s32` staged through a cast; the same reading kills a `u16` widening, since a halfword test would be a bare `beqz`. What survives on that body is the mfhi scratch only (retail `mfhi $v0`, ours `mfhi $t3`): `cc1 -da/-dl` lists no allocation at all for `$t3` and prints `Spilling reg 11` twice, so the mfhi destination is a spill rather than a priority contest, and the third 0xFF store's address staying live across it is the consequence. objdiff's percentage is not monotone here - the 118-insn body scores 91.69 and the 117-insn one 91.24 - judge by the instruction count.
- id: f-a-subtraction-of-two-products-expands-the-subtrahend-first | keywords: mult, mflo, order, subtraction, determinant, cross, subu, temp
  **IN `a*b - c*d` cc1 2.7.2 EXPANDS THE MINUEND'S PRODUCT FIRST (`mult ey,nx` / `mflo` / `mult ex,ny` / `mflo` / `subu`), AND RETAIL'S REVERSE (`mult ex,ny` then `mult ey,nx` with `subu dst,t1,v0`) NEEDS THE SUBTRAHEND NAMED IN ITS OWN VARIABLE BEFORE THE STATEMENT, or the negation form `-(c*d) + a*b`** (round 487, battling/main/misc3 func_80075888, 452 bytes / 110 insns, MATCH). Measured with one `cc1_probe.sh battling/main/misc3` snippet holding four variants of the same 4-argument function: `return ey*nx - ex*ny;` and `h = ey*nx; return h - ex*ny;` both emit ey*nx first, while `h = ex*ny; return ey*nx - h;` and `return -(ex*ny) + ey*nx;` emit ex*ny first (`subu $2,$8,$2`, i.e. `dst = (second mflo) - (first mflo)`). In the real body the temp has to be assigned AFTER the dot-product statement and BEFORE the cross statement (`along = ...; exNy = ex * ny; cross = (ey * nx - exNy) / 4096;`) - with the temp hoisted above `along` or the cross written inline, the two mults come out in the wrong order AND the dot product's own mults sink below them.

- id: f-a-narrow-scale-local-is-what-keeps-a-constant-multiply | keywords: mult, mflo, li, constant, narrow, u8, synth, shift-add
  **A CONSTANT MULTIPLY THAT RETAIL DOES WITH `li r,K` / `mult` / `mflo` COMES OUT AS A 4-5 INSTRUCTION SHIFT-ADD CHAIN FROM `power * 50` AND AS RETAIL'S THREE FROM `power * scale` WHERE `scale` IS A `u8`/`s16` LOCAL INITIALISED TO 50 - cc1 2.6.0 does not propagate a NARROW constant into SImode arithmetic, so the multiply's operand stays a pseudo and `expand_mult` takes the `mulsi3` path instead of `synth_mult`** (round 477, battle/main/misc18 func_80098D2C, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0, 91.59 -> 93.05% by this alone, and it is what makes the function linkable). Measured with `cc1_probe.sh battle/main/misc18`: `p->power * 50` and `50 * p->power` both synth (`sll/addu/sll/addu/sll`), `(unsigned short)p->power * 50` synth, `int v = p->power; v * 50` synth, while `u8 s = 50; p->power * s`, `short s = 50;` and a top-level `u8 s10 = 10;` all emit `li $2,0x32` / `mult $3,$2` / `mflo $2`. The function-top initialiser also reproduces retail's `li t0,0xa` hoisted into the FIRST `beqz`'s delay slot (dbr lifts the entry block's constant), so put the scale local at the top of the body when retail's `li` is up there. Companion spelling from the same function: the store's address form follows the STATEMENT that names it - `pBase->slotAmounts[slot] = amount;` folds the constant into the store's displacement (`addu v1,a1,a3` / `sw v0,24428(v1)`) while `pAmounts = pBase->slotAmounts; pAmounts[slot] = amount;` gives retail's `addiu v0,a3,24428` / `addu v0,a1,v0` / `sw v1,0(v0)`, worth the one instruction that was missing.

- id: f-divisor-argument-original-passes | keywords: division, mfhi, andi, div, move, s32, signed, sll
  A divisor/argument the original passes with a plain move/div and no andi or sll/sra pair wants the narrow SIGNED type (s16), not u8/s32.
- id: f-signed-product-cast-u32 | keywords: division, mfhi, multu, cast, mult, signed, srl
- id: f-mult-operand-order-follows | keywords: mult, operand, order, lbu, clamp, source-order, slti, preset
  **THE `mult` OPERAND ORDER FOLLOWS SOURCE ORDER AND THE LOAD CLUSTER FOLLOWS THE SAME SOURCE ORDER, so a park whose retail `mult v1,v0` is the REVERSE of its load cluster is unreachable from C under gcc 2.7.2** (round 396, battle/main/misc5 func_8007AA60, parked 99.09% at retail's exact 88 bytes / 22 insns; the only differing line is `mult v1,v0` against `mult v0,v1`, i.e. one ENCODING - the product is identical, so objdiff can never close it and the bytes cannot link). Measured: `p->operand2 * pRow[p->operand1]` emits retail's cluster exactly (`lbu idx`, `lbu operand2`, `addu`, `lbu row`) with `mult` in v0,v1; writing the row first (`pRow[...] * p->operand2`, an `u8` local pair for the operands - copy-propagated away - the typed `g_BattleSlotRegs[arg1].byteRegs[i]` form, or a `volatile` read of `p->operand2`) all give 71.05-71.09, where the operand2 `lbu` sinks below the row load and the mult then puts the row value in v0, i.e. the RIGHT operand order with the WRONG cluster. The two are locked together because 2.7.2 expands the multiply's operands in source order. Preset is not the way out: 2.6.0 and 2.7.2-cdk both emit retail's cluster from the row-first body but write `slt` where retail has `slti` (2.6.0 scores 99.55), and `-fschedule-insns`/`-fschedule-insns2` under 2.7.2 leave the stream unchanged (checked in cc1's own output, not with try_flags). A prior permuter run (2259 iterations, base=20 best=20) agrees; round 411 re-measured the same unit and confirmed it from both sides (`s32 mul = p->operand2;` then `pRow[p->operand1] * mul` keeps operand2 in `$v1` and scores 71.09) and a third 3-minute permuter run (1733 iterations) returned base=20 best=20.
  Round 424 measured the last spelling pair on the same function: `u8 imm = p->operand2;` as a statement before a row-first multiply is 71.05 and mirrors the whole allocation (the base `lui/addiu` also moves below the `addu`), i.e. splitting the operand read into its own statement does NOT decouple the cluster from the mult order. Park, do not re-spell.
  A signed product cast to u32 before dividing gives mult + multu/srl; a u32 product gives multu.
  Round 437 CORRECTS the 2.6.0 half of this entry: the claim that 2.6.0 leaves `slt` where retail has `slti`
  is false - it came from the TYPED spelling's reloc addend, not from the compare. `extern u8
  g_BattleSlotByteRegs[][0x40];` + `u8 *pRow = g_BattleSlotByteRegs[arg1];` +
  `s16 v = pRow[p->operand1] * p->operand2; if (v > 0xFF) v = 0xFF; pRow[p->operand1] = v;` compiles
  BYTE-IDENTICALLY to retail under gcc-2.6.0-psx (objdump -dr of the function, relocations and addends
  included, cmp-clean), i.e. 100.00 rather than 99.55, and `try_flags.sh battle/main/misc5 --all --gcc
  gcc-2.6.0-psx` scores every OTHER function of the unit exactly as under Default (all six matched ones
  stay 100.00), so the unit switch buys this function for free. The lesson generalises: a park note's
  "N under 2.6.0, it emits X instead of retail's Y" can be the RELOC FOLD of a typed `g_BattleSlotRegs`
  spelling rather than a codegen difference, so re-dump the candidate object and compare instruction
  text before believing a compiler can't produce retail's stream - and when the address of a bank
  member is a symbol of its own (g_BattleSlotByteRegs = g_BattleSlotRegs+0x30), spelling it as that
  symbol is what closes the last addend.
  Round 427 found the mirror image under 2.6.0 - COMMUTATIVE OPERAND ORDER CAN BE THE ONLY RESIDUAL EVEN WHEN THE CLUSTER AND THE REGISTERS ARE ALREADY RETAIL'S, and it is then not source-controllable either: battle/main/misc19 func_8009A2D4's best 2.6.0 body (313 insns / 1252 bytes, retail's exact size) differs in exactly `mult v1,v0` against retail's `mult v0,v1`, `addu a0,v1,v0` against `addu a0,v0,v1` and `addu v1,v0,a0` against `addu v0,v0,a0`, with the three loads (`lbu v0,87(s0)` / `lhu v1,0(a1)`, `lbu v0,18(s0)`, `lbu v0,34(s0)`) and every destination in retail's register. Measured with NO effect: writing the product row-first (`rowCosts[0] * volatile statBonuses[7]` - cluster and mult byte-identical), writing the sum weapon-first (`weaponData[0].attack + attack` - output byte-identical), and storing the second sum with no local (`pWork->attackAmount = attack + weaponData[2].attack;` fixes that destination but flips the earlier product's load cluster, 21 differing lines instead of 19). So treat an encoding-only commutative swap as 99.74-class ceiling: park it, do not spend spellings.
- id: f-mfhi-mflo-destination-is-the-preset | keywords: division, mfhi, mflo, destination, coalesce, srl, preset, 2.6.0, carve-out
  **A DIVMOD WHOSE ONLY RESIDUAL IS THE `mfhi`/`mflo` DESTINATION IS A PRESET SIGNATURE, NOT A SPELLING**: retail writes the highpart/quotient straight into the register the next instruction consumes (`mfhi a0 / sra a0,a0,5`, `mflo v0 / sh v0,38(a1)`, `mfhi v0 / srl v0,v0,3`), and gcc 2.7.2-psx always inserts a temp (`mfhi a1 / sra a0,a1,5`, `mflo t0 / sh t0,...`, `mfhi t0 / srl v0,t0,3`) - the divmod's md names a fresh pseudo that the allocator does not coalesce with the consumer. Round 414, battle/main/misc19: `func_8009A9D0` is 99.66% (116 bytes, 29/29 insns, the ONLY differing line is that pair) and 100.00 under gcc-2.6.0 (try_flags), while -O3, cdk, `50 > rand() % 100`, `<= 49`, the modulo result in a local and two permuter runs (base=10 best=10) all leave it at 99.66; its near-twin `BattleRollPercentAndSetState38` has retail's `mfhi a0` under 2.6.0 because misc18 is a XenoBattle260 unit, so a twin is only evidence for the md when it shares the preset. The same unit's `func_8009A2D4` (313 insns) carries three of these sites and moves only 99.19 -> 99.52 under 2.6.0. So: count the mfhi/mflo destinations in the diff before writing a spelling, and if they are the residual, screen the unit with `try_flags.sh <unit> --all --gcc gcc-2.6.0-psx` and propose a one-function carve-out (PRESET_260) instead of hunting shapes - and park the body at retail's byte count with the md named.
- id: b-pointer-sum-flips-a-whole-8-store-block | keywords: addu, operand, index-first, store, struct, array, allocno, permuter
  **FOR A STRUCT-ARRAY ELEMENT STORE, `(idx + array)->field` INSTEAD OF `array[idx].field` FLIPS NOT JUST THE `addu` BUT THE WHOLE STATEMENT'S ALLOCATION - and the permuter finds it in one edit** (round 409, menu/main/misc4_260 func_801D02D8, 98.48 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 1660 bytes / 415 insns, gcc 2.6.0). The function's eight `slotHighlightQuads[g_Menu->renderContext].uN/vN` stores each re-read `g_Menu`, its `renderContext` and `pPrimBuffer` (an `lw`/`lw`/`lw` cluster), and with the subscript form every cluster loaded `g_Menu` into `$v1` where retail has `$a1`, cascading into eight permuted blocks (172 differing lines) that no declaration order, operand order or `* 16` / `16 *` swap moved. One statement rewritten as `(g_Menu->renderContext + pPrims->slotHighlightQuads)->u3` took it to 98.70; all eight took it to 100.00. The permuter's only edit was exactly that (RESULT PERMUTER_BETTER base=630 best=540, 1813 iters, 4 min), and its 540 was the one-site body - so when a diff shows the SAME load cluster permuted at N sibling stores of one struct array, try the pointer-sum form at ONE site, re-measure, then apply it to the rest. Same mechanism as `b-index-first-subscript-pointer`, but here it also moves the allocno of the reloaded global, not only the `addu` operands.

- id: f-a-plain-sra-means-the | keywords: division, sra, shift, div, rounding, power-of-two, blocks, srl
  **A POWER-OF-TWO DIVISION THAT RETAIL EMITS AS A BARE `sra` IS A SHIFT IN THE SOURCE: gcc's signed `/32` adds `addiu x,31` / sign-fix instructions that no `>>` produces, so a 2-instruction size excess on the same body is that division, not the allocator** (round 419, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_b func_800460A0, 91.29 -> 94.79 in one edit; `blocks = total / 32` also emitted the rounding TWICE because the value feeds two places). Compare against the neighbouring `/2` in the same body: it keeps the full rounding (`srl 31 / addu / sra 1`), so the source did divide by 2 - the two spellings sit side by side and the plain `sra` is the tell. The give-away in a diff is `addiu t,x,32` (or `+31`) next to the shift.

- id: f-dividend-dies-at-the-division | keywords: division, in-place, sra, addu, shift, size, copy, blocks
  **THE ROUND-UP GOES IN PLACE ON THE DIVIDEND'S REGISTER (and the later shift gets a FRESH callee-saved register with a copy) ONLY WHEN THE DIVIDEND IS DEAD AFTER THE DIVISION - so `total / 2` and `total >> 5` on the same variable can never produce it; divide into a `size` local and derive both the block count and the remainder from `size`** (round 420, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_b StoreImage func_800462DC, 97.80 -> 99.29 -> 99.94 -> 100.00, PSY-Q preset). Retail is `mflo a2 / addiu v1,a2,1 / srl v0,v1,31 / addu v1,v1,v0 / sra a0,v1,1 / bgtz a0 / sra s0,v1,5 / ... / addu v1,s0,zero / sll v0,v1,4 / subu s0,a0,v0 / addu s4,v1,zero`: the shift reads the ROUNDED value, which is only reachable through `(total/2) >> 4` folded into `t >> 5`, i.e. the source has no second use of `total`. `blocks = size >> 4; rest = size - blocks * 16;` then loses retail's two copies (96.09, 4 bytes short): the closing spelling is the permuter's `rest = size >> 4; rest = size - rest * 16; blocks = size >> 4;` - the SECOND computation of `size >> 4` is a separate pseudo whose register rest then takes, which is what forces `move v1,s0` + `addu s4,v1,zero`. `blocks = rest; rest = ...` coalesces them back (96.09), so the repeat is load-bearing; note it in the source. Companion measured on the same body: the guard must be `if (size <= 0)`, not `if (total / 2 <= 0)`, or the divisor's round-up lands in a fresh `$v0` and every register downstream shifts.

- id: f-a-narrow-divisor-buys-the-sltu-pick-and-loses-the-intmin-guard | keywords: div, break, sltu, u16, narrow, divisor, guard, pick
  **DECLARING THE VALUE THAT FEEDS BOTH AN UNSIGNED-LOOKING MIN-PICK AND A DIVISION AS `u16` WINS THE PICK (`sltu`) AND LOSES THE DIVISION: gcc then knows the divisor's range, folds the signed `/` into an unsigned one, and drops retail's `addiu at,-1 / bne / lui 0x8000 / bne / break 6` INT_MIN/-1 guard (4 instructions) while ADDING an `andi 0xffff` on the divisor** (round 460, battle/main/misc23 func_800A7064 = lib_gear/main/main func_801E1A14, 569-insn body, XenoBattle260Div0 = gcc-2.6.0 -G0 --expand-div). Retail's pick is `sltu $v0,$v1,$a3` at 0x800A7590 (two `lhu` operands of a `u16*` cursor) and its `rowStep = vSpan / nSegs` at 0x800A75B0 is the FULLY CHECKED signed form, with $a3 the raw zero-extended `lhu` value and no mask - so the source has one 32-bit-ish signed value that the compare happens to compile unsigned, not a 16-bit declaration. `s32 nSegs` is 562 insns (the pick compiles to `slt`), `u16 nSegs` is 565 (pick fixed, guard lost), `rowStep = vSpan / (s16)nSegs;` is 567 (2 of the 4 guard instructions back, at the cost of a `sll/sra` pair on the divisor). This CORRECTS the count in `g-a-16-bit-unsigned-count-gives-sltu-pick-and-keeps-div-signed` (round 459, the same function in lib_gear): `u16` does buy the `sltu` pick, but it does NOT keep the signed breaker here - the 4 instruction shortfall IS that guard. Read this before trying a narrow type to fix a `slt`/`sltu` residual: check whether the same value is a divisor, and count the `break 6` in retail first.

## loop shape and invariant hoisting

- id: a-descending-fill-whose-base-is-the-tables-bottom-entry | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, order, preheader, indexed, walk, block-head, counting-down
  **A DESCENDING FILL WRITTEN AS A WALKING `*p--` FROM THE TABLE'S TOP EMITS THE RIGHT BYTES BUT PUTS THE HOISTED VALUE AND THE FOR-INIT AFTER THE POINTER'S `addiu`, WHILE THE SAME LOOP AS `p[i]` WITH `i` COUNTING DOWN AND `p` NAMING ONE ELEMENT BELOW THE FIRST WRITE EMITS THEM BEFORE IT - i.e. retail's own `li v0,-1 / li a1,0x2 / addiu s0,s0,-0x70` order** (round 497, field/main/misc3 func_800705DC, Default = gcc-2.7.2; 95.29 -> 97.90% on the same 426 insns / 1704 bytes, and the three fills' preheaders became retail's). gcc's strength reduction of `p[i]` puts the reduced pointer's init in the preheader AFTER the loop's own for-init and after the hoisted store constant, which is exactly where retail has it; the walking form emits the pointer derivation at the source statement's position, first. The base has to be the table's LOWEST element, so derive it from what retail already has in a register (`pSlot = (s16*)(pBank - 0x74); for (i = 2; i >= 0; i--) pSlot[i] = -1;` from `s0 = &bank`, `pRenderSlot = pIndex + 0x4E; for (i = 0xF; i >= 0; i--) pRenderSlot[i] = 0x1D;` from the `&g_FieldScriptRenderContextIndex` that is still live in `$v1`) - the same source with `pBank - 0x70`/`pIndex + 0x5D` (the top entry) is instruction-identical in shape but writes 4 bytes higher, and the reduced pointer then reads `addiu s0,s0,-108` / `addiu a2,v1,216` instead of retail's -112 / 186. Two traps measured on the same body: a fill whose FIRST write is the bare symbol must STAY a walking pointer (indexing `D_800B22DE` emits `D_800B22DE+0x3E` plus an extra `li a1,0x1f` in the preceding branch's delay slot, 427 insns against retail's 426), and two fills must use two locals (`pSlot`/`pRenderSlot`) - one shared local ties both to the first one's register (`$s0` where retail has `$a2`).

- id: an-indexed-frame-walk-kills-the-duplicate-induction-base | keywords: giv, biv, loop, pointer, increment, index, subscript, induction, base, duplicate
  **A LOOP THAT WALKS A STRUCT ARRAY WITH `p++` AND ~8 CONSTANT FIELD OFFSETS MAKES `loop.c` KEEP TWO BASES WHERE RETAIL HAS ONE (`$sX = p` AND `$sY = p + 2`, BOTH BUMPED BY THE STRUCT SIZE); REWRITING THE SAME LOOP AS `p[i].field` WITH `i++` REMOVES THE USER BIV, AND THE SECOND BASE, THE `addu` THAT BUILT IT AND A STACK SLOT GO WITH IT** (round 491, slus_006.64/system/rendering func_8001D53C, XenoRendering = gcc-2.7.2 `-O2 -G8 --dont-expand-li`; 80.76 -> 83.99% at the same 1436 bytes, and the loop tail became retail's exact `addiu base,base,24 / addiu i,i,1 / lw count / bne (addu pEntry,pEntry,3 in the delay slot)`). Retail keeps ONE base (`addu $s0,$a1,zero` in the preheader, all field offsets 0x0..0x14 as displacements), and with the pointer form gcc derived a giv at +2 (the first struct field that is not at offset 0) and used THAT as the main base, so every offset shifted by -2 and the loop end carried two `addu ...,24`. The duplicate is `loop.c`'s biv/derived-giv pair, not a source pointer, so no local, cast or declaration order removes it - only losing the biv does. Two traps on the rewrite: a raw `(u8*)p + 0x13` cast inside the body keeps addressing ELEMENT 0 once `p` becomes an array base (write `((u8*)&p[i])[0x13]`, or the function both loses a field store and gains a reload of the base from its home slot: 82.07 vs 83.99 here), and the array base has to stay a pointer PARAMETER-like local - `pCurRenderFramesData` is `void*` in the header, so `p[i].field` needs no cast. Check the argument for this rewrite at the loop end: retail's `addiu base,base,<sizeof>` is what confirms the original was an index walk and not two source pointers.

- id: a-for-ever-loop-with-a-redundant-guard-reproduces-retails-rotated-shape | keywords: loop, rotated, backedge, while, for, continue, break, guard, cse
  **`while (count != 0) { ... }` GIVES A `bnez count,top` BACKEDGE; THE SAME BODY AS `for (;;)` WITH A REDUNDANT `if (count == 0) continue;` IN FRONT OF ITS CALLS GIVES RETAIL'S ROTATED SHAPE INSTEAD - EXIT TEST AT THE LOOP HEAD JUMPING TO THE INNER `break` TEST, ONE `beqz count,top` GUARD PER CALL, AND AN UNCONDITIONAL `j top` WHOSE DELAY SLOT CARRIES THE LOOP-BODY INITIALISER - WORTH 4.5 POINTS ON A BODY WHOSE REGISTER SPLIT WAS OTHERWISE UNCHANGED** (round 489, battle/main/misc34 func_800C0314, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0 -O2 with `-fschedule-insns`; 91.91% / 592 bytes / 148 insns -> 96.37% / 584 / 146, both residuals being a callee-saved rotation and the index's `or` order). The wait loop polls a live-slot array until no sprite still has a script timer; retail's tail re-tests `count` before EACH of its two calls and ends in `j top` with `pending = 0` in the delay slot (14 insns), which no `while` spelling produces. Two consequences: the guard's `continue` is what supplies the head test, so `for (;;)` plus one guard per call reproduces the layout even though `count` never changes in the loop; and cse then merges the guards (count is a local that lives in a callee-saved register and no call can change it), so a park that is two instructions short at this point is missing exactly the second `beqz`/`move` pair and no re-spelling of the guard recovered it (`if (count != 0) {call} else {continue;}` identical, `while` + both guards 149 insns at 93.91, a third guard at the top of the body 147 at 93.91).

- id: j-an-s16-parameter-turns-a-shift-into-a-hoistable-invariant | keywords: s16, s32, parameter, prototype, truncation, sll, sra, hoist, invariant, callee-saved, frame, giv
  **AN `s16` PARAMETER MAKES `x >> 16` AN `(s16)`-IN-HIGH-HALF VALUE (`sra` + `sll`), AND loop.c THEN HOISTS THAT PAIR OUT OF AN INNER LOOP INTO A SPARE CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER WITH A PER-USE `sra` - where retail recomputes the plain `sra`; declaring the callee's coordinate parameters `s32` in the CALLING unit removes the conversion, the hoist, the save/restore and the frame growth at once** (round 500, battle/main/misc14 func_80088B80, XenoBattle260 = gcc 2.6.0, 92.61 -> 95.80% at 1224 bytes / 306 insns against retail's 1208 / 302). The 2x10 sprite grid does `BattleDrawSpritePackage(..., sx >> 16, sy >> 16)` with `sy` a fixed-point biv of the OUTER loop (step 0xBD0000): with `extern s32 BattleDrawSpritePackage(s32, s32, s16, s16)` (the definition in misc2.c really is s16) the inner-loop preheader carries `sra v0,s5,0x10 / sll s6,v0,0x10` and the body `sra a3,s6,0x10`, which is a 7th callee-saved register and 8 more bytes of frame; the source CANNOT avoid it - a block-scope `s32 y = sy >> 16;`, `s32 x, y;` assigned in the body, and every declaration order measured byte-identical (310 insns). With the coordinates declared `s32` the conversion node is gone, cc1 emits retail's per-iteration `sra a3,s5,0x10`, and the body drops to 306. The truncations retail DOES have for that prototype (the `0x11A + n * 6` third argument in the two neighbours) are reproduced by writing `(s16)(0x11A + n * 6)` explicitly: both neighbours stay 100.00 and the 8-byte sll/sra pair comes back, so a caller-local prototype that disagrees with the definition is a legitimate lever as long as every truncation the original object shows is spelled as a cast. So when a loop-invariant shift out of a fixed-point biv is hoisted and retail recomputes it, check the callee's parameter WIDTH in this TU before blaming loop.c.

- id: a-do-blocks-extent-decides-which-invariants-are-hoisted | keywords: loop, extent, hoist, invariant, do-block, preheader, load, constant, boundary
  **THE `do { } while (0)` EXTENT IS ITSELF A KNOB: EVERY INVARIANT INSIDE IT MOVES TO THE PREHEADER, SO MOVING A GLOBAL LOAD OR A CONSTANT STORE INTO THE BLOCK SCRAMBLES A STRAIGHT-LINE BODY THAT WAS MATCHING** (round 488, world_map/main/misc7 func_800813E8, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2 --dont-expand-li, 34 insns / 136 bytes = retail's exact size, parked 94.71%). Three extents measured on one body whose retail order is `lw slots / li 0x1000 / sw RMV / addu / sw 0x7C / three global loads / li 0x78 / six target stores / sh cmd / li / jr / sh state`: with EVERYTHING inside the block and the slot pointer declared in it, 33.50% / 78 differing lines, because loop.c hoists the fade level's `li v0,120` to slot 1 where retail has it at 13; with the block starting AFTER the fade-level store (only the six target stores plus the command store are the body), 65.74% / 36 lines, because `posY` and `posZ` are loop-invariant loads and both get hoisted above the rotation-matrix store; with the block starting before the three loads, 94.71% (retail's schedule). Two consequences worth carrying: if retail has NO load hoisted and no constant at slot 1, its function is one straight-line block and an `li` sitting several instructions above its store is sched2's work, not loop.c's; and a residual that reads "the whole entry block's schedule differs" should send you to the block boundary before you touch declarations or spelling.

- id: j-a-separate-tile-plus-header-add-stops-the-minus-sixteen-fold | keywords: fold, reassociation, constant, shift, offset, row, addiu, -16
  **`base + 0x200 + (zone << 4)` AFTER `zone--` IS REASSOCIATED INTO `sll zone,4 / addiu 496` (the -16 of `(zone-1)*16` merges with the 0x200 and retail's `addiu r,r,-1` disappears); WRITING THE HEADER ADD AS ITS OWN STATEMENT FIRST, WITH THE ROW OFFSET ADDED AFTERWARDS IN A NAMED LOCAL, KEEPS BOTH INSTRUCTIONS** (round 485, world_map/main/misc2 func_80075E7C, XenoWorldMapDiv; 4 instructions of the sum-loop preheader, retail `addiu v1,v1,-1 / sll v1,v1,4 / addiu v0,v0,512 / addu v1,v0,v1`). The closing form is `pSrc = (s32)g_WorldMapTileGroupData[index] + 0x200; row = zone << 4; pSrc += row;`. Insensitive: `zone * 16` instead of `zone << 4`, and the assignment order of `zone = 1` / `pLimit = ...`.

- id: a-loop-carried-update-belongs-after-the-store-block | keywords: move, copy, loop, position, order, callee-saved, swapped, accumulator
  **A LOOP-CARRIED ACCUMULATOR ASSIGNMENT WHOSE RETAIL COPY SITS IN A LATE DELAY SLOT BELONGS AFTER THE STORE BLOCK, NOT NEXT TO THE ARITHMETIC - moving the one statement 75.62 -> 86.25% and restored retail's mirrored callee-saved pair** (round 481, slus_006.64/system/temp2_r1 func_800278F8, XenoGraphicsLibrary = gcc-2.6.0 -O2 -G8; 1068 -> 1072 bytes against retail's 1096, 205 -> 148 differing lines, pair col `$s3` / pPrim `$s4`). The loop computes `remainder = (s16)(col + width) % pBlock->unk328;` early, and `col = remainder;` written right after it measures 75.62 with col and pPrim MIRRORED on every line of the 60-instruction body; written after the eight vertex stores (before the `GetTPage` call) it measures 86.25 and the pair is retail's, because retail's `move s3,a1` copy sits in the delay slot of the texColumn `/64` `bgez` that follows the stores. Read where the copy sits before believing a "5 copies plus a block order" note: one moved statement can be 57 differing lines. Companion measurements on the same body, all byte-identical or worse: loop statement order (u/width before vs after texColumn), the embedded assignment `width = 0x100 - (u = ...)`, `pPrim`'s declaration position, and routing a division through a reused local; the still-mirrored variants measure 78.22 (rows as a hoisted-single-arm if) and 74.36 (col fixup as an if/else, which also moves the divisor register).


- id: outer-loop-as-goto-moves-the-hoist-one-level-down | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, goto, prologue, preheader, nested, symbol, table
  **AN OUTER `while (1)` WHOSE ONLY JOB IS TO RESCAN MAKES gcc HOIST THE INNER LOOP'S INVARIANTS TWO LEVELS, INTO THE FUNCTION PROLOGUE; WRITING THE RESCAN AS A `goto` LEAVES ONE LEVEL OF LOOP, SO THE SAME INVARIANTS LAND AT THE RESCAN LABEL - WHICH IS WHERE RETAIL HAS THEM** (round 476, battle/main/misc34 func_800C0564, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0, 86.15 -> 92.65% at retail's exact 384 bytes / 96 insns). Retail forms the inner loop's invariants - `lui/addiu` of `g_BattleConditionAnimIds` and two pointer copies of the state-work base - at `.L800C05A8`, the outer loop's head, and only the `switch`'s jump-table address in the prologue. With `while (1) { ... if (!needsWait) break; func_800BE790(); }` all six of those instructions sit in the prologue; with `pBase = ...; needsWait = 0; i = 0; rescan: pSlot = (BattleActorSlot *)pBase; pSpriteSlot = (u8 *)pSlot; do { ... } while (i != 11); if (needsWait != 0) { needsWait = 0; func_800BE790(); i = 0; goto rescan; }` the six land at the label and only the jump-table address is one level too deep. So when a park's residual is "the whole entry block's schedule differs" and retail's own prologue contains exactly one hoisted symbol address, count whether the hoist is one or two levels before touching the spelling - the loop STRUCTURE, not the operand, decides it. Residual after the switch: the jump table address, the pSlot walker anchored at +7 instead of +0, and a 0x8C8C constant gcc splits into `li 0x8000` + `lw 0xC8C(reg)`.

- id: increment-in-a-branch-slot-versus-the-preheader-copy-are-exclusive | keywords: loop, counter, increment, delay-slot, reorg, preheader, copy, constant-propagation
  **WHEN RETAIL HAS THE LOOP COUNTER'S INCREMENT IN THE DELAY SLOT OF THE BRANCH THAT TESTS A CALL'S RESULT AND ITS `idx = i` COPY IN THE LOOP-BACK BRANCH'S SLOT, THE TWO COME FROM DIFFERENT SPELLINGS AND NO ONE BODY HAS BOTH: `idx = i++` at the body top gives the preheader/latch `move s3,s1` (reorg steals the copy) but puts the increment at the head, while an explicit result local with `i++` between the call and the test plus `idx = i` as the last body statement gives the increment in retail's slot and the copy in retail's latch slot but lets cc1 CONSTANT-FOLD the pre-loop copy into a prologue `move s3,<const>` and drop the callee-saved save order** (round 455, battle/main/misc9 func_8007DA1C / func_8007DE78, the five-member func_8007D8C0 family). Measured on DA1C: `idx = i++` 95.38% / 88 insns (retail 87), the ok-shape 91.46% (`idx = i` decl-initialised) / 92.51% (assigned before the loop) / 90.75% (count declared first), copy-at-bottom-only 89.03%, all 86 insns; DE78 the same pair 93.64 vs 91.33. Both members are then one instruction short in the opposite direction (the reorg DUPLICATE of the loop `slti` into the second `beqz` slot appears only with the shape whose increment is at the head), so the family is a genuine two-way wall, not a spelling to find. The profitable half: the R398 two-pointer recipe (`pField = pRow` after the head store, index-first base with an `(s32)` cast on the symbol, `u16 value` local at the tail) transfers to DE78 unchanged, 89.33 -> 93.64%.
  Round 469 addendum (both stubs re-measured): the LOOP SYNTAX is worth a point and a half on DE78 even though it is byte-neutral on DA1C - `while (i < 3)` with `idx = i++` scores 95.25% / 352 bytes / 88 insns against the do-while this stub parked with at 93.64% / 344 / 86, i.e. the while form takes DE78 from one instruction SHORT to one OVER, the same side of retail DA1C was already on. And the two branches merged into one `&&` test compile BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the nested `if`s on DA1C (92.51% / 344 / 86 either way), so the branch spelling is not a knob here - only the increment's position is.
  Round 482 addendum (both stubs measured from the ok-shape on both sides): THE WALL IS ONE INSTRUCTION, NOT TWO - the ok-shape's body is 86 insns / 344 bytes / 92.51% (DA1C) and 92.95% (DE78) with the increment in the beqz v0 slot and the idx copy in the bnez slot exactly as retail, and its only residual is reorg's obstruction DUPLICATE of the latch `slti` in the second beqz's slot (retail splits the block there, so its second beqz targets the bnez while ours targets the slti); the `idx = i++` body is the same loop with a THIRD slti copy in the first beqz's slot (88 insns / 352 bytes). So 87 = 86 + that duplicate and 88 = 87 + one slti too many - do not hunt for a third residual. Two keepers: the test written `0 < 3 - i` DOES reach retail's exact 87 insns / 348 bytes but at 90.43%, because it spends `li / subu / bgtz` on the test instead of slti+bnez, so byte count is not the gate; and dropping the `pField` two-pointer local from the ok-shape is 85 insns / 87.08%.
  Round 495 addendum (the GATE members of the family, battle/main/misc9 func_8007DB78 / func_8007DFD4,
  retail 96 insns / 384 bytes each, byte-identical streams apart from ClearRecordIdle's second argument):
  PUTTING `offset += 8` IN THE FOR-CLAUSE - `for (i = 0; i < 3; offset += 8) { idx = i++; if (...) {...} }`, i.e. the
  loop's only other per-iteration statement written as the for's increment - is what makes reorg duplicate the loop
  test `slti v0,s1,3` into ALL THREE conditional-branch delay slots (the ClearRecordIdle-result beqz, the flag-gate
  beqz and the `and` beqz), which is retail's copy count on the gated stubs. It takes both from 85.10% (376 bytes /
  94 insns) to 95.64% (388 / 97) in one step on top of the `pField = pRow` recipe, and it beats every other loop
  spelling measured here: while with offset at the body end 88.59% (380 / 95), do-while the same 88.59%, `for`,
  with `i++, offset += 8` as the increment 89.28% (368 / 92), `idx = i; idle = call(idx,...); i++;` 82.77% (364 / 91),
  increment at the body end 84.55% (368 / 92). The residual it leaves is ONE instruction and is this same wall: the
  for-clause shape still emits `addiu s1,s1,1` at the loop head, so the first beqz's slot takes a fourth slti where
  retail has the increment (retail, with the increment there, is not threaded and carries three).
  Round 497 CLOSES THE FAMILY, and the wall was the wrong noun: the increment's slot is bought with a CALL RESULT LOCAL
  plus a loop-bound statement, and nothing else about the body changes. battle/main/misc9 func_8007D8C0 (slots 0..3) and
  func_8007DCF8 (3..0xB, with the g_BattleSlotFlags gate) both reach MATCH / 100.00% at retail's exact 348 and 384 bytes
  from parks that had sat at 84-95% for five rounds, with ONE recipe, applied in this order:
  (1) `u8 idx = i;` as the loop body's first statement, NOT `idx = i++`: the truncation keeps `idx` a pseudo of its own,
  so the buffer store stays `sb <idx>` and the for-clause `i++` no longer has a use of `i` textually after it - which is
  what lets sched2/reorg hoist the increment into the ClearRecordIdle beqz's slot, retail's position, for free. A
  `s32 idx = i;` propagates away (the store becomes `sb <i>`), the increment then cannot move above it and stays at the
  body end: 84.24% / 82 insns. The masks an s32 `idx` would need at its two u8 call arguments CSE into retail's single
  `andi s0,s3,0xFF` either way.
  (2) `u8 idle = <call>(idx, 0); i++;` - the result in its own local with the increment BETWEEN the call and the test.
  That is the half the round-482 note found; combined with (1) it costs nothing, and reorg's duplicate of the latch
  `slti` into the second beqz's slot appears with it, so the "exclusive" trade only ever existed for `idx = i++` bodies.
  (3) the loop's OTHER per-iteration statement (`offset += 8`) in the FOR-CLAUSE (`for (; i < 0xB; offset += 8)`): the
  round-495 finding holds and is what duplicates `slti` into the remaining slots. The gated member needs it for retail's
  three copies; the 0..3 member has two and `while (i < 3)` is exact there.
  (4) THE ROW-BASE COPY IS BOUGHT BY A TAIL-ONLY LOCAL, AND THE TAIL NEEDS ONE PER VALUE. `u16 *pRow = ...; pField = pRow;`
  gives retail's `addu v1,v1,v0` / `move s5,v1`; then `s32 rowIndex;` assigned `arg1` AFTER the head store and used in the
  tail's base re-form. Do not stop at one: func_8007DCF8 needed a SECOND such local (`rowMask = 0xFF;` before the loop,
  `rowIndex & rowMask` in the tail) before its entry block reached retail's v0/v1 mirror - the `(u8)rowIndex` cast that
  removes the local measures 94.45% at the same 96 insns, so the local is load-bearing, not decoration.
  (5) `s16 last = count - 1;` as a statement BEFORE the `if (count != 0)`, not the expression inside the call, is what
  puts `addiu a1,s2,-1` in the `beqz s2` delay slot where retail has it instead of `move a0,zero` (94.45 -> 99.51).
  (4)'s second half and (5) were permuter finds (PERMUTER_ZERO after 30-60 s from a 99.51% / 94.45% body) that ported
  byte-exactly; so run the permuter on the LAST ordering residual only, after (1)-(3). The siblings should fall to the
  same recipe - read the retail stream's `slti` copy count first (2 = func_8007DA1C/func_8007DE78, 3 =
  func_8007DB78/func_8007DFD4) to pick `while` vs for-clause, then apply (1)-(5).
- id: an-o-equals-i-times-stride-body-keeps-the-symbol-store-form | keywords: loop, counter, offset, accumul, regalloc, swapped, biv, giv, stride
  **A CLEAR LOOP WHOSE TWO VARIABLES LAND MIRRORED (COUNTER IN `$a2`, BYTE OFFSET IN `$a3`) POINT THE BODY AT ACCUMULATING `o += 6` WHERE RETAIL ASSIGNS `o = i * 6`, AND THE ASSIGNMENT FORM ALSO PRESERVES WHICH OF THE TWO STORE FORMS gcc PICKS: with a NAMED s32 offset retail's stores come out as `lui at,%hi(sym) / addu at,at,o / sh %lo(sym)(at)` (the offset added per store), which the assignment form reproduces exactly, and the offset then takes `$a2` with the counter in `$a3`** (round 452, battle/main/misc13 func_800877E0, 60.72 -> 62.91% at 448 bytes, retail 456: loop 1 went from every line differing by register name to exact). Writing `= i * 6` inside the body instead of `o += 6` makes gcc build the GIV `i*6` and keep it as a scalar because the address is `symbol + o`; the accumulator spelling gets the two BIVs the other way round. The limit found on the same body: the same trick does NOT fix a second loop whose offset also competes with a loaded table pointer (`lw a2,%lo(g_BattleSlotParamTable)` takes `$a2` and pushes the offset to `$t0`) - there the residual is which pseudo wins `$a1`/`$a2`, and a typed struct chain for the same offsets scores WORSE (59.85 / 452), because gcc's emission for the typed form differs.

- id: g-the-rebuild-loop-counter-is-the-shared-index-variable | keywords: loop, counter, callee-saved, swapped, shared, variable, index, live-range
  **WHEN A FUNCTION HAS A REBUILD LOOP AND A LATER/OTHER ARM THAT USES AN INDEX VARIABLE, RETAIL'S CALLEE-SAVED HAND-OUT USES THE SAME REGISTER FOR BOTH - so the loop counter IS that variable, and a fresh `int i` mirrors the pair** (round 443, field/main/misc7 func_80099214, Default preset, 97.91 -> 97.99 with the 12 register-diff lines on the loop gone). `for (walkmesh = 0; walkmesh < g_FieldWalkmeshTriCount - 1; walkmesh++)` with `walkmesh` also used as the walkmesh id in the tail gives retail's `$s1` counter / `$s0` normals-base pair, because one pseudo with disjoint live ranges ranks in global.c as the tail's variable does; a separate `int i` gives `i` `$s0` and the base `$s1`, the mirror. Declaring the counter in the `for()` or as a `while` with `walkmesh++` at the bottom compiles byte-identically, so the lever is the VARIABLE, not the loop syntax. Its residue here is that reorg then has only the result store to fill the `bnez` slot with (loop.c would have had to hoist the `a2 = i` argument copy to leave retail's `addu a2,s1,zero` in the slot), which is worth one instruction and is not reachable from source.

- id: g-a-plus-one-in-the-loop-test-is-what-hoists-the-argument-copy | keywords: loop, hoist, movable, argument, copy, preheader, latch, test, giv
  **A LOOP-ARGUMENT COPY THAT RETAIL HOISTS INTO A PREHEADER COPY PLUS A RE-COPY AFTER THE BIV INCREMENT IS REACHED BY PUTTING A `+ 1` IN THE LOOP TEST - that literal sum is what makes loop.c treat the copy as a movable - AND THE SAME `+ 1` COSTS A SECOND ADD OFF THE INCREMENTED COUNTER, SO THE HOIST AND RETAIL'S 3-INSTRUCTION `< n - 1` TEST ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE** (round 455, field/main/misc7 func_80099214, Default preset, the residue the round-443 entry above called unreachable). Retail is `addiu s0,sp,0x58 / addu a2,s1,zero` then the loop head, and `bnez v0,<loop> / addu a2,s1,zero` at the back edge with the result store inside the block; the honest `for (walkmesh = 0; walkmesh < g_FieldWalkmeshTriCount - 1; walkmesh++)` keeps one `a2 = walkmesh` copy at the loop head, reorg sinks the `sh` into the `bnez` slot and the body is 1896 bytes / 474 insns against retail's 1900 / 475 (97.99%). Spelling the test `walkmesh + 1 <= g_FieldWalkmeshTriCount - 1` reproduces BOTH copies and puts the store back in the block, but gcc then needs `walkmesh + 1` off the already-incremented counter (`addu v0,s1,1`), so the body is 1904 / 476 with frame 0xB8 instead of retail's 0xC0 - 98.89% and one instruction over; the `walkmesh + 1 < g_FieldWalkmeshTriCount` bound is retail's exact 1900 / 475 at 98.50% but its guard degenerates to `slt $t1,count / beq` where retail has `addiu v0,v0,-1 / blez` and it burns `$t1`. Measured dead on the same body, none of which hoists: `walkmesh <= g_FieldWalkmeshTriCount - 2` (97.71 / 1896), a reversed `count - 1 > walkmesh`, an empty `do { } while (0)` before or after the store, splitting the call result into a local, a separate `triIndex` copy of the index, and one 3-minute permuter run (973 iterations) which found only the `+ 1` test. So read a missing preheader/latch copy pair as "the original's test had an arithmetic operator on the induction variable", then count the instructions: if retail's test is bare, the copy is not source-reachable after all. Re-measured round 469: the `walkmesh + 1 < g_FieldWalkmeshTriCount` form is NOT a step toward the match even at retail's exact 1900 bytes / 475 insns, because the `+ 1` giv takes `$v0` and pushes the switch root's `li v0,1` to `$t1` (148 differing lines against the honest body's 141) and its frame is 0xB8 / vars 128 where retail is 0xC0 / vars 136 - i.e. the exact-size form is worse on every other residual, so park the honest `< n - 1` body.


- id: g-two-preheader-inits-are-one-comma-statement | keywords: loop, preheader, counter, init, move, lui, addiu, comma, statement-order
  **A PREHEADER THAT ZEROES THE COUNTER AND THEN FORMS THE WALKED BASE (`move a3,zero` / `lui a2,%hi(g_Table)` / `addiu a2,a2,%lo`) IS ONE `for (i = 0, p = g_Table; ...)` INIT, NOT `p = g_Table;` FOLLOWED BY THE `for`** (round 453, world_map/main/misc10 func_8008A5B8, 90.48 -> 92.63%, XenoWorldMapDiv, 93 insns both: with it the whole body except the prologue is exact, 14 differing lines -> 12; measured in the same edit as dropping a `void* pSprite` temp, so the two together own the 2.15 points and the preheader hunk is the part visibly gone). The two-statement form let cse/sched2 put the base's `lui/addiu` first and the `move a3,zero` after it, while retail has the counter's zeroing first, which is the order a left-to-right comma init forces. Cheap and byte-neutral to try on any loop whose only non-prologue residual is the order of two preheader instructions. CONFIRMED TO CLOSE A MATCH (round 480, world_map/main/misc11_c func_8008C530, 97.12 -> 100.00% at retail's exact 444 bytes / 111 insns): after the gear arm's `goto`-labelled dispatch was settled, the only residual was exactly this pair - retail `move a3,zero` (i = 0) then `lui/addiu a2,%hi(g_WorldMapTrail)`, ours the other way round - and the comma init `for (i = 0, pTrail = g_WorldMapTrail; i < 0x20; i++, pTrail++)` was the whole of the last 2.88 points. The same unit's misc10 func_8008A5B8 body already carries this spelling, so this function was a port, not a find.

- id: cse-merges-one-offset-expression-across-a-two-way-join | keywords: cse, duplicate, expression, join, merge, inline, helper, callee-saved, offset
  **TWO TEXTUALLY IDENTICAL OFFSET EXPRESSIONS ARE ONE PSEUDO TO gcc EVEN ACROSS A TWO-PREDECESSOR JOIN, SO A BODY WHOSE RETAIL RE-FORMS THE OFFSET AFTER THE JOIN CANNOT SPELL IT TWICE - BUT PUTTING EACH COPY BEHIND A TINY INLINED HELPER MAKES TWO SEPARATE RTL TREES AND THE RE-FORMING APPEARS** (round 482, battle/main/misc13 func_800881B8, Default, parked 87.06% / 492 bytes / 123 insns against retail 500 / 125; the old park was 79.52% / 472 / 118 with a 40-byte frame). Retail computes `ofsB = (u8)arg1 * 0x1C` once into `$v0` before the early-out compare and AGAIN into `$s2` after the `sel` ladder's join, while `ofsA` is formed twice more (`$v1` at the compare, `$a1` after the `BattleReleaseCharSlot` call) - i.e. four offset computations in 125 instructions. Spelling all four inline measures 63.31% / 464 / 116 (gcc forms one pseudo, hoists the symbol address into a register and drops the `lui at,%hi(sym) / addu at,at,ofs` store form entirely); spelling `ofsA`/`ofsB` as function locals measures 78.02% / 496 / 124 with both offsets in callee-saved registers and a 40-byte frame. Inserting `static inline s32 SlotRecordOffset(s32 i) { return (u8)i * 0x1C; }` and using it for the compare's SECOND index and for `ofsB` gives retail's split (top copy in `$v0`, post-join copy in `$s2`, `$a1` for ofsA) at 87.06%, frame 32 and the saved set ra/s0/s1/s2 exact - the inliner emits the multiply as its own expression so cse cannot unify it with the inline spelling at the other site. The helper is not shippable-looking C; treat it as the probe that proves which two values retail kept separate, then look for a spelling that duplicates the expression naturally. Same-function lessons: a `u8 slot` local for `(u8)arg0` used at the call and at a later `slot < 3` test is what puts retail's `andi s0,a0,0xFF` in the branch delay slot and `sltiu s0,s0,3` off the same register; and a `u16 param` temp assigned in both arms of an if/else is what reproduces a cross-jumped shared `sh` (retail's `j` plus one store at the join). Residual left there: gcc forwards the `sb g_BattleSlotRecords[ofsA]` into the next two loads (retail reloads both, two instructions), and the permuter's only fix for that is marking the shared global `volatile`, which is not usable in a unit whose other functions are matched.

  - id: a-loaded-byte-in-its-own-local-breaks-an-index-cse | keywords: cse, reload, index, multiply, local, join, permuter, byte
  **THE NATURAL SPELLING THE LEVER ABOVE ASKS FOR IS A LOCAL HOLDING THE LOADED BYTE AT THE SECOND SITE: `slot = *p;` between the two uses, with the second site reading `Table[slot]`, keeps the load CSE'd but makes the INDEX TREE different from the first site's `Table[*p]`, so cc1 re-forms the whole `sll/subu/sll` multiply after the branch join** (round 490, battle/main/misc12 func_80084854, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0; 87.82% / 536 bytes / 134 insns -> 91.30% / 556 / 139 against retail's 548 / 137, permuter score 1360 -> 1200). Retail loads `*p`, computes `*p * 0x1C` and reads two u16s, and after the `if (dx < 0)` arm's two-way join does the SAME five instructions again (lbu / nop / sll / subu / sll) for the x axis; every inline spelling lets cse keep the multiply and the address `addu at,at,<index reg>` reuses it. One `u8 slot` local assigned just before the second site, used only there, gives retail's re-form - and the bgez arm that follows then also takes retail's shared-delay-slot `mult` shape. Companion measurement: using the same local at BOTH sites puts the two index trees back in one class (86.87%, 536 bytes), so the local must appear at one site only. Not measured here: whether a `volatile` cast achieves the same without the extra local.

symptoms: loop rotated or not, constant hoisted or reloaded
try: loop hoist invariant rotated

- id: d-do-not-hoist-an-expression-retail-computes-in-every-arm | keywords: hoist, division, arms, local, sra, size, inline
  **IF RETAIL SHOWS THE SAME `bgez/addiu/sra` DIVISION SEQUENCE IN EVERY ARM OF A NESTED IF/ELSE, THE ORIGINAL WROTE THE DIVISION INSIDE EACH CONDITION: a hoisted `position = x / 256;` local costs one sequence per OUTER arm (2 instead of 4 = 6 instructions short) while every other instruction already matches** (round 492, menu/main/misc2 func_801C8324, XenoMenu260: hoisted local 116 insns / 464 bytes / 72.89%, division inline in each condition retail's 126 / 504 / 100.00%). Judge it on the instruction COUNT first - a body that is short by one copy of a 3-instruction sequence per arm is this, not the allocator.

- id: g-which-four-invariants-are-hoisted | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, callee-saved, frame, rematerialise, saved-set, local
  **THE SAVED SET NAMES WHICH LOOP INVARIANTS RETAIL KEPT, AND A BODY CAN ONLY MATCH IF gcc HOISTS THE SAME FOUR: a park whose calls, frame size and per-iteration instruction stream are already retail's can still be 2 insns short purely because the four callee-saved registers hold different invariants** (round 433, slus_006.64/system/temp3 func_8001B970, re-parked 86.53% / 404 bytes / 101 insns against retail's 424 / 103, Default preset). Retail keeps `$s0` = the byte offset `i`, `$s1` = `pRow = base + i`, `$s2`/`$s3` = `inBuf + 1` / `inBuf` and REMATERIALISES both the odd byte's base (`lui t2,%hi(g_GameState+1)` / `addiu t2,t2,%lo(...)` per row) and the terminator `0xF` (`li t1,0xf` per row); every body tried keeps `i`, the source base, `outBuf`'s address and `0xF` instead, so `inBuf`'s address is recomputed per row into a caller-saved register and the odd base takes a fifth callee-saved. Spelling the odd base as its own pointer local (`u8 *pOdd = (u8 *)&g_GameState + 1;` read `pOdd[i + j]`) does not stop the hoist (84.11% / 420 bytes / 105 insns, six saves) and neither does hoisting the `inBuf`/`inBuf + 1` pairs to pre-loop pointers (identical code: gcc deletes the dead stores). So before hunting an address form, diff the SAVED SET and the two cheapest rematerialisations (`lui/addiu` of a constant address, `li` of a small constant) -  Round 456 second measurement, menu/main/misc3 func_801CB184 (89.15% / 268 bytes / 66 insns under XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, retail 280 / 66): the same loop without the bank load and testing `bnez` on 0 instead of `!= 0xF` parks on the SAME fifth save, and there the culprit is visible in one line - retail's `lui %hi(g_GameState+1)`/`addiu %lo(...)` sits at the TOP OF THE OUTER BODY in the call-clobbered `$t0`, while the compile folds it to `addiu $s2,$s0,1` in the PROLOGUE off the strength-reduced row pointer `$s0` (= `&g_GameState` there), where the plain `addiu` IS hoistable. The two spellings of the odd base (`u8 *pOdd = (u8*)&g_GameState + 1` read `pOdd[offset + j]`, and the bare `((u8*)&g_GameState)[offset + j + 1]`) are BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the fold is cse/combine's, not the source's: a `high` insn cannot be hoisted but `symbol+1` folded onto a register that already holds the base can, and the even read's LSR pointer always provides that register. -O3 87.02, 2.7.2 86.42, cdk rejects the body.
  Round 459 third measurement, slus_006.64/system/temp3_b func_8001B970 (Default, re-parked 89.50% / 404 / 101 against retail's 412 / 103 - the best body this function has had, +3 points over the round-433 park): the body to start from is B1 (`pRow` advanced 0x14 per row, even read `pRow[j]`, odd read `((u8*)&g_GameState)[rowOffset + j + 1]` with `rowOffset = i;` the first statement of the row body, which is the only shape that reproduces retail's `move t0,s0`), and the one edit that pays is INDEXING the row copy's source (`*pDst++ = outBuf[k++]`) instead of walking a `pOut` pointer: that removes `outBuf`'s address from the invariant set and with it B1's fifth save (84.02 / 416 / 104 -> 89.50 / 404 / 101), so the same body then keeps `i`, `pRow`, `0xF` and `s1+1` and rematerialises the `inBuf` pair. Measured dead on the 89.50 body: the odd index spelled `i` instead of `rowOffset` (drops retail's `move t0,s0`, 88.60 / 400 / 100); outer loop as `do {} while`, byte-identical; and the fully typed form `pSrc = (u8*)g_GameState.strings` with `sizeof(g_GameState.strings)` / `sizeof(StringEntry)` bounds, which is 86.44 / 416 / 104 because a `size_t` bound turns retail's `slti` into `sltiu` and cse folds the odd base back onto the row pointer (`1(v1)`, plus `$s4` = outBuf) - use a signed literal bound when the typed spelling is wanted. Residual left: the row preheader is one insn short (`addiu s3,s1,1` where retail has `lui`+`addiu` of `%hi/%lo(g_GameState+1)`), the `s3` save/restore pair, retail's `bne` delay slot `addiu a0,a0,2` against our `nop`, and `sltu` vs `slt` on the row-copy compare.
  Round 461 fourth measurement, same function (still parked at 90.07% / 420 / 105): the fold and the walk are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE from source, and the fold's trigger is the register copy of the symbol address (`pRow = (u8*)&g_GameState;`), not the odd read's spelling. With no pointer to the symbol anywhere - both inner reads indexed off the bare counter (`inBuf[j] = ((u8*)&g_GameState)[i + j]; inBuf[j + 1] = ((u8*)&g_GameState)[i + j + 1];`, row copy `pDst = (u8*)&g_GameState + i;` walked with `(int)` casts) - gcc emits retail's own residual (`lui`+`addiu %hi/%lo(g_GameState+1)` and `li 0xf` per row) in retail's four saves with no `$s4`, at the price of the LSR walk (two `addu` per iteration where retail has `move a0,s1` then `addiu a0,a0,2` in the bne slot) and of those two invariants being hoisted a SECOND level, out of the outer loop, which rotates it (`move a3,zero` in the backedge slot): 89.19% / 404 / 101. Adding back only a walking pointer for the row copy re-creates the fold (84.40 / 416 / 104), and adding `rowOffset = i;` for retail's `move t0,s0` does the same (86.33 / 420 / 105). So a body here can have retail's saved set or retail's walk, not both; the remaining 2 insns are the row preheader.
- id: g-pointer-locals-mint-a-derived-giv-per-base | keywords: loop, giv, induction, pointer, frame, callee-saved, row, stride
  **THREE ROW POINTERS INCREMENTED PER ITERATION COST gcc ONE DERIVED INDUCTION VARIABLE PER BASE (`pAhead`, `pAhead+4`, `pBehind`, `pBehind+4`, `pDest+4`), WHICH IS TWO CALLEE-SAVED REGISTERS AND A FRAME THAT RETAIL DOES NOT HAVE; spelling the two outer rows as `(pDest + stride)[k]` lets gcc derive them from the `pDest` biv and the frame disappears** (round 430, slus_006.64/system/system func_80034FFC, 58.11 -> 60.59 -> 66.79%, 424 retail insns / 1696 bytes against 421/1684, 413/1652 and 391/1564). Retail's backbone is four increments in the latch (`addu t3,t3,t4` / `addu t1,t1,t4` / `addu t2,t2,t4` / `addu a2,a2,t4` = the three rows plus one `pDest+4` giv), the word accesses stay 0/2/4 immediates off the two row registers, the stride is loop-invariant in `t4`, and the loop needs no callee-saved register at all. With the pointer locals the compile instead gives every base its own +4 giv and the loop no longer fits in caller-saved registers, so the count of `addu <reg>,<reg>,<stride>` in the latch is the thing to read in the diff before trying spellings. The inline form then overshoots the other way: gcc picks the `pDest+4` giv as the loop variable and re-derives `pDest`/`pBehind` from it (`move a2,a0`, a `subu` per use). Recomputing the two row pointers as statements at the top of the body scores 63.23% - between the two.
- id: g-hoist-the-row-pointer-and-the-id-pointer | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, index, pointer-walk, scale, andi, induction, mult, array
  **A LOOP-INVARIANT SCALED BASE THAT RETAIL KEEPS IN A SAVED REGISTER (`fp = arg0*0x48`, then `addu v0,fp,%lo(ids)` + `addu v0,v0,i`) IS NOT RE-FORMED PER ITERATION IF THE SOURCE HOLDS THE ELEMENT POINTER: `u16 *pRows = &g_BattleCommandRows[arg0 * 0x24]` read as `pRows[i]` gives retail's walked `s3` (`la` once, `lh/lhu 0(s3)`, `addiu s3,s3,2` in the latch), and the same for the sibling index** (round 428, battle/main/misc13 func_80085618, park 60.72 -> 63.97 with the row pointer and 64.20% / 1140 bytes with `u8 *pCmd = &g_BattleActorCommandIds[arg0 * 0x48]` + `switch (pCmd[i])`, Default preset; retail 1196 bytes / 299 insns, still 14 insns short). Indexing the same array inline makes cc1 re-form `(u8)arg0 * 0x48` from an `andi 0xff` at EVERY site (5 insns for the id read, 2 per row read - 20+ insns over ten sites) even though the identical scaled value was computed in the prologue, because the loop's expression reaches it through a fresh QImode pseudo. Generalises to any `arr[invariant + i]` read in many arms of a switch: hoist the element pointer, not the offset. Watch the trade: the pointer walk gives ONE induction variable where retail may have TWO (the offset form), so expect the frame and saved set to shift - re-read retail's latch before crediting the gain.
- id: c-a-volatile-global-read-does-not-stop-the-latch-hoist | keywords: delay-slot, load-delay, reorg, volatile, read, increment, latch, hoist
  **A `volatile` READ OF THE GLOBAL WHOSE LOAD DELAY SLOT IS BEING FILLED DOES NOT STOP REORG HOISTING THE LOOP INCREMENT INTO IT - only the store side of that lever exists** (round 455, battle/main/misc1 func_80072938, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0, still parked 95.62% / 348 bytes against retail's 352). The parked body's last chain is `lw $2,g_BattlePrimStartIndex` and cc1's own `.s` puts the latch `addu $18,$18,1` in that load's delay slot plus the b0 `sb` in the `bnez` slot; writing the last index as `*(volatile s32 *)&g_BattlePrimStartIndex + prim` with a `*(volatile u_char *)&pPrim[...].b0` store compiles BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the same volatile-store body (352 bytes, store after the `slt`, one instruction displaced from retail), and a `while (i < last) { ...; volatile store; i++; }` body reaches retail's size and retail's bnez-slot `nop` while the increment is STILL in the load slot. So a load delay slot is filled from a long forward scan of the block past every insn that uses the loaded register, a volatile load is no barrier, and any body whose increment cannot be emitted after the loop test stays 4 bytes short of this shape - park it.

- id: g-index-form-keeps-the-divisor-in-the-loop | keywords: loop, hoist, division, divisor, index, pointer-walk, frame, spill
  **A LOOP-INVARIANT DIVISOR THAT RETAIL RE-COMPUTES EVERY ITERATION (`srl/addu/sra` right before a variable `div`) IS KEPT IN THE LOOP BY INDEXING THE ARRAY AT THE TOP OF THE BODY INSTEAD OF WALKING A POINTER - and with it go the spill, the +8 frame and the whole saved-register block** (round 427, battling/main/misc5 func_8007DC74, 78.83 -> 80.47 with the frame going 0x70 -> retail's 0x68 and the saved set 0x48.. -> retail's 0x40..). Retail's spray loop divides by `dy / 2` at the `div`; the pointer-walk body (`for (i = 0; i < N; i++, pSlot++)`, everything reachable through the walking pointer) made cc1 hoist the shift pair into the preheader, allocate it a stack slot at sp+0x40 and push every saved register 8 bytes up. Writing `pSlot = &((BattleSpriteSlot *)g_BattleSpriteSlots)[i];` as the first statement of the body keeps the divisor in the loop and reproduces retail's frame and epilogue exactly, and it also pulls the `spread - (len2 >> 31)` correction back into the `rand()` delay slot where retail has it. The trade it makes is the induction pair: the index form gives ONE biv (a byte offset counted in the latch, `s1 = base + offset` formed once) where retail keeps TWO (base and base+2, both incremented), so a body can be at retail's frame and still 2 instructions short - use this lever for the frame/hoist half, then look for the second induction variable separately. Measured worse on the same function: the correction inlined at its four uses (74.59, 236 insns) and an early `pBase` local with `&pBase[i]` (79.81, 230 insns, it reloads the table base after the intervening calls).
- id: g-a-named-offset-local-pins-the-giv | keywords: giv, offset, induction, cse, fold, symbol, local, loop
  **NAMING ONE OF A LOOP'S TWO BYTE-OFFSET SUBEXPRESSIONS IN ITS OWN LOCAL IS WHAT PINS THE GIV PAIR cse OTHERWISE RE-FOLDS INTO ONE BASE PLUS A SYMBOL ADDEND** (round 419, battle/main/misc3 func_8007819C, 98.39 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 372 bytes / 93 insns, Default preset). Retail keeps two offset induction variables, A = 0x60+0xC0k (used by both symbol stores `D_800D36C0 + A` / `g_BattleTextSlotBuffers + A` and by the RECT copy destination `slotRects + A`) and B = 0xC0k (used only by the `&slotRects[i*0x60] - 0x50` argument), and the two stores show the symbol re-formed each iteration (`lui at,%hi(D_800D36C0); addu at,at,A; sw v0,0(at)`). Every spelling that computed the store offset inline from the loop index got it canonicalised as `symbol+0x60 + B` (relocation `D_800D3720`, `sw v0,96(at)`), so A and B traded `$s3`/`$s0` and the body sat at 98.39 with retail's exact size and instruction count; writing the OTHER offset into a named local before its two uses (`offPrev = i * sizeof(Row);`) restores retail's pair and the whole function matches (permuter found it in 74 iterations, base 420 best 0). Measured on the same body: the loop rewritten as a typed struct-array index (`g_BattleTextSlotRects[i].pBuf`, `[i + 1].pBuf`, `[i].rect`) is 90.23% / 101 insns because cc1 emits `lui/addu` per `arr[i]` access instead of strength-reducing it, and giving BOTH offsets their own explicit incremented locals (init 0x60 and 0, `+= 0xC0` at the bottom) is 90.00% / 95 insns because cse then re-derives the copy destination from the rect pointer. Companion negative from the same round: a typed `POLY_FT4 *p` walk with `->` members does NOT stop loop.c minting a field giv (func_80076D58 measures 92.31% identically to the `u8 *` + byte-offset form), so g-index-form-makes-the-field-givs does not transfer to a do-while whose cursor is a pointer.
- id: g-giv-preheader-order-follows-the-use | keywords: loop, giv, preheader, hoist, strength, order, accumulator, inline
  **A STRENGTH-REDUCED BASE THAT RETAIL HOISTS INTO THE PREHEADER IN A GIVEN ORDER COMES OUT IN RETAIL'S ORDER ONLY WHEN THE SCALED EXPRESSION SITS INLINE AT ITS USE (a call argument, with the invariant part a plain scalar set before the loop) - hoisting it into a source local at the top of the loop body records that giv at the wrong point and swaps the preheader `li` pairs** (round 418, shop_menu/main/misc func_801CEB3C, 99.92 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 1892 bytes / 473 insns, XenoLibrary preset; the park had been measured six ways over two rounds and two permuter runs). Retail's preheader is `li s8,0x1000 / li s7,0x3020 / lui+lw g_Menu / li s6,0x49 / lw pShop / li s5,0x27B0`; the park's `x = 0x49 + j * 0x1A;` at the top of the loop body plus `for (k = 0, col = x; k < 3; )` + `col += 8` gave s6=0x27B0 and s5=0x49 (six instructions, the two `move s1,sN` copies, one `addu`, two latch addius and the `li` pair). The closing spelling is the one the matched twin GearShopMenuBuildPurchaseItemDetails uses (gear_shop_menu/main/render.c): `x = 0x49;` before the outer loop and, in the func call's argument list, `(j * FONT_LETTER_HEIGHT * 2) + x + (k * MENU_DIGIT_SPACING)` - so cc1 derives TWO givs from the one use, the outer one (`li 0x49`, `addiu 0x1A` in the outer latch) recorded where cse creates it, and the inner one (`addu s1,s6,zero` at loop entry, `addiu s1,s1,8` in the latch) exactly as retail has them. Generalisable: read the retail preheader as giv-recording order = source order of the USES, and do not introduce a source accumulator or a pre-loop `x = base + j*stride` assignment for a value the original likely wrote inline.
- id: g-scaled-record-index-is-a-giv | keywords: loop, giv, strength, reduce, multiply, sizeof, index, allocator
  **A SCALED RECORD INDEX IN A HOT INNER LOOP IS STRENGTH-REDUCED INTO ITS OWN INDUCTION REGISTER WHATEVER THE SPELLING, AND THAT ONE REGISTER IS WHAT SHIFTS THE WHOLE ALLOCATION** (round 406, battle/main/misc29 func_800B7424, parked 73.66% at 1092 bytes / 273 insns against retail's 1100 / 275 under XenoBattleTailCdk0). Retail recomputes the sprite address every iteration - `sll v0,fp,0x5 / subu v0,v0,fp / sll v0,v0,0x2` (column * 0x7C) then `addu v1,pWork+blockOffset / +rowBytes / addu s2,v1,v0` - and keeps `radius` in a STACK SLOT (0x48) while `$fp` holds the column counter; cc1 2.7.2-cdk instead makes `col * 0x7C` a mult giv (`addiu sN,sN,124` in the latch), spills the column counter to make room, keeps `radius` in `$fp`, and then every record address and every store through it differs (269 of 550 lines). `col * sizeof(BattleEffectSprite)` and `&((BattleEffectSprite *)base)[col]` compile to the SAME code, so a typed index is not the escape. - id: g-hoisted-loop-invariant-constant | keywords: loop, hoist, cc1, move, prologue
  **A hoisted loop-invariant constant CAN be stopped from source (round 327; this corrects the round-316 note below).** `loop.c` hoists a constant iff `threshold * savings * m->lifetime >= insn_count`, where `threshold = (loop_has_call ? 1 : 2) * (1 + n_non_fixed_regs)`, `savings` is the number of loads of that value (doubled by `combine_movables` when two loads set the same constant), `lifetime` is the luid span between that value's first and last USE, and `insn_count` is the loop's real-insn count. So you shrink `lifetime` by moving the two uses CLOSER together, or raise `savings` by forcing one load per use. Measured on the animation-script VM: `-9` hoisted at life 14-16 and at 7 but NOT at 5-6, and `0xF03FFFFF` hoisted at 7 but not at 6 - eliminating both took the body 72.61 -> 91.20 with its prologue byte-identical to retail's. Diagnose with `cc1 -dL` on the unit's `.i` inside the container and read `Insn N: regno R (life L), move-insn savings S moved / not desirable`. A hoisted TABLE BASE is still not defeatable (the round-316 probes); an invariant CONSTANT is.
  Round 446 addendum (slus_006.64/system/sound SoundSpuMemoryAllocateBlock, re-measured 94.58% / retail's exact 256 bytes / 64 insns, 40 differing lines, all one cause): read the two loop heads side by side to see WHICH shape of the hoist you are fighting. Retail's is a fresh two-instruction constant load (`lui v1,%hi(Arr)` / `addiu v1,v1,%lo(Arr)` in the `lh`'s load-delay slot) because no register in its loop equals `&Arr` (its `la s1` IS pPrevBlock, overwritten by `move s1,a0`); the compile's is a one-instruction `move a2,s0` plus a `nop` filler, because the preheader `la` left `&Arr` in the register that later becomes pPrevBlock, so `move_movables` moved the REG_EQUAL register instead of the symbol. Both are per-iteration copies at the same slot, so this is not 'hoisted vs not hoisted' and the threshold arithmetic above does not apply - and the register snapshot is what then swaps the whole callee-saved pair. Pointer arithmetic on the struct type (`Arr + pPrevBlock->nextBlockIndex`) is byte-identical to the `(u8 *)Arr + (i << 4)` cast form (the 15th spelling on that function).
  Addendum (round 435, battle/main/misc35 func_800C11CC, parked 67.82% / 3700 bytes against retail's 3708): the dump names the numbers on ONE line each, so read it before hunting a spelling - `Insn 935: regno 399 (life 9), move-insn savings 9  moved to 2336` against `Loop from 10 to 2321: 995 real insns` was the ONLY movable in a 927-insn function to move, and it stays 9/9 after two different source attacks. Two facts this measures: **each merged `set reg,const K` load contributes `savings 3`, not 1** (three merged const-1 loads -> savings 9), and **dropping one *use* does not drop the group's savings**: rewriting that function's `(flags & 3) != 1` test as `(flags & 3) - 1 != 0` (which removes the const-1 load entirely) produced byte-identical 925 insns / 3700 bytes with the hoist intact, and hoisting its `1 << mode` into a local whose result is consumed on the next line left both savings AND `life` at 9. So the source-side knob on a wide gap (`81 * threshold >= 995` here) is only reachable when a spelling changes the *mode* of the constant (`a-constant-cse-is-per-mode`) or deletes whole arms; on a body whose merged uses live in arms retail materialises separately, park and record the -dL line instead of permuting. Round 461 closed the last source-side route on that body: casting the group's store constant to the field's own width (`pSpriteData->animScriptWaitTimer = (s16)1;` into an `s16` field) is folded back to the same SImode const - byte-identical 925 insns / 3700 bytes, `li $s7,1` still in the preheader - so the mode knob is only reachable when the constant's OWN type changes, not when the destination's width is narrower. The same round priced the residual exactly: retail materialises 13 `addiu $x,$zero,0x1` sites, the compile 10 plus that one hoisted `li $s7,1` (three uses), so breaking the hoist would pay the 2-insn / 8-byte deficit AND the 9th saved register at once - count literal materialisations on both sides to check whether a loop-invariant park has one cause or many.

- id: g-two-sequential-do-while | keywords: loop, hoist, li, lui, volatile
  **TWO sequential `do {} while (0)` blocks place hoisted constants where ONE block cannot** (round 325): a do-block's preheader is where `loop.c` hoists one invariant constant per free register, so a single block puts two constants together at its head, while splitting the group into two blocks puts each constant where retail has it - and a constant that must hoist above two volatile stores has to be INSIDE the second block. If a park's residual is two `li`/`lui` constants landing in the wrong places, count the blocks before the registers.
- id: g-hoisted-constant-sits-after | keywords: loop, hoist, li, preheader, argument, la, permuter
  **A hoisted invariant constant that sits AFTER your preheader statements is a preheader SOURCE STATEMENT boundary, and removing the statements to move it costs the copy they were buying.** round 393, movie/main/misc1 func_800704E8 (gcc 2.6.0, parked 99.04 at retail's exact 2276 bytes / 569 insns): retail's preheader is `ori s3,zero,1` / `lui+addiu s4,&g_MovieStreamReadCount` / `addu s2,s1,pWork`, our body emits the last two first and the hoisted `li` last, and the residual is that one row plus the `la a0` of the block's format string. Measured negatives: an empty `do { } while (0);` between the call and the two statements moves nothing (identical rows); inlining the counters base (`pCounter = (u32*)g_MovieStreamReadCount`) drops the s4 copy (97.69, 2264 bytes, 566 insns); assigning `pBase = pWork;` at the top of the in-loop teardown instead of before the loop drops the s2 copy (99.05 but 2272 bytes / 568 insns, so it can never link). Both preheader copies are the source statements, so the hoist's position is not source-reachable from there. A 4-minute permuter run on such a body is blind: base 460 = best 460 over 1067 iterations, because the reloc-name-only rows dominate the score - do not spend a second run on it.
- id: g-switch-dispatch-makes-loop | keywords: loop, hoist, frame, goto, switch, callee-saved, case, lui
  **A `for (;;) { switch ... }` dispatch makes `loop.c` hoist invariants to the FUNCTION preheader; write the dispatch as a `goto` loop instead** (round 329, the strongest lever of that round). `for (;;) { switch (x) { case ...: } }` gives the outer construct LOOP notes, so every invariant constant in every arm is hoisted once, into the function preheader - which is what pushes constants into the wrong callee-saved registers and changes the frame. Rewriting the dispatch as `dispatch: ... goto dispatch;` removes those outer loop notes so EACH inner loop hoists its own copy, which is what retail's per-preheader `lui`/`ori` look like. That closed `field/misc5` func_800A5924's last two residuals with no register change at all (frame 0x40 -> 0x38).
- id: g-while-if-x-k | keywords: loop, hoist, li, move
  **`while (1) { if (x != K) break; ... }` stops `duplicate_loop_exit_test` rotating a loop** where `while (x == K)` rotates it (95.13 vs the matched form), and a **comma init in a `for`** (`for (i = 0, n = 0x2c0; ...)`) is what puts the zero move before the constant's `li`. Both measured on the same body (round 329).
- id: g-rotated-entry-j-to-bottom-test | keywords: loop, hoist, rotated, entry, j, beq, thread, preheader, jtbl
  **A retail loop whose entry evaluates the condition in the PREHEADER and `j`s straight to the single bottom test (`j .Ltest` landing on the `bne`, constants in the two delay slots: `ori a3` in the `j`'s, the comparand's `li` hoisted as far as an earlier branch's delay) was NOT reproduced from ANY loop spelling under gcc 2.6.0, 2.7.2 or 2.7.2-cdk** (round 398, battle/main/misc1 func_800723E0, parked 77.55 at 352 bytes vs retail's 332 / 88 vs 83 insns; probed with cc1_probe.sh under all three compilers). `duplicate_loop_exit_test` gives the two-eval ROTATED form but keeps the entry's own inline branch: while/for/do-while/guarded-do-while/goto-check shapes all emit [preheader: eval; `beq` -> exit][body][eval; `bne` -> body], 4+ instructions over retail's [preheader: eval; `j` bottom-test][body][eval; `bne`]. The threading of the entry branch into the bottom one may need a compiler pass none of the three has (gcc 2.8+? not in tools/). Cost of the residual is also register-wide: the shared branch is what lets retail keep the comparand (`t0`=1) and the wrap constant (`a3`=0xB) in registers across the loop and lets the exit handler reuse the loop's slot register.
