Park on this shape and say ROTATED_ENTRY; worth re-probing if a 2.8.x preset is ever added. Companion structural facts from the same body, all measured: an if/else chain with the reset-call arm LAST gives retail's `bnez`-forward-to-end block layout (`if (mask == 0) { ... } else { Reset(); }`), a `func(0)` call shared by two arms placed AFTER the inner if/else cross-jumps into the one call block retail shares three ways, and a mid-loop `func(0); return;` exit jumps directly to that shared block just like retail's `beq` at the loop head.
- id: g-a-break-at-the-body-top-buys-the-frame-not-the-entry | keywords: loop, frame, vars, entry, break, duplicate, while, preheader
  **THE LOOP-EXIT-TEST DUPLICATION AND THE SPURIOUS `vars=8` FRAME SLOT ARE TWO SEPARATE SYMPTOMS: a spelling that removes the duplication does NOT recover retail's entry, and the one that recovers the frame costs instructions elsewhere** (round 485, battling/main/misc15 func_8008BD70, XenoBattleDiv = gcc-2.7.2-psx; retail `addiu sp,-0x20` / 55 insns / 232 bytes with `j .Ltest` and one `bne`). `i = count; while (1) { if (--i == -1) break; ... }` measures 81.64% / 232 bytes / 58 insns at retail's exact frame 32 and saves-stores, and `i = count; while (--i != -1)` measures 87.64% / 236 / 59 at frame 32 - against 93.67% / 228 / 57 at frame 40 for `i = count - 1; while (i != -1) { ...; i--; }`. The 93.67% body wins because cc1 folds `count - 1 == -1` into `beqz count` at the entry, i.e. the fold is what keeps the duplication to ONE extra instruction; kill the fold (both spellings above) and the entry costs `li -1 / beq` instead. Read a frame 8 bytes over retail's as evidence that the entry test was duplicated, not as a separate residual to chase.

- id: g-construct-decides-loop-c | keywords: loop, hoist, do-while, goto
  **THE CONSTRUCT DECIDES `loop.c`'s INVARIANT HOISTING, not only the cost model** (round 338): `field/misc4` func_80078D44 refused to match while its stream loop was written `for`/`while`, and the `do { ... } while (ArchiveDataSync() != 0);` form is what stopped retail's constants being hoisted out of the loop - the body then matched at 100.00 with retail's exact 1348 bytes. So before tuning the cost model (round 327's lifetime/savings rule), change the loop CONSTRUCT: do-while, while, guard+bottom-test and goto each give loop.c different notes.
  Round 495 addendum (slus_006.64/system/animation_scripts func_80022660, XenoGraphics = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -O2 -G8; parked 95.81% / 788 bytes = retail's exact size): read the -dL numbers before guessing the life you need, because the file goes to `<dumpbase>.loop` and NOT to stderr. On that loop the dump says `Loop from 14 to 454: 180 real insns` with `Insn 158: regno 129 (life 15), move-insn savings 1  moved to 465` and `Insn 237: regno 149 (life 6), move-insn savings 1 not desirable`, i.e. with insn_count 180 the cut is life 7-8 and the ONLY surviving positions are the ones that leave the constant's two uses ~6 insns apart. There, retail reuses 0xF03FFFFF across a 15-insn window (a tail RMW and the `if (count == 0)` block after it), so the instruction order retail shows cannot be typed: every spelling that puts the AND before the `srl` / before the `sll` hoists (93.42 / 796, mask in `$s5` and a 7th saved register taken from the scriptIndex parameter), only the parked body's AND after the `sll` stays in-loop (95.81 / 788). Presets do not help either (plain 2.7.2 87.78, 2.6.0 87.60, both also breaking the unit's already-matched functions), so a park of this shape is the ceiling, not a missing spelling.
- id: g-pointer-local-what-makes | keywords: loop, hoist, lbu, frame, lui, pointer, struct
  **A POINTER LOCAL IS WHAT MAKES A LOOP-HOISTED ADDRESS SHARE ONE BASE** (round 336): retail keeps `&A`, `&B`, `&C` in three saved registers across a loop and reaches each by displacement (`lbu 1(s0)` for the byte after it), where writing the globals inline gives `lui $v0,%hi(sym+1); lbu 0(v0)` at every use (87.16, +44 bytes, frame 0x48). Source-level `p = &global;` assignments placed JUST BEFORE the loop reproduce retail's preheader exactly and took battle/misc14 func_80089CCC 87.16 -> 99.01 -> 100.00 (RELOC). The pair `D_800C3E28` + `g_BattleLastMenuEvent` is one 2-byte struct, and typing it that way is what makes the base shareable.
- id: g-induction-base-fix-worth | keywords: loop, hoist, pointer, struct, addu, lui, s32
  THE INDUCTION-BASE FIX (worth three functions in one unit): when a loop stub is stuck at 99.3-99.6% with only base-register/offset differences, write the loop as an INDEXED access ('pSlot[i].field' plus an s32 i) instead of an incrementing pointer ('p->field; p++'). With p++ gcc's combine_givs re-bases the induction register onto the address of the body's LAST memory reference, so every displacement is shifted by the struct offset; with p[i] the biv is p + i*stride, the base register stays the symbol, and the displacements are the literal struct offsets - retail's shape. Try this before any other source shape. Counter-example: when the indexed form makes gcc reach every field through a lui $at / addu $at,$at,$s0 sequence (a folded HI16 addend) it has gone too far and the pointer form was better (field/main/misc4 func_8007A5C4, 77.28% vs 73.51%).
- id: g-second-loop-invariant-lever | keywords: loop, hoist, pointer, move, permuter
  THE SECOND-LOOP-INVARIANT LEVER (round 170, battle/misc8 func_8007C9D4, 98.55 -> 100): when retail's loop preheader ends with a COPY of a loop-invariant pointer ('move sX,a1') and yours coalesces it away, the source had a SECOND variable holding the same pointer value, re-derived AFTER a loop-body use of another loop-invariant. gcc's move_movables hoists both into the preheader in body order, which reproduces retail's order, and the copy survives because its source pseudo dies in the previous block (func_8007D478 in the same file closed with the identical shape; a 4-minute permuter run on the 98.43% body found nothing).
- id: g-do-while-block-also | keywords: loop, hoist, pointer
  THE DO/WHILE BLOCK ALSO FORCES A LOAD ORDER, and it may be EMPTY: an empty 'do { } while (0);' after a pointer local stopped gcc 2.7.2 hoisting a global load above an address formation in world_map/misc7's func_80081174 (100.00% with it, 65.26% without). Leave a one-line comment - it looks gratuitous and is not.
- id: g-retail-s-loop-shape | keywords: loop, hoist, cse, delay
  Retail's loop shape is while (1) { if (pEntry->unk0 == 0xFFFF) break; pEntry++; i++; }, not while (cond): when the original has a top test, a j back edge and both increments in the delay slots, gcc inverts a while (cond) into tests at both ends with bne (field/main/misc8 func_80085788: 72.15% -> byte-identical inner scan). Same function: a global read at three sites is RELOADED by gcc each time (it does not CSE a global across calls), so one local is required.
- id: g-loop-bound-spelling-x | keywords: loop, hoist, slti, li, addiu, switch
  Loop bound spelling: `for (x = 0; x != N; x++)` gives retail's `li v0,N; bne`; `x < N` gives `slti/bnez` instead (round 44, battle/misc28: worth 6 instructions). If your C is right and the loop tail differs by exactly that, switch the comparison. gcc 2.6.0 is the opposite: in a unit on that compiler it rewrites an ascending `slti/bnez` count loop into a countdown (`li a0,N-1 / addiu -1 / bgez`), and the only source lever found to keep retail's `slti` is a zero-statement `do { } while (0);` at the end of the body (round 56, menu/misc9) - report that ROUGH rather than shipping the empty block.
- id: g-unrotated-top-tested-loop | keywords: loop, hoist, li, s32
  Unrotated top-tested loop with `li t2,-1` hoisted ONCE before it: write `s32 limit = -1; while (1) { if (--count == limit) break; ... }`. The `while (1)`/break form stops gcc's duplicate_loop_exit_test rotation, and the LIMIT LOCAL (not a literal -1, not the parameter) is what hoists the li (round 47, system/temp2 func_80026F44: 72.66 -> 74.63% at retail's exact size).
- id: g-read-bump-lever-round | keywords: loop, hoist, addiu, delay
  THE READ-AND-BUMP LEVER (round 121, four functions in menu/misc7 from one find): when retail has the counter's 'addiu' in the BRANCH DELAY SLOT of the loop condition's own test and no latch copy, the source both read and bumped the index in ONE expression and kept the running value in a local - 'for (i = 0; i < 9; ) { digit = g_Menu->digits[i++]; ... }' - and a second running variable carried the x argument, incremented at the END of the body ('for (i = 0, x = a0; i < 9; ) { ...; x += 8; }'), which is what puts 'addiu s1,s1,8' in the back-branch slot. 'digits[i]' twice plus 'for (...; i++)' can never produce that shape; a for-loop latch increment cannot either.

- id: g-while-entered-with-no-top-test | keywords: loop, do-while, while, rotated, entry, top-test, poll, duplicate-exit
  **A LOOP RETAIL ENTERS WITH NO TOP TEST AND LEAVES WITH A BACKWARD BRANCH WAS A `do {} while` IN THE SOURCE** (round 400, field/main/misc9 func_800ABA98, 82.61 -> 84.86 = 2.37 points, the whole control flow then matching). Retail falls straight from the previous loop's exit into `jal FieldClearAndSwapOTag / ... / andi v0,v0,0x100 / beqz v0,body`: no entry test at all. Written as `while (!(g_FieldButtonsPressedOnce & 0x100)) { ... }` cc1 keeps a top-test block and puts the test at the bottom, which costs an extra `j` in the PREVIOUS loop's exit (the exit must jump forward over the body to the test). `do {...} while (!(...));` reproduces retail instruction for instruction. So read the loop's ENTRY path, not only its latch: a `while` has an entry test, a do-while does not, and the previous loop's exit shape is what shows which one the original was.
- id: g-giv-per-loop-level-is-not-source-reachable | keywords: loop, giv, strength, duplication, spill, frame, park, biv, spill-count
  **`loop.c` GIVES THE SAME TABLE-FIELD REFERENCE ITS OWN GIV AT EACH NESTING LEVEL, AND WHICH REFS GET ONE IS NOT SOURCE-REACHABLE - it sets the frame, the spills and the instruction count of any loop reading a table's fields** (round 400, field/main/misc9 func_800AB808, parked 68.25% at 592 bytes vs retail's 668 / 148 vs 164 insns). Retail reads the four fields of `RECT D_800AF5C0[5]` through SIX givs - three at the outer level (y, w, h) plus three fresh copies inside the inner `memcpy` loop - and re-forms `x` from the symbol every inner iteration, so the loop counter (0x38) and the rect walker (0x48) spill, pFile/pImage spill to 0x28/0x30, and the frame is 0x80. The same C gives three givs (x, y, h), keeps the counter in a register and re-forms w instead (frame 0x58, 148 insns). Measured dead on it: the table inline (`D_800AF5C0[i].x` everywhere, so gcc reaches each field through `lui $at / addu $at,$at,$s18`), through a local pointer, and as word arithmetic `(u_long*)tim.paddr + (j + y) * 0x50 + x / 4` - the last one IS what the original object wrote (its relocation names D_800AF5C6, i.e. the `lh 0(D_800AF5C0+6)(reg)` macro form) and it still emits the same 148 instructions. Park on a giv-count difference; `twin_for` and m2c have nothing to port, because the difference is inside strength_reduce.
- id: g-derived-giv-only-when-the-biv-init-is-outside | keywords: giv, induction, loop, biv, init, preheader, duplicate, s-register
  **`loop.c` DERIVES A `biv + const` GIV ONLY WHEN THE BIV'S INITIALISER SITS OUTSIDE THE LOOP, SO A PARK WHOSE ENTIRE RESIDUAL IS THAT ONE DERIVED REGISTER HAS NO SOURCE SPELLING: the giv-less shape needs the init inside the body, which re-runs it at the loop header (an infinite loop) and duplicates it into a preceding branch's delay slot** (round 443, movie/main/misc2 func_80075D8C, 308 insns, XenoMovie260G0 = gcc-2.6.0 -O2 -G0; the honest body is 96.43% / 1248 bytes / 312 insns against retail's 1232 / 308 and the init-inside body is 99.66% / 1236 with one duplicate `move s0,s1`). The loop is `j = entry; do { ... ArchiveDecodeSector(j + 1) ... j++; } while (j < entry + 0x14);`; retail recomputes `addiu a0,s0,1` at all three `j+1` call sites and saves s0-s6, ours keeps `s1 = j + 1` (`addiu s1,s0,1` twice at the loop head, `move a0,s1` at the sites, `addiu s1,s1,1` before the latch's `addiu s0,s0,1`) and saves s0-s7 with a frame 8 bytes bigger. Nothing else in the 308 instructions moves, so read the two rows together: a duplicated preheader copy PLUS a latch `+1` on a register retail does not have is this wall, not two bugs. Measured dead on the same body: the `for (j = entry; j < entry + 0x14; j++)` form 95.49% / 1260 / 315, a `next = j + 1` local 96.49, `++j` in the condition and `1 + j` operand order 96.43, gcc-2.7.2 95.11 (so the 2.6.0 preset stands), and two permuter runs (6 min from the init-inside body base 112 best 112, one from the init-outside body base 1481). `j + 1` cannot be made non-`biv + const` while still emitting `addiu` (an invariant variable addend buys `addu` and a register retail does not use), which is what closes it.
  Companion rule for the same shape: when the duplicate lands in a delay slot of a test that ENDS the preceding statement group, the trailing `+1`/`move` in that slot is `reorg` filling from the loop head, not a second source assignment - do not spend runs reordering the statements around it.
  **ROUND 469 MEASURED THE THRESHOLD THAT MAKES THIS CLOSED, with `cc1_probe.sh` on this unit's own cc1 (gcc 2.6.0 `-O2 -G0`): a replica of the inner loop costs the `biv + 1` giv as soon as the loop has TWO uses of `j + 1`** (even when they sit in the two format branches and `dbr` then cross-jumps the calls into one `move`), and has NO giv with ONE use, where the add stays inline (`addu $4,$16,1`). So the derivation is decided by the COUNT of `biv + const` uses, and retail's three separate inline `addiu a0,s0,1` sites therefore require three source occurrences of `j + 1` - which forces the giv. The two requirements are contradictory, so no source spelling reaches retail's 308 insns; that is the proof this lever previously only asserted. The same probe also shows the giv takes exactly the register that would otherwise hoist `entry + 0x14` (the replica hoists it to the preheader and tests `slt` against a register, while retail and this body both recompute `addiu v0,s1,0x14` in the latch), which is why the rest of the body agrees instruction for instruction. Re-measured dead on the parked honest body the same round: `while (1) { ... j++; if (j >= entry + 0x14) break; }` is byte-identical to the `do`/`while` test (312 insns, 96.43%).

- id: g-invariant-product-hoist | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, mult, mflo, cse, reload, array
  **A THREE-BYTE LOCAL STORED PER ITERATION IS WHAT FORCES RETAIL'S RE-READS OF A SOURCE POINTER, and the invariant products beside them are still hoisted whatever the spelling** (round 427, world_map/main/misc13 func_800931D8, parked 65.59% at 356 bytes / 87 insns against retail 380 / 92). The inner body reads `*pIn` FOUR times in retail (`lhu v0,0(a3)` after each of three `sb` stores) because the source stores the extracted components into a `u8 rgb[3]` local and then writes the mix expression with `*pIn` again: gcc 2.7.2 has no alias analysis, so each byte store to the stack kills the CSEd load, while the `rgb[k]` reads themselves come back from the register cse recorded for the store (there is NO `lbu` from the stack). Writing the four reads as a single `v = *pIn` local gives one load and a 316-byte body; the `u8 rgb[3]` spelling reproduces the four loads, the three `sb`s in retail's positions, `bnez` with no `andi` (the test must read `*pIn`, not a u16 local) and `srl ...15` (so the row ratio and its complement are `u32`; `s32` emits `sra`). What it does NOT reproduce: loop.c hoists the three invariant products `fr*t`, `fg*t`, `fb*t` from the pixel loop into the row loop (a mult+mflo pair each = exactly the 24 missing bytes, and 3 saved registers instead of retail's 5) and every measured spelling hoists them - three statements into a `u32` accumulator (byte-identical), `t*fr` operand order, `u8*` vs `u16*` parameters, `s32`/`u8` factor locals. `pFactors[k]` inline in the loop keeps the products in place (65.81, 368 bytes, 90 insns) but adds three `lbu`. Preset screened and not the answer: gcc-2.6.0 58.52, gcc-2.7.2-cdk does not compile the body.
- id: g-invariant-addend-keeps-mul | keywords: loop, hoist, pointer, biv, sll, addu, multiply, strength
  **AN INVARIANT ADDITIVE TERM IN THE INDEX EXPRESSION IS WHAT STOPS strength reduction of `base + index * stride` into a pointer biv** (round 389, battle/main/misc1 func_800728B8: park 78.84% -> 100.00, retail's exact 128 bytes). When the base is a loop-invariant PARAMETER, `for (...) { AddPrim(ot, &pBase[index]); index += 2; }` makes loop.c's combine_givs fold the base into a pointer induction variable (`addiu p,p,0x50` per iteration, one extra callee-saved register, frame 0x28 -> 0x30). Retail instead recomputes the product every iteration (`sll a1,s0,2` in the back-edge delay slot, then `addu a1,a1,s0`, `sll a1,3` = synth_mult's `(x*5)<<3` for 40) and adds the base with `addu a1,s3,a1` - which is what you get by folding the step into the index and keeping the start as an ADDEND: `&pBase[i * 2 + primStart]` with `i` the plain `for` counter. The addend makes the giv a sum of two induction quantities, so only the `i*2 + start` part is reduced (to the `s0 += 2` biv) and the multiply survives. The already-matched twins of this stub, `ShopMenuRenderString` (shop_menu/main/misc) and `MenuRenderString`, are written exactly that way; a body that increments the index in the loop instead is 78% forever.

- id: g-source-local-holding-the-doubled-index | keywords: loop, strength, biv, giv, sll, frame, callee-saved, global
  **WHEN THE INDEX IS `symbol + i * 2` AND THE SYMBOL IS A GLOBAL (a reload per use, so no invariant addend exists), a SOURCE LOCAL assigned `index2 = i * 2;` as the loop body's FIRST STATEMENT is what stops loop.c folding `i*2` into a `+= 2` biv - and that one line buys the frame, the saved set and the in-loop `sll`** (round 429, battle/main/misc1 func_80072938, 89.10 -> 95.62% at 348 bytes against retail's 352, XenoBattle260). With the index written inline (`pPrim[g_BattlePrimStartIndex + i * 2]`, either operand order) this cc1 derives `i` from a doubled biv: `sll s0,a1,1` in the preheader, `addiu s0,s0,2` in the latch, the loop test rewritten as `slt s0,2*last`, five saved registers and a 0x28 frame. Retail keeps `i` raw (`sll s0,s2,1` at the loop top, `addiu s2,s2,1`, `slt v0,s2,s3`), six saved registers and a 0x30 frame, which the `index2` local reproduces exactly - the same first-statement-local trick that the `g-invariant-addend-keeps-mul` body gets for free from a parameter addend, and it is needed BECAUSE the global is reloaded and therefore cannot supply that addend. Residual left in that park (95.62, 4 bytes short): with `i` dead at the top of the body, loop.c emits the latch increment before the last store's address chain, so reorg steals it into the `lw symbol` load-delay slot and the b0 store into the `bnez` slot, where retail has the increment after the store and two `nop`s. Measured dead on the same body: `s32` return type (the `c-stolen-delay-slot-retail` lever), a while-loop with `i++` as the body's last statement, and the index inline (89.10 both operand orders).

- id: g-power-of-2-mult-giv-survives-only-with-strength-reduce-off | keywords: loop, giv, biv, sll, multiply, strength, mult, frame, callee-saved, narrow, s16
  **A LOOP WHOSE RETAIL BODY RE-EMITS `sll r,biv,5` / `sll r,biv,7` (a POWER-OF-2 MULTIPLY that was NOT strength-reduced) CANNOT BE REACHED FROM ANY C SPELLING OF THAT MULTIPLY UNDER -O2: loop.c reduces shift givs as happily as a synth_mult one, so the multiply becomes a callee-saved accumulator bumped at the latch and the frame grows. THE DECISIVE TEST IS `cc1_probe.sh <unit> src/<unit>.c --opt '-O2 -fno-strength-reduce'`: if that reproduces retail's frame, saved set, instruction count and sll sites, the residual is a per-file flag question and the C is already right - report PRESET_NO_STRENGTH_REDUCE instead of re-spelling** (round 487, menu/main/misc4_260 func_801CE860, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0: the parked body is 90.29%, 796 vs 792 bytes, 199 vs 191 insns, with two extra mult givs in `$s4`/`$s5` and a 0x48 frame with six saves; under -fno-strength-reduce the same text gives retail's 0x48 frame, `s0`-`s3`+`ra`, 191 insns and both `sll a0,s0,5` / `sll a1,s0,7`, leaving only operand side and one register). gcc 2.6.0, 2.7.2-cdk and 2.7.2 all reduce the shifts (2.7.2 rejects this unit), so the compiler version is not the answer. The one C-level handle that does kill the givs is making the multiply's operand a NON-biv: writing the index as an `s16` copy (`s16 row = i;` then `row * 0x20`) leaves the mult operand a subreg of a HImode value, so `general_induction_var` refuses - measured 88.90 -> 90.29 - but the copy itself costs `sll 16` + `sra 16` per iteration (199 insns) and a `s16` loop counter costs the same in the latch, so neither can reach 191. Measured dead on the same body: `i << 5` / `i << 7` for the products (byte-identical to `i * 0x20` / `i * 0x80`), a `rowOfs = i * 0x20` local with `rowOfs * 4` for the 0x80 product (identical), and writing all four products inline with no accumulator locals (85.24, 828 B, 207 insns - the explicit 0x140/0x48 accumulator locals are load-bearing).

- id: g-alias-pointer-cannot-hold-a-base | keywords: loop, hoist, preheader, move, lui, biv, alias, move-order
  **A PLAIN ALIAS POINTER CANNOT PUSH A SYMBOL'S `lui/addiu` AHEAD OF ANOTHER INIT IN THE PREHEADER; only a WALKING pointer keeps the base in the entry block, and that costs a guard** (round 393, battle/main/misc14 func_8008A684, parked 99.03% at retail's exact 828 bytes / 207 insns). Retail's loop preheader is `[t0 = g_BattleStateWork][lui/addiu a2 = D_800D32F8][move a0,zero][addiu t2,a2,12]`; the parked body emits `move a0,zero` BEFORE the a2 base, and since both are loop.c inits (a0 = the byte offset, a2 = the array base) the insertion is newest-biv-first, so retail's a2 must have come from the ENTRY block. Measured: `pSlot = D_800D32F8;` used as `pSlot[i]` is copy-propagated back to the array form (byte-identical output, as is the same init in the for-comma list), so it cannot supply that entry-block instruction; `for (pSlot = D_800D32F8, offset = 0; pSlot < D_800D32F8 + 3; pSlot++)` does keep the base in the entry block but the pointer compare buys a pre-test guard plus `sltu` (94.76%, 852 bytes, 213 insns). Not a preset question: 99.03 under 2.6.0 -O2 and -O3, plain 2.7.2 -O2, and 2.6.0 -G0; cdk 85.29, cdk -G0 71.94. A third permuter run (base=60 best=60, 867 iterations) found nothing.

- id: g-two-source-inits-emit-in-source-order | keywords: loop, preheader, biv, move-order, do-while, pointer-walk, slt, strength
  **TWO SOURCE INITIALISERS THAT BOTH BECOME `loop.c` INITS IN THE PREHEADER ARE EMITTED IN SOURCE ORDER, so a residual showing `move idx,zero` before a symbol's `lui/addiu` is fixed by initialising the WALKING POINTER BEFORE the index - and the pointer walk has to be a `do {} while` with a signed compare, because the index-loop form makes that base a strength-reduced biv instead** (round 418, battle/main/misc14 func_8008A684, 99.03 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 828 bytes / 207 insns, XenoBattle260; this CLOSES the wall claimed by `g-alias-pointer-cannot-hold-a-base`). Retail's preheader is `[la a2 = D_800D32F8][move a0,zero][addiu t2,a2,12]` where a0 walks the 8-byte counter stride and a2 walks the actor-pointer array. The body that reproduces it: `pSlot = D_800D32F8; offset = 0; do { ... (*pSlot)->unk15FA ... ; offset += 8; pSlot++; } while ((int)pSlot < (int)(D_800D32F8 + 3));` - with the pointer assignment written BEFORE `offset = 0` the `la` prints first; swapping those two statements (offset first) is the 99.03 body, so the statement order alone is worth the match. Load-bearing, each measured: (1) the `for (i = 0; i < 3; i++)` index loop with `D_800D32F8[i]`, or a folded alias `pSlot[i]`, is 99.03 whatever the statement order, because the base is then a strength-reduced biv and its init goes before the source biv's; (2) the `for` form of the pointer walk buys a pre-test guard plus `sltu` (94.76, 852 bytes, 213 insns) - `do {} while` has no top test because retail's loop is entered with none; (3) the `(int)` casts make the compare `slt` (retail's) where a plain pointer compare emits `sltu` (99.71); (4) `offset = i * 8` inside the body makes the offset a derived giv, which flips the preheader correctly but moves the loop test onto the offset (`slti a0,24`, 824 bytes), so the offset must stay a real biv. Measured and dead (all 99.03 or worse): `offset`/`i` as `u32` (98.74 and 92.56), `i <= 2`, `*(D_800D32F8 + i)`, `offset = offset + 8`, a `sizeof` stride, declaration reordering, dropping the unused `pSlot`, and moving `offset += 8` earlier in the body (it moves the latch increment but NOT the preheader, which disproves the "newest-biv-first" reading in `g-alias-pointer-cannot-hold-a-base`).
  **BOUNDARY, MEASURED (round 465, menu/main/misc11_r2_260 func_801E61B0, parked 97.58 at retail's 672 bytes / 168 insns): the relative order of TWO giv inits derived from the SAME source biv is NOT source-controlled.** Retail's preheader is `[la g_MenuSlotResourceIds][move s3,zero = j*0x50][move s5,zero = j*4][li s4,0xa98 = j*0x87C+0xA98][move s2,zero = j*0x87C]`; a body that writes `primOffset = j * 0x87C + 0xA98` as the loop body's FIRST statement still emits the unbiased `j*0x87C` giv's init before primOffset's (and the round-452 measurement of the same assignment moved BELOW the inner loop is byte-identical), so this pair of rows cannot be closed by moving the assignment, by the declaration order, or by the latch comma order (also measured identical). The same body is the fork: keeping `offset` a source biv puts its init first (front-end inits always print before loop.c's) but gives retail's seven base-first `addu v0,v0,s2` sums; making it a giv gives retail's group order but flips all seven to `addu v0,s2,v0`.
  **SECOND MEASUREMENT of the `(int)`-cast -> `slt` half (round 460, slus_006.64/system/temp3_b func_8001B970, 89.53 -> 90.07 parked at 420 bytes / 105 insns against retail's 412 / 103): it is NOT tied to an index loop.** The row copy there is a plain `u8*` walk entered unconditionally (`pDst = pRow; do { *pDst++ = outBuf[k++]; } while (pDst < pRow + 0x14);`), which emits `sltu v0,a0,a1`, and the single edit `while ((int)pDst < (int)(pRow + 0x14))` gives retail's `slt v0,v1,a1` with every other instruction unchanged (the pointer and bound keep their registers). So when retail's copy-loop compare is `slt` and the body is a pointer walk with no index to sign, cast both sides of the bound - it is 1 line, it is the last row-copy residual here, and it costs nothing elsewhere in the function.
- id: g-biv-init-and-latch-move-together | keywords: loop, hoist, biv, preheader, prologue, callee-saved, pointer, strength
  **RETALL'S BIV INIT POSITION IN THE PREHEADER AND ITS `addiu +4` IN THE LATCH MOVE TOGETHER, so a residual that shows BOTH is one source cause, not two** (round 394, movie/main/misc1 func_80072F98, parked 98.67 at retail's exact 912 bytes / 226 insns). Retail's six pointer inits are `[pColB][pTargetB][pColG][pTargetG][steps-base][pColR][pTargetR]` and its six latch increments are the same order; ours puts the strength-reduced steps base LAST in both places, because `strength_reduce`/`move_movables` insert a hoisted biv after every source statement of the block. Reading retail's order as "the last two pointers are compiler-DERIVED givs (`combine_givs` emits their init AND their increment after the biv's own)" is the only shape that explains both rows at once. Do not chase the two rows separately: `pStep[i]` (932 bytes), `*pStep`+`pStep++` (880), a mid-block `if (i == 0) {...}` (no change) and the typed `g_Table[i].field` form (896 bytes, 222 insns, the derived base chosen as `+2` = retail's) were all measured on it; the typed form is 4 short because the plain load is CSEd where retail re-reads, and the `volatile` cast that buys the re-read kills the biv derivation (frame 0x60, 90.47). Swapping two independent `pX += 4` lines moves objdiff's fuzzy 98.67 -> 98.71 without changing the residual - another non-monotone score. **ROUND 419 CLARIFIED THE SHAPE AND WHY IT IS UNREACHABLE: retail's ordering is produced by the six-derived-giv (typed array) body ONLY, and that body cannot also produce the re-reads.** Measured: the full typed form (`g_MovieDarkColours[i].r/.g/.b` for all six walks, no pointer locals) emits retail's preheader order exactly - colours base at +2, target base at +2, the -1/-1 derived inits, the steps base, then the -2/-2 derived inits, and the same order in the latch - but is 222 insns / 896 bytes / 90.47% because gcc CSEs the three sum reads retail re-reads; making those three reads volatile on that body drops the giv derivation and gives 246 insns / 992 bytes / 81.67%; `pColB[-2]` / `pTargetB[-2]` in place of the two R pointer locals folds the offsets inline as displacements with no derived giv at all (224 insns / 904 bytes / 95.77%); and the hybrid that keeps a source `s32* pStep` walking pointer while durations stay indexed by `i` makes the durations base a hoisted register and shrinks the frame to 0x48 (218 insns / 880 / 93.25%) - the same failure as `*pStep` + `pStep++`. So the six source bivs are the only body that yields the three re-reads, and the source order of their initialisers cannot move the steps biv init out of last place. Treat as a documented park.
- id: g-sentinel-guard-must-deref | keywords: loop, sentinel, constant, register, loop-carried, load, guard, cse
  **A `-1`-TERMINATED POINTER WALK CAN HAVE EITHER RETAIL'S BARE `li` SENTINEL OR RETAIL'S SEPARATE GUARD LOAD, NOT BOTH: the two source shapes trade one residual for the other** (round 398, world_map/main/misc9 func_8008868C, parked 76.81% at 152 bytes vs retail's 148). Retail: guard `lh v1,0(a1); beq v1,a0` with `li a0,-1` in the entry block, then body `lh a0,0(s0) / addiu s0,s0,4 / lh a1,0(s1) / addiu s1,s1,4 / addu / jal`, then bottom test `lh v1,0(s0); li v0,-1; bne v1,v0`, i.e. the sentinel is a bare CONST_INT at the compare AND the guard re-loads the element the next body iteration loads. `if (*pX != -1) { do { s32 vx = *pX; s32 vy = *pY; pX += 2; pY += 2; f(base+vx, base+vy); } while (*pX != -1); }` reproduces every load, both `addu`s and the jal operands (76.81%) but cse registers the twice-used -1 (`li s3,-1` in the preheader, +4 frame bytes), which displaces the bne delay slot's `li v0,1`. The plain `while (*pX != -1) { vx = *pX; ... }` (ONE static use of the sentinel) DOES leave the sentinel a CONST_INT, but loop.c then reuses the guard's halfword load as the next iteration's body value (`lhu $6,0($16)` hoisted, `sll/sra` re-extension in the body, frame 0x38): 69.00%, 168 bytes. An early `if (*pX == -1) return 1;` before the do-while merges back to the identical 76.81 body. So on this shape park unless you can break the constant's cse by MODE (`a-constant-cse-is-per-mode`) - the sentinel and both comparisons are SImode here, so there is no spelling that does.
- id: g-loop-form-sets-the-copied | keywords: loop, rotated, slti, delay, duplication, reorg, increment, while
  **THE LOOP'S SOURCE FORM SETS HOW MANY TIMES REORG COPIES THE EXIT TEST INTO DELAY SLOTS - `do {} while` gives one copy, `while` gives three, retail has two with the increment in the slot after the call** (round 398, battle/main/misc9 func_8007DA1C, 75.77 -> 95.38% by moving the same body from `for (i = 3; i < 0xB; i++)` to `while`; parked at 352 bytes against retail's 348, so neither form can link - one instruction either way). Retail's `slti v0,s1,0xB` appears in the `beqz v1` (mask test) delay slot and again at the join label plus the latch - two copies - and its `beqz v0` (ClearRecordIdle result) delay slot holds `addiu s1,s1,1`, i.e. retail incremented `i` unconditionally BETWEEN the call and the test. With `idx = i++` cc1 puts the increment at the loop head, so that slot takes a COPY of the join's `slti` instead and the body is one instruction too long; the do-while rotation leaves ONE `slti` and is one short. Getting the increment into that slot needs the call result in a local, which wrecks the allocation (s32 idle 88.25%, 336 bytes; increment at the body end 88.67%, 332), so this family's residual is the increment POSITION, not the loop form - but measure the while form first on the sibling stubs (DB78/DCF8/DE78/DFD4), since it also carries the func_8007D8C0 R370 two-pointer recipe.

- id: a-loop-counter-set-before-the | keywords: loop, preheader, li, counter, for, allocation, order
  **A `li` FOR A LOOP COUNTER LANDS IN FRONT OF THE POINTER SETUP WHEN THE COUNTER IS ITS OWN STATEMENT ABOVE THE LOOP, NOT IN THE `for` INITIALISER** (round 400, world_map/misc16 func_80099708, 91.34 -> 94.82 at retail's exact 260 bytes / 65 insns). Retail's preheader is `lui t0,0x1f80 / move t3,s0 / li t7,8 / lui t9,%hi(table) / lui t6,%hi(col) / lw t6 / li t8,-1`; with `for (oi = 8; oi != -1; oi--)` the `li t7,8` is emitted with the rest of the preheader after the table's `lui/addiu`, and with `oi = 8;` as a statement above a `for (; oi != -1; oi--)` it comes out in retail's position. The loop body, the -1 sentinel and the back-branch delay slots are identical either way, so this is worth one edit on any preheader whose only residual is the position of one `li`.
- id: g-giv-anchor-follows-source-order | keywords: giv, base, anchor, combine, displacement, store, order, reduce
  **THE REDUCED-GIV ANCHOR IS THE LAST DEST-ADDRESS GIV `loop.c` RECORDS, RECORDING FOLLOWS *SOURCE* ORDER, AND A LATE-COMPUTED STORE GROUP CAN STILL SIT LAST IN THE ASM - so when retail's base is `addiu s0,s2,0x25` and yours is `0x20`, move the store GROUP whose anchor you want to be LAST UP IN THE SOURCE, not down.** (round 404, world_map/main/misc7 func_80081D80, 99.88 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 564 bytes / 141 insns, a park standing since round 377.) Retail keeps the quad pointer at `prim+0x25` (the last byte field, `v3`) and addresses all sixteen corner stores at 0..-0x1D; the parked body picked `prim+0x20` (the last `sh`, `x3`) with every displacement 5 larger, same addresses. Three probes pin the rule: a duplicate `pQuad->v3 = i + 1;` appended after the x stores moved the base to 37 (+1 insn, 99.29% / 568 bytes, the duplicate emitted next to the FIRST v3 store), moving `x0` last moved it to 8, and the fix was to write the four `x` stores ABOVE the `y2/y3/v2/v3` group: their values come from the `rand() % *pFade - *pFade / 2` delta, so cc1 sinks them below it in the emitted code and the ASM store order stays retail's (`y2,y3,v2,v3` then `x0..x3`) while `v3` is the last giv recorded. Do not trust the asm store order as source order when a store group's values are computed late in the body; the park note's "source statement order cannot reproduce it" was wrong for that reason. The indexed form (`pQuad[i].field`) is not the answer here: 79.45% / 139 insns.


- id: g-s16-counter-pre-decrement | keywords: loop, counter, s16, sll, decrement, tail, narrow, move
  **A COUNTDOWN TAIL OF `addiu v0,a2,-1 / move a2,v0 / sll v0,v0,0x10 / bnez v0` IS A `s16` COUNTER WITH `--count`; a two-variable tail lets gcc test the loop-carried copy instead and emits `sll v0,a2,0x10`** (round 404, slus_006.64/system/sound func_8003C4C4, 99.92 -> 99.96). The `move` into the loop-carried register plus a `sll 16` on the fresher value is the HImode pre-decrement: `s16 count = elementCount; do { ... } while (--count != 0);` reproduced it exactly, where the parked `next = count - 1; count = next;` tested through `(s16)next` was one instruction off (gcc knows the two are equal and sign-extends the carried one). Measured dead on the same body: `s32 count` with `--count` drops the `sll` (a word test needs no extension), `u16 count` with `--count` folds the decrement into `addu a2,a2,t3` off a hoisted 0xFFFF plus `andi 0xffff` (98.42, one instruction SHORT), and a post-decrement tests the OLD value so it never gives the `move`-then-`sll` pair. Check the counter's declared width and the operator position before changing the loop's source form. **SAME LEVER, THE PRE-INCREMENT SIDE (round 420, slus_006.64/system/archive func_80029EB0, 93.07 -> 94.47%, 960 -> 948 bytes): a PCclose retry tail retail emits as `beqz a0,done / jal GfxDrawArchiveReadRetry / addiu v0,s0,1 / sll v0,v0,0x10 / sra v1,v0,0x10 / slti v0,v1,4 / bnez v0,loop / bnez v1,ret-6` narrows ONCE and reuses $v1 for both the loop test and the trailing `if (nClose != 0)`; `while ((nClose = f())) { g(nClose); nClose = nClose + 1; if (nClose >= 4) break; }` keeps the value in the call-result register, narrows twice and costs the two `move $vN` copies plus a `sll` (3 instructions). The body that reproduces it is a do/while with the counter incremented IN THE CONDITION: `do { nClose = f(); if (nClose == 0) break; g(nClose); } while (++nClose < 4);` then `if (nClose != 0) return -6;` - the break path jumps straight past the -6 test, which is exactly retail's `beqz` target. So the same rule holds for both directions: write the counter as the loop variable and put the increment inside the loop condition, not as a separate statement, whenever retail's tail tests with the freshly narrowed register.

- id: g-at-symbol-plus-register-is-assembler-only | keywords: at, addu, lui, symbol, register, strength, hoist, absolute
  **`lui $at,%hi(SYM); addu $at,$at,$off; lhu %lo(SYM)($at)` IS THE ASSEMBLER'S EXPANSION OF ONE `SYM($off)` OPERAND, SO NO C REPRODUCES IT - and the two C shapes that come closest each fail on the opposite register** (round 411, battle/main/misc1 func_8007171C, parked 78.73% under 2.6.0 at 400 bytes against retail's 416; -G0 78.73, 2.7.2 80.27, 2.7.2-cdk compile-failed). $at is gas/ASPSX's own scratch register, so an address that reaches it can only come from a symbolic operand plus a register, not from anything cc1 allocates. The inline spelling `*(u16 *)((u8 *)SYM + off)` with `off` a for-clause biv scores 70.61 and makes a POINTER BIV per symbol (lhu 0(a1) with `addiu a1,a1,0x170`), even for 2-use expressions like `SYM + i * 2`; re-assigning a pointer local at each site (`pWord = (u16 *)((u8 *)SYM + off); ... *pWord ...`) scores 78.73 and gives no biv, but cc1 hoists the symbol's `lui/addiu` pair into the preheader and every site becomes a single `addu a0,a1,t2`. Same two-way split as the misc1 func_800728B8 lever, so measure it, do not re-spell it: a diff whose per-site address forming is 2 insns in retail and 3 in yours (one instruction and one $at) is a park.
  SUPERSEDED FOR world_map/main/misc9 func_8008615C (round 443, 95.40 -> MATCH at retail's exact 644 bytes / 161 insns, check_bin OK): the `la $21,D_8009D618` was NOT a compiler-version signature, it was a body problem, and the recipe transfers to any diff whose symptom is "one extra callee-saved register and a 0x30 frame instead of 0x28 because gcc splits a symbol address that retail reaches with the `$at` macro". Four edits closed it, in this order of payoff: (1) hoist a loop-invariant global READ out of the call arguments into its own block-local assignment inside the same arm (`otHead = g_WorldMapRenderContext[0x1C];` then pass `otHead`) - that alone dropped the split, the s5 save/restore and the frame back to 0x28, 98.50%; (2) spell the scratchpad copy as `pDst[0x34 + i]` off `pDst = (u16*)0x1F800000` instead of `pDst = (u16*)0x1F800068` with `*pDst++` - retail keeps 0x1F800000 in the register and stores at displacement 0x68, and the +0x68-in-the-immediate form costs a `lui/ori` pair; (3) address the two s16 globals as ONE base with a negative displacement (`extern s16 g_WorldMapGridTileRowOrigin[]; pRowOrigin = g_WorldMapGridTileRowOrigin; ... pRowOrigin[0] ... pRowOrigin[-2]`, retail's disps 0 and -4) - declaring them as two scalars, or as a struct at the lower one, makes gcc form `lui %hi / lh 0` for the second and costs a register; (4) `pEntry = pTable - (-id)` for a struct-index sum whose retail form is IN PLACE on the index (`sll v0,v0,0x3 / addu v0,v0,s3`): the plain `pTable + id`, `&pTable[id]`, `id * 8 + pTable` and the inlined-index form all give the mirrored `addu a0,s3,v0` with the address in a reload scratch, and only the double negation ties it to the dying index. Residual after all four is 99.97%, and it is splat's own hi/lo inference (the copy loop's loop-back `addiu $v1,$v1,2` was paired with the `lui $v1,0x1F80` above it and printed as `%lo(D_1F800002)`, so the expected object has imm 0 plus a reloc and the C has the literal) - report that as MATCH/RELOC with check_bin, not as a compiler miss. Note the two permuter runs on the old body found (1) and (4) here, and both were led by the `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop`/"2.6.0-only shape" reasoning being wrong: measure a loop-invariant ARGUMENT read as a local before concluding a preset split.
  Round 429 measured the sibling case in world_map/main/misc9 func_8008615C (parked 95.40% / 660 bytes against retail's 640, XenoWorldMap): the split is a COMPILER-VERSION signature, not a source one. The same body under gcc-2.7.2 emits `la $21,D_8009D618` in the loop preheader plus `addu $2,$2,$21` per access (so the base costs a sixth callee-saved register: s5, frame 0x30), while gcc-2.6.0 emits the macro form `lh $3,D_8009D618($2)` - and both are visible in cc1's own `.s`, before maspsx. `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop` under 2.7.2 keeps every matched function of that unit at 100.00 and still splits, so the post-loop CSE is not the pass involved. Because the unit's other eleven matched functions drop to 55-97 under 2.6.0, this is a mixed-TU artefact to report (PRESET_260), not a switch; two further spellings measured on the way both split: an explicit `slot` biv (`D_8009D618[slot + i]`, 90.80 / 672, splits the tile-id base too, s5 AND s6) and the byte-cast form `*(s16*)((u8*)D_8009D618 + (row * 5 + i) * 2)` (95.40 / 660, identical code).
  Round 471 narrowed the same symptom from the other side, battle/main/misc15 func_8008C4A8 (parked 93.72% / 908 bytes / 227 insns against retail 884 / 221 under XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0): retail re-forms TWO of the three 72-byte command-table bases inside the loop with the `lui $at / addu $at,at,v1 / sb %lo(sym)(at)` macro while the park hoists both into `$s5`/`$s4` in the preheader (+6 insns: two `la` pairs, one save/restore pair), and the THIRD symbol (`g_BattleCommandRecords`) is NOT hoisted in either compile. Two facts that save the next lane: (1) the SAME C subscript expression stores through the two hoisted symbols BEFORE the loop and BOTH compiles emit the macro form there (`sb $18,g_BattleCommandCodes($2)`), so the hoist is not a subscript spelling - it is a cse1/loop.c ordering on a symbol that already carries a REG_EQUAL, and the correlation with "referenced before the loop" is exact (the never-hoisted symbol is referenced only inside it); (2) it is not strength_reduce either - `cc1 -dL` on the loop prints five movables (const 0xFF and 0xFFFF "not desirable", the `count * 0x40` ashift "cond savings 1 not desirable", two life-4 values "moved to 491/493/495") and NO `dest address ... add (symbol_ref)` giv line, where BattleQueueOneActorCommand and BattleParseNumberToDigits in the same dump do print one. `-fno-strength-reduce`, `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop`, `-fno-caller-saves` and `-fno-cse-follow-jumps` each still emit both `la` pairs, and try_flags gives -G0 93.72 identical, -O1 79.60, -O3 compile-failed, 2.7.2 91.31, 2.7.2-cdk compile-failed - so no flag and no preset removes it. Park this shape.
- id: a-source-offset-local-stops-loop-c-hosting-a-symbol-address | keywords: at, addu, lui, symbol, hoist, preheader, la, offset, local, count
  **THE C THAT KEEPS RETAIL'S `lui $at / addu $at,at,$off / sb %lo(SYM)(at)` FORM INSTEAD OF HOISTING THE SYMBOL INTO A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER IS A SOURCE-LEVEL OFFSET LOCAL RE-ASSIGNED BEFORE EACH STORE: writing `off = count * sizeof(Record); table[off] = v;` (and `off = ...` again for the next store, so the count is re-read) closes the round-471 park of battle/main/misc15 func_8008C4A8 to MATCH at retail's exact 884 bytes / 221 insns under XenoBattle260 (gcc-2.6.0), where the inline `table[count * sizeof(Record)] = v;` form scores 93.72% / 908 / 227** (round 485). Retail's loop re-forms TWO of its three 72-byte command-table bases inside the loop through `$at` and reloads `g_BattleCommandQueue` and its count before each store; the inline body instead materialises both symbol addresses as `la` in the preheader (+2 insns each, plus the `$s4`/`$s5` save/restore pair and a 0x30 frame instead of 0x28). Three measurements that narrow it, all on the same body: (1) the pre-loop reference to those same symbols is NOT the cause - deleting the pre-loop stores leaves both `la` pairs in the preheader (81.68%), so the round-471 "cse1/loop.c on a REG_EQUAL" reading is wrong; (2) `*(volatile u8 *)&table[count * ...] = v` is byte-identical to the plain store (93.72), because loop.c hoists the invariant ADDRESS insns, not the store; (3) a SHARED `off` local for both stores kills the hoists and gives the wanted `$at` form (95.95%) but also CSEs the second scale chain, 8 insns short of retail - the re-assignment before each store is what restores retail's per-store reloads AND keeps the macro form. If a diff shows `lui sN,%hi(sym)` in a loop preheader where retail has the `$at` macro, try the offset-local spelling before judging the function a compiler wall.

- id: battle-go-loop-left-justified-himode-iv | keywords: induction, giv, sll, sra, shift, scaled, lui, multiply
  **A SCALED LOOP ARGUMENT RETAIL TRACKS AS `lui 0x2A` + `sra a2,s1,0x10` + `+0x200000` PER ROW IS A `s32` LOCAL KEPT LEFT-JUSTIFIED BY 16, NOT THE SImode EXPRESSION** (round 411, battle/main/misc17 func_80092B74, 64.13 -> 87.17% in one edit, 1252 bytes against retail's 1336 under XenoBattle260). Retail's third argument is `i * 0x20 + 0x2A` but no multiply appears: it is `lui s1,(0x2A0000 >> 16)`, `sra a2,s1,0x10` at the call and `lui v0,0x20 / addu s1,s1,v0` in the latch, and the second argument's row is the same with 0x1A0000 in its own register. Writing `s32 x1, x2; x1 = 0x2A << 16; x2 = 0x1A << 16;` then passing `x1 >> 16` / `x2 >> 16` and stepping both with `x += 0x20 << 16` in the loop body reproduces all of it (the SImode `i * 0x20 + 0x2A` gives `li`/`sll`/`ori` instead and parks in the 64-72% band). The idiom was already matched elsewhere in the overlay: battle/main/misc14's BattleBuildFlaggedSlotSpriteColumn does exactly this with `s32 pitch = 0x6E << 16` / `pitch >> 16` / `pitch += 0xA0000`. Reach for it whenever a scaled x/y argument in a loop shows a bare `sra ... ,0x10` or a `lui` of a small constant times 0x10000.
- id: g-one-constant-in-the-preheader-and | keywords: loop, invariant, hoist, gcse, li, constant, rematerialise, reassign
  **A LOOP-INVARIANT VALUE THE BODY RE-ASSIGNS IS HELD IN ONE REGISTER ACROSS THE WHOLE LOOP WHILE A CONSTANT EXPRESSION OF IT IS RE-MATERIALISED PER ITERATION - that is the only way to get one `li` in the preheader and a different one inside the loop** (round 418, battle/main/misc11 func_8007FBE0, parked 99.39% at retail's exact 264 bytes / 66 insns). Retail fills a PSX prim's four halfwords with `0xC` (from a preheader `li t2,0xC`) and `0x12` (from a `li v1,0x12` INSIDE the loop) in two different registers. Spelling both as a constant relation - `x = 0xC;` before the loop and `x + 6` at the second store - lets GCSE hoist BOTH into registers (94.39%, still 66 insns, 26 differing lines), while the reassignment form `... = (x = 0x12)` reproduces retail's two shapes exactly and leaves only an allocator tie on x's register (a 6x quotient gap, so not closable). Read a preheader `li` plus an in-loop `li` of a related value as one variable the body writes, not as two literals.

- id: a-block-move-limit-as-a-third-giv | keywords: giv, strength, reduction, block, memcpy, struct, copy, frame
  **A TRAILING `pPoly[1] = pPoly[0]` STRUCT COPY MAKES loop.c GIVE THE BLOCK MOVE'S LIMIT ITS OWN GIV, AND THAT ONE REGISTER IS THE WHOLE RESIDUAL** (round 413, field/main/misc4 func_8007A5C4, parked 77.28%, 568 bytes vs retail's 560). Retail keeps exactly two givs off the loop pointer - the Quad (+0x70) and `&quad->polys[0]` (+0x70) - and recomputes `addiu t0,s1,32` from the second inside the loop; our compile makes the copy's limit (`quad+0x40`) a third giv, bases the other stores off it with negative offsets and needs a 10th callee-saved slot (frame 0x58 vs 0x50, the uv+7 pointer spilled). The copy itself is right: 0x28 bytes as a 4-word loop plus an 8-byte tail, retail's exact shape. Tried, all 77.28 or worse with the same code: `pQuad->polys[0]` inline, a `POLY_FT4* pPoly` local, a `POLY_FT4* pNextPoly` for the copy, a `SVECTOR* pVertex` for the vertices, indexing `D_800B0FEC[i]` (73.51), `vy=0` before `vx` (73.31). A 4-minute permuter run reached 81.72 by taking `&pQuad` in one vertex store: that puts the loop pointer in memory, so gcc stops strength-reducing it and derives `&polys[0]` from the reload each iteration - a different body, not retail's, and not source anyone would write. Park rather than permute if a struct copy at the end of a loop body is the only residual. **Round 426 corrected the mechanism:** the limit giv is not the cause, it is the LAST link of one `combine_givs` chain - deleting the copy alone re-bases all twelve vertex stores onto `quad+0x2E` (the `pPoly->clut` store, the last address the loop assigns) with negative displacements, so gcc anchors the whole quad-relative address set on the LAST address recorded and retail's `add_val 0` quad base plus a second chain at `+0x20` is what this C cannot express (`pPoly` folds into `quad + 0x20`, so every address in the loop shares one chain). Also measured: retail's `vy = 0` FIRST store order 73.31 / 572 bytes / 143 insns, and the eight inline uv arguments replaced by `u_char* pUV = &D_800ADE70[i * 8];` + `pUV[0..7]` 78.04 / frame 0x48 (one saved register fewer but the second ADE70 pointer is lost, so it is further from retail than the 77.28 body). gcc-2.6.0 is 73.31 on the vy-first body and compile-fails on the parked one; 2.7.2-cdk compile-fails.
- id: g-index-form-makes-the-field-givs | keywords: induction, giv, pointer, walk, index, struct, loop, field, address
  **A STRUCT-ARRAY WALK WRITTEN AS `pRect++` WITH `pRect->field` MAKES `loop.c` KEEP ONE POINTER WITH DISPLACEMENTS AND NO FIELD GIVS, WHILE `arr[i].field` MAKES ONE GIV PER FIELD - so when retail's loop shows a register per field (`addiu s3,s3,8` written back four times at the loop bottom) the source is the INDEX form and a pointer-walk rewrite measurably destroys the shape** (round 411, field/main/misc9 func_800AB808, parked; the shape question, not the match). Retail holds four outer field walkers (`&h`, `&y`, `&w` and `&x` in a stack slot), each `addiu +8` at the outer bottom, plus inner recomputations, and spills `i`, `&x`, `pFile` and `pImage` into a 0x80 frame. Measured on the same body: the index form 68.25% / 592 bytes / 148 insns with three field givs (h, x, y) plus `i*8`; the pointer walk 68.26% / 528 bytes / 132 insns with ZERO field givs (every access becomes `lh -4(s1)`/`lh 0(s3)` off one walker), and taking the pointer per iteration for the prect stores only, inner loop still indexed, 63.69% / 576 bytes / 144 insns. So the fuzzy score can be flat (68.25 vs 68.26) across two bodies whose loop-state register sets differ completely: judge this class by the giv/increment rows, not the percentage, and never convert an index-form loop to a pointer walk to raise it. Preset closed with try_flags.sh --sweep (2.6.0 / 2.7.2 / 2.7.2-cdk x -O1/-O2/-O3 x -G4/-G8 x -mcpu 3000/r8000) plus cdk -G0 and 2.6.0 -G0: Default -O2 is the maximum and -G0 == -G8 whenever the base symbol is a plain global, so a giv-count residual of this kind is a `loop.c` heuristic, not a preset.

- id: g-wait-loop-tests-the-status | keywords: loop, volatile, status, wait, inverted, branch, sense, register
  **A GPU/DEVICE WAIT LOOP IS `while (!(status & bit))` - the loop exits when the BIT IS SET - so a park written with the test uninverted matches the branch senses mirrored and cannot reach 100 whatever else is right; the tell is retail's `bnez v0,<past the loop>` on the entry test and `beqz v0,<loop top>` at the bottom** (round 420, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_b LoadImage func_800460A0 98.36 -> 100.00 and its twin StoreImage func_800462DC, PSY-Q preset). The park had `while (*g_GpuGp1Port & 0x04000000) { if (func_80046F30()) return -1; }`, which is also the wrong semantics (it gives up as soon as the GPU asks for DMA); inverting it closes both the two branch senses and, with the divide-into-`size` fix above, took each of the two stubs from a parked 98.36 / 97.80 to 100.00 at retail's exact byte count. Read a wait loop's polarity off the entry branch: `bnez` to PAST the loop means the loop runs while the bit is CLEAR.

- id: g-front-end-statement-places-a-preheader | keywords: preheader, invariant, li, constant, loop, cse, placement
  **A SOURCE STATEMENT CREATING A CONSTANT MATERIALISES IT AT THE TOP OF THE LOOP PREHEADER, BEFORE THE ASSIGNMENTS WRITTEN ABOVE IT, WHEREAS THE SAME CONSTANT SHARED BY cse AND HOISTED BY `loop.c` LANDS AT THE END - so a retail preheader `li sN,K` that sits FIRST is a front-end statement, and spelling that constant as a named local reproduces its slot; the price is that cse then stops sharing the register with a `case K` compare** (round 423, `movie/main/misc1` func_800704E8, 569 insns, XenoBattle260Div, parked 99.04 -> 99.28% at retail's exact 2276 bytes). Retail's preheader is `li s3,1 / la s4,g_MovieStreamReadCount / move s2,s1`; with the constant only appearing inside the loop body (`1 - g_MovieDebugBufferParity`, two `isbg = 1` stores, `switch` `case 1`) cc1 emits `la s4 / move s2 / li s3` and no arrangement of the two assimilations reaches retail's group order (earlier rounds measured writing the assignments inside the loop, reordering them, and a `do{}while(0)` barrier). Adding `s32 isbg; ... isbg = 1;` as a statement right after the preceding call and reading it in the parity computation and the two stores moves the `li` into retail's slot exactly - the same rule the `b-strength-reduce-giv-is-always-first` entry states from the other end (front end first, loop.c after). What it costs: the switch's `case 1` test then materialises its own `li v0,1 / beq v1,v0` where retail reuses `beq v1,s3`, because the constant's register equivalence is flushed at the loop-start label; going back to `1 - x` restores the compare but returns the `li` to the end of the preheader and costs 12 bytes (2288 / 572 insns / 98.69, measured). So treat the two rows as ONE trade and probe the shape with `cc1_probe.sh` (a standalone copy of the preheader + switch shows `li $16,1` then `beq $3,$16` when both are in one extended block, which is why the loop case loses it). Not a preset question: 99.02 under gcc-2.7.2-psx, 82.76 under cdk.

  **UPDATE round 436: the trade in this entry is CLOSED - move ALL the loop-invariant statements whose hoists retail shows into the loop** (movie/main/misc1 func_800704E8, 99.28 -> 100.00 / `check_bin` OK at 2276 bytes / 569 insns). With `isbg = 1;` alone in the loop, loop.c hoists the `li` to the END of the preheader (after `la s4`/`move s2`, i.e. one row off); with `isbg = 1; pCounters = g_MovieStreamReadCount; pBase = pWork;` as the loop's first three statements, IN THAT ORDER, loop.c emits retail's whole preheader group `li s3,1 / la s4 / move s2` AND rewrites the in-loop `case 1` compare to `beq v1,s3`, so the "cse flushes the constant at the loop-start label" price does not apply to a hoisted one. Rule: a preheader whose instructions are all of one kind (front-end `li` first, or all loop.c insertions at the end) tells you which of them the original wrote INSIDE the loop; the group's ORDER is the source order of the in-loop statements.

- id: g-flat-pair-index-form-gives-the-two-givs | keywords: loop, giv, induction, sentinel, index, struct, pair, cse
  **AN INTERLEAVED `{s16,s16}` PAIR TABLE WALKED WITH THE FLAT INDEXES (`ids[i * 2]`, `ids[i * 2 + 1]`) GIVES RETAIL'S TWO INDEPENDENT INDUCTION POINTERS, WHILE THE TYPED STRUCT-ARRAY FORM (`pairs[i].parent`, `pairs[i].child`) MAKES cc1 KEEP THE INDEX AND RE-FORM THE SECOND FIELD AS A SYMBOLIC `D_...A2` + VARIABLE INDEX** (round 424, world_map/main/misc9 func_8008868C, `extern s16 ids[]; while (ids[i * 2] != -1) { WorldMapSetSpriteSetParent(base + ids[i * 2], base + ids[i * 2 + 1]); i++; }` = 100.00% at retail's exact 148 bytes / 37 insns, XenoWorldMap). Retail has `move s0,base` / `addiu s1,base,2` then `lh a0,0(s0) / addiu s0,s0,4 / lh a1,0(s1) / addiu s1,s1,4` - two givs, one per address expression. Measured on the same function: the struct-array form 69.89% / 168 bytes / 42 insns (second field loaded as `lui at,%hi(D_*A2) / addu at,at,i*?`), and the two-`s16*`-pointer walk (`pX = ids; pY = ids + 1; if (*pX != -1) do { ...; pX += 2; pY += 2; } while (*pX != -1);`) 76.81% / 152 bytes, because there both -1 compares cse to one register. **This corrects g-sentinel-guard-must-deref:** that entry concluded "no spelling breaks the sentinel's cse, park on this shape" - the index form does, because the guard's and the body's element loads are then one MEM with two different pseudos (`i`, `i + 1`), so the loop's -1 stays a bare CONST_INT. Read a sentinel loop's `.s` for TWO walkers before writing two pointer variables.

- id: g-source-walkers-give-the-field-givs | keywords: loop, giv, walker, pointer, struct, array, prologue, frame
  **FOR A `RECT`-SHAPED TABLE (FOUR s16 FIELDS AT +0/+2/+4/+6, STRIDE 8) READ INSIDE A NESTED LOOP, THE FOUR SOURCE-LEVEL FIELD WALKERS (`pH = &t[0].h; pW = &t[0].w; pY = &t[0].y; pRect = &t[0];` incremented at the loop bottom, plus a separate `s32 offset` = slot*8) ARE WORTH +9 POINTS OVER THE FULLY INDEXED BODY AND ARE THE ONLY FORM THAT REPRODUCES RETAIL'S PROLOGUE** (round 426, field/main/misc9 func_800AB808, parked 68.25 -> 77.38% at 572 bytes / 143 insns against retail's 668 / 164; Default preset confirmed by a full `try_flags.sh --sweep`). Retail keeps one walking register per field (`s3`=&h, `s7`=&y, `s8`=&w, the &x walker spilled to 0x48), spills `i` (0x38), pFile (0x28) and pImage (0x30) and runs a 0x80 frame; with the body written as `g_FieldSpriteSlotRects[slot].h/.w/.y/.x` everywhere the prologue differs from instruction 1 (frame 0x58, pFile/pImage kept in registers). The walker spellings make the first 38 instructions identical, including the two spills and the ten saved registers. The reader `memcpy` source stays indexed (`g_FieldSpriteSlotRects[slot].x / 4`), which is also retail's `symbol + offset` form. Residual: retail's frame is still 0x80 vs 0x68 because it keeps one MORE value live than this cc1 does - a second address for the inner-loop `h` test (`s4 = offset + &h` alongside the &h walker), preheader copies of the &y and &w walkers (`move s6,s7`, `move s2,s8`), and `tim.prect` re-loaded from its stack slot before each of the four store sites. Measured on that shape and dead: the inner test as `t[slot].h` instead of `*pH` (75.69 / 147 insns), dropping the pH walker and indexing `h` at both uses (77.16 / 145), a single `offset/8` counter instead of separate `slot` and `offset` (73.18), the pointer walk with all fields through one `pRect++` (68.26 / 132 - cc1 then merges every walker into displacements off one base), and `while` instead of `do{}while` for the outer loop. So when a struct-array loop's diff opens with a frame size and a spill list that are all wrong, try the per-field walker locals before typing the access.

- id: g-structbase-index-form-keeps-one-vector-walker | keywords: loop, walker, induction, vector, increment, split, delay-slot, struct
  **ZEROING A STRUCT FIELD AND PASSING ITS ADDRESS SPLITS INTO TWO INDUCTION REGISTERS 8 APART WITH `pVector++`, BUT KEEPS ONE WALKER WHEN BOTH USES ARE WRITTEN AS THE SAME `&pSlots->vectors[i]` INDEX EXPRESSION** (round 438, field/main/main func_80077AB4, parked; Default preset). Retail zeroes `sh $zero,0/2/4($s2)` off ONE register and does `addiu s2,s2,8` in the `jal` delay slot; the `pVector->vx = 0; ... func(..., pVector++);` body emits `sh $zero,0($sN)` off the pre-increment pointer and `sh $zero,-2($sM)` / `0($sM)` off the post-increment one - two callee-saved registers for one pointer. Writing the three stores as `pSlots->vectors[i].vx/vy/vz` and the argument as `&pSlots->vectors[i]` gives retail's single walker plus the delay-slot addiu. Worth 3.5 points on the same body (75.93 vs 72.42 under the array-decl form of that unit's count global). The same body's remaining residue is a MULT giv, not this: see `g-qimode-index-blocks-the-mult-giv`.- id: g-conditional-const-pair-folds-away-the-third-constant-use | keywords: loop, hoist, constant, callee-saved, frame, ternary, fold, negu
  **A SMALL-CONSTANT LOOP INVARIANT THAT RETAIL KEEPS IN A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER NEEDS THREE REGISTER USES INSIDE THE LOOP, AND `if (c) x = A; else x = B;` (OR THE TERNARY) BETWEEN TWO CONSTANTS FOLDS TO ARITHMETIC, WHICH REMOVES ONE OF THEM - no spelling tried avoids the fold under gcc-2.6.0** (round 429, menu/main/misc8_r2 func_801D9F98, re-measured 95.67% / 1288 bytes / 322 insns against retail's 1296 / 324, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0). Retail's three in-loop uses of 2 are all register compares (`beq v1,s5` at the switch root, `beq v0,s5` at the choice site, `beq v0,s5` at the case-4 test), plus its `ori s5,zero,0x2` preheader load and the `$s5` save/restore pair that makes the frame 0x48 instead of 0x40; our body can only produce TWO register compares because the choice site becomes `xori a0,a0,0x2; sltiu a0,a0,1; negu a0,a0; andi a0,a0,0x7` (= `7 & -(x == 2)`), and at two uses loop.c never pays for the move (preheader ori + save + restore = 3 insns breaks even at three uses). Measured byte-identical at 95.67 / 322, each: `choice = 7; if (x != 2) choice = 0;`, `if (x == 2) choice = 7; else choice = 0;`, the ternary passed straight to the call (`f(x == 2 ? 7 : 0)`), and a `u_char choice` (that one adds a surplus `andi a0,a0,0x7`). So the saved-set diff and the fold are ONE residual, not two: when retail compares against a register holding a small constant and your body has an `xori/sltiu/negu/andi` chain at one site, retail's constant was hoisted and that fold is why yours never is. Also screened on the same body and dead: `-O3` 82.35, gcc-2.7.2-cdk `-G0` 78.56, gcc-2.7.2-cdk `-G8` compile-failed.
  **ZEROING A STRUCT FIELD AND PASSING ITS ADDRESS SPLITS INTO TWO INDUCTION REGISTERS 8 APART WITH `pVector++`, BUT KEEPS ONE WALKER WHEN BOTH USES ARE WRITTEN AS THE SAME `&pSlots->vectors[i]` INDEX EXPRESSION** (round 438, field/main/main func_80077AB4, parked; Default preset). Retail zeroes `sh $zero,0/2/4($s2)` off ONE register and does `addiu s2,s2,8` in the `jal` delay slot; the `pVector->vx = 0; ... func(..., pVector++);` body emits `sh $zero,0($sN)` off the pre-increment pointer and `sh $zero,-2($sM)` / `0($sM)` off the post-increment one - two callee-saved registers for one pointer. Writing the three stores as `pSlots->vectors[i].vx/vy/vz` and the argument as `&pSlots->vectors[i]` gives retail's single walker plus the delay-slot addiu. Worth 3.5 points on the same body (75.93 vs 72.42 under the array-decl form of that unit's count global). The same body's remaining residue is a MULT giv, not this: see `g-qimode-index-blocks-the-mult-giv`.
- id: g-op-histogram-tells-a-cse-residual-from-a-missing-binding | keywords: loop, cse, andi, ori, histogram, residual, register, pressure, park
  **COUNT OPCODES PER LOOP BODY ON BOTH SIDES BEFORE HUNTING A SPELLING: WHEN THE BRANCH, `lhu` AND `sh` COUNTS MATCH AND ONLY `andi`/`ori`/`or` DIFFER, NOTHING IS MISSING FROM THE SOURCE - retail's compile did LESS common-subexpression elimination than yours, so the gap is register pressure and the body is ready to park** (round 444, slus_006.64/system/system func_80034FFC, 424 retail insns, parked 66.79%; the method is what the park note records). Retail's plane-0 loop is 156 insns and its compile is 126: andi 37 against 24, ori 26 against 22, or 12 against 9, sltu+negu 4 against 2, but branches 27 against 27, lhu 13 against 13, sh 12 against 12 - retail re-forms every `word & bit` test (its `$v0` is clobbered by the next test) and re-derives each `(word & 0x80) ? C : 0` bool, while ours keeps `word & 0x10` in a register across two columns. Extract both histograms in one command each: retail's body from the address range in `asm/<bin>/nonmatchings/<unit>/<Func>.s` (`/* OFFSET */` column), yours from the generated `build/src/<unit>.c.s` between the loop label and its backward branch, skipping `.set`/labels/`#nop`. This separates "my body is short an operation" (a load, store or call count differs - keep hunting) from "the compiler deduplicated more here" (park), which the objdiff percentage alone cannot tell you.
- id: g-three-incremented-pointer-locals-mint-a-plus4-giv-per-base | keywords: loop, giv, induction, pointer, frame, callee-saved, increment, spill
  **THREE POINTER LOCALS INCREMENTED IN THE `for`-UPDATE MAKE cc1 MINT ONE DERIVED GIV PER BASE (`pA+4`, `pB+4`, `pC+4`), SO THE LOOP CARRIES SIX REGISTERS INSTEAD OF FOUR AND THE FUNCTION GROWS A FRAME AND A CALLEE-SAVED SAVE - and the two cheaper spellings of the same loop body are measured too** (round 444, slus_006.64/system/system func_80034FFC: writing a 3-word stride walk as `pAbove`/`pBelow`/`pDest` all advanced in the `for`-update scored 60.46% / 413 insns / 1652 bytes with an 8-byte frame and `$16` saved; assigning `pAbove`/`pBelow` from `pDest` at the top of the body instead scored 64.92% / 397 / 1588 with no frame, and leaving them as address expressions `(pDest - rowStride)[k]` / `(pDest + rowStride)[k]` off the one advanced pointer scored 66.79% / 391 / 1564 with no frame - retail is 424 / 1696 with four increments and no frame). So when retail's loop increments three row pointers plus the base and shows only ONE `+4` giv, the source did not hold all three as locals: reach for `g-op-histogram-tells-a-cse-residual-from-a-missing-binding` before spending runs on pointer spellings, and note that `rowStride` scaled in two separate places (retail `sll v1,a3,16 / sra v1,v1,16 / sll v0,v1,1` for one pointer, a second `sll v1,v1,1` for the other) is the shape loop.c's giv addends take - folding both into one `sra 15` is what the expression form does. Re-measured round 457 (same function, same note, REDO lane): spelling retail's ONE `+4` giv explicitly - `pRow2 = pDest + 2;` at the top of the loop body with `pRow2[-1] |= mask;` / `pRow2[0] |= mask;` replacing the `pDest[1]`/`pDest[2]` stores - is 66.80% / 392 insns / 1568 bytes, i.e. +4 bytes and +1 instruction over the expression form and still 32 instructions short, and the three-local form re-measured at 59.33% / 411 / 1644 with the 8-byte frame. So the +4 giv is worth 4 bytes, not the match: the 24 missing `andi` and the two missing `sltu`/`negu` bools (retail computes the `(word & 0x80) != 0` bool once per column, the body once per plane) are the whole of it, and no pointer spelling moves them.

- id: g-a-mult-after-the-jal-is-an-inlined-expression-not-a-giv | keywords: loop, hoist, cse, call, mult, spill, frame, expression
  **A `mult` THAT RETAIL RE-EXECUTES INSIDE EACH ITERATION OF A LOOP WHOSE BODY CONTAINS A `jal` IS THE SOURCE WRITING THE EXPRESSION IN THE STORE STATEMENTS, NOT A HOISTED LOCAL: gcc cannot CSE a value across a call, so `nV = texY + rowStep * (j + 1);` before the loop is computed ONCE while `pPoly->v2 = texY + rowStep * (j + 1);` gives retail's per-iteration `mult/mflo/addu` - but writing it inline also makes retail's registers (texX*4, texY, the running end value, clut) stay live across every call, and forcing the inline form onto a body that had hoisted them RAISES pressure instead of lowering it** (round 446, lib_gear/main/main func_801E1A14, re-parked 76.11% / 2172 bytes / 543 insns against retail's 2276 / 569, XenoLibraryDiv). Read the two shapes as a set: retail's outer segment loop is 147 insns and the hoisted body 133, the difference being 2 extra static mults (v2 in loop 1, v0/v1 in loop 2), EIGHT words spilled around each `SetPolyGT3` against six (the extra two are the invariant registers), a second induction pointer `s1 = pSeg + k * 0x28` (field stores at disp 0x14..0x2D) where the hoisted body uses one base at `pSeg + 8 + k * 0x28` (disp 0xC..0x25), and a `addu a1,t6,zero` copy of the multiplicand. Measured on that body: dropping the `nV1` local and writing the expression inline in both k-loops gave 16.57% / 2268 bytes / 567 insns - retail's instruction COUNT to within 2 - but the frame grew 0x130 -> 0x140 and the whole allocation rotated, i.e. the reading is right and the pressure is the wall. Also measured on the same body and dead: `pSeg->polys[k].field` instead of the `pPoly` local (75.25 / 2176 / 544) - the local is not what anchors the `+8` in the base. So decode the store-by-store semantics FIRST (both k-loops there store retail's exact values) and park on the hoist/pressure statement rather than hunting the `+8`.

- id: g-movable-copy-hoist-is-context-not-spelling | keywords: loop, hoist, move, copy, preheader, latch, movable, body
  **A LOOP-ARGUMENT COPY THAT RETAIL KEEPS IN THE BODY (`addu a1,s1,zero` right after the loop label) BUT YOUR COMPILE HOISTS INTO A PREHEADER COPY PLUS A RE-COPY AFTER THE BIV INCREMENT (in the back-edge delay slot) IS A loop.c move_movables DECISION ABOUT THE LOOP'S SURROUNDING RTL, NOT ABOUT THE LOOP - so no spelling of that loop, its bound or its counter reaches it** (round 454, field/main/misc2 func_80074108, re-parked 97.44% / 1432 bytes / 358 insns against retail's 357, one instruction over and so never linkable, XenoFieldNoGp). Retail has three such loops and the same body reproduces two of them (loop 1 body copy, loop 2 init+latch) while only loop 3 hoists. Measured dead on it, each 358 insns: changing loop 1's bound to 2 iterations (0x16) and to 4 iterations (0x18, loop 3's exact trip count) leaves ITS body copy in place, so the movable's iteration-count savings are ruled out; a fresh counter pseudo for loop 3 (`k` instead of the shared `i`) still hoists (96.42); and the four pointer/index spellings in the park note all hoist. `permute.sh` cannot run on such a body when it holds a struct-typed cast the permuter's parser rejects (`conversion to non-scalar type requested` on the preprocessed base), so the park gets no permuter pass until the body is simplified. Round 467 addendum (same function): the ONE-ARRAY spelling is dead too - `&D_800B06BC[i]` for the third loop, whose preheader folds to the same 0x800B0FEC immediate because the array really is contiguous (`D_800B0FEC` IS `D_800B06BC[0x15]`), measures 97.41 / 1432 / 358 with the SAME latch copy, so the index ADDEND is not the trigger either. Also worth knowing before blaming a neighbouring residual: loop optimization runs before register allocation, so a tail that keeps retail's mask in `$a3` where yours uses `$t1` (this park's residual 2) CANNOT be the cause of the hoist, and both would have to close to reach 100.

- id: g-counter-init-before-the-address-lifts-the-hoist-order | keywords: loop, hoist, preheader, order, invariant, movable, counter, for-init
  **A LOOP-INVARIANT ADDRESS THAT RETAIL FORMS IN THE PREHEADER *AFTER* THE COUNTER INIT COMES OUT BEFORE IT WHEN THE ADDRESS IS A SOURCE STATEMENT ABOVE THE `for` - WRITING THE COUNTER INIT AS ITS OWN STATEMENT AND LEAVING THE `for`'s INIT EMPTY (`i = 0; pItemId = &g_Global->array[idx]; for (; i < 3; i++)`) PUTS THE TWO IN RETAIL'S ORDER, because the front end then emits `i = 0` first and the address sits where loop.c's move_movables places a hoisted invariant** (round 456, menu/main/misc9 func_801DB920, still parked: 97.70 -> 98.45%, 36 -> 34 differing lines, retail's exact 1068 bytes / 267 insns). Retail's preheader is `move s1,zero` (refresh) / `move s0,zero` (i) / `lui+addiu` (the 0x2026 base) / `addu s2,s8,v0`; the plain body emits refresh, la, addu, then `move s0,zero` - the same instructions in the other order - and the same `move s1,zero`/`move s0,zero` pair at the top of the function is NOT affected. Companion statement-placement measurement on the same body, also a source-only win: `result = 0;` belongs INSIDE the `if (refresh)` body as its first statement, which is what puts retail's `move s3,zero` in that branch's delay slot (97.47 -> 97.70); written above the `if` it is hoisted into the preceding `jal`'s slot instead. The same seam from the other side is `g-two-preheader-inits-are-one-comma-statement` (a `for (i = 0, p = ...)` comma init forces retail's order); that spelling was NOT measured here, this one needs no comma list and also keeps the address out of the `for` init. Both edits are byte-neutral in size, and neither moves the residual: that body's two open items are a `$s1`/`$s2` refresh-vs-pointer swap and an unreachable base-then-constant `addu` pair.

- id: g-a-pointer-local-for-a-global-array-buys-the-mask-hoist | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, pointer, local, global, mask, preheader
  **A `pVerts = g_QuadCorners;` LOCAL THAT ONLY MIRRORS A GLOBAL ARRAY COSTS A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER, BECAUSE THE LOCAL'S EXISTENCE MAKES loop.c HOIST `addPrim`'s 0xFFFFFF MASK INTO THE PREHEADER: SPELLING THE ELEMENTS THROUGH THE GLOBAL (`g_QuadCorners[k].vx`) INSTEAD CLOSED 89.56 -> 93.85 AND REMOVED THE HOIST** (round 457, slus_006.64/system/rendering_atfree func_8001EE88, XenoRenderingAtfree = cdk -G0, re-parked 93.85% / 848 bytes against retail's 844; func_8001F1D4 in the same unit reached 91.22% on the same recipe, itself up from a 77.38% park). With the local the preheader emits `lui s7,0xff / ori s7,s7,0xffff` (retail materialises both masks INSIDE the loop) and the saved set rotates: pOt, needed across the `jal RotAverage4`, no longer gets a callee-saved register and is spilled to 48(sp) with a `move` copy in the entry, which is the whole of the extra instruction. Retail's own `.s` for both functions keeps `lui t1,%hi(g_QuadCorners)` live and spills it to 0x30(sp) around the call, i.e. the %hi form is retail's and the local is not. Two companion measurements from the same bodies: `width` must be re-loaded from the frame entry AFTER the RotAverage4 call (kept live it takes a callee-saved register), and the frame loop is a `do {} while (++i != count_bytes[0] >> 2)` with INDEXED `pFrameData[i]` - the `for` form duplicates the exit test (+4 instructions) and `pFrameData++` with `pFrameData->` re-bases the induction register. Both parks' residue afterwards is only the callee-saved hand-out (pSpriteData/pPrim/height/z rotated) plus one nop where retail fills the flags-load delay slot with the tileY shift.


- id: g-a-pointer-walk-not-an-index-decides-where-the-biased-giv-base-lands | keywords: loop, giv, strength-reduce, index, pointer-walk, biased-base, addiu, offset
  **WHEN RETAIL ADDRESSES A LOOP BODY'S FIELDS THROUGH A SECOND BASE BIASED INTO THE MIDDLE OF THE STRUCT (`addiu a3,t1,0x51` for offset 0x50/0x51 plus `-0x4d/-0x4a/-0x4e` for 0x3/0x4/0x7) AND YOUR COMPILE USES ONE UNBIASED BASE, THE SOURCE IS A POINTER WALK: `pSlot = g_BattleEffectSlots; for (i = 0; i < n; i++, pSlot++)` produces loop.c's biased giv, `pSlot = &g_BattleEffectSlots[i]` produces one base with positive offsets and comes out two instructions short (no preheader `addiu` and no second `+= stride` in the latch), 1852 against retail's 1860 bytes** (round 458, battling/main/misc5 func_8007B388, Default, 95.35 -> 98.68% and retail's exact 465 insns once the walk replaced the index). The bias is whichever field the giv survives for, not necessarily the first: the same body with the four colour bytes written as four `sb`s also yields the biased base, so it is the walk, not the statement order, that decides it.



- id: a-a-28-stride-byte-index-needs-its-own-for-clause-iv | keywords: biv, strength, reduce, multiply, 28, for-clause, iv, synth_mult
  **cc1 2.6.0 WILL NOT STRENGTH-REDUCE A `slot * 0x1C` INDEX (it derives 28i as 4*(8i-i) inline, three insns, from the loop counter) BUT IT DOES REDUCE AN EXPLICIT FOR-CLAUSE IV INCREMENTING BY 0x1C - so a global walked at a non-power-of-two stride needs its own `actorOff` variable and gives retail's `addiu $t6,$t6,0x1C` at the loop bottom where every `table[slot * 0x1C]` spelling computes the product per pass** (round 474, battle/main/misc2 func_80075938, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0; `for (slot = 0, actorOff = 0; slot < 3; slot++, actorOff += 0x1C, pTimer++, pLimit++)` with `g_BattleSlotActorIds[actorOff]` measured 92.72 -> 93.40% and 201 -> 181 differing lines). The same body's 8-stride and halfword-stride accesses (`g_BattleSlotFlags[slot * 8]`, the `u16` tables walked by 2) DO get bivs for free, which is the tell: a shift stride reduces, a synth_mult stride does not. The same shape is recorded in battle/main/misc1's parked func_80073538 note, which found it first for the same table.
- id: a-guarded-for-keeps-its-entry-test-a-do-while-does-not | keywords: loop, inverted, rotated, entry, do-while, guard, preheader
  **A `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)` INSIDE `if (n != 0)` STILL GETS AN ENTRY TEST UNDER cc1 2.6.0 WHERE RETAIL'S BODY IS BOTTOM-TESTED, AND WRITING THE SCAN AS `do { ... i++; } while (i < n);` REPRODUCES RETAIL'S ROTATED LOOP - it also fixes the PREHEADER CREATION ORDER, i.e. the loop's hoisted invariants go before the front-end pointer sums, which un-rotates a whole block of callee-saved registers** (round 476, menu/main/misc9 func_801DE5CC, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0; 92.45 -> 92.77% and -4 insns, then the `pQuantities`-before-`pIds` swap and making the second access index a for-clause biv took it to 93.22). Companion on the same body: a sum of a spilled parameter and the loop counter (`g_X[arg1 + i]`, retail `lw s4,0x38(sp)` once + `addiu s4,s4,1` in the latch and `lui at,%hi` + `addu at,at,s4` per use) is reached by giving it its own for-clause iv - `for (i = 0, j = arg1; i < 8; i++, j++)` with `g_X[j]` - which is the same lever as the 0x1C stride entry above. LIMIT, measured round 478 (menu/main/misc11_r2_260 func_801E61B0, same preset): the preheader-creation half does NOT reach a loop whose init statements are plain assignments in the block that falls into the loop - `j = 0; offset = 0; do { ... } while (offset < 0x1974);` compiles BYTE-IDENTICAL to the `for (j = 0, offset = 0; ...)` form, because the hoisted invariant and every giv init are still appended after those statements. That lever only moves the invariants when loop.c has to build a new preheader block (a guard in front of the loop), so a residual whose only difference is that retail's preheader starts with the hoist is not a do-while away.

- id: a-repeated-store-address-in-a-do-while-is-a-strength_reduce-giv | keywords: loop, giv, strength-reduce, address, repeated, store, frame, callee-saved
  **A STORE ADDRESS THAT APPEARS TWICE IN A LOOP BODY (ONE PER ARM OF AN IF/ELSE) IS A CSE PSEUDO, AND strength_reduce HOISTS IT AS A GIV: `addiu s0,s1,0xE` IN THE PREHEADER, A SIXTH CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER AND A FRAME ONE SLOT BIGGER. RETAIL'S PER-ITERATION `addu v1,s0,zero` PLUS `sh v0,0xE(v1)` IS THE SAME SUM NOT HOISTED** (round 476, battle/main/misc3 func_80076D58, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0, parked 92.31% / 344 bytes / 86 insns against retail's 332 / 83).
