PROOF it is the PASS and not the source: the identical body compiled with `tools/gcc-2.6.0-psx/cc1 -O2 -G8 ... -fno-strength-reduce` comes out with retail's exact shape (frame 0x28, five saved regs, `sh $2,14($16)`, `addu $16,$16,40 / addu $2,$18,80 / slt`), missing only retail's one extra copy. Every source shape that mentions the address twice keeps the giv: typed `p->clut` 91.65 (and a typed POINTER compare makes the loop test `sltu` where retail has `slt`, so the cursor really is a signed byte pointer), `u16 *pClut = (u16 *)p` with `pClut[7]` 92.31, `for (i = 0; i < 2; i++, p++)` 91.52 (`slti`, extra index register). try_flags: 2.7.2 92.31, cdk compile-failed, -O1 82.36, -O3 compile-failed. So when retail's frame is one callee-saved register SMALLER than every spelling and the extra register's only job is a hoisted `addiu base,const`, read the loop for a repeated store address and report the -fno-strength-reduce measurement instead of hunting spellings.

- id: g-a-masked-local-from-a-wider-parameter-is-copy-propagated | keywords: mask, andi, narrow, local, parameter, copy-propagation, callee-saved, hoist
  **A `u8 slot = arg0;` LOCAL CANNOT BE USED TO FORCE RETAIL'S ONCE-MASKED REGISTER WHEN THE PARAMETER BEHAVES LIKE `u32`: cc1 2.6.0 copy-propagates the local back to `(u8)arg0` and re-emits `andi 0xff` at every site, so the register the park is missing never appears** (round 480, battle/main/misc17 func_80091064, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0, parked 91.38% / 1444 bytes / 361 insns against retail's 1440 / 360). Measured on the same body: `u32 arg0` plus `u8 slot = arg0;` before the first flags test, with `slot` used for the char-id index, both strides and both row bases = 91.28% / 1444 (the mask is re-formed at all four sites, i.e. exactly as without the local, while retail keeps one copy in `$s3`); the same local assigned INSIDE EACH ARM (retail's `move s4,a0` in both arms) = 91.80% but 1452 bytes / 363 insns, so it grows the loop-invariant hoist instead of removing it. So when retail holds one `andi 0xff` in a callee-saved register and your compile re-masks per site, the missing thing is a FREE callee-saved register and not a spelling: find the invariant address occupying it (the table-base entry above), and do not spend runs on masked locals.

- id: g-a-typed-store-is-what-lets-the-latch-hoist-the-invariant | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, latch, typed, store, alias, cast, u8, preheader, copy, move
  **A LOOP-INVARIANT GLOBAL-POINTER LOAD THAT RETAIL HOISTS INTO THE LATCH AS A COPY (`move a2,v1`, the guard's own load left dead in `$v1`) IS REACHED BY MAKING THE LOOP'S ONLY STORE A TYPED STRUCT-FIELD STORE - a raw `*(u16 *)((u8 *)g_Table + i)` store compiles the SAME instruction stream but makes cc1 2.7.2 keep the load inside the loop and reload the pointer every iteration (four extra instructions)** (round 480, battle/main/misc4 func_80078998, Default preset, 98.16 / 408 bytes -> 99.42% / 412 = retail's exact 412 bytes / 103 insns with every non-reloc line identical). The missing instruction was ONE `move` and the whole park history blamed an allocator tie; the discrimination is 5 minutes of variants on the same body: `for (n = 0; n < g_BattleCommandQueue->count; n++) { if (g_BattleCommandSlotIds[i] == 0xFD) { *(u16 *)((u8 *)g_BattleCommandRecords + i) = mask; break; } i += 0x48; }` measures 93.20 / 416 (pointer reloaded in the latch, `lui+lw+lbu` every iteration), and the identical body with `g_BattleCommandRecords[n].command` / `.slotMask` measures 99.42 / 412. Two companion measurements on the same function: a `pQueue = g_BattleCommandQueue;` local used by the loop test collapses the copy away and is the park that cannot link (98.16 / 408, one instruction short), and indexing the byte table as `g_BattleCommandSlotIds[n * 0x48]` next to a record-index walk makes gcc hoist that table's BASE into a callee-saved register instead of sharing the byte offset (`lui/addiu $s0`, frame 0x28 -> 0x30, 95.38 / 412). So when retail's latch keeps an invariant load in a caller-saved copy, read the loop's store width/typing before its register allocation, and prefer the typed struct-field walk over the byte-offset cast form even when the cast form is the unit's documented idiom.

- id: for-and-while-are-the-same-loop-form-and-the-operand-order-is-not-free | keywords: loop, for, while, do-while, form, identical, canonical, operand, order, slt, reorg, copy
  **`while (i < n) { body; i++; }` COMPILES BYTE-IDENTICALLY TO `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)` UNDER 2.7.2 (so the for/while choice is NOT the knob for how reorg duplicates a loop-head instruction), AND A COMPARISON'S OPERAND ORDER IS ONLY FREE IN THE DIRECTION cc1 CANONICALISES** (round 482, field/main/misc7 func_80099214, Default; parked 97.99% / 1896 bytes / 474 insns against retail's 1900 / 475). Retail duplicates a loop-head `addu a2,s1,zero` into the latch's branch delay slot; that only happens when sched2 leaves that copy as the block's first movable instruction, so it is an allocator/sched2 consequence of the whole loop body, not a source form. Measured on the same body: `walkmesh < count - 1` 97.99 / 1896 / 474 with 141 diff lines; the `while` form BYTE-IDENTICAL (same four numbers); `if (count - 1 > 0) { i = 0; do { body } while (++i < count - 1); }` 97.95 / 1896 / 474 with 177 diff lines (more residual for the same size); `count - 1 >= i + 1` 97.66 / 1904 / 476 against `i + 1 <= count - 1` at 98.89 / 1904 / 476 - only the written order `i + 1 <= ...` gives retail's preheader guard `addiu v0,count,-1 / blez` and retail's `sh` schedule, and its remaining loop residual is the giv's `addiu v1,i,1 / slt v0,v0,v1 / beqz` against retail's `slt v0,i,v0 / bnez`. So read a park's `<`/`<=` spelling and its operand order as part of the measurement, and do not spend a lane on for-vs-while.
- id: g-two-loop-invariants-hoist-each-on-its-own-life | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, constant, callee-saved, frame, life, order, li
  **A LOOP WITH TWO LOOP-INVARIANT CONSTANTS HOISTS THEM INDEPENDENTLY, EACH ON ITS OWN LUID SPAN, SO MOVING ONE SIBLING LOAD CAN HOIST THE *OTHER* CONSTANT AND COST A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER - which is why a park that blames constant X for the sixth saved register can be wrong about which one is left to fix** (round 482, slus_006.64/system/animation_scripts func_80022660, XenoGraphics = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -O2 -G8, parked 95.81% / retail's exact 788 bytes / 197 insns / s0-s5 + ra). Two measurements on the same body, each changing ONE thing: (a) moving the 0xBE arm's 0x3C load after the `flags_0xAC` store (to chase retail's `lbu/lbu/lw a1,60` order) measures 93.50% / 796 / 199 - the extra byte pair is `li s5,-9` in the PROLOGUE with `and a1,a1,s5` / `and a0,a0,s5` in the arm, i.e. the FLIP MASK -9 hoisted because that move pushed its second use 6 instructions further from its first; (b) putting the tail's `newFlags = flags & 0xF03FFFFF` first (retail's AND position) with the 0xBE arm untouched measures 796 / 199 with `lui s5,0xf03f / ori s5,s5,0xffff` in the prologue instead. Both constants are materialised inside the loop, twice each, in retail - so retail's source kept BOTH of their spans short enough and no C spelling here does. Read which `li`/`lui` appears in the prologue before accepting a park note that names one constant: the one still inside the loop is not the residual.

- id: g-a-redundant-mask-on-a-shifted-loop-test-hoists-but-is-not-folded | keywords: loop, hoist, invariant, constant, mask, fold, lui, and, dead
  **A REDUNDANT `& 0xFFFF0000` ON A `(x << 16)` LOOP TEST DOES MAKE cc1 HOIST `lui r,0xffff` INTO A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER, BUT THE AND IS NOT FOLDED, so the constant keeps a real use and the spelling costs a register plus an instruction instead of producing retail's dead one** (round 483, battle/main/misc35 func_800C0FAC, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0, parked). Retail carries a DEAD `lui s5,0xFFFF0000` in the outer preheader (saved and restored, never read) beside `li s6,-1` and `lui s7,%hi(g_BattleWdsEntry)`; rewriting the wait as `while (((SoundGetPendingSpuCommandType(0) << 16) & 0xFFFF0000) != 0)` does emit `lui s3,0xffff` in the prologue - so the constant IS an invariant cc1 hands a callee-saved register and a park note that blames "one more invariant constant than the body produces" is right about the mechanism - but the emitted test is `sll v0,v0,16 / and v0,v0,s3 / beqz`, i.e. 2.7.2-cdk's combine does not delete the redundant and, and the extra invariant also displaces the `-1` hoist into the switch arm (`li s0,-1` per iteration): 91.55% / 400 bytes. Retail's dead constant therefore comes from a fold that runs AFTER loop.c hoisted it, and no spelling of the loop test reaches that shape - park such a function instead of hunting the mask. Companion measurement on the same body: storing through a pointer-to-global local (`SoundWDSEntry **pWdsSlot = &g_BattleWdsEntry;`) is the only spelling measured that reproduces retail's `sw %lo(g_BattleWdsEntry)(s7)` store and its 9-save frame, but cc1 then materialises the FULL address in the preheader (`lui v0,%hi` + `addiu s7,v0,%lo`) where retail carries the `%hi` alone with the symbol's low half as the store's offset: 94.34% / 400 bytes / 100 insns against retail's 404 / 101, versus 94.06 / 392 for the direct `g_X = ...` spelling, which re-forms `%hi` inline every iteration.

- id: i-a-while-scan-is-inverted-and-a-goto-scan-is-not | keywords: loop, rotated, inverted, goto, index, strength, giv, copy, scan
  **EVERY `while (cond)` FORM OF A SCAN LOOP IS LOOP-INVERTED BY 2.7.2 (entry test duplicated, `beqz` back edge), SO RETAIL'S TOP TEST WITH A `j` BACK EDGE AND THE `addu a0,a1,zero` POINTER COPY CANNOT BE TYPED AS A `while`/`for` AT ALL - BUT THE SAME BODY AS A `goto` SCAN KEEPS THE TOP TEST, AND WRITING THE SCAN ON THE INDEX (`buf[i]`) INSTEAD OF A POINTER IS WHAT MAKES gcc STRENGTH-REDUCE `i` INTO THE WALKING REGISTER AND EMIT THE COPY** (round 485, world_map/main/misc2 func_80075E7C, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2 --dont-expand-li; parked 89.46 -> 97.59% at retail's exact 540 bytes / 135 insns, the whole pick loop then instruction-identical). Measured identical-inverted for `while ((cell = *pCell) == 0) pCell++, i++`, `while ((cell = buf[i]) == 0) i++`, `for (;;) { if (cell = *pCell) break; ... }` and `while (pick > 0) { ... }`; the goto form `scan: if ((cell = buf[i]) != 0) goto found; i++; goto scan; found: buf[i] = cell - 1;` inside a `do { pick--; ... } while (pick > 0)` reproduces retail's `move a0,a1 / lbu v0,0(a0) / bnez / addiu v0,v0,-1 / addiu a1,a0,1 / j / addiu t1,t1,1 / bgtz / sb v0,0(a1)` exactly. Keep the loaded byte in a `u8 cell` local or the store reaches for a reload instead of retail's delay-slot `addiu v0,v0,-1`.

- id: f-a-digit-quotient-staged-in-a-u8-local-is-what-reuses-the-masked-quotient | keywords: div, modulo, quotient, u8, andi, digits, sfx, reload, tens
  **A TWO-DIGIT SPLIT WHOSE RETAIL IS `sb q,off(sp)` / `andi v0,v0,0xff` / shift-add-by-10 / `subu a1,a1,v1` WITH THE RAW ARGUMENT ON THE LEFT IS ONE `u8` LOCAL STAGING THE QUOTIENT: `u8 tens = arg1 / 10; digits[0] = tens; digits[1] = arg1 - tens * 10;` - and neither `arg1 % 10` nor `arg1 - digits[0] * 10` reaches it** (round 492, battle/main/misc17 func_80092B74, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0; the head plus both following calls went instruction-identical, 87.17 -> 89.40%). `% 10` multiplies the ANDI'd copy of the division's input (`andi a0,s4,0xff` then `subu a0,a0,v1`, no `andi` on the quotient, and the `sb` sinks below the shift chain), and reading the ARRAY ELEMENT back makes cc1 reload it (`lbu v1,16(sp)`, one instruction more) - only the scalar local leaves the quotient in its register so the store's truncation is that register, i.e. the `andi` retail has. The tell: retail stores the quotient and then masks the same register, while the subtraction uses the PARAMETER register raw.

- id: l-the-for-clause-order-decides-whether-the-increment-is-duplicated-into-the-arm | keywords: loop, increment, duplicate, delay, slot, jal, for, count
  **WHEN RETAIL HAS THE LOOP INCREMENT TWICE - once in the arms' `jal`/`j` DELAY SLOTS, once in the shared continue/else tail - THE KNOB IS THE ORDER OF THE TWO INCREMENTS IN THE `for` CLAUSE: pointer-first duplicates, index-first does not** (round 494, field/main/misc8 func_80086590, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8). Retail's tail loop runs `for`-rotated with `addiu s0,s0,8` in the `FieldUpdateActorSoundSlot` jal slot, `addiu s1,s1,1` in the following `j`'s slot and a second copy of both before the `j`; `for (i = 0; i < 3; pDelta += 4, i++)` reproduces that instruction for instruction (loop.c duplicates the increment block into the arm, reorg fills both slots), while the same body with `for (i = 0; i < 3; i++, pDelta += 4)` keeps ONE copy - 4 instructions / 16 bytes short of retail, which is what an "eight bytes short" park note there was chasing. A manual-increment body (increments written inside the arm before a `continue`) reproduces the duplication too but leaves gcc free to hoist one of them above the call, so prefer the `for` clause. Read the two increments' ORDER in retail's own delay slots before writing the clause, and count instructions afterwards, because the index-first spelling looks identical in the source.

## store ordering and volatile

- id: h-a-scratchpad-store-through-a-typed-pointer-macro-is-the-serial-schedule | keywords: scratchpad, store, svector, cast, schedule, sched1, serial, load-delay, nop
  **THE SAME THREE SCRATCHPAD STORES COME OUT OF sched1 SERIAL WHEN WRITTEN THROUGH A TYPED POINTER MACRO (`((SVECTOR *)0x1F8000A0)->vx`) AND AGITATED WHEN WRITTEN AS THREE `*(s16 *)0x1F8000Ax` CASTS, so a park stuck at 84% on a store group that retail keeps in statement order is a TYPING job, not a scheduling wall - check the unit for a `WORLD_MAP_TILE_POS`-style define before trying barriers** (round 495, world_map/main/misc7 func_80080944, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2 --dont-expand-li, unparked from 84.76% / 164 bytes / 41 insns to 100.00% / 168 / 42 with one edit). Retail's group is `lw v0,0x28 / sh zero,4 / sra / sh 0xA0 / lw v0,0x2C / sra / sh 0xA2 / lw v0,0x30 / nop / sra / sh 0xA4`, all three values in `$v0`, i.e. one register and statement order with a load-delay `nop` on the third; the cast spelling makes sched1 hoist the z load to the group head, fill the x load's slot with it, sink the neighbouring `command = 0` store into the z load's slot (one instruction short, 41 vs 42), and take the slot base into `$a3`. Compiling the unit's own `.i` with `-fno-schedule-insns -fno-schedule-insns2` shows RTL already holds retail's order with the single `$2` pseudo, so the RTL is not the problem; a 6-variant cc1 sweep in one probe (cast with a shared `v` local, three inline casts, `((SVECTOR *)...)` with `->vx`, a `s16 *pTile` local with `pTile[0]`, empty-`do{}while(0)` barriers between the casts, three separate `s32` locals) gives retail's exact stream ONLY for the SVECTOR form - the `s16 *` local emits `sh $2,0($7)` for the first store and the barriers change nothing (byte-identical, which is why the earlier park recorded them dead). The stores still print as `sh $2,528482464` in cc1's `.s`, so the difference is the address rtx being one CSE'd pseudo in the cast form; do not reason it out, sweep the spellings.

- id: h-volatile-on-an-absolute-address-store-costs-a-register | keywords: volatile, store, absolute, literal, address, register, lui, at, scratchpad
  **A `volatile` CAST ON A STORE THROUGH A LITERAL ABSOLUTE ADDRESS DOES NOT KEEP THE ASSEMBLER'S `lui $at / sh %lo(0x1F8000A4)(at)` FORM: gcc has to put the address in a REGISTER, so the body gains a `lui aN,0x1F80 / ori aN,aN,0xA4` pair and every later allocation shifts - measure it on a scratchpad store before reaching for volatile as a scheduling barrier** (round 471, world_map/main/misc9 func_80088720, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2 with --dont-expand-li, parked 97.59% / retail's exact 1056 bytes / 264 insns, whole residual a store-block schedule). `*(volatile s16*)0x1F8000A4 = 0;` measures 95.88 / 1064 (a3 = 0x1F8000A4, `sh zero,0(a3)`), where the plain store is the two-instruction `lui at` + `sh`; the same cast on ONE of the two clears buys the same `lui aN / ori aN` pair (read off the diff, not scored). The lever that volatile normally buys (`h-volatile-store-pins-the-arg-pair`) needs a store whose base is ALREADY a register, so check the addressing form in retail's `.s` first: a `lui $at` there means the plain store is the right pin.
- id: h-a-volatile-final-store-keeps-it-out-of-the-exit-jumps-delay-slot | keywords: volatile, store, delay-slot, reorg, jr, tail, clamp, jump, nop
  **A STORE THAT ENDS A FUNCTION-SIZED BLOCK AND IS FOLLOWED BY A JUMP TO THE COMMON EXIT IS FILLED INTO THAT JUMP'S DELAY SLOT BY reorg, WHICH COSTS ONE INSTRUCTION AGAINST RETAIL'S `lui $at / sh / j / nop`; SPELLING THE STORE `*(volatile s16 *)&g_X[0] = 0x80;` PINS IT BEFORE THE JUMP AND GIVES RETAIL'S SHAPE** (round 477, world_map/main/misc6 func_8007E4E4, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2, parked 91.55 -> 91.59% at 1736 bytes / 434 insns against retail's 1752 / 438; the arm is `if (g_WorldMapCameraRot[0] >= 0x81) g_WorldMapCameraRot[0] = 0x80;` at the end of the tail shared by three switch arms). Same round, the neighbouring residual was NOT fixed this way: a volatile cast on the *load* of the same global (`*(volatile s16 *)&g_X[0] >= 0x81`) does give retail's per-access `lui`+`lhu`/`lui`+`sh` forms and the closer byte count (1744 / 436) but gcc zexts the volatile load and adds an `sll`/`sra` pair, dropping the score to 89.46 - check the load WIDTH after any volatile cast.

- id: h-changing-the-stored-constant-proves-a-cross-jump-wall | keywords: cross-jump, cross-jumping, store, constant, merge, duplicate, jal, tail, register
  **A BODY THAT CROSS-JUMPS TWO `g_X = 1;` STORES RETAIL KEEPS APART WILL NOT BE SEPARATED BY ANY SPELLING OF THE STORE, AND THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SETTLES IT IN ONE RUN IS TO WRITE A DIFFERENT CONSTANT IN ONE ARM: `= 0` keeps retail's block shape and jumps the score to 98.41 (336 bytes against retail's 340), which proves the shared body is right and the ONLY residual is the merge** (round 476, field/main/misc func_8008F7B8, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, parked 92.24% / 320 bytes / 80 insns against retail's 340 / 85). Retail stores the flag twice: one block shared by two arms with the value in `$v0`, and the third arm's own store with the value in `$v1`, which still holds the 1 built for a later `== 1` compare - so at post-regalloc jump time the two store blocks are not identical. This build merges all three into one tail block, the merged block's live range makes cse reuse its constant register in the third arm, and every spelling keeps it: the two conditions split into separate else-ifs, a flat early-return form, an empty `do {} while (0)` around an arm, `*(volatile s32 *)&g_X = 1;` (cc1 emits the same `lui $at` + `sw`), `(s32)1`, and the 2.6.0 / 2.7.2-cdk presets (all 92.24). Read the two store sites' SOURCE registers in retail's `.s` before spending a lane on a duplicated store: when they differ, the merge is an allocator consequence and the wall is real; when they are the same register, retail merged them too and the duplication is elsewhere (see h-one-retail-store-at-a-join and h-an-in-place-or).

- id: h-the-block-split-and-the-block-position-are-opposite-knobs | keywords: cross-jump, store, position, then, else, return, block, order
  **THE TWO HALVES OF A KEPT-APART STORE BLOCK ARE OPPOSITE KNOBS: MAKING THE DUPLICATED STORE THE `THEN` BLOCK OF AN if/else CHAIN SEPARATES ITS SOURCE REGISTER EXACTLY AS RETAIL BUT EMITS THAT BLOCK BEFORE THE ELSE BODY, AND MAKING IT THE `ELSE` (OR A per-arm `return`) RE-MERGES IT** (round 489, field/main/misc func_8008F7B8, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8; same function as h-changing-the-stored-constant-proves-a-cross-jump-wall). `} else if (g_GameWdsStreamInProgress == 1 || g_GameWdsBankLoadState == -1) { g_FieldScriptVMStopFlag = 1; } else { <body> }` produced retail's `sw $v1` for the third store and retail's `sw $v0` + own `j` for the first two, i.e. the registers are right and the merge is gone - but gcc 2.7.2 emits the then block before the else body (no -freorder-blocks), so the store lands mid-function and pays a `j`+`nop`: 344 bytes / 86 insns / 90.82% against retail's 340 / 85 / (92.24 for the merged body). Adding `return;` inside that then block changes nothing (same 344). Inverted to `else if (stream != 1 && loadState != -1) { <body> } else { stop; }` it re-merges to 320 / 80 / 92.24. So when a park note says "the merge is an allocator consequence", the remaining question is only WHERE retail's kept-apart block sits: if it is the function's last block, no gcc 2.7.2 body reaches both; if retail's block sits before the else body, the then-block form is the whole answer.

- id: h-an-extra-retail-jal-can-be-a-call-the-body-omits | keywords: cross-jump, jal, duplicate, argument, register, copy, extra, call
  **A PARK NOTE THAT EXPLAINS RETAIL'S EXTRA `jal` AS "THE BUILD CROSS-JUMPS TWO IDENTICAL CALLS" IS OFTEN WRONG: COUNT THE JAL TARGETS AND THE REGISTER EACH ONE'S ARGUMENT COMES FROM BEFORE ACCEPTING IT, BECAUSE RETAIL MAY SIMPLY MAKE A CALL THE BODY DOES NOT HAVE** (round 489, field/main/misc func_8008C334, Default gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8: 90.91% / 1172 bytes / 293 insns -> 92.66% / 1188 / 297, i.e. retail's exact size, from adding ONE `func_8008BF38(0);`). The old note read retail's two `jal func_8008BF38` in party case 0 as one shared `a0=1` copy that the build had cross-jumped, but the first copy's delay slot is `move $a0,$zero` - same target, different argument - so the case really is `func_8008C180(0); func_8008BF38(0); func_8008BF38(1);` and only the second call is the shared tail that case 1 falls into. The tell: the two jal words are byte-identical (same function) yet the park's body contains that function exactly once per arm, and the surrounding instruction count is short by exactly one jal plus its argument setup. So when a park note blames cross-jumping, diff the jal COUNT per arm against the body's call count instead of trusting the note; a missing call explains both the size deficit and the fuzzy score at once.

- id: h-sched2-is-on-so-order-is-the-schedulers-not-the-sources | keywords: order, sched2, schedule, schedule-insns2, position, li, return, local-alloc, store
  **cc1-2.7.2 AND cc1-2.6.0 RUN sched2 (`-fschedule-insns2`) IN THE PRESETS THIS REPO USES, SO THE INSTRUCTION ORDER OF A MATCHED FUNCTION IS THE SCHEDULER'S OUTPUT AND RETAIL'S STORE ORDER IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THE SOURCE STATEMENT ORDER - but REGISTER assignment is NOT the scheduler's, because local-alloc runs before sched2** (round 471, world_map/main/misc6 func_8007FC8C, XenoWorldMapDiv, parked 93.41% at retail's exact 164 bytes / 41 insns). Measured: recompiling the unit's own `.i` with the unit's cc_flags plus `-fno-schedule-insns2` reorders WorldMapInitGroup16Actor, which matches at 100.00% as the unit builds it (its `lw g_WorldMapSlots` and `sll` swap), so sched2 is on and load-bearing; two invariants follow for a park. (1) A retail `addiu v0,zero,3` holding `$v0` ACROSS a store group whose constants then take `$v1`/`$a0` cannot be a scheduling artifact: sched2 cannot change which pseudo owns `$v0`, so retail's `(set (reg 2) (const 3))` was already live before those stores in RTL. cc1 emits a `return CONST`'s set in the EXIT BLOCK of a `do { } while (0)` (the initial RTL, `cc1 -dr`, has NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG, the store block, an unreachable back edge, then the `(set (reg/i:SI 2) (const_int 3))` after NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END), so every `return 3` spelling lands it after the stores - the v0-held-by-3 shape needs a source order that cse deletes before regalloc, i.e. parked, not spelling-fixable. (2) The do-block's order agreement is the loop optimizer, not the source: it hoists the block's invariant `lui`/`ori` constant pairs into the preheader, which is why the do-block body's order is retail's and the no-block body's is not (88.66). Probe matrix on a scratch replica of the tail, twelve bodies (`.s` store order, field order, positions-grouped, `return 3` inside the block, `nRet = 3` first and last in the block, `nRet` returned after the block, one call instead of two, an early constant-1 store into v0) under 2.7.2 at -O1/-O2/-O3 and 2.6.0 at -O1/-O2/-O3: all emit `li $2,3` last with `$2` reused for the constants. So before inferring source order from a matching order, spend one `-fno-schedule-insns2` compile on a neighbour that already matches.
  Round 481 addendum - the positive direction of this lever, and how to recover a loop's source order from it (battling/main/misc10 func_80085EC8, Default preset, 96.16 -> 96.78% at retail's exact 1516 bytes / 379 insns, still parked). A previous park note had justified a loop body's statement order with "the store order below is right, so this is sched2" - which this lever says proves nothing - and the loop was in fact mis-ordered. The knob that DID move it: **the order in which `loop.c` hoists the body's loop-invariant constants into the preheader is the source order of their FIRST USE, so a retail preheader `li t7,4 / lui+ori t5,0x2000FF00 / li t6,0x140` says the `0x140` constant is first used LAST in the body, regardless of where its stores land in the output**. Reordering the loop to y0 first, then the two len/SetRGBC pairs, then y1, y2, then the three `0x140 - x` statements reproduced retail's preheader order AND its load interleave (y0, y1, x0, y2, x1, x2) with the stores still coming out in retail's order, i.e. sched2 put them back. One compile per permutation, and the preheader alone tells you whether you are converging.

  Round 482 addendum - the NEGATIVE direction, and the probe that turns "the loop tails differ" into a park (battling/main/misc14 func_8008B730, Default, 93.45% at retail's exact 764 bytes / 191 insns): retail puts each loop's `addiu i,1` BEFORE the count reload (`lw pConfig / addiu i,1 / lh count / nop / slt`) where all three loop spellings emit it after. Compiling the unit's own `build/src/battling/main/misc14.c.i` with the unit cc1 plus `-fno-schedule-insns -fno-schedule-insns2` gives 88.33% / 808 bytes, i.e. retail's order is NOT the RTL order either - the scheduler moved our stream INTO retail's neighbourhood, so the residual is its choice and not the source's. Same body this round: `-fschedule-insns` fails to compile it, `-fschedule-insns2` identical, gcc-2.6.0 91.77, gcc-2.7.2-cdk 91.79, `-G0` 93.45, `-O3` fails, and a 4-minute permuter run is base=545 best=545 (1309 iterations).

  Round 494 addendum - **sched1 (`-fschedule-insns`) is ON in the Default preset too, and it is the pass that hoists a block's constant chain to the top, so read the two dumps before blaming the allocator for a hoist that is missing or misplaced** (battling/main/misc10 func_80085EC8, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8, parked 96.78% at retail's exact 1516 bytes / 379 insns, whole residual the nine hoisted meter constant words' registers plus the schedule around them). Recompiling the unit's own `.i`: `-fno-schedule-insns` alone (sched2 still on) STOPS the nine constants being hoisted - each is re-materialised inline and reuses `$v0` - while `-fno-schedule-insns2` alone keeps the hoist and only regroups the gauge loop (two `lhu` grouped at its top instead of interleaved with the stores). Consequence for retail's shape there: retail keeps the two `lhu` of the `gaugeMirror[1].y0--` / `.x2--` pair at their SOURCE positions, so their VALUES are live across the constants and own `$v0`/`$v1`, which is what pushes the nine constants to `a1,t2,t1,a3,a2,t0,t5,t4,t3`; and no source position pins those loads, because every intervening store is a constant offset off the same base (`s8`) and 2.7.2's `memrefs_conflict_p` proves them disjoint. Measured on the same body: both `--` moved to the END of the function 95.95% / 380 insns / 1520 bytes (sched1 hoisted the first load to the top of the block but left the second as an inline load/addiu/store trio, and its load-delay slot became a real `nop`, hence +1 instruction); reads into two `u16` locals at their source positions with both stores at the end 96.77% / 379 / 1516 (sched1 hoisted BOTH loads to the top, into `$v1`/`$a0`, so the constants start at retail's `a1` but run `t5,t4,t2,t0,t3,t1,a3,a2`). So a load/store pair that retail keeps split is sched1 freedom, not a spelling to hunt.

- id: h-a-volatile-cast-of-an-absolute-symbol-costs-an-extra-la | keywords: volatile, cse, duplicate, load, la, addiu, absolute, do-while, cross-jump, boundary
  **`*(volatile u32 *)g_AbsSymbol` COSTS ONE MORE INSTRUCTION THAN `*(u32 *)g_AbsSymbol`: the volatile lvalue makes cc1 build the address with `la` (`lui` + `addiu` + `lw`), where the plain cast leaves the mem operand a bare `symbol_ref` and maspsx expands the `lw sym` macro to `lui` + `lw %lo(sym)(reg)`** (round 461, world_map/main/misc6 func_8007EE34, XenoWorldMapDiv, 98.42 -> 99.47% and 2684 -> 2676 bytes against retail's 2680, still one instruction SHORT and parked). Proved with `cc1_probe.sh`: `*(volatile u32 *)arr`, `((volatile u32 *)arr)[0]` and `*(volatile u32 *)&arr[0]` all print `la $2,sym` / `lw $2,0($2)`, while `*(u32 *)arr` prints the bare `lw $3,sym`. So when a park uses a volatile load only to STOP cc1 duplicating it into two cross-jumped switch arms, the price is an `addiu`; the cheap pin is a block boundary instead: `do { } while (0);` between the arm's stores and the assignment (the same barrier as `h-an-empty-do-while-pins-a-run-of-stores`) keeps the plain load inside the merged tail and reproduces retail's exact size. Both directions measured on that body: plain load with no boundary 2692 (sched2 hoists BOTH loads into each arm), volatile 2684, plain load + boundary 2680. A `s32 n = pActor->dirX;` hoist local above the boundary is worse again (2696 without it, 2720 with), because the local's live range then drags the whole arithmetic chain into both arms.

- id: h-statement-order-between-a-wide-reload-and-its-store-kills-the-nop | keywords: store, order, delay, slot, nop, lbu, lw, reload, stack, argument
  **A `lw` OF A STACK ARGUMENT WHOSE RESULT IS STORED IMMEDIATELY COSTS ONE EXTRA `nop` AGAINST RETAIL'S `lbu`/`lhu` - AND THE NOP DISAPPEARS WHEN AN INDEPENDENT STATEMENT (`pBlock->opcode = absolute + 3;`) SITS BETWEEN THE RELOAD AND ITS STORE IN THE SOURCE, BECAUSE THAT STATEMENT'S `addiu` FILLS THE LOAD DELAY** (round 459, battle/main/misc21 func_800A1CF4, 92.92 -> 94.60% and 288 -> 286 insns, retail's exact 1144 bytes; the function stays parked on its allocno permutation only). The init block stores five fields of a freshly selected block and retail's order is inUse, flags, opcode, tag; written inUse, opcode, flags, tag the compile emits `sb 0` / `addiu` / `sb 2` / `lw 0x8C(sp)` / `nop` / `sb 1` (9 insns against retail's 8) at each of the two init sites. Reordering to retail's inUse, flags, opcode, tag lets the opcode `addiu` sit in the load delay and the pair costs nothing. So when a park note blames the narrow stack-argument reload (`j-a-narrow-stack-argument`) for an instruction-count gap, measure the store ORDER of the same block first: the wide reload's nop is reachable from the source even though its width is not. Same body, measured this round: the block-selection skeleton retail wants (tag test on the QUEUED block before the allocation call, alloc as the NULL else, one shared `if (pBlock != NULL) INIT else FREE` after it with the tag-0xFF edge going to a label) is worth +2 instructions and 86.05 -> 92.92%, and its permuter run's only improvement deletes a `v1 = (v1 - rot[1]) & 0xFFF` assignment (wrong code, rejected).
- id: h-a-do-while-wrap-helps-by-presence-not-granularity | keywords: barrier, do-while, granularity, schedule, store, order, preset, stale
  **A PARK NOTE'S `do { } while (0)` MEASUREMENTS ARE PRESET-SPECIFIC, SO RE-MEASURE THEM UNDER THE UNIT'S CURRENT COMPILER BEFORE TRUSTING OR EXTENDING THEM - and when they do help, only the PRESENCE of the boundary matters, not its granularity** (round 474, battle/main/misc3 func_80077990, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0: the body's own note had recorded the wraps as worth 0.64 in the gcc-2.7.2 era). Measured on one body: with every wrap in the rect block removed 92.61% / 97 differing lines, with the wraps around each x group and its w/h/y trio 92.83 / 61, with a wrap around EVERY statement instead of each group 92.83 / 61 - so a statement-level wrap is not a finer lever than a group-level one. Three shapes that made no difference at all there (all BYTE-IDENTICAL to the unwrapped source, so no diff run can see them): moving four `pGfx->uploadRect[i].w = K;` stores after the four `...y = ...;` stores, a `do { } while (0);` between the two groups, and wrapping the whole region in one block. Also re-proved on it: a `s32 k; k = CONST;` single-assignment local used by four stores is folded straight back to the immediate (so it cannot be used to force a live register / a prologue `li`).

- id: h-an-empty-do-while-is-a-load-hoist-barrier | keywords: store, order, barrier, delay, slot, nop, lbu, lhu, hoist, do-while
  **AN EMPTY `do { } while (0);` BETWEEN A STORE AND THE LOAD THAT FOLLOWS IT IS ALSO A BASIC-BLOCK BOUNDARY FOR sched2, SO IT STOPS A LOAD BEING STOLEN *BACKWARDS* INTO THE PREVIOUS BLOCK'S LOAD-DELAY SLOT - which is what closes a two-instruction gap that reorg-only reasoning calls unreachable; a `volatile` lvalue is NOT a substitute** (round 460, slus_006.64/system/system func_80034888, parked at 98.99 = retail's EXACT 1572 bytes / 393 insns; the barrier alone took 97.26 -> 97.93 and 391 -> 393 insns). Retail's merge block is `lbu v0,0x68(s0)` / `nop` / `sb v0,0x69(s0)` / `lhu v1,0x10(s0)` / `nop` / `andi v0,v1,0x40`; written as `pString->unk69 = ...; if (pString->flags & FLAG) { ... }` cc1 scheduled the flags `lhu` FIRST and filled the `lbu` delay slot with it and the `lhu` slot with the `sb`, dropping both nops. Inserting `do { } while (0);` between the store and the test splits the block so neither load nor store can cross, and reorg leaves both retail nops. Same mechanism as `h-an-empty-do-while-pins-a-run-of-stores` and `n-an-empty-statement-between`, read on a LOAD the scheduler was pulling UP rather than a store being sunk. Measured dead on the same seam: `flags = *(volatile u16 *)&pString->flags;` used by the whole test is byte-identical to the barrierless body (97.26 / 1564), and a volatile u8 store of the unk69 byte changes nothing.

- id: h-a-bitfield-clear-run-goes-where-the-loop-source-says | keywords: store, order, bitfield, loop, read-modify-write, schedule, mask
  **A `u_int` BITFIELD RUN IN A LOOP BODY FOLLOWS SOURCE ORDER, NOT REORG: the plain field write (`scripts[i].flags_0 = 0xFFFF;`) written BEFORE the `state`/`isInUse`/`flags_0x17`/`flags_0x12` clears splits the read-modify-write of the same word and emits the halfword store FIRST, while writing it LAST emits retail's `lw word / and,and,and / or / sw word / sh word` order** (round 441, field/main/misc8 func_80080A74: 82.88 -> 83.17, 1228 bytes / 307 insns, the only edit of four that moved the score). So on a loop whose word RMW and its sibling wide/narrow stores differ only in order, re-order the SOURCE statements of the same word before assuming the scheduler did it.

- id: h-a-do-while-in-both-arms-pins-a-shared-tails-argument-setup | keywords: store, order, barrier, cross-jump, tail, argument, delay, slot
  **A SHARED TAIL REACHED FROM TWO if/else ARMS LOSES ITS FIRST INSTRUCTION'S MERGE - retail's tail begins with the call's argument setup (`j tail` + `nop`, then `jal BattleSetScreenMode` with `addu a0,zero,zero` in the slot) while the compile emits `j tail` + `move a0,zero`, a second `move a0,zero` at the end of the other arm and a `nop` in the slot (204 bytes against retail's 200) - and AN EMPTY `do { } while (0);` BETWEEN THE LAST ARM STORE AND THE FIRST TAIL STATEMENT IN **BOTH** ARMS IS THE WHOLE FIX** (round 452, battling/main/misc8 func_80080C48, 95.60 -> 100.00% MATCH at retail's exact 200 bytes / 50 insns, Default preset). Duplicating the tail in both arms already reproduces retail's block order `[test1][A][j tail][test2][B][tail][else]` (tail-once is 79.80, a switch 66.70, `s32 mode = 0` for the argument no help, a 3-minute permuter run base=221 best=221 - the park had all five), and the barrier in only ONE arm measures 92.70, so the two barriers are both load-bearing: they stop sched1/reorg hoisting the constant out of each arm's block, which is what keeps it inside the region cross-jump merges. Same mechanism as `h-an-empty-do-while-pins-a-run-of-stores` / `n-an-empty-statement-between`, read on a cross-jumped tail.

- id: h-a-three-group-tail-rotates-under-source-order | keywords: store, order, three, group, gt, ptr, tail, rotate
  **IN gcc-2.7.2 A STRAIGHT-LINE TAIL OF THREE INDEPENDENT STATEMENT GROUPS COMES OUT AS `(source 1, source 3, source 2)` - THE MIDDLE STATEMENT'S GROUP IS EMITTED LAST - so when retail's order is `(a, b, c)` the source that emits it is `(a, c, b)`** (round 443, field/main/misc7 func_80099214, Default preset; the park went 96.45 -> 97.91 on this single edit). The tail is the walk-to-position rebuild exit: two flag-word read-modify-writes (`scriptFlags.flags &= ~0x10000;`, `flags &= ~0x200000;`) and the `scriptInstructionPointer += 0xD` halfword bump; retail emits `lw 0/sw 0/lhu 204/addiu/sh 204/lw 4/and/sw 4`, i.e. flags0, ptr, flags4. Written ptr-first (the natural reading order: advance then clear) the compile rotated to ptr, flags4, flags0 (96.45); written flags0, ptr, flags4 it rotated to flags0, flags4, ptr (96.26); written flags0, flags4, ptr it emits retail's exact three groups (97.91, 153 -> 141 differing lines). So on a tail whose groups are all instruction-identical and only rotated, try all three source permutations - the pair of measured rotations is enough to solve for the third, and sched2 was not involved.


- id: h-a-four-way-switch-shares-one-cross-jumped-store-tail | keywords: store, order, cross-jump, switch, tail, call, argument, register
  **WHEN RETAIL'S FIVE STACK-ARGUMENT STORES FOR A CALL LIVE IN ONE BLOCK THAT FOUR `switch` CASES `j` INTO, THAT IS jump.c CROSS-JUMPING FOUR SEPARATE CALL SITES WHOSE ARGUMENTS ALREADY SIT IN `$a1`/`$a2`/`$a3`/`$v0` BEFORE THE JUMP - so a compile that instead keeps three of the five stores inside one case's body is reporting an ALLOCATOR difference (the case's values are not landing in the argument registers), not a store-order residual** (round 454, field/main/misc5 func_800A8BA4, parked 85.21%). Retail's four `FieldClampPolyFT4UVs` calls became one `jal` at .L800A8E08; each case tail is only the arg computation plus the last `addu` in the `j` slot, and the `move a0,s0` / `addu a0,s0,zero` that sets the first argument is still PER CASE (in three cases and in the delay slots of the branches that lead to the fourth), which is what says four call sites and not one call after the switch. Diagnosis order: before spending anything on the store order: if the body is behind on callee-saved registers, fix the register count first - the store placement follows the argument hand-out. The same function's other residual is the one to attack instead: it is a `nQuad * 8` mult giv (loop.c made three `addiu +8` pointer givs where retail recomputes `sll v0,s2,3`), and retail's nine callee-saved registers are all live there, i.e. g-qimode's rule applies (no `andi` on the index, no `sltiu` test => not source-reachable).

symptoms: stores in another order, reload of a global, volatile
try: store volatile reload order

- id: a-base-pointer-local-assigned-after-a-call-collapses-the-per-statement-reloads | keywords: store, reload, pointer, local, base, global, size, extra
  **A POINTER LOCAL FOR A POINTER-TO-ARRAY GLOBAL ASSIGNED IMMEDIATELY BEFORE A RUN OF `pBase[...]` STATEMENTS COLLAPSES ONE GLOBAL RELOAD PER STATEMENT INTO RETAIL'S SINGLE LOAD, AND CLOSES THE BYTE GAP - `pBase = g_Ptr;` placed AFTER a call keeps the base caller-saved, so the "a pointer local costs a callee-saved register" worry does not apply to it** (round 477, battle/main/misc11 func_80080C94, Default, 1244 -> 1220 bytes = retail's exact size, 311 -> 305 insns, 88.65 -> 88.70%). Retail's case-1 block is `lui a1,%hi(g_BattleCommandQueue) / lw a1` AFTER the `BattleSlotBitMask` call, then `lbu a0,730(a1)` / the records `sh` / `lbu v0,730(a1)` / `addiu` / `sb v0,730(a1)` - one base for three statements, re-read only the 0x2DA byte across the aliasing store. Assigning `pQueue = g_BattleCommandQueue;` at that point reproduces it; spelling the three statements as `g_BattleCommandQueue[k]` reloads the HI/LO pair before each one and is the whole +24 bytes. The reclaimable gap in a park is therefore worth counting in LOADS of one global, not in instructions: 3 loads to 1 was exactly the 6 excess instructions.
- id: c-a-copy-block-from-element-four-is-a-pointer-walk | keywords: copy, halfword, block, pointer, walk, addiu, u16, globals
  **SIX HALFWORD COPIES WHOSE SECOND GROUP RETAIL REACHES WITH AN EXTRA `addiu vN,vN,0x8` AND THEN LOADS AT 0/2/4 ARE A POINTER WALK FROM ELEMENT 4, NOT `arr[4]/[5]/[6]`**: `p = g_States + 4; dst[0] = p[0]; dst[1] = p[1]; dst[2] = p[2];` reproduces retail's `lui/addiu` + `addiu v0,v0,8` + the three 0/2/4 load/store pairs, and the indexed spelling costs exactly that instruction (it folds the offsets into 8/0xA/0xC instead) - which shows up as one instruction short and 3 points low, and would shift the whole overlay if converted (round 439, battle/main/misc30 func_800B905C: 94.47% / 508 bytes -> 96.61% / 512, and the same `pStates = g_BattleAnimGroupStates + 4; pStates[1..2]` idiom is in misc31's MATCHED code, i.e. read the unit's neighbours for the walk). With that fixed the block's remaining residual was only which base pair holds `$v0`/`$v1`, which the hoisted-compare lever above then closed by landing the exact 508 bytes.

- id: h-an-empty-do-while-pins-a-run-of-stores | keywords: store, order, sink, barrier, loop-note, do-while, scheduler, arms
  **A RUN OF PLAIN STORES THAT gcc SINKS BELOW THE VOLATILE STORES THAT FOLLOW THEM IN SOURCE IS PINNED BACK BY AN EMPTY `do { } while (0);` AFTER THE RUN - the loop note is a scheduling boundary, and this works where `volatile` cannot (the run's stores are to a parameter's struct and the volatile ones are globals)** (round 430, world_map/main/misc7 func_800828DC, 74.00 -> 76.40% and 461 -> 427 differing instructions, XenoWorldMapDiv preset, still parked at 75.62 / 1664 bytes / 416 insns against retail's 1672 / 418). The body is a command/state machine: each of the five big arms writes `command = 0; state = N; unk5C = <const>;` then three volatile rotation stores, and cc1 emitted the three plain stores AFTER the two volatile ones and hoisted the `lh` reload of the just-stored global into the gap. Adding `do { } while (0);` after the `unk5C` store in each arm put them back in retail's order; a second barrier after the ViewRotationZ store also stopped the `lh` hoist. So when an arm's stores come out rotated and the tail of the arm is already right, try the empty do/while between store groups before re-ordering the source (the same barrier is documented in this unit's WorldMapBeginSlotAnimFrame for a load, and in g-switch-dispatch-makes-loop for a dispatch).
  Round 490 addendum - the barrier also pins a `sh` CONSTANT STORE at the TOP of a switch arm against a run of global loads that sched2 would otherwise hoist above it, and it is what buys retail's byte count: world_map/main/misc12 func_8008E190 went 91.93 -> 98.59% and 860 -> 868 bytes (= retail's size) by putting `do { } while (0);` after `pPlayer->state = N;` and after the two position stores below it, where the un-barriered arm batched all five `lui`/`lw` global loads above every store and lost the two load-delay `nop`s. Cured with the same edit in both switch arms; measured dead on that body: no barriers (91.93), barriers with the arm's statements in retail's own order (94.76), the angle assignment moved after the x store (97.23) - and the residual left in the barriered body is a store retail keeps TWO blocks below its load, which no statement order reaches.


  Round 492 addendum - the barrier also splits a RUN OF STRUCTURED READ-MODIFY-WRITES so that each one keeps its own element pointer: field/scripts/virtual_machine func_800A24C4 has six updates of the shape `g_FieldActors[i].transformMatrix.t[k] += *(volatile s32 *)(pShake - N);` and with no barrier gcc CSEs `i*sizeof + g_FieldActors` across the three updates of a group (18 insns where retail has 24, 76.59%), while `do { <update> } while (0);` around EACH update reproduces five of retail's six 8-insn blocks verbatim (85.58 -> 90.44%). It is a CSE question, not a scheduling one here: the barrier's loop note stops the element-pointer pseudo being shared between the statements. Residual on that body: the t[1]/t[2] blocks still sink their volatile delta load one instruction late (`lw a0,g_FieldActors / nop / addu / lw v0,36(a0) / lw v1,-18(a2) / nop` where retail has the delta load in the `lw a0` slot); routing t[1] through a static-inline helper instead measures 88.06.
- id: h-a-do-while-group-pins-a-scheduled-store-block | keywords: store, order, do-while, barrier, scheduler, block, register, 260
  **A `do { one group of stores } while (0)` PER GROUP PINS A SCHEDULED STRAIGHT-LINE BLOCK'S ORDER IN A XENOBATTLE260 UNIT (plain -O2, no -fschedule-insns in the flags) AND MOVES THE BLOCK'S POINTER INTO RETAIL'S REGISTER - so the ordering rows of such a diff are block boundaries, not statement positions** (round 433, battle/main/misc3 func_80077990, 92.19 -> 92.83% and 97 -> 61 differing lines, still parked at 1820 bytes / 455 insns against retail's 1816 / 454). The proof that this unit schedules at all is cc1's own `build/src/<unit>.c.s`: the same C emits each rect's `lhu` above the neighbouring constant stores and its `andi/sll/sh` behind them, where retail's head is pure RTL order (value-then-address per statement, no store crossing another). Wrapping each rect's `x = ...` and the `w/h/y` trio that follows it in their own `do { } while (0)` put the stores back in retail's per-group order AND gave `pRects` `$v1` / the coords pointer `$a1` exactly as retail has them (before that they were `$a0`/`$a1`). Two measured refinements: a block PER STATEMENT instead of per group compiles BYTE-IDENTICALLY (only the group boundary is a lever), and a matched extension of this lever is the empty `do { } while (0);` of h-an-empty-do-while-pins-a-run-of-stores. Not reachable this way on the same body: retail's `li v0,1` / `li v1,0xC6` placed before the block's pointer load, retail's first `lhu` above a four-store group, and retail's StoreImage argument setup (`addu a0,s0,s7` / `move a1,s6`) sitting above the eight rect stores - that last one is a scheduler hoist with no C statement behind it.
  COUNTER-CASE with the EMPTY-barrier form (round 434, field/main/misc9 func_800AC3AC, a
  56-store POLY_GT4 head): one `do { } while (0);` after each of the five constant groups
  collapsed the body from 380 to 333 instructions and 97.89% to 71.92 / 1332 bytes - cc1
  merged stores across the barriers instead of pinning them - so the barrier family is not
  free on a body whose stores are already grouped by constant; measure it before trusting it.
- id: h-an-empty-do-while-pins-a-store-below-an-address-computation | keywords: store, order, barrier, address, addu, sll, do-while, sched2, regalloc, family
  **THE SAME EMPTY-BARRIER LEVER READ ON A STORE sched2 HOISTS *UP*: `grid = p->unk50 >> 12; pPoint = &table[grid]; p->unk54 = grid;` emits the `sw` BETWEEN the `sra` and the `sll`/`addu`, and one `do { } while (0);` between the address and the store recovers retail's `lw / lui+addiu / sra / sll / addu / sw` order - but it also rotates the register family, so the two spellings trade ORDER against NAMES and neither is 100%** (round 495, world_map/main/misc4 func_80077E68, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2 with `--dont-expand-li`, 92.97 -> 94.16% at retail's exact 1060 bytes / 265 insns, still parked on a 3-way register rotation: retail `grid=$v0 base=$a0 shifted=$v1`, barriered body `grid=$v1 base=$v0 shifted=$a0`). Measured on the same body: the store written BEFORE the address statement (no barrier) gives retail's `grid` in `$v0` but sinks the `sw` back above the `sll` (93.50); a barrier between the `sra` and the address computation is 92.21 / 1064 (one instruction over, the grid pseudo becomes cross-block); the offset-first cast sum `(T *)(grid * sizeof(T) + (u32)table)` is byte-identical to the barriered body. The same barrier in the arm right after a `state++` store is worth its own 1.2 points here (93.63 -> 94.16) but then leaves the arm's call argument setup below the stores where retail hoists it to the top of the arm and moves a `li` one load early - so on a two-region residual, place one barrier at a time and read the WHOLE diff: each barrier re-schedules every block after it.
- id: h-a-join-store-of-arms-that-store-different-values-is-one-source-store | keywords: store, join, cross-jump, value, arms, constant, shared, tie
  **THE COUNTERPART OF `h-one-retail-store-at-a-join-is-a-cross-jumped-per-arm-store`: WHEN THE ARMS STORE DIFFERENT VALUES gcc 2.7.2 DOES NOT CROSS-JUMP THEM, SO A RETAIL STORE AT THE JOIN MEANS THE ORIGINAL HAD ONE STORE STATEMENT BELOW THE JOIN (a value temp), AND THE PER-ARM SPELLING SCORES HIGHER WHILE BEING STRUCTURALLY WRONG - take the lower percentage; it is the one with retail's bytes** (round 437, field/main/misc10 func_8009635C, Default preset, 176 bytes / 44 insns = retail's exact size in BOTH bodies, still parked on register allocation). Retail is `beq s0,-1,new / addu v1,q+n / lbu a0,0(v1) / sltiu v0,a0,99 / beqz v0,exit / nop / j JOIN / addiu v0,a0,1` and `new: ... sb s1,0(v0) / li v0,1` then `JOIN: sb v0,0(v1)`, i.e. one store reached by both arms with the address register live from the load. Per-arm stores (`if (q < 99) q++;` vs `q = 1;`) measure 96.70% and reorg fills the `j`'s delay slot with path 1's `sb` (blocks not merged, because the two stores' values are a register and a `const_int`). Writing the quantity into a temp in each arm and ONE `pQuantities[nIndex] = nQuantity;` after the if/else reproduces retail's block layout and instruction count exactly (90.41%, everything else register-only). So judge such a park by the store COUNT in the `.s`, not by objdiff: the higher-scoring body was the wrong shape. On the `q < 99` test, `nQuantity = pQuantities[nIndex]; if (nQuantity < 99) nQuantity++;` gives `slti` (89.16%) - the comparison has to be written on the byte, `pQuantities[nIndex] < 99`, for retail's `sltiu`.
  AMENDMENT (round 463, same function func_8009635C, Default preset, still parked at 96.70%): the honest single-store shape's 90.41 is an ALLOCATOR artefact, not the ceiling of the shape. Retail's registers ($s1 = the parameter, $s0 = the slot index) come back by giving arm 1 a POINTER LOCAL for the quantity slot and assigning the same pointer in the else arm - `pQuantity = &pQuantities[nIndex]; if (*pQuantity < 99) nQuantity = *pQuantity + 1; else return; ... pQuantity = &pQuantities[nIndex]; pIds[nIndex] = nItemId; nQuantity = 1;` then one `*pQuantity = nQuantity;` below the chain: 92.16% at retail's exact 176 bytes / 44 insns with every register retail has, i.e. +1.75 over the subscript form and higher than the per-arm spelling's 96.70 in STRUCTURE. Two measured trade-offs on that body, for whoever picks it up: computing the else arm's `pQuantity` BEFORE the ids store (retail's `addu v1,s4,s0` sits in the `beq` delay slot, so that is retail's source order) scores 95.91 but hands the quantity address to `$a0` and the value to `$v1`; and in every spelling so far the single store still comes out DUPLICATED into arm 1 with the `j` aimed past the shared block (retail aims the `j` at the store, with `addiu v0,a0,1` in its delay slot), so the merge, not the register set, is the last residual - retail's `j` target has two predecessors (`j` plus the else arm's fall-through), which is a goto-label tail in the source (see c-a-switch-shared-tail-sits-at-a-label), and that spelling is the untried lead.
- id: h-a-volatile-store-defeats-store-to-load-folding-keeping-the-symbol | keywords: volatile, store, fold, lh, symbol, relocation, constant, read
  **A CONSTANT STORED TO A HALFWORD GLOBAL AND READ BACK A FEW STATEMENTS LATER IS FORWARDED BY cse (the store's value replaces the load, and the `lui`/`lh`/`sll` retail has disappear), and the cheap escape is a VOLATILE STORE with a PLAIN READ: `*(volatile u16 *)&g_X = 0x400;` then `v = (s16)g_X;` keeps retail's `lh %lo(g_X)` AND ITS OWN SYMBOL, where the older escape (reading through a neighbouring symbol with a `[1]`/`[2]` subscript) leaves a base+addend relocation that diff_func reports as a mismatch forever** (round 443, world_map/main/misc8 func_8008390C, XenoWorldMapDiv, park 96.15 -> 96.48% at retail's exact 244 bytes / 61 insns). The two reads here are the view angles, stored a few statements earlier in the same block; making only the two STORES volatile removed 8 relocation diff lines and moved nothing else (the read still emits a real load). A volatile READ is the wrong direction - the sibling park in the same file records that spelling as worse. Same trick as the `func_80083A00` park's volatile refill, which uses it for the opposite reason (to stop cc1 folding `K << 12` into an immediate).
- id: h-volatile-store-pins-the-arg-pair | keywords: volatile, store, sched2, argument, ori, hoist, load
  **A CALL'S COMPUTED ARGUMENT (`ori a1,a2,<const>` off a base the block's stores already use) THAT RETAIL PLACES WITH THE BLOCK'S FIRST STORE AND YOURS PLACES AFTER THE BLOCK'S GLOBAL LOADS IS PINNED BY MAKING THAT FIRST STORE `volatile` - sched2 will not sink a store past, nor hoist a load past, a volatile MEM, so the pair stays at source position and the address form comes with it** (round 419, world_map/main/misc5 func_8007C3B8, 98.13 -> 99.95% at retail's EXACT 876 bytes / 219 insns, every instruction identical, XenoWorldMapDiv preset). The switch case fills a scratchpad vector and calls `WorldMapInitSpriteGroupSprites(0x14, &pScratchPos[0x50], 0)`; retail is `li a0,0x14 / ori a1,a2,0xA0 / sh zero,0xA2(a2) / lui+lw g_WorldMapCameraTarget / lui+lw ...TargetZ / sra / sra / sh 0xA0 / sh 0xA4 / jal`, and the plain body (`pScratchPos[0x51] = 0;` then the two stores) emits the SAME four instructions but with the `ori` + `sh zero` pair after the two loads, i.e. 53 differing lines and 98.13% with nothing else wrong. Writing the FIRST store as `*(volatile u16 *)&pScratchPos[0x51] = 0;` (the other two stores plain, no other change) reproduces retail's order in one edit. Measured dead on the same body at 876 bytes / 98.13: the three plain store orders (including `sh zero` last), the two shift results in function-top locals, an `u8 *` / `s16 *` / `u16 *` scratch local for the argument, one `u16 *pTilePos = &pScratchPos[0x50]` used for all three stores AND the argument (CSE folds the base back either way), and a 4-minute permuter run (2179 iterations, base=120 best=120). So when a diff's only delta is where a computed call argument sits relative to the block's loads, try the volatile cast on the store that retail keeps adjacent to it before permuting - and note the counterpart from `h-one-retail-store-at-a-join-is-a-cross-jumped-per-arm-store`: volatile on a store whose ADDRESS the pointer-iv would otherwise fold costs the body 8 bytes, so put the cast on a scratchpad or plain-base store, not on a field of an iv-walked struct. The resulting body still cannot be committed in this unit (its jump table lands 4 bytes late; lever i-jtbl-midchain-4mod8), so it is parked at 99.95.
- id: h-one-retail-store-at-a-join-is-a-cross-jumped-per-arm-store | keywords: store, order, hoist, join, arms, scheduling, cross-jump, block
  **WHEN RETAIL HAS ONE STORE AT AN IF/ELSE JOIN AND YOUR COMPILE SCHEDULES THAT SAME STORE BELOW THE NEXT STATEMENT'S ARGUMENT LOADS, the original stored in EVERY arm and cc1 cross-jumped them back into the one at the join - write the store once per arm and the block boundary reproduces retail's order with no other change** (round 418, world_map/main/misc8_b func_80085CDC, 99.18 -> 99.94% at retail's exact 636 bytes / 158 insns, XenoWorldMapDiv). The tail is a four-arm turn-step slew where every arm assigns the new step into one `d`, then `pActor->redStep = d;` and `func_800223B0(pActor->pSprite, (d - g_WorldMapViewRotationY - 0x400) & 0xFFF);`. With the store once below the join, cc1's scheduler hoists the `lw a0,0(s0)` of the callee's first argument above the store and sinks the `sw` into the `lhu` stall: `lw a0 / lui+lhu / sw / subu` where retail is `sw / lui+lhu / lw a0 / subu` - same instruction multiset, same frame, 99.18%. Repeating `pActor->redStep = d;` in all four arms gives retail's exact body: cc1's cross-jumping merges the four stores into one at the join, and the merged insn is the first of that block, so it stays ahead of the argument loads. Two things that do NOT work and are worth skipping: `*(volatile s32 *)&pActor->redStep = d;` also fixes the order but the volatile MEM is never entered in cse, so the address is re-formed off the array base instead of the pointer iv (`sw v1,92(s2)` for `sw v1,16(s0)`), a base register has to stay live across the loop, and the body grows to 648 bytes / 161 insns (95.45%); a `void *pSprite` local for the callee's first argument is copy-propagated away (identical 99.18%). The per-arm `pActor->redStep += 0x100;` / `= pActor->angle;` spelling (no `d` store) does NOT cross-jump - three separate `sw`s, 648 bytes, 93.77% - so the arms must all store the same value `d` for the merge to happen. AMENDMENT (round 449, field/main/main FieldMain, Default preset, 99.50 -> 100.00% at retail's exact 3284 bytes / 821 insns): the arms need NOT store the same value - one arm storing the constant `0xFF` and the other a global load (`lhu`) also cross-jumps into ONE `sw` at the join, and that is the fix for the mirror residual (a store at the join with an independent LOAD hoisted above it): `if (x == 0) { g_A = 0; g_B = 0xFF; } else g_B = g_C;` instead of a `bankIndex` temp and one store below, which compiles as `lw v1,g_FieldSystemMode / sw v0,g_B` where retail has `sw v0,g_B / lui v1+lw v1,g_FieldSystemMode`. Mechanism proved on the same body by compiling the unit's `.i` with the unit's cc1: `-fno-schedule-insns2` reproduces retail's order exactly, `-fno-schedule-insns` does not (so this is sched2), and neither a `*(volatile s32 *)&g_B = bankIndex;` store nor a volatile read of the loaded global stops the hoist - both are byte-identical at 99.50, so do not spend runs on the volatile barrier for a post-reload sched2 swap; the per-arm store is the lever.
- id: h-a-moved-group-of-volatile-stores | keywords: volatile, store, order, group, block, offset, diff, reassociation
  **A DIFF WHERE A WHOLE IDENTICAL RUN OF VOLATILE STORES SITS 60+ INSTRUCTIONS FROM WHERE RETAIL PUTS IT IS THE C'S STATEMENT-GROUP ORDER, NOT THE ALLOCATOR OR THE SCHEDULER - and the line diff hides it, so read the offset SEQUENCE (`sh/sb <reg>,<off>(v0)` in emitted order) instead** (round 416, battle/main/misc16 func_8008DE04, 80.93 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 1580 bytes / 395 insns, XenoBattle260). The park's body listed quad 0's corners, quad 0's texcoords, quad 1's corners, quad 1's texcoords; retail emits BOTH quads' corners (16 `sh`) and then BOTH quads' texcoords (16 `sb`), and inside one volatile group gcc emits exactly the source order. The old note had spent two rounds on a "three-register rotation" that was really this: with the groups reordered the same body scored 98.20 and the registers fell into place on their own. Two embedded-assignment locals then closed it: `(bottom = arg2 + 0xFFF8)` reproduces retail's `li 0xfff8 / addu` where a bare `arg2 - 8` folds to one `addiu`, and naming the sums `(mid = left + (half = (arg3 - 16) / 2))` / `(right = mid + half)` gives one `addu` each, where the inline `(arg1 + 8) + half` reassociates to `arg1 + (half + 8)` (`addiu v1,a3,8 / addu a1,a1,v1`). Plain statement locals before the stores hoist (the earlier 75.99 measurement); the embedded form does not, which is why both matched neighbours of this row-builder family are written that way.
- id: h-volatile-prefix-pins-an-arms | keywords: store, order, volatile, hoist, load, delay-slot, arms, switch
  **VOLATILE ON AN ARM'S FIRST STORES PINS BOTH THE STORE ORDER AND THE GLOBAL LOADS THAT FOLLOW, BUT THE ARM'S LAST STORE MUST STAY PLAIN OR IT CAN NEVER REACH THE JUMP'S DELAY SLOT - mark the prefix, leave the suffix** (round 435, world_map/main/misc6 func_8007EE34, 91.50 -> 98.17% on a 676-instruction command/state machine with three switch jump tables, XenoWorldMapDiv; still parked at 2692 bytes / 673 insns against retail's 2704 / 676). Every command arm is `command = 0; state = N; x = <recomputed from g_WorldMapPlayerPosition>; z = <recomputed>;` and cc1 hoisted the `lw g_WorldMapPlayerPositionY` and the `lw 0x40(pActor)` above the two `sh`, moved the y store above the x store, and floated the `li` of the state constant; retail keeps source order and fills the load-delay slots with the stores. Writing the prefix as `*(volatile s16 *)&pActor->command = 0; *(volatile s16 *)&pActor->state = N; *(volatile s32 *)&pActor->x = ...;` reproduced retail's order in all six arms in one edit (96.96% from 91.50), and the same marking on the two constant-only arms took it to 98.17. Making the z store volatile too REGRESSED to 2724 bytes: retail's `sw` sits in the `j` delay slot of the arm's tail jump (or in a cross-jumped shared tail), and a volatile store cannot be moved past a control transfer, so the arm grew a `nop` and the store moved up - leave the last store of a suffix-shared arm non-volatile. Two companion measurements on the same body: (a) declare per-arm scratchpad pointers INSIDE the case block, never at function scope, or their `lui/ori` pair lands in the entry block, costs a frame slot and pushes the whole body out (`pPos`/`pAngle` at function scope measured 91.50 with an extra `$s7` save); (b) a `(SVECTOR *)((u32)pScratch | 0xA0)` spelling gives retail's `ori a1,s4,0xa0` at a single-use call site where `pScratch + 0xA0` gives `addiu`; and (c) write the LAST switch's case labels in the order the machine-coded blocks appear rather than by value (0/1/16/25, then 4/17/65, then 2/3), which removes the extra `j` + `move v0,s6` a fall-through return costs (95.51 -> 96.44 in one edit). Preset ruled out on the final body: gcc-2.7.2-cdk 83.56.

- id: h-volatile-cast-restores-a-repeated-load | keywords: volatile, lbu, cse, reload, double-load, address, order
  **A RETAIL DOUBLE LOAD FROM ONE CSE'D ADDRESS (`addiu v0,v0,0x140` / `addu a0,v0,a3` / `lbu v1,0(a0)` for a compare / `lbu v0,0(a0)` for the value) IS ONLY REPRODUCIBLE BY CASTING THE LOAD `volatile`: plain C makes gcc cse the two loads into one** (round 412, battle/main/misc13 func_800877E0, 59.15 -> 60.24%, 440 -> 448 bytes against retail's 456, Default preset). When a byte from a streamed table is tested and then used twice, write `*(volatile u8 *)(base + <full index expression>)` at each of the four sites: cc1 then keeps the shared ADDRESS (the index arithmetic is still cse'd, which is why retail has one `a0`) and reloads the byte, and the per-store recompute of the whole chain comes for free because the intervening stores to the globals kill the table reads. Do NOT hoist a `u8 *pParam = <global>` local instead - gcc then hoists the whole index chain out of the loop (43.58%, 436 bytes). This buys the instruction COUNT and shape only; the residual on that function is the allocator (i/o in a2/a3 swapped), so park on it rather than permuting from 60%.
- id: h-a-pointer-local-caches-a-global-retail-reloads | keywords: reload, global, pointer, local, cse, store, alias, pointer-to-global
  **A POINTER-TO-A-GLOBAL LOCAL (`BattleSlotState *p = g_X;` used at every later site) KEEPS ONE LOAD WHERE RETAIL RELOADS THE GLOBAL POINTER AFTER EVERY INTERVENING STORE, because a store through any pointer may alias the global's storage - so spell the global expression (`g_X->field`) at each site and let cse merge only the sites no store separates** (round 421, battle/main/misc20 func_8009CBC4, 97.13 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 1936 bytes / 483 insns, XenoBattle260 gcc 2.6.0, ported from its misc17 twin). Retail loads `g_BattleTargetSlotState` once for eight consecutive effect-flag tests, then reloads it (`lui v0,%hi / lw v0,%lo`) in each of the three later tests, because each is preceded by a store (`g_BattleTargetSlotEntry->activeEffectFlags2 |= 0x40`, `g_BattleCurveTargetModes[i] = 3`, the table `sw`) and the global is a pointer variable a store could alias. Holding the pointer in a local - the twin's spelling, `pAtkState = g_BattleTargetSlotState;` - is legal and pins it in `$a1` across all eleven sites: three `lui`+`lw` pairs (6 insns / 24 bytes) disappear and the function reads 1904 against retail's 1936. Replacing the local with the direct global expression everywhere reproduced retail exactly in one edit, register `$a0` included. Check this before blaming the allocator when a diff's only quantity difference is a missing `lw` of a `g_X` pointer."

- id: h-a-store-through-a-typed-field-lets-the-base-globals-load-hoist | keywords: reload, hoist, loop, store, alias, void, typed, field, count, global
  **A LOOP WHOSE BOUND IS RELOADED EACH ITERATION FROM THE SAME GLOBAL POINTER THE BODY STORES THROUGH ONLY RELOADS IT WHEN THE STORE'S LVALUE IS `void*`/char-TYPED - the same store written as a typed struct field (`pRecord->pSource = ...`) lets gcc hoist the pointer's load out of the loop, so retail's per-iteration `lui`/`lw` pair is 3 instructions and 12 bytes unreachable that way, and rewriting the store as `*(void **)pRecord = ...` (identical bytes, one cast) restores them** (round 473, battle/main/misc23 BattleInitColorTintTable, XenoBattle260Div0 = gcc 2.6.0 -G0; a REWRITE of an already-matching body into view-struct form). Retail's image-list walk is `lw a0,0x118(v0)` once, then per iteration `lhu v0,0x1A(a0)` / `sw v1,0(a0)` / `lui v0,%hi(g_BattleImageList)` / `lw v0,%lo(...)` / `lbu v0,0x10E(v0)` / `slt`; the typed body (`pTexture->isLoaded`, `pTexture->pSource = (Temp8 *)g_BattleImage;`, `i < g_BattleImageList->numTextures`) reads 353 insns / 1412 bytes with the load hoisted into a register the branch jumps back past (hoisting only the FIELD's `lbu 0x10E(a0)`), and spelling the identical store as `*(void **)pTexture = g_BattleImage;` gives retail's 356 / 1424. Also measured dead: declaring the extern `BattleActor *g_BattleImageList` with `g_BattleImageList->numTextures` in the condition (same 353), and a `volatile` alias of the global for the count read (forces the reload but adds it to the pre-loop read too: 357 / 1428, 98.61). So when a loop's bound is a `u8`/`u16` field of a struct reached through a global pointer and retail reloads that pointer every iteration, the store's lvalue type is the knob, not the field's spelling.

- id: h-store-then-read-back-of-a-global | keywords: store, reload, global, fold, hoist, volatile, aliasing, halfword
  **cc1 2.7.2 FORWARDS A HALFWORD STORE INTO A LATER `lh` OF THE SAME SYMBOL, SO A RETAIL SEQUENCE `sh $v0,%lo(G)` / ... / `lh $v0,%lo(G)` CANNOT BE WRITTEN BY NAMING G TWICE - and the two escapes both cost the block order** (round 409, world_map/main/misc8 func_80083A00, six switch cases each store a view-rotation halfword and then read it back to scale it by `<< 12`; parked 63.80%, 352 insns against retail's 395). Measured, all six sites the same: naming the symbol (`(s16)g_WorldMapViewRotationY << 12`) folds the read to a constant (`lui $v0,0x40`, 3 insns short per site) even with two pointer stores in between - gcc 2.7.2 does forward across an unknown-base store here, so "the stores defeat it" is false; reading through the neighbouring symbol instead (`((s16 *)&g_WorldMapCameraRot)[1]`, base+addend, the spelling that closed the sibling func_8008390C) stops the fold but cc1 then treats the two symbol_refs as distinct objects and HOISTS the `lh` above the `sh` that writes it (`lh $3,g_WorldMapCameraRot+2` before `sh $2,g_WorldMapCameraRot`), which is a stale-value reorder and silently wrong code; `*(volatile s16 *)&G` keeps the load after the store but every non-volatile store in the case block floats around the barrier (the case's `li`/`sh`/`sw` order scrambles, 59.73%) and the load comes out `lhu` + `sll 16` when the extern is `u16`. So on a diff whose only shape difference is a retail `lh` of a global your body just wrote, the fold is the wall: park with the base+addend spelling (right instruction count) rather than the symbol (right reloc) and say which. Not yet tried from this file's levers: an address-taken pointer local to the global (`h-address-taken-load-blocks-hoist` above) as the load barrier.
- id: h-independent-loads-hoist-above-the-store | keywords: store, hoist, load, order, global, inline, lbu, pointer, local
  **A PARK NOTE THAT SAYS "gcc SINKS THESE LOADS BELOW THE STORE, SO RETAIL'S LOADS-FIRST ORDER IS UNREACHABLE" WASTES A LANE: put the loading statement FIRST in source and write the store through the INLINE global expression, and cc1 hoists the store's own global-pointer load above the independent loads, exactly as retail has it** (round 411, battle/main/misc3 func_800785D4, 132 bytes / 33 insns = retail's size with every one of the 33 instructions identical; the residual is only that retail names the flat `g_BattleCommandCodes` / `g_BattleCommandSlotMasks` where the typed `g_BattleCommandRecords[slot].actorSlot / .param` spelling emits the same address as base+addend, and `check_bin.sh battle` prints OK - the MATCH RELOC class). The 75.45% park that had sat there read `pEntry = g_BattleCommandQueue; tile = <two lbu>; store(pEntry);` and its note listed eight spellings; re-measured, that body did not compile at all (it still named two symbols that had since been folded into a struct), and with a pointer local assigned twice cc1 gives BOTH queue pointers `$a2` and keeps the tile `lbu`s below the `sb` (98.79%). Two edits closed it: the tile statement FIRST, and the first store written as `g_BattleCommandRecords[g_BattleCommandQueue[0x2DA]].actorSlot = color;` (the inline form this unit's matched neighbours already use) - that reproduces retail's order AND its register pair (first queue temp `$v0`, the tail pointer `$a2`; with one variable for both, `$a2`/`$a2`). So on a load/store ordering residual: re-measure the park first, then try the inline-global store form with the loading statement first, before believing the note's "gcc cannot do this".
  **cc1 2.7.2 FORWARDS A HALFWORD STORE INTO A LATER `lh` OF THE SAME SYMBOL, SO A RETAIL SEQUENCE `sh $v0,%lo(G)` / ... / `lh $v0,%lo(G)` CANNOT BE WRITTEN BY NAMING G TWICE - and the two escapes both cost the block order** (round 409, world_map/main/misc8 func_80083A00, six switch cases each store a view-rotation halfword and then read it back to scale it by `<< 12`; parked 63.80%, 352 insns against retail's 395). Measured, all six sites the same: naming the symbol (`(s16)g_WorldMapViewRotationY << 12`) folds the read to a constant (`lui $v0,0x40`, 3 insns short per site) even with two pointer stores in between - gcc 2.7.2 does forward across an unknown-base store here, so "the stores defeat it" is false; reading through the neighbouring symbol instead (`((s16 *)&g_WorldMapCameraRot)[1]`, base+addend, the spelling that closed the sibling func_8008390C) stops the fold but cc1 then treats the two symbol_refs as distinct objects and HOISTS the `lh` above the `sh` that writes it (`lh $3,g_WorldMapCameraRot+2` before `sh $2,g_WorldMapCameraRot`), which is a stale-value reorder and silently wrong code; `*(volatile s16 *)&G` keeps the load after the store but every non-volatile store in the case block floats around the barrier (the case's `li`/`sh`/`sw` order scrambles, 59.73%) and the load comes out `lhu` + `sll 16` when the extern is `u16`. So on a diff whose only shape difference is a retail `lh` of a global your body just wrote, the fold is the wall: park with the base+addend spelling (right instruction count) rather than the symbol (right reloc) and say which. Not yet tried from this file's levers: an address-taken pointer local to the global (`h-address-taken-load-blocks-hoist` above) as the load barrier. Round 411 tried it on the world_map/misc7 twin func_80081470: a `s16 *pRot = &g_WorldMapCameraRot;` used for BOTH the -0x80 store and the reload that fills unk58/unk54 does not survive - cc1 propagates the address and emits the store through $at anyway (77.21%, 600 bytes), and a `pRot[0]` read instead of `((s16 *)&g_WorldMapCameraRot)[1]` measures the identical body, so the pointer local is not the lever. In that function the +2 neighbour read was NOT hoisted above the store (retail keeps the store first anyway) but the address is then no longer CSE'd into $a0 the way retail has it, which is the remaining frame difference.
- id: h-stack-arg-store-sink-is-a-war-tie | keywords: store, order, stack, argument, sll, shift, li, schedule, war
  **A 6-ARGUMENT CALL'S SECOND STACK-ARG STORE (`sw v0,0x14(sp)` moved to the END of the argument setup, past `sw ra`) IS NOT A SOURCE ORDER - IT IS THE SHIFT TEMP'S REGISTER: when the index shift of the call's own base pointer takes `$v0` it makes a WAR dependency on the `li v0,0x40` that feeds that store, so sched2 must emit the store before the shift** (round 402, world_map/main/misc11 func_8008B54C and func_8008BDD0, both parked 93.37% at retail's exact 248 bytes / 62 insns, the same 6 lines off). Retail: `li a1,0x110 / sll v1,a0,7 / li v0,0x100 / sw v0,0x10(sp) / li v0,0x40 / ... / sw ra,0x1C(sp) / sw v0,0x14(sp) / jal / addu s0,s0,v1`; ours: `li v0,0x40 / sw v0,0x14(sp) / sll v0,a0,7 / ... / addu s0,s0,v0`. The tail of both functions is already byte-identical, so the whole residual is that allocation. Measured dead on the same body: the tail's source order replaced by the twin's (unk24, dirZ, dirY, dirX, moveSpeed, state, trailDelay, angle) is identical 93.37 (sched2 puts retail's order back), `g_WorldMapSlots + index` in place of `&g_WorldMapSlots[index]` identical, `try_flags.sh --sweep` tops out at 93.37 (2.6.0 93.03, cdk 83.19, -O1 49.74), and a 4-minute permuter run gave PERMUTER_BETTER base 410 best 395 whose only edit swapped SpriteSetScale above SpritePlayAnimation (wrong code). Note that the matched 4-statement-tail twin WorldMapInitPartyActorSprite2 has the SAME retail prologue and does get `sll v1`, so a longer tail is what loses the contest - park this shape rather than hunting a spelling.
  Round 417 confirms the allocno side of it: an explicit `s32 offset = index * 0x80;` with the base built from it (`(WorldMapActor *)((u8 *)g_WorldMapSlots + offset)`) and `g_WorldMapSlots + index` both compile to the SAME body (93.37, 62 insns - cse folds the offset back into the base expression), so the shift's allocno cannot be made to overlap the 0x100/0x40 constant allocnos from source, and `pActor = g_WorldMapSlots; pActor += index;` reads 85.84 because the `lui/lw` of the anim file then moves below the `lui/lw` of g_WorldMapSlots. Both functions re-measured live at 93.37% / retail's 248 bytes before parking.
  Round 468, world_map/main/misc10 func_8008A5B8 (92.63% / retail's 372 bytes / 93 insns, 12 differing lines, XenoWorldMapDiv) and its sibling func_8008A2C8 (95.46% / 612): the SAME head with a DIFFERENT symptom - retail gets `sll a2,a0,0x7` plus the base in `$v1`/`addu s0,v1,a2` and `sw v0,0x14(sp)` past `sw ra`, while this unit's cc1 uses `sll v1` for the shift, `$v0` for the base and emits that store at insn 8; both tails are byte-identical, so it is the whole residual for both functions. Two more aliases measured identical at 92.63 (plain `&g_WorldMapSlots[arg0]` with no offset local, and the anim file in a named `void*` local) and, new: compiling the unit's own `.i` with the unit's cc1 plus `-fschedule-insns` produces cc1 output with the SAME `sll $3` / base `$2` and the same 95.46, so sched1 is not the cause and no scheduling flag can be - the two constants and the pointer share `$v0` because the arg store is emitted early in the expand order, and the aliases above do not change that.
- id: h-address-taken-load-blocks-hoist | keywords: store, order, hoist, load, address, pointer, local
  **TAKING THE ADDRESS OF THE LOADED FIELD INTO A POINTER LOCAL, AND GROUPING THE REST IN A `do {} while (0)`, STOPS cc1 HOISTING LOADS ABOVE A STORE TO A GLOBAL** (round 378, battling/main/misc4 func_8007A768, 92.44 -> 96.90 at 284 bytes / 71 insns, retail 288). Retail stores `p->y` to one global, loads `p->x` only AFTER that store, `addiu`s the y register by -0x400 and finally stores z, i.e. it never hoists; every plain spelling (`g = p->y; h = p->x; i = p->y - 0x400 - gRig; j = p->z;`, the same with a `s32 y` local, split statements, `*(s32*)&p->x`) hoisted all three p->x/p->y/p->z loads above the first store, because cse will not CSE a load through a parameter across a global store, so the second `p->y` reload came out and the stores were reordered. What reproduced retail's store order and the single load was `y = p->y; gTargetY = y; new_var = &p->x; y -= 0x400; gTarget = *new_var; do { gPosY = y - gRigYOffset; gTargetZ = p->z; } while (0);` - the address-taken pointer is the load barrier (`permute.sh` found it, base 625 -> 70, and its do-while grouping is the h-constant-retail-materialises-head lever above). Residual after it: retail fills the `rand()` jal slot with the `move` of rand's result and uses two registers for x and z where this body reuses one. Reach for it when a diff shows YOUR body loading several struct fields at the top and retail loading each field at its store.
- id: h-forward-defeats-a-struct-store-alias | keywords: store, reload, forward, global, aliasing, halfword, struct, u16
  **READING THE GLOBAL INSTEAD OF A LOCAL DOES NOT BRING BACK A RELOAD RETAIL DOES ACROSS TWO STRUCT-MEMBER STORES: cc1 2.6.0 forwards the stored halfword anyway, because the guard's memory expression survives a store through a struct pointer** (round 410, slus_006.64/system/libarchive func_80028F30, parked 83.12%). Retail stores `sh $v1,%lo(g_ArchiveDebugStreamBlockCount)` from a `lhu` of a sector header, sign-extends that value with `sll 16`/`sra 16` for the `slt` guard, and then RELOADS the symbol with `lh` after two `sh` stores into a `u16` struct (`pSection->state`, `pSection->id`); the parked body held the value in an `s16` local, so the `lh` was missing and the block count came out of the earlier register. Declaring the extern `s16` and writing the guard as `pSection->size < g_ArchiveDebugStreamBlockCount` with the reload as a fresh `nBlockCount = g_ArchiveDebugStreamBlockCount` produced a byte-identical 1300-byte / 325-instruction body (83.12% both ways): gcc 2.6.0 forwards the stored `(mem:HI)` into the later sign-extending load even across the two struct-pointer stores, so the "read the global, not the local" fix does not apply to this shape - check a `MATCH`-less park's missing `lh` against this before spending runs on it.
- id: h-cross-jump-restores-tail | keywords: store, order, hoist, li, cross-jump, do-while, arms, constant
