  **TWO ARMS THAT END IN THE SAME STORE ARE CROSS-JUMPED INTO ONE SHARED STORE BLOCK WHEN THE VALUE COMES FROM THE SAME REGISTER, AND WRITING THE ARM'S `|` IN PLACE (`bits |= x; p->step = bits;`) KEEPS THE STORE'S SOURCE IN THE ARM'S OWN REGISTER SO NO MERGE HAPPENS - which is worth one instruction and is the difference between retail's two separate `j`/`sh` pairs and a body one instruction short** (round 469, battling/main/misc14 func_8008B730, Default preset: 92.55 -> 94.16 with the in-place form, then 93.45 at retail's EXACT 764 bytes / 191 insns once the second finding below was applied - still parked on three allocator/scheduler residuals). Retail's opcode decoder has `or a0,a0,v0 / j L / sh a0,2(s0)` for the six-bit-plus-second-byte arm and, immediately after, `j L / sh a0,-2(s0)` for the wait arm; with `pTrack->step = bits | ((s8)(pScript[1] << 6));` gcc gives the arm a FRESH result register, so its `sh v0,2(s0)` is identical to the else arm's and cross-jumping folds them into one store reached by `j`, losing the instruction (760 bytes, 190 insns, and objdiff scores the shorter body HIGHER at 94.16 - so judge by the byte count, not the percentage). Companions measured on the same body: the opcode local must be a byte (`s8 c;` + `c = *(s8 *)pScript;`) to get retail's `move v1,v0` (a QImode pseudo promoted to int), which costs 8 bytes of frame that the park's unused-local array has to give back (`s32 pad[2]` -> `s32 pad[1]` for retail's 0x60), and `(s8)(pScript[1] << 6)` keeps retail's `lbu` + `sll 0x18` + `sra 0x12` where `(s8)pScript[1] << 6` folds the extension into a signed `lb` + `sll 6` (extend-before-shift vs after shifts is not reachable from either spelling, nor via a `u8` local).

- id: h-a-pointer-load-has-to-be-read-before-the-absolute-store-run-to-sit-there | keywords: load, hoist, store, order, absolute, sched1, lhu, alias, local, head
  **A HALFWORD LOAD THROUGH A POINTER IS NEVER HOISTED ABOVE A STORE TO AN ABSOLUTE-ADDRESS GLOBAL (the two may alias), SO A RETAIL HEAD THAT READS TWO SPRITE HALFWORDS ABOVE THE FIRST OF ITS GLOBAL STORES IS THE SOURCE'S OWN ORDER: read them into locals there, in retail's sequence** (round 472, battle/main/misc27 func_800B5588, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0, a 95.60% / 356 bytes / 89 insns park that three earlier rounds had left to the scheduler -> MATCH at retail's 348 bytes / 87 insns, `check_bin.sh battle` OK). Retail's head is `sw %lo(D_800D2FD8)` / `lhu v1,0x48(s0)` (radius) / `lhu a0,0x2E(a1)` / `lhu a2,0x34(a1)` / `sh %lo(D_800C3E9C)` / `lhu`+`sh %lo(D_800C3D4C)` / `lw v1,0x3C(s0)` / `beq a2,v1` / `sh %lo(D_800D3334)` in the delay slot, while the park emitted each load immediately before its own store. The matching body reads `radius = pTask->radius; field2e = *(u16*)&pSpriteData->field_0x2e; frame = *(u16*)&pSpriteData->curSpriteFrame;` BEFORE the three stores, stores radius then semiTrans, then reads `curFrame = pTask->curSpriteFrame;` between the semiTrans store and the edge store, then tests `frame != curFrame`. Each piece is load-bearing, measured on that body: loads written next to their stores 93.10 / 352 / 88 (whole head one register rotated); dropping the `radius` local, so its `lhu` is emitted inside the store statement, 99.54 / 348 with only the two `lhu`s two slots late (so the value stored first needs the local even though it is read once); `u16 frame` instead of `u32` adds the `andi 0xffff` the 32-bit store needs (356 bytes, 95.60) - the frame must be 32-bit AND read through a `*(u16*)` cast so the `lhu` survives and no mask appears; and the `curFrame` local is what sinks the edge store into the `beq` delay slot (compare it against `pTask->curSpriteFrame` inline and the `lw` is emitted before the edge store and the slot takes the `move a0,a1` instead).

- id: h-a-sunk-store-row-is-a-consequence-of-a-reused-register | keywords: store, order, sink, waw, register, reuse, sched2, consequence
  **A STORE THAT SITS EARLIER THAN RETAIL'S IN A DIFF IS OFTEN NOT A SEPARATE RESIDUAL: CHECK WHETHER THE STORE'S SOURCE REGISTER IS REWRITTEN A FEW INSNS LATER - if it is, the WAW pins the store before that insn and the store's position is a CONSEQUENCE of the register assignment, so fix the register pair and the row moves for free** (round 473, battle/main/misc31 func_800BB350, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0, re-parked 98.10% / 496 bytes / 124 insns = retail's exact size, closed after five earlier rounds). Retail's tail is `or a0,a0,v0` / `srl v0,s5,0x2` / `lw v1,0xAC(s0)` / `andi v0,v0,0x3` / `sw a0,0xA8(s0)` / `and v1,v1,s3` / `or` / `sw v1,0xAC(s0)`: the 0xA8 store sits three slots past the OR whose result it stores, and retail's `$v0` is then re-written by the `srl` with no dependency on it. The build gives the loaded word `$v0` and the shift `$a0` (retail the other way round), so it stores through `$v0` and the immediately following `srl v0` is a WAW on the store's source - the store cannot move and lands straight after the OR. One register mirror therefore produced BOTH diff rows, and every attempt to steer the store alone (`volatile` on it, a do/while block around it, splitting the statement) either moved it the wrong way or cost an instruction, because the value and the store are one RTL chain. Read a store row this way before spending runs: name the register that holds the stored value and check the next few instructions for a write to it - if there is one, the store row is not spellable and the register pair is the whole job.

- id: h-an-address-cast-read-is-not-volatile-but-a-volatile-pointer-local-is-propagated | keywords: volatile, cast, address, symbol, load, symbolic, lui, lw, probe
  **A CC1_PROBE SETTLES THE TWO VOLATILITY CLAIMS THAT KEEP APPEARING IN PARK NOTES: `(*(T**)&gVolatileGlobal)` IS NOT A VOLATILE READ - it emits the bare symbolic `lw $2,g` (retail's `lui %hi`/`lw %lo` form, one per site, cse'd only where no store separates them) - while a `volatile s32* p = &g;` LOCAL DOES NOT KEEP THE ADDRESS IN A REGISTER, because cse propagates the constant address into every MEM and emits a fresh `lui`/`lw` pair per read** (round 474, field/main/misc6, `cc1_probe.sh field/main/misc6`, Default preset). So on a diff whose residual is "retail re-forms the address symbolically where my body reloads through a live `$sN`", the cast spelling is the right read shape and the remaining cost is elsewhere: measured on misc6's func_800A0524, cast at every site 74.12% (404 bytes) against a pointer-to-pointer local's 91.72% (440 of retail's 452) - the cast body emits the wanted tail loads but its aliasing-visible stores make cc1 interleave the eleven field-copy stores with the copy loop, which is worth more than the 3 tail instructions it buys. The same probe showed retail's "cached address + reloaded value" shape (`lui t2,%hi` / `addiu t2` / two `lw 0(t2)`) cannot be spelled with a `volatile s32*` local: in misc6's func_800A08B8 that body measures 924 bytes / 231 insns against retail's 916 / 229 with three fresh `lui`/`lw` pairs instead of the `la`, so a retail `$tN` holding a symbol ADDRESS across a store is evidence of a register the source named and cc1 chose to keep - not of the volatile qualifier.

- id: h-a-chained-assignment-is-retails-pair-of-stores | keywords: store, reload, global, cse, index, chain, pair, side
  **gcc 2.7.2 CSEs a global's load AND the whole index chain across ONE STATEMENT BUT NOT ACROSS TWO, so retail's "two stores, one index computation, one loaded value" block is written as a CHAINED assignment (`a = b = expr;`), and two plain statements re-form the index and reload the value per store** (round 476, battling/main/misc2 func_800740E4, Default preset, 92.03 -> 99.33%, 1464 -> 1424 bytes; three chained store statements took the whole gauge block from five re-forms to retail's three). Retail stores a per-side record through five separately named symbols - `sw v0,0(at)` with `%lo(D_80096FC8)` ... `%lo(D_80096FBC)` - i.e. one 0x14-byte record whose members are separate symbols; writing `g_BattleSlotGauges[side].frameStart = g_BattleSlotGauges[side].frameCurrent = pActor->frameAccum;` and `...value = ...prevValue = g_BattleGaugeHighlightValue;` reproduces retail's per-pair `lh 0x99E(s1)` + `srl/andi/sll/addu` chain + two stores exactly, and the chained form also cost 8 counted-but-unused frame bytes (`vars` 32 -> 40) which was the phantom slot a later dead array then filled. Note the assignment ORDER: in `A = B = v` gcc stores B first, so read retail's two `sw` order to learn which member is B.

- id: h-a-store-between-two-reads-of-one-extern-does-not-stop-cse | keywords: cse, load, twice, adjacent, store, volatile, symbol, extern
  **TWO IDENTICAL READS OF ONE EXTERN IN A BLOCK ALWAYS MERGE, EVEN WITH A STORE TO ANOTHER GLOBAL BETWEEN THEM - so retail's two ADJACENT `lw` of one symbol cannot be produced by separating the reads with a store (gcc 2.7.2's cse entry for the loaded MEM survives it), and a `volatile` second read gives the two loads but PINS the second at its own statement instead of hoisting it, which is a boundary, not a spelling** (round 478, battling/main/misc6 func_8007EE68, Default preset; parked 87.66% / 124 bytes / 31 insns against retail's 128 / 32, and the clean body is 76.72% / 100 / 25). Retail's `arg != 0` arm is `lui v1,%hi(g_SpuChannelMask)` / `lw v1` / `lui a0,%hi(...)` / `lw a0` / the arm's stores, red taking the first value and green the second. Measured on that body: the two expressions as plain statements with `g_BattleTextBlue = 0xFF;` between them compile BYTE-IDENTICAL to the version with no store between them (gcc sinks the store and merges the loads anyway, 76.72 both times), `*(volatile s32 *)&g` on the green read gives retail's two `lw` but at 124 bytes with the volatile load stuck at green's statement (87.66, one instruction short of retail and unlinkable), and every cast spelling of the second read had already been measured to fold to the same MEM. A retail head like this means the original source had TWO NAMES for the address; check `config/symbol_addrs.<bin>.txt` for a second symbol there before anything else, and note that a duplicate entry stops splat (the overlay yamls load the same file).
- id: h-a-prim-store-forces-retail-to-re-read-the-index-with-a-cast-away-volatile | keywords: volatile, cast, index, reload, store, recompute, prim, primstart
  **A READ OF THE PRIM-START INDEX AGAINST A SECOND USE AFTER A PACKET-POOL STORE IS `lw`+`sll/addu/sll` AGAIN IN RETAIL, AND A PLAIN `g[i]` LETS GCC KEEP THE `i * 0x28` PRODUCT IN A REGISTER ACROSS THE STORE (4 instructions and 16 bytes short); READING THAT ONE SITE AS `*(volatile s32 *)g_BattlePrimStartIndex` REPRODUCES RETAIL'S RELOAD AND RECOMPUTE** (round 478, battle/main/misc17 func_800930AC, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0, 90.96% / 1204 bytes / 301 insns -> 93.09% / 1220 / 305 against retail's 1228 / 307, `check_bin.sh battle` OK). Retail's tail is `lw v0,0(s0)` (index) / `... 40*index` / `sh pal,0xE(base)` (the pool store) / `lui at/addu at/lw v1,41520(at)` (pool base reloaded, which any body does) / `lw v0,0(s0)` / `sll a0,v0,2` / `addu` / `sll a0,a0,3` / `jal`; the store invalidates the loaded index for gcc, but the *product* is a pure value, so a plain read keeps it in `$a0` and the call site costs three instructions less than retail. battle/main/misc1 records the same lever for a different reason (`*(volatile s32 *)&g_BattlePrimStartIndex` at eight row indexes, 79.85 -> matching) - it is the same store-between-two-reads situation, so try it on any battle tail whose only residual is a missing reload of a global index. Note the sites that follow a *call* need no volatile: the reload is forced anyway, so apply it only at the first site after a store.

- id: h-a-two-arm-vertex-block-stores-in-source-order-in-both-arms | keywords: store, order, arm, if, else, branch, hoist, reorder
  **WHEN BOTH ARMS OF AN `if`/`else` STORE THE SAME TWO VALUES INTO THE SAME FOUR SLOTS IN DIFFERENT PLACES, WRITING EACH ARM'S STORES IN ASCENDING SLOT ORDER REPRODUCES RETAIL, AND WRITING THE "SHARED" VALUE'S PAIR FIRST LETS CC1 HOIST THOSE TWO STORES ABOVE THE BRANCH AND RE-STORE THEM IN THE OTHER ARM** (round 486, slus_006.64/system/rendering_atfree func_8001E3D8, XenoRenderingAtfree = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0, still parked at 88.72%). Retail's quad-corner `vy` arms are `sh v1,2(s2) / sh v1,10(s2) / sh v0,18(s2) / j / sh v0,26(s2)` and, in the else arm, `sh v0,2(s2) / sh v0,10(s2) / sh v1,18(s2) / sh v1,26(s2)` - offsets ascending in BOTH arms, i.e. `pVerts[0]`, `[1]`, `[2]`, `[3]` in source order. The park wrote `[2],[3]` (edgeY) first and `[0],[1]` (the tile value) second in both arms, which is the same 8 bytes of result but emits the edgeY pair above the `bnez` and stores it twice on the other path: 88.36 -> 88.44% for a pure reorder. Read the branch's two arms in the .s and note whether the store offsets ascend; if they do, the source stored the quad in index order and no other residue explains it.

- id: h-splitting-one-shift-expression-restores-the-whole-prologue-hand-out | keywords: regalloc, prologue, split, shift, expression, statement, prologue-order, sllv
  **A LOCAL COMPUTED AS `(s8)p->a << ((g->f >> 8) & 0x1F)` IN ONE STATEMENT MAKES CC1 LOAD THE TWO GLOBALS IN THE WRONG ORDER AND HANDS THE FIELD'S BASE A DIFFERENT REGISTER; SPLITTING IT INTO TWO STATEMENTS (`x = (s8)p->a;` then `x = x << n;`), THE WAY ITS SIBLING ALREADY WAS, MADE AN ENTIRE 377-INSTRUCTION PROLOGUE REGISTER-FOR-REGISTER IDENTICAL** (round 486, slus_006.64/system/rendering_atfree func_8001E3D8, XenoRenderingAtfree = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0; 88.44 -> 88.72%, 308 -> 282 differing lines, and the first 17 instructions then matched retail's `lw v0,32(s4) / lw a1,64(s4) / lw a0,172(s4) / srl / andi / lb s8,61(v0) / lb s6,60(v0) / lw a2,48(v0) / sllv s8 / beqz a0 / sllv s6 / negu s6` exactly). The sibling `offsetX` had been split by an earlier round for +1.1 points; the lesson is that when a mirrored pair of locals is computed from the same two globals, BOTH have to be spelled the same way, because the merged form's extra `sll`-bearing expression is what reorders the loads and rotates the base's register. Check paired locals first on a prologue-only residue.

- id: h-a-volatile-lvalue-re-reads-but-cse-keeps-the-address-and-sched2-reorders-the-run | keywords: volatile, reload, cse, address, la, sched2, order, lui
  **A RUN OF STORES WHOSE INDEX RETAIL RE-READS WITH ITS OWN `lui v1,%hi` / `lw v1,%lo(v1)` PAIR PER STORE CANNOT BE REACHED BY CASTING THE READ THROUGH A POINTER: cc1 cse's the ADDRESS of a volatile MEM, so every spelling that takes its address (`volatile s32 *p = (volatile s32 *)arr;`, and the same cast written inline at all 16 sites) emits ONE `la` plus one `lw 0(base)` per store - the reload right, the per-store two-instruction form and its relocations wrong** (round 492, battle/main/misc17 func_80092B74, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0; 89.40% at 1256 bytes / 314 insns against retail's 1336 / 334, the 16 missing instructions being exactly those pairs). Only a SCALAR extern has the single-insn symbolic MEM that prints as the macro `lw $r,sym` (which maspsx expands to `lui $r,%hi` + `lw %lo($r)`, i.e. retail's form): a second name at the same address declared `volatile s32` gave retail's exact per-store pair and 324 insns, but sched2 then interleaves two store groups at a time (`load,load,chain,chain,store,store`, 70.71%) where retail's tail is in strict source order; declared plain `s32` the same second name has all 16 reads cse'd into ONE (65.97% / 1044 bytes / 261 insns). So check the ORDER of the result, not only the load form, before adopting a volatile spelling for a repeated read, and prefer parking with the shared `la` when sched2 will not leave the run alone.

## switch, jump tables and exit shape

symptoms: case body order, jump table vs chain, early-exit fold
try: switch jtbl case exit
- id: i-a-shared-case-exit-block-carries-the-globals | keywords: switch, case, exit, shared, fallback, block, store, semantic
  **WHEN TWO `return` STATEMENTS OF ONE CASE ARE ONE BLOCK IN RETAIL, THAT BLOCK USUALLY DOES MORE THAN THE DUPLICATED CALL - read its stores before writing the two exits; respelling the case so gcc merges its exits into one trailing block was worth 6.3 points on its own** (round 446, world_map/main/misc14 func_80095414, 64.84 -> 71.12% at 2152 bytes / 538 vs retail 2240 / 576, XenoWorldMapDiv). Retail's SEARCH case has two "give up and go to the terrain" exits (`beqz s4` after `WorldMapFindSpriteSet`, `beq s2,s4` after the check loop) and both land on ONE block, .L8009570C, which calls `WorldMapResolveStepAgainstTerrain` and then stores -1 into BOTH `D_8009C16C` and `D_8009C840` before returning. The parked body had `return WorldMapResolveStepAgainstTerrain(...);` at each exit - two instructions missing and no shared block - so the whole search half read as mismatched. Spelling it as `found = 0; if (count != 0) { check loop } if (count != found) { second loop; returns } ret = Resolve(...); D_8009C16C = -1; D_8009C840 = -1; return ret;` gives exactly one copy of the tail (the nesting, not a `goto`, is what makes cc1 merge it) and that half then matched instruction for instruction. So: count the exits a case has in the .s, and when retail has fewer blocks than the body has `return`s, diff the body of the shared block against the call the body duplicates.
- id: i-a-continue-arm-belongs-outside-the-switch | keywords: switch, case, continue, chain, order, root, default, if
  **A `switch` ARM WHOSE BODY IS `continue` MUST BE AN `if (...) continue;` BEFORE THE SWITCH: as a `case` it becomes part of cc1's decision tree and moves the whole compare chain (and costs 2 instructions), as an `if` the switch is left with the dense case set and the chain comes out as retail's** (round 445, battle/main/misc13 func_80086F98, 91.49 -> 93.69% at 2128 bytes / 532 insns against retail 2120 / 530). Retail's sprite loop tests `0xFF` first with `ori v0,1` in the first compare's delay slot, then `1`, then `slti v0,2`, then `0`/`2` - that is the tree for cases {0,1,2} only. With `case BATTLE_COMMAND_NONE: continue;` in the switch (four cases incl. 0xFF) cc1 roots the tree at 1 and puts the 0xFF test after the `slti`, adding an extra `j`+slot; moving the arm out as `if (g_BattleCommandQueue[0x2CC + i] == BATTLE_COMMAND_NONE) { continue; }` reproduces retail's chain instruction for instruction. Also measured on that body and dead: `default: continue;` with cases 0/1/2 (89.83, 2092 bytes), `default:` on the last case arm (89.46, 2092), and the case labels written in retail's chain order (91.48 - cc1 sorts the list, source order is not the lever). Symptom to pass to lever.py: a diff whose switch chain tests the sentinel value in the wrong position, or whose tree root is not the case value retail tests first.
- id: i-two-case-tree-root-is-the-lowest-value | keywords: switch, case, tree, root, slti, order, two-case, 260
  **FOR A TWO-CASE `switch` cc1 MAKES THE LOWEST CASE VALUE THE TREE ROOT NO MATTER WHAT ORDER THE `case` LABELS ARE WRITTEN IN, so when retail's root is the HIGHEST value followed by an `slti` range test on the subtree, that shape is not reachable from a two-case switch - and the constant it compares against is the thing to look at next, because retail keeps it in a callee-saved register** (round 430, menu/main/misc8_r2 func_801D9F98, parked 95.67% at 1288 vs retail 1296 bytes / 322 vs 324 insns, XenoMenu260 = gcc 2.6.0). Retail's tree for cases {0,2} on `g_MenuOverlayIndex` is `beq x,s5(2) -> case2 / slti v0,x,3 / beqz v0 -> end / bnez x -> end / [case 0]`, and `s5` holds `ori s5,zero,0x2` from the loop preheader reused at three sites in the loop - that register is exactly retail's 8th callee-saved save/restore pair and its 0x48 frame, and it is worth 8 bytes against the 0x40 frame the body gets by rematerialising `li v0,0x2` per site. Both source orders measured and NO help: `case 0` first and `case 2` first both give `beqz v0,x -> case0 / li v0,0x2 / beq x,v0 -> case2 / j end` (cc1 sorts the case list, so the root is not source-order controlled), as does `default: break;`, and an explicit empty `case 1: break;` makes it worse (328 insns, 95.02). The if/else spelling of the same two arms tests 2 first like retail but drops the range test entirely (319 insns, 95.21), so the switch is the closer base. Useful control in the same body: the four-case switch on `g_Menu->input` (1,3,4,5) DOES get retail's `slti v0,a0,4` tree under 2.6.0, so the tree-with-range-test method is reachable - just not for two cases. Other measured spellings here: `(MenuBeginCardOperation() & 0xFF) != 0` is retail's `andi` (the bare call is one insn short), a ternary argument folds branchless into `xori/sltiu/negu/andi` (+4 insns) where `choice = 7; if (x != 2) choice = 0;` gives retail's `beq` + `li` in the delay slot, and moving `s32 result;` to the top of the local list changes nothing (95.67 both ways). gcc-2.7.2 scores 94.37 on this body, so the unit preset is not the answer.

- id: i-code-after-the-switch-may | keywords: switch, case, trailing, epilogue, target, beq, default, layout
  **CODE THAT LOOKS LIKE IT FOLLOWS A `switch` MAY BELONG INSIDE THE LAST ARM: compare the target of the EMPTY case and of the dispatch default against the trailing block and the epilogue, because if they land on the EPILOGUE the source's last case ran to the end of the function** (round 412, battle/main/misc11_b func_80081B58, park 98.51 -> 99.32 with the byte count going from 1352 to retail's exact 1356 / 339 insns). Retail's dispatch is `beq v1,5,<epilogue>` and `j <epilogue>`, and the two `if (gaugeValue == 0)` / `if (unk2E5 != 0)` blocks sit between the last case's arm tail and the epilogue, i.e. they are the last case's own trailing statements: with them written after the switch (the obvious spelling) every non-taken path executes them, all three tree branches target the trailing block instead of the epilogue, and the function is 4 bytes SHORT. Moving the two `if`s inside `case 6:` before its `break` fixed every one of those targets at once. The tell is cheap: dump the retail `.s` for the switch and read the TWO targets of the empty case / default - equal to the block that follows the switch means "after the switch", equal to the epilogue's `lw ra` means "inside the last arm". Same round's second finding on the same body: an unused `s32` return type is what keeps retail's `nop` in the empty case's `beq` delay slot (levers.md c-stolen-delay-slot-retail), worth 99.03 -> 99.32 there.
- id: i-state-arm-stores-its | keywords: switch, case, store, compare, cse, scroll, arm
  **WHEN A CASE ARM COMPARES AGAINST A COMPUTED VALUE AND THEN STORES THE SAME KIND OF VALUE, SPELL THE STORE WITH THE COMPARE'S OWN EXPRESSION AND PUT IT BEFORE THE INCREMENT** - retail then computes that value ONCE and stores it from the compare's register, and all four arms share one store tail. battle/main/misc15 func_8008B478 (round 396, gcc 2.6.0, 1176 -> 1168 = retail's exact bytes, 292 insns, objdiff 99.97 with only the jtbl operand left): the parked body stored `g_BattleCursorScrollY = j * 16` AFTER the arm's `j++`, which is the same value as the compare's `(j + 1) * 16` but not the same tree, so gcc rematerialised `andi/sll` in each arm (+2 instructions, and the park spent two rounds blaming the allocator). Writing `g_BattleCursorScrollY = (j + 1) * 16;` as the arm's FIRST statement, before `j++`, makes cse share one register, and doing it in EVERY arm is what lets gcc merge the four identical `sw/sb/andi` tails into retail's shared `.L` block. The mirror trap is real: the same fix applied to only one arm measures worse (1192), because the arms then no longer end identically. A `s32 nextY` local holding the target is NOT the same spelling (1192) - the shared expression has to be the compare's, not a variable.
- id: i-list-the-even-case-values | keywords: switch, jtbl, density, chain, default, case, sparse
  **A SWITCH OVER A BIT-COMBINATION NEEDS ITS UNUSED VALUES LISTED EXPLICITLY OR cc1 2.7.2 EMITS A COMPARISON CHAIN INSTEAD OF THE JUMP TABLE RETAIL HAS** (round 399, world_map/main/misc11 func_8008C364). The value is three boolean bits (`partyMembers[index] != 0xFF`, a per-actor angle `>= 0x400`, `gearRide[index] == 1`) and only 1/3/5/7 have bodies; written as `case 1: ... case 3: case 7: ... case 5: ... default:` cc1 produced a `beq/slti` chain at 60.90%. Naming the dead values (`case 0: case 2: case 4: case 6:` sharing the default body) makes the label set cover 0..7 and cc1 emits retail's 8-word table at 91.52% - the table's even entries are exactly the default block. The switch's range check and the table itself then match retail word for word. Also measured on that function: retail's nine-shape block layout was reproducible as long as the two `*(volatile s32 *)&pActor->x` / `*(volatile s16 *)&pActor->unk24` pins from lever a-inline-field-reads-beat-locals' neighbours were kept (93.26 -> 95.87%, 460 bytes = retail's exact size); the residual is one branch POLARITY - retail reaches a shared `result = 3` block with `beq` from case 1 and keeps its own copy at the value-0 position, cc1 emits `bne` and merges the block into case 1's region - which no case order (even-first, case-1-first, duplicated tails) moved.
- id: i-case-0-label-keeps-table-base | keywords: switch, jtbl, sltiu, case, default, index, table, bound
  **A `case 0:` LABEL SHARING THE DEFAULT BODY IS WHAT KEEPS RETAIL'S UNBIASED JUMP TABLE; without it cc1 folds the index and emits one entry fewer** (round 400, world_map/main/misc6 func_80080370, 97.15 -> 99.92 at retail's exact 520 bytes, the only residual then the jtbl operand). The switch covers 1..0x40 with no case-0 body: retail reads `lh v1,0x20(s0)` / `sltiu v0,v1,0x41` and indexes a 65-word table whose slot 0 is the default block, while `default: break;` alone makes cc1 subtract the low bound - `addiu v0,v0,-1 / sll / sra / sltiu v0,v1,64`, a 64-word table and an `lhu` selector. Writing `case 0:` directly above `default: break;` restores retail's `lh` + `sltiu 0x41` + 65 entries with every other instruction already identical. Count the retail table's words against the case count first, then add the `case 0:`.
- id: i-gcc-emits-switch-case | keywords: switch, exit, case
  **gcc 2.6.0 emits switch case BODIES IN SOURCE ORDER and gives the fall-through arm to the FIRST-LISTED case.** So when retail inlines one arm (bne -> default plus the body) and jumps to the others, the listing order of the case labels is the lever, not the shape of the switch: battle/misc18 closed from 97.11% by listing 0x8000, 0x4000, 0x1000 (not ascending) and putting the 0xC group first.
- id: i-leading-continue-inlines-the-fail-block | keywords: block, order, continue, nested, fail, exit, if-else
  **A `if (a == 0) {fail} else if (b == 0) {fail} else {main; continue;} rows[i] = 0;` body makes gcc 2.7.2 lay BOTH fail bodies INLINE at the top with inverted `bnez` branches (two extra `j` + slot fills); writing the same chain NESTED with the POSITIVE outer test and the main body inside it - `if (a != 0) { if (b != 0) { main; rows = 1; } else { failB; rows = 0; } } else { failA; rows = 0; }` - puts them OUT OF LINE at the end, in retail's order, with the two identical `rows = 0` blocks cross-jumped into one** (round 394, menu/main/misc8_r2 func_801DA5BC: 91.33% -> 93.54% for the nested form with the inner test `== 0`, -> 95.44% with the inner `!= 0` so the main body is generated before its else, 1024 vs retail's 1012 bytes). The block layout follows the RTL generation order of the if/else arms, so in general: write the arm retail falls through FROM first (the `!=`/positive test with the body) and the fail arm as the `else`. The same unit's 8 already-matched functions stayed 100.00 across all three bodies.

- id: i-or-condition-sense-decides-the-arm | keywords: block, order, if-else, arm, sense, or, and, negate, exit
  **THE SENSE OF AN `||`/`&&` GUARD DECIDES WHICH ARM'S TESTS ARE INVERTED, AND RETAIL'S TESTS USUALLY POINT AT THE ARM IT LAID OUT FIRST** (round 402, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_b func_8004574C, 74.66 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 656 bytes / 164 insns, first try after the flip). Both arms of the `isbg` block are ~10 statements of duplicated GP0 emission, so a wrong arm order costs a full-body diff; retail is `bnez v0,L_armA` (x test), `beqz v0,L_armB` (w test), arm A inline, `j` end, arm B last. Writing the guard in the NEGATED sense (`if ((x & 0x3F) == 0 && (w & 0x3F) == 0) { armB } else { armA }`, i.e. the arm physical order retail has) makes cc1 invert BOTH tests and jump past the inline arm on the negative result (`bnez` x -> armA far away, `bnez` w -> armA), which reads as a 75% body with the arms swapped and every store in the wrong half. Writing the POSITIVE sense for the arm that comes first (`if ((x & 0x3F) != 0 || (w & 0x3F) != 0) { armA } else { armB }`) gives retail's `bnez`-to-A / `beqz`-to-B exactly. So: read which arm the retail tests BRANCH to versus fall into, and put that arm's condition in the positive form in the `if`.
- id: i-early-exit-gcc-folds | keywords: switch, exit, cast, delay, goto
  **An early exit that gcc folds to a constant is fixed by one shared exit.** Replace the early returns with a goto to a done label and a single return of the result variable at the end: gcc then copies that variable into $v0 in every branch delay slot as retail does, instead of proving the value is zero (battle/misc4 went 98.55 -> 99.78, and it also stopped gcc re-deriving a cast operand).
- id: i-if-c-return-x | keywords: switch, exit, delay, epilogue, permuter
  **`if (c) { return X; }` is a LAYOUT trap**: 2.7.2's `-fthread-jumps` threads the branch to the epilogue and folds the return-value copy into the branch's delay slot, which is shorter than retail's inline block. Wrapping the rest of the body in an `else` stops the threading, and an empty `do { } while (0);` as the LAST statement of the if block (after the return) is what produces retail's exact layout. Both are permuter finds; neither looks like source, and both are load-bearing.
- id: i-shared-block-reached-through | keywords: switch, exit, goto
  **A shared block reached through a label beats if/else for block ORDER** (round 320, `field/misc11` func_80092894 48.90 -> 91.82): `if (radius < distance) goto walk; arrived: <arrival>; return 0; walk: <test>; if (stuck < MAX) { ...; return -1; } goto arrived;` puts the arrival block physically between the test and the walking arm and makes the give-up test branch BACKWARDS into it, which is what retail does and no if/else arrangement reproduces.
- id: i-case-label-what-unbalances | keywords: switch, exit, case, cc1, li, slti
  **A `case 0:` label can be what unbalances a switch tree** (round 323): retail's chain (`beq 1; slti <2; bnez end; li 2; ...`) is what cc1 2.7.2 emits for FOUR case nodes, and adding `case 0: break;` (a value that does nothing, same as default) converts a balanced pivot-2 tree into retail's chain. It is the node COUNT, not the label order - so when a switch's control flow matches but its tree shape does not, count nodes before trying orderings.
- id: i-check-jtbl-owner-before | keywords: switch, exit, volatile
  **Check for a `jtbl_` owner BEFORE carving an island out of a unit.** round 330a tried the round-314 menu/misc7 procedure on `battle/misc19` (whose park note said one function is 100.00 under 2.6.0 only): the split produced correct runs and the known chunking bugs were fixed by hand, but the LINK then failed with ``undefined reference to jtbl_800704A0`` from a stub in the new tail run, because carving the `c` range moves the stub's asm into a new directory while battle's jump tables live in a shared rodata blob. Splitting is safe only in a unit that owns its rodata (or has had `own_rodata.py` applied) and whose stubs own no `jtbl_`. Also: a `volatile` READ is cheap enough that it should be tried before ANY split, since it beats the split entirely when the delta is a folded load.
- id: i-constant-original-loads-once | keywords: switch, exit, li
  A constant the original loads ONCE into a call-clobbered register before a switch ('li v1,0xA0', 'li a2,0x70): assign it to a source local before the switch; a literal gives a per-block li.
- id: i-case-body-order-switch | keywords: switch, exit, case
  CASE-BODY ORDER IN A 'switch' IS SOURCE ORDER under this preset: list the case labels in retail's body order and the arms come out in that order, reproducing its cross-jumped shared tails (round 221, battle/misc26 func_800B1720: 78.81 -> 99.71 by listing the labels in retail's order; world_map/misc12 saw the same). Same function: ONE STATEMENT PER ARITHMETIC STEP ('kind = code & MASK; kind |= ...;', 'abr = (mode - 1) & 3; abr <<= 5;') stops gcc coalescing the result back into the source register.
- id: i-switch-block-order-follows | keywords: switch, case, order, jtbl, block, duplicated, tail
  THE BLOCK ORDER IS THE SOURCE ORDER OF THE CASE LABELS WHILE THE JUMP TABLE'S ENTRY ORDER IS BY CASE VALUE, so a retail table whose arms sit in an odd physical order is reproduced by listing the labels in that odd order (round 398, menu/main/misc3 func_801CA750, 2.6.0/XenoMenu260, 368 bytes = retail's exact size, objdiff 99.89 with only `jtbl_` vs `.rodata` left). Retail's six arms sit `.L794`(4), `.L79C`(5), `.L7A4`(0), `.L7CC`(2), `.L7F4`(1), `.L81C`(3, fall-through); listing 0,1,2,3,4,5 measures 90.00% at 372 bytes with the two `result = n; break;` arms appended after case 3 and a duplicated tail, and listing exactly 4,5,0,2,1,3 reproduces retail instruction for instruction. Read the arms' physical order off the `.s` before writing the switch; do not assume ascending, and do not read the table's word order as the source order.
- id: i-two-more-exit-shape | keywords: switch, exit, case, frame, goto
  Two more exit-shape levers measured in rounds 214-215: an early return that retail keeps OUT OF LINE is reproduced by a `goto` to one shared exit with a `ret` variable (func_80045C10 went 0.00 -> 100.00 with it after the block order had resisted every if/else spelling), and the mirror case - retail cross-jumping two identical `return n` at the same block level - is fixed by NESTING the second one inside its branch (func_80046DB4: `if (n == 0) return 1; return n;` inside the not-ready arm, plus a final `return n;`; the duplicate is load-bearing). A `switch` on a NARROW index (`u_char v = mode & 7;` then `switch (v)`) is what makes gcc 2.7.2 emit retail's balanced case tree instead of a comparison chain (func_80046C58 73.5 -> 98.6%), and an unused local is the lever when retail allocates a frame it never stores into (func_80045A34).
- id: i-switch-becomes-jump-table | keywords: switch, exit
  A `switch` becomes a jump table in .rodata; `if/else` chains do not. If the original has a `jtbl_` reference, use a switch, and vice versa.
- id: i-fcross-jumping-merges-identical | keywords: switch, exit, volatile, case, merge, duplicate
  -fcross-jumping merges identical call tails: if retail has the call twice, duplicate it in the source. **But duplicating the arm is not enough when retail's two blocks are byte-identical**: cc1 2.6.0 still merges them, and the merge rule is the INSTRUCTION SHAPE, not the memory flags. `battle/misc20` func_8009E788 has `case 0:` and `case 15:` both `idx = g_BattleTargetSlotState->extraWeaponIds[0]; break;` as separate blocks in retail (`.L8009E7C0` and `.L8009E814`, both `lui/lw/nop/lbu v1,4/j/nop`); the plain body merges them (200 vs retail's 224 bytes, 89.11%). Three spellings measured with `cc1_probe.sh` on a self-contained copy all still merge (one block, both case labels pointing at it, the copy placed at the LATER case's source position): (a) the plain duplicate arm; (b) routing case 15's load through a `u8` temp local (`w = p->e[0]; idx = w;` - the QI copy is folded away before the merge pass); (c) making case 15's POINTER load volatile (`(*(u8 *volatile *)&g) [4]`), i.e. overturning the 'flags differ so rtx differ' guess. Only a case arm that costs a different NUMBER of instructions keeps both blocks: `idx = *(volatile u8 *)&p->e[0];` does, because the un-fusable volatile QI load costs an extra `andi v1,v0,0xff` (224 bytes at retail's size, 98.66%, andi where retail has `lbu v1,4`+`nop`). So when a park's residual is 'retail has two identical arms and mine has one', no flag-level spelling will help - either find the source-level statement that costs an instruction there, or park it. **The merge is also NOT switchable in gcc 2.6.0** (round 417 re-check): its cc1 rejects `-fno-cross-jumping` outright ("Invalid option"), so a 2.6.0 unit cannot opt out for one function; `gcc-2.7.2` scores the same body 85.41 and `gcc-2.7.2-cdk` 66.39, so a preset switch is no answer either. Writing the two arms in retail's own block order (case 0, group, case 15, group, returns) reproduces retail's layout exactly at 200 bytes / 89.11 percent, which is the best an honest body reaches. One more spelling ruled out (round 402, live body): `u8 idx` instead of `s32 idx` with the volatile
  load un-parks 224 -> 208 bytes / 84.29, because a QI local makes the OTHER arm's `extraWeaponIds[3]`
  load gain an `andi v1,v0,0xff` too; the 224-byte volatile spelling needs the s32 index local. And the
  pseudo-register hope (two source variables so jump.c sees rtx-unequal blocks before allocation) is dead:
  cse records the two variables equal and folds the copy before jump.c runs (measured 200 bytes).
- id: i-qi-narrowing-causes-the-cross-jump | keywords: exit, merge, delay, andi, u8, cross-jump, return
  **A LOCAL'S WIDTH DECIDES WHETHER TWO IDENTICAL `return 0` BLOCKS CROSS-JUMP, and QI NARROWING IS WHAT TRIGGERS THE MERGE** (menu/main/misc10 func_801E31C0, parked 99.75 at retail's exact 1020 bytes). Retail's tail is `beqz v1,EXIT / move v0,zero / j EXIT / move v0,s2` (the deep arm's 0 in the beqz delay slot, mpFull in the j's) plus a second `move v0,zero` falling into the epilogue; with the flag declared `u8` (a QI-mode compare, giving retail's `andi v1,s1,0xff`) cc1 2.6.0 cross-jumps the deep arm's 0 onto that second block and inverts the branch (`beqz v0,<zero> / move v0,s2 / j / nop`, 99.69). Declaring the flag `unsigned int` - a permuter find, base 216 -> 205 - stops the merge and gives retail's exact tail, but drops the `andi` (a `nop` fills the slot): 99.75, same size. Every spelling that re-narrows the value brings the merge back - `(flag & 0xFF) == 0` gives the andi and re-merges (99.69), `(u8)flag` in the test and a `u8 copy = flag;` both measure 98.67 / 1012 with the copy replacing the andi, and last-arm `if (...) return v; return 0;` / `else if` chains measure 98.18 / 1004 because the value copies merge too. So when retail materialises the same constant in two places and yours branches to one copy, first check the WIDTH of the variable being tested: QI/HI uses add the `andi` that costs the merge, and the merge is what moves the constant out of the delay slot. Round 405 re-measured it from both sides and the wall is a `jump.c` redirect, not a source shape: the merge fires for EVERY spelling whose 0x4000 test operand is a masked temp - `(flag & 0xFF) == 0`, `(flag & 0xFF) ? v : 0`, `(u8)flag`, and a QI-to-SI copy (`u8 flag; unsigned int flagW; flagW = flag;`) all measure 99.69 at retail's exact 1020 bytes - while any spelling with retail's tail (an SI test on the variable itself) has no `andi`. Two 3-minute permuter runs, one from each side, returned NONE at base 205 and a 124-scoring candidate from the masked body whose only change (routing the deep arm through a local) measures 99.51 / 1024, one instruction MORE than retail. So do not reopen this park without a compiler-level lever: it needs the `andi` and the un-redirected block at once. Round 418 closed the compiler side: `try_flags` scores 91.96 (gcc-2.7.2), 91.3 (2.7.2-cdk), 99.75 (-O3) and 99.75 (-G0), so 2.6.0 with the unit's flags is the only compiler near it; and the redirect is NOT `flag_thread_jumps` - `cc1 -O2 -fno-thread-jumps` emits a `.s` identical to the `-O2` one (diff the two pre-maspsx files: only the option comment differs), so no preset can turn it off. A third 3-minute permuter run from the SI body: NONE, base 205 best 205.
- id: i-a-cross-jumped-block-keeps | keywords: cross-jump, merge, case, block, fallthrough, goto, placement
  **A CROSS-JUMPED BLOCK KEEPS THE POSITION IT WAS EXPANDED AT, SO RETAIL'S COPY SITTING NEXT TO (AND FALLING THROUGH INTO) THE NEXT CASE'S BLOCK IS NOT REACHABLE FROM SOURCE ORDER** (round 397, battling/main/misc3 func_80077A9C, re-parked 97.90% at retail's exact 1720 bytes). Two switch arms each contain `if (pEntry[0] == 0) { p->actionWaitTimer = 0xF; BattleResetMessageQueue(p); }`; cc1 2.7.2 does merge the two copies into one (correct), but it emits it between the case-1 and case-2 entries and ends it with `j <case 0's block>` (3 instructions), where retail's single copy sits after the shared arm body and FALLS THROUGH into case 0's `jal BattleResetMessageQueue` (2 instructions). Two spellings measured: sharing the block explicitly with case 0 through a label (`p->actionWaitTimer = 0xF; goto resetQueue;` in both arms plus `case 0: resetQueue: BattleResetMessageQueue(p);`) gives 94.72% / 1764 bytes - the block still lands at case 1's source position, now with an inverted branch AND the `j`, so the goto does not move it either; and listing the body first (`if (pEntry[0] != 0) {body} else {reset}`, which would put the reset after the body) gives 95.52% / 1760 bytes because the cross-jump stops firing altogether. Case listing order is already retail's 1,2,0,3,4,5 (other orders measure 92.52 / 97.74). So when a park's residual is "same instruction multiset, one merged block in the wrong place", check first whether retail's copy falls through into a neighbouring block: if it does, gcc's expansion order cannot produce it and the park is a BLOCKED placement, not a spelling.

  **SUPERSEDED IN PART (round 421, same function): the "BLOCKED placement, not a spelling" verdict was wrong about HOW to reach it.** Retail's case-1 and case-2 arms share one body (case 1 jumps to the merged `jal BattleActorSelectActionEntry` with `li a1,1` in the jump's delay slot, case 2 falls in with `move a1,zero`), so writing the two duplicated arms as a REAL shared block - each arm `pEntry = BattleActorSelectActionEntry(p, N); goto actionEntry;` and a single `actionEntry:` label between the last arm and the next case, holding the `if (!(p->state & 2)) { if (pEntry[0] != 0) {body} else {reset} }` - makes gcc emit the body at the label's source position, i.e. AFTER case 2 and before case 0, and the reset block then falls through into case 0's `jal BattleResetMessageQueue` exactly as retail has it. Measured 97.90 -> 99.49% at retail's exact 1720 bytes / 430 insns with the whole body instruction-identical. Two load-bearing details: the body-first polarity is required inside the shared block (`== 0` puts the reset before the body and costs a `j`, 1724 bytes / 98.19%), and the duplicate-arm spelling CANNOT work because cross-jump leaves the merged body at the second arm's position while the reset block stays at the first arm's. So before parking a "merged block in the wrong place" switch residual, check whether retail's two arms share a `jal` too: if they do, the shared body is source-level in retail and a `goto` label reproduces the block order.

- id: i-a-do-while-latch-swallows-the-label-position | keywords: cross-jump, block, placement, goto, label, switch, latch, do-while
  **A `goto` TARGET LABEL PLACED INSIDE THE SWITCH (AFTER ITS LAST CASE) IS NOT A PLACEMENT KNOB FOR A DO-WHILE LATCH BODY: THE SHARED BLOCK STAYS LAST EITHER WAY** (round 472, world_map/main/misc14 func_80095414, XenoWorldMapDiv, re-parked 71.73% / 2156 bytes of retail's 2240). The park's five-arm `goto resolve;` block (`ret = WorldMapResolveStepAgainstTerrain(...); g_WorldMapStepTriangleIndex = -1; g_WorldMapStepSpriteSet = -1; again = 0;`) sat after the `do` body's `continue`, while retail emits it at .L80095B2C between the dir[0] and dir[1] shared tails; moving the label to the end of the switch's compound statement (source position right after the last case, which is where retail's block sits relative to case 6's own tails) measured IDENTICALLY - 71.73%, 2156 bytes, 539 insns, same 601 differing lines and the same block order. So in a body this large the shared-block order is decided by the whole CFG (see residual e), and only the two spellings `i-a-cross-jumped-block-keeps` describes (label BETWEEN two case bodies, where the block is a fallthrough target as well as a goto target) are worth a run.

- id: i-trailing-table-word-null-carve | keywords: jtbl, rodata, pad, carve, check_bin, tile, align
  **A UNIT'S LAST JUMP TABLE CAN CARRY A TRAILING ZERO WORD THAT NO `switch` EMITS, AND A SPLAT `rodata` CARVE AT THAT OFFSET SUPPLIES IT - so this shape of the "4 mod 8 / trailing pad" family is NOT a park** (round 401, menu/main/misc10 func_801E3ECC, 169 insns, XenoMenu260). The body was 99.94% at retail's exact 676 bytes / 0x2A4 with the `jtbl_801C522C` vs `.rodata` operand as the only diff, i.e. an ordinary MATCH-JTBL candidate, and `check_bin.sh menu` then failed by 4 bytes (build/out/menu.bin 153860 against disc's 153864) with 130466 differing bytes over 396 symbols starting at byte 0 of the overlay. That is the signature of a rodata size change, not a code change: `.menu` puts every unit's `.rodata` in subsegment order and `menu_TEXT_START` follows it, so 4 bytes lost in misc10's rodata moves EVERY `.text` address down 4 and rewrites every code pointer in the overlay's rodata (disc 0x801C5448 vs build 0x801C5444 at offset 0). Cause: retail's `jtbl_801C522C` is EIGHT words - the seven case entries plus `00000000` at 0x248 - while a seven-case `switch` emits seven, and misc10's range 0x18C..0x24C tiles as 0x28/0x28/0x28/0x28/0x20. Measured non-causes: the tables sit at section offsets 0/0x28/0x50/0x78/0xA0 (all 8-aligned), so no `.align 3` pad is missing or added anywhere, and the three matched neighbours that own C tables are unaffected. FIX, one line in the yaml and no C change: add `- [0x248, rodata]` between `- [0x18C, .rodata, main/misc10]` and `- [0x24C, .rodata, main/misc11]`; gears then writes a 4-byte asm rodata object for it and lists it between `misc10.c.o(.rodata)` and `misc11.c.o(.rodata)` in `linker/menu.ld`, the unit tiles to 0x24C again, and `check_bin.sh menu` prints OK with the C body live (verified both ways in round 401: OK with the carve, MISMATCH without). Apply the test arithmetically before parking anything in this family - if the unit's LAST table ends 4 bytes before the next subsegment boundary, carve the gap and the switch converts; the carve only works at a unit BOUNDARY, so a pad BETWEEN two 4-mod-8 tables inside one range (i-jtbl-midchain-4mod8) still blocks.

- id: i-jtbl-offset-follows-file-position | keywords: jtbl, rodata, align, family, chain, order, include_asm, check_bin
  **A C SWITCH TABLE IS EMITTED AT ITS FUNCTION'S POSITION IN THE .c FILE, INTERLEAVED WITH THE .rodata OF THE `INCLUDE_ASM` STUBS AROUND IT - so converting an in-family stub IN ADDRESS ORDER keeps retail's table offsets and does NOT need the whole family converted in one go** (round 403, battle/main/misc11_b func_80081318/80081504/800816F8, all three 99.90-99.92% at retail's exact byte counts and `check_bin.sh battle` prints OK). The unit's `.rodata` range starts 8-aligned (0x80070010) and holds eight 0x20-byte tables: five owned by asm stubs (0x520, 0x540, 0x560, 0x580, 0x5A0) and two by already-matched C functions (0x5C0, 0x5E0). Converting the SECOND table's stub moves that table from .rodata+0x20 to the position of its C definition, which is still between the first stub's asm table and the third's, so the offsets come out 0x20/0x40/0x60 unchanged; the trap in the "convert the WHOLE switch family in address order" rule is only the case where the converted function's definition is NOT in address order (the older parks here had all their C defs at the END of the file, which is what put their tables after every asm table and produced the +4 pad measurements). Rule of thumb: keep the definition where the stub was, re-run `check_bin.sh <bin>` (objdiff cannot see this), and ignore park notes that call this JTBL_LAYOUT - the three parks this closed had blamed the section alignment for four rounds when the residual was only the `jtbl_X` vs `.rodata` operand. Reading the result: the object's `.rodata` grows by 0x20 per converted switch in report mode, and only matching mode tells you the interleaved order.

- id: i-equal-field-return-cannot | keywords: exit, return, fold, beq, move, epilogue, prevFrame, polarity
  **`if (frame == p->field) return p->field;` CANNOT KEEP THE FIELD'S LOAD IN `$v0` FOR THE EPILOGUE - gcc records the equality on the branch edge and returns the register it compared, so that exit costs one instruction however it is spelled** (round 404, battle/main/misc22 func_800A3E98, parked 90.65% / 1040 bytes against retail's 1028, and its lib_gear twin func_801E1258 88.98%). Retail is `lhu v0,0x18(s0) / nop / beq s1,v0,<epilogue> / nop`, i.e. the value handed back is the loaded field and the taken edge does no work at all. The early-return form compiles to `bne s1,v0,<body> / li ... / j <epilogue> / move v0,s1`; moving the early return OUT and wrapping the body (`if (frame != prevFrame) { ...; return (s16)level; } return prevFrame;`) does produce retail's `beq s1,v0,<epilogue>` directly - with the mode's `li v0,0x1` even landing in the delay slot - but the equal path still needs its own `move v0,s1`, that block lands after the truncating exit, and the truncating exit then needs a `j`: +2 at the tail instead of +1 at the branch (90.65 vs 90.63). Measured dead on the returned expression: the field, a u16 local, an s32 local, a u32 local of it, and both compare operand orders. Use the shared-exit restructure for the branch POLARITY and count the tail block as its price; do not expect the fold to go away.
  ROUND 479 transferred that solved shape to the lib_gear twin func_801E1258 (the ported body is now parked there) and it comes out 4 bytes CLOSER than the battle copy: 1036 bytes / 259 insns / 89.35% against retail's 1028 / 257, where battle's same body is 1040. So the restructure is worth doing on any twin before parking it, and the remaining +2 is the same two rows in both binaries - a `move v1,s2` that materialises the 0x18 store's truncation (retail stores the raw callback register straight out of `sh s2,0x18`) plus the equal path's own exit. Two spellings measured dead on the lib_gear copy this round: `pTexture->prevFrame = frame;` instead of `= level;` (byte-identical, 1036 / 259), and the function's return type s32 with `return prevFrame;` (same 1036 bytes but 88.32, its equal path folds to `move v0,s1`). A s32 `level` local plus s16 `frame` does NOT reproduce retail's `move s2,v0 / sll v0,s2,16 / sra s1,v0,16` entry: every use of `level` in the body truncates (a halfword store, s16 returns), so cse coalesces it into the truncated value and the raw copy disappears.
  ROUND 492 re-measured both shapes unchanged on the battle copy (wrapping body 90.65% / 1040 / 260, early-return form 90.63 / 1036 / 259) and closed two more spellings. `return frame;` at ALL THREE exits instead of `return (s16)level;` DOES delete the `move v1,s2` store truncation - the 0x18 store then lands in retail's `beq` delay slot as `sh s2,0x18(s0)` - but the body stays 260 / 1040 (90.28, the cost moves into a second `li v0,0x1` for the `sb v0,0x11`), and at the tail exit alone it is two worse (264 / 1056). The REALISTIC typed loops (`u16 *pDst = pDstBase + dstRect.x + x; pDst[(dstRect.y+y) * pSource->rect28.w] = pSrc[(srcRect.y+y) * pArg->rect28.w];`, `pArg->pRows[y].pixels[x]` for the mode>=4 arm) are byte-count identical (260 / 1040) and score 89.29, because pointer arithmetic emits the BASE first in every address `addu` where retail has the index first (`addu a0,a0,t3`, `addu a1,a1,v0`); the u32-cast spelling carries retail's operand order, which is why the park keeps it - so `addu` order pins the spelling here, not taste. Presets for this residual: 2.7.2-cdk 86.68, plain 2.7.2 does not compile the unit's C.
- id: i-a-shared-repair-block-goes | keywords: if-else, chain, block, order, goto, label, merge, branch, exit
  **A RETRY/REPAIR BLOCK THAT SEVERAL FAILURE TESTS SHARE SITS *BEFORE* THE REMAINING TESTS IN RETAIL, AND THE ONLY SPELLING THAT PUTS IT THERE IS A LABEL INSIDE THE FIRST ARM'S Then-BODY THAT THE OTHER ARMS `goto`** (field/main/misc4 func_8007BAC0, round 406, gcc 2.7.2 Default, parked 99.22% at retail's exact 269 insns / 1076 bytes). Retail's shape after the probe is `slt / beqz v0,L_FLAGS / addiu a0,sp,0x50` (the fixup falls through the first test) with `L_FLAGS`, the 0x420000 arm and the 0x40 test laid out AFTER the fixup block and each `b`/`j`ing back to it. Measured on one body: the plain `if (A || B || (C && D) || E) {fixup} else {restore}` OR-chain compiles the tests first, fixup last - 81.90%; `if (A) { retry: fixup } else if (B) goto retry; else if (C) { if (D) goto retry; } else if (E) goto retry; else restore` (a label at the head of the first then-block) reproduces retail's block order and every branch target - 94.15%; duplicating the restore block into two arms so cross-jumping merges it is WORSE (260 insns / 1040 bytes / 93.93), so do not duplicate the merged block, duplicate nothing and use the label.
  Two more measured facts on the same body: (1) an arm whose test feeds the shared block must branch on its FALSE case (`if ((mat & K) == 0) goto restore; goto retry;`) - with the true case spelled `if (...) goto retry;` cc1 merges that branch with the next arm's into one `j` + shared compare and costs 3 instructions (94.15 vs 98.30, 1068 vs 1076 bytes); (2) an inert `if (ptr) {copy} else {copy}` around the merged block is LOAD-BEARING for the reloads retail has (a post-reload cross-jump gives the merged block a copy's allocation, so retail's two extra reloads appear) - worth 98.30 -> 99.22 at retail's exact byte count, but say so in the park: it is a spelling no one would ship. Residual after all of that is ONE displaced load (`lw a2,0x24(s2)` two slots early in retail) and two permuter runs (1629, 1775 iterations) found nothing.
  **CLOSED in round 419: that 99.22 body was WRONG CODE, and the two claims above about the `if (ptr)` duplication are stale.** The successful-retry arm, written as the last statement of the first test's then-block, FALLS OUT of the if/else chain into the restore block, so it put the saved probe values back on the path retail jumps past; objdiff showed it as the only remaining unexplained row, `j <func+0x388>` against retail's `j <func+0x3ba>`-style `func+0x3b8` - and a `j` whose addend differs from retail's is a REAL control-flow difference (unlike the branch rows, whose printed addresses are per-object), i.e. the label landed exactly on the restore block's first instruction. Spelling the retry as `pActor->scriptFlags.flags |= K; goto storeback;` plus a `storeback:` label at the store-back block gives retail's `j` target and 99.24% at the same 269 insns, and THEN the inert `if (pVec) {copy} else {copy}` is no longer needed at all: the plain six-assignment restore measures 100.00% / 1076 bytes, so delete it rather than shipping a spelling no one would type. The last displaced load closes by writing the retry's direction components in retail's evaluation order, `dir.vx = -v.vx >> 8; dir.vy = ((out.vy << 16) - pActor->position.vy) >> 8; dir.vz = -v.vz >> 8;` (vy between vx and vz), which issues `lw a2,0x24(s2)` two slots earlier into `a2` - 100.00%, and `check_bin.sh field` prints OK. Lesson beyond this function: when a park explains its own size by an inert construct, check the control flow first - a wrong code path can own the bytes a spelling was credited with.

- id: i-a-shared-jal-tail-is | keywords: jal, tail, merge, cross-jump, epilogue, fall-through, block, order
  **A SHARED `jal` TAIL THAT SEVERAL ARMS JUMP INTO IS NOT CROSS-JUMPING THAT gcc LOSES - 2.7.2 merges identical call tails by itself, and what it needs is every arm ENDING AT THE SAME EPILOGUE, i.e. the success arm written as an early `return` and the error handler out of line** (round 412, world_map/main/misc15 func_80096C0C, 64.15 -> 100.00 at retail's exact 780 bytes / 195 insns, XenoWorldMap preset). The park blamed the layout plus "the single shared `jal CdControlF` that retail cross-jumps the three call sites into, for 5 extra instructions", and factored the command into a `cmd`/`pParam` variable to hunt the merge. Both were wrong: the unit's already-matched neighbour WorldMapCdReadCallback (same file, retail .s in `asm/<bin>/matchings/`) has the identical `jal CdControlF` tail with four entries and a constant per arm (`li a0,1` / `li a0,9` / `li a0,0x13` / `li a0,2`) written as SEPARATE calls, so the merge is ordinary tail sharing of `jal X; nop` followed by the same block. What produced it here: `if (mode == 1) { CdGetSector(...); if (sector == expected) { ...; g_ExpectedSector++; return; } <error handler A> } else { <error handler B> }` - the POSITIVE test on the success condition puts the success chain in the fall-through, both error copies end at the function's last block (the `CdControlF` call), and the `return` at the end of the success chain is what keeps the `expected++` block shared by its other four entries. Cost of not doing it: 800 bytes against retail's 780, and the top test coming out `beq` into the success chain. Two more residuals from the same match: a `u_char` FIRST PARAMETER emits `andi a0,a0,0xff` before the `li`/`bne` (retail has none -> the parameter is `s32`, and its `CdlCB` callback typedef then needs an incompatible-pointer warning tolerated or a cast at the `CdReadyCallback` call site), and a local reused for two different values (`sector` for the head sector and again for the next chunk's) forces ONE register where retail keeps `a0`/`a1` - two separate locals (`sector`, `nextSector`) is what restores both.

- id: i-jtbl-keeps-its-own-offset | keywords: jtbl, rodata, family, offset, include_asm, world_map, align, check_bin
  **CONFIRMED IN A SECOND BIN, FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION: converting ONE stub of an asm-owned table family leaves that table at retail's offset, so a park note that says "the whole switch family has to be converted in address order" is stale - the only tables C cannot produce are the 4-mod-8 ones, and `.align 3` is what blocks those** (round 414, world_map/main/misc12 func_8008E4F4, 99.80% at retail's exact 396 bytes / 99 insns, XenoWorldMap preset). The unit's `.rodata` is 0x258 bytes of nine tables starting 8-aligned at 0x800709F8, with E190's two at +0x00/+0x18 and this one's at +0x38 all owned by `INCLUDE_ASM` stubs; converting E4F4 alone (its definition is in address order, where its stub was) kept its table at +0x38 and `check_bin.sh world_map` printed OK, with `cmp build/out/world_map.bin disc/world_map.bin` byte-identical - the C table was assembled after the earlier stub's asm tables because it is emitted at its own function's place in the file. The residual objdiff cannot fold here is the table operand (`jtbl_80070A30` against `.rodata`) plus `addiu $s0,$s2,%lo(D_1F8000A0)`, which this body writes as the folded literal 0xA0 off the same base; naming the symbol to get the reloc costs the shared base register (388 bytes, 93.12), so 99.80 is this function's floor and MATCH-level. Companion: the unit's five tables at and after +0x15C are all 4 mod 8 and stay unconvertible, and the same round corrected the world_map/misc12 park notes that had called the whole prefix JTBL_LAYOUT.

- id: i-case-body-order-is-source-order | keywords: switch, case, block, order, arm, jump table, dispatch
  **RETAIL'S CASE BLOCKS ARE EMITTED IN THE ORDER THE `case` LABELS APPEAR IN THE SOURCE, SO A SWITCH WHOSE ARMS ARE NORMALISED INTO NUMERIC ORDER CAN NEVER MATCH A RETAIL DISPATCH THAT IS SCRAMBLED - reordering the labels alone took a body from 6.21% to 69.42%** (round 415, battle/main/misc30 func_800B9508, parked 72.11%, XenoBattleTailCdk0). Retail's 13-entry table (0xF3..0xFF) has its bodies laid out F3,F4,F5,F6,F7,F8,FA / F9 / FF / FE / FD / FC / FB / default, i.e. descending 0xFF->0xFB after the group, with the 0xFB arm LAST - so the source's `case` labels were in that order and every arm had to be moved to match. The table itself is emitted in case-VALUE order and is unaffected, which is why the dispatch head and the table were already exact while the whole body after the `jr` was shifted; a `diff_func` run on such a body prints hundreds of differing lines and reads like a broken structure rather than a reordering. Read the arm order out of the original `.s` (walk the `jtbl_` entries to their labels, then note the code offsets, not the case values) before writing a switch with more than three arms in a cdk/-G0 battle unit.

- id: i-a-last-table-takes-the-unit | keywords: jtbl, rodata, pad, range, carve, yaml, culprit, check_bin
  **CONVERTING THE UNIT'S *LAST* TABLE KEEPS RETAIL'S OFFSET BUT DROPS THE ASM STUB'S TRAILING PAD WORD, SO THE UNIT'S `.rodata` COMES UP 4 BYTES SHORT OF ITS YAML RANGE AND EVERY SYMBOL AFTER IT IN THE OVERLAY SHIFTS - the fix is a 4-byte `rodata` carve before the next unit's range, not a different C** (round 419, menu/main/misc9 func_801E05D0, parked 98.88% at 2468 bytes against retail's 2472). The earlier table levers (`i-jtbl-offset-follows-file-position`, `i-jtbl-keeps-its-own-offset`, `i-jtbl-misc5-bbec-converts-alone`) all converted a table that had an asm sibling AFTER it, whose own 4-byte pad kept the range's total size; here the converted function is the last of the three, so nothing replaces the pad. Measured, unparked and built in matching mode: the object's `.rodata` is 0x8C with the two remaining asm tables at +0x00/+0x30 and the C table at +0x60 - retail's exact address, because cc1 emits function_rodata after its function's body (the `.align 3` table is the last thing in `build/src/<unit>.c.s`, after the earlier stubs' `.include`d `.rodata`) - and `culprit.sh menu` then lists the whole overlay as differing, which is the 4-byte shift, not the functions. `config/menu.yaml` already carries the precedent for this exact situation one unit later (`[0x248, rodata]` after main/misc10, with a comment naming jtbl_801C522C's unemitted trailing zero word). Read a `culprit.sh` run that flags dozens of unrelated functions together with `check_bin.sh`'s byte counts as a layout shortfall, not as a bad match.

- id: i-compare-tree-switch-is-recoverable-from-the-lui-ori-pairs | keywords: switch, dispatch, compare, tree, lui, ori, arm order, case values, sparse
  **A SPARSE 32-bit SWITCH EMITS A BINARY COMPARE TREE, NOT A TABLE, AND BOTH THE CASE VALUES AND THE ARM ORDER CAN BE READ STRAIGHT OUT OF IT: each node is a `lui $v0,hi` / `ori $v0,$v0,lo` pair (the `.s` writes the FULL constant inside both the `>> 16` and the `& 0xFFFF` expressions, so mask them yourself) followed by `beq $v1,$v0,TARGET`, `sltu $v0,$v0,$v1` and `bnez` - collect (constant,target) and group by target to get each arm's case labels, and take the arms' CODE OFFSET order as the source order** (round 423, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_c func_800477D0, 1208 insns / 0x12E0 bytes, matched 100.00% on the first scored run, PSY-Q preset). Two parsing traps: a block's `ori` at a branch target continues a `lui` that was hoisted into the PREDECESSOR's delay slot (so a linear scan attributes the wrong high half - the same low half always appears twice, once in the fallthrough path where the `lui` is explicit), and the mask constant's own `lui/ori` sits in the last `beq`'s delay slot on the way to the default arm. Here the 16 arms were 8 primitive families x {L, non-L}: code order was F3L,G3L,FT3L,GT3L,F3,G3,FT3,GT3,F4L,G4L,FT4L,GT4L,F4,G4,FT4,GT4 while the case values are sorted by the id word, so writing the labels in value order emits 16 blocks in the wrong place. Companion lever from the same function: the arm bodies are a per-primitive-type copy of a packet parameter block whose fields overlap at DIFFERENT widths (`lbu` at 0x8 in one arm, `lhu` at 0x8 in another), so do not try to find one typed source struct - declare the packet as a union of `u_long tag` / `u_char bytes[N]` / `u_short shorts[N/2]` views and index it by packet offset; gcc emits the load modes exactly and the redundancy (the same byte loaded three times) survives because every store to the destination may alias the packet.


- id: i-two-empty-extra-labels-are-what-root-a-case-tree-at-the-middle | keywords: switch, case, tree, branch, empty, default, slti, beq
  **A SMALL SWITCH WHOSE ONLY BODY SITS IN THE LOWEST CASE STILL EMITS RETAIL'S `beq hi / slti hi+1 / bne lo` CHAIN IF THE SOURCE CARRIES TWO EXTRA BODYLESS LABELS - one empty case label merges into the default and leaves a single compare, two of them give cc1 three case nodes, root the balanced tree at the MIDDLE value and produce exactly the retail chain** (round 424, world_map/main/misc7 func_80081470, 81.84 -> 89.94% on the switch edit alone with the byte count and instruction count both landing on retail's 620 / 155, XenoWorldMapDiv; cc1_probe.sh reproduces it in isolation: `switch (x)` with cases {1,2} emits one `bne x,1`, with cases {1,2,3} and empty bodies on 2 and 3 emits `beq x,2` / `slt x,3` / `bne x,1` all targeting the switch exit). So do not read retail's extra compare as a missing second body: count the compare chain, and let the labels' values (2 and 3 here) fix the source's case values.

- id: g-jumptable-span-is-min-to-max-case-not-the-distinct-arms | keywords: switch, jtbl, table, case, span, min, max, tree, case-labels
  **A RETAIL JUMP TABLE WHOSE RANGE CHECK IS WIDER THAN THE DISTINCT ARMS MEANS THE C HAS (EMPTY) CASE LABELS DOWN TO THE TABLE'S MINIMUM: gcc spans min..max over ALL case values and fills the rest with the default label, and with only the distinct arms it emits a `beq` TREE instead of a table** (measured with `cc1_probe.sh battle/main/misc34`, gcc-2.7.2-cdk -G0, round 428). battle/main/misc34 func_800BFE48 has `addiu v0,s0,-5 / sltiu v0,11` and an 11-word table in BOTH bit-walk loops, but only bits 13/14/15 have distinct bodies (8 of the 11 entries are the loop-continue): `switch (bit) { case 13/14/15: ... }` compiles to three `beq`s and no table at all, while adding `case 5: case 6: case 7: case 8: case 9: case 10: case 11: case 12: break;` reproduces retail's `addu $2,$16,-5 / sltu $2,$2,11`, the `li -20` table-base bias and the 11-word table exactly. Same reading on the same function's first switch, where the table spans 5..21 for the five real arms (5/7/14/15/21). So count the table words against the arms BEFORE rewriting the arms: the surplus entries are case labels in the source, not padding.
- id: g-switch-index-narrow-type-adds-the-sll-sra-range-check | keywords: switch, jtbl, sll, sra, andi, index, narrow, char, sign
  **A RANGE CHECK THAT SIGN-EXTENDS THE SUBTRACTED INDEX (`addiu v0,v0,-5 / sll v0,v0,24 / sra v1,v0,24 / sltiu`) MEANS THE SWITCH INDEX IS A SIGNED CHAR EXPRESSION: `switch ((s8)field)` gives exactly that, a bare `u8` field or a `u8` local gives the same three instructions WITHOUT the sll/sra pair** (measured with `cc1_probe.sh battle/main/misc34`, round 428, battle/main/misc34 func_800BFE48: the `(s8)` cast was worth 85.29 -> 85.96% and one instruction). The load stays `lbu` in both, so the sign extension in the range test - not the load opcode - is the tell that the source cast the byte to `s8` at the switch.

- id: g-symmetric-switch-arms-cross-jump | keywords: switch, arm, cross-jump, tail, merge, do-while, preheader, hoist
  **SIX SWITCH ARMS THAT EACH END IN THE SAME STORE QUADRUPLE GET THEIR TAILS CROSS-JUMPED INTO ONE SHARED BLOCK, WHICH RETAIL DOES NOT HAVE: an empty `do { } while (0)` after the quadruple stops the merge but makes loop.c hoist the refill load into its preheader, out of retail's order** (round 429, world_map/main/misc8 func_80083A00, 377 insns, XenoWorldMapDiv; parked, best 69.79 percent / 347 insns against retail's 395, and the same body without the do-block is 60.45 / 351 with the tails merged). Both halves are measurable in one diff each: plain arms, or arms whose tails were made non-identical by moving a store into the refill, merge or scatter (60.45, 58.78); with the do-block the quadruple stays duplicated but the `lh` that refills the just-written halfword rises above the two int stores through the actor pointer (gcc 2.7.2 has type-based alias sets only, so a short load crosses an int store freely) and the two constant stores sink below it. Neither spelling reaches retail's order AND block count. Companion fact from the same function, which is the reusable half: a view-angle refill must be a VOLATILE STORE with a plain read (`*(volatile s16 *)&g_WorldMapViewRotationY = K;` then `... << 12`); a volatile READ instead moves every store in the arm and costs the whole case, and pinning the neighbouring stores volatile to hold the order pays less than it costs (67.08 / 366, 66.74 / 345).

- id: g-case-arms-are-emitted-in-source-order-not-case-value-order | keywords: switch, case, arm, order, block, layout, goto, tail, source-order
  **A SWITCH'S ARM BODIES ARE EMITTED IN SOURCE ORDER, SO WHEN RETAIL'S ARMS ARE NOT IN CASE-VALUE ORDER THE C MUST LIST THEM IN RETAIL'S PHYSICAL ORDER - writing the natural 1..N order leaves every arm 4-8 bytes off and objdiff collapses 89.47% -> 76.16% on a byte-for-byte identical instruction multiset** (round 430, battling/main/misc1 func_8007107C, a 426-insn battle-script interpreter with a 35-word table, Default preset, parked 89.47% / 1684 bytes; read retail's arm order off the `.s` addresses and its case values off the table). Retail's 34 arms sit at .L80071120.. in the order 1,2,3,4,5,6,**8,7,10,9**,11,12,13,**15,14**,**20,18,19,27**,21,22,... - i.e. three runs where a later opcode's body comes first - and since a `case` label's value does not depend on its position, listing the blocks in that order costs nothing and is the whole 13 points. Two companion facts measured on the same body: (a) `case 0: return;` must exist - retail's guard is `sltiu v1,0x23` with table entry 0 pointing at the epilogue, so opcode 0 ends the script and only the OUT-of-range value is the default; without it cc1 biases the index (`addiu v1,v0,-1 / sltiu v1,34`) and the table moves; (b) the shared tails retail has (one `armWait` block reached from four arms, one `turn` block from four more, one `cursor++`/`cursor+=2` latch) ARE reproduced by `goto` labels inside the `for (;;)` - cc1 2.7.2 does merge those - so do not duplicate the tails to "look natural" and do not conclude the arms are unmergeable; the leftovers on that park are one private `li <angle>` + tail copy per constant-angle arm instead of retail's single block entered with the angle in `$v0`, plus the `sll`-in-the-beqz-delay-slot insn (`c-stolen-delay-slot-retail` class).

- id: a-gcc-puts-an-if-then-block-last-and-a-switch-default-where-its-label-is | keywords: switch, case, default, block, order, if, goto, layout
  **gcc 2.7.2 EMITS `if (c) A; B;` WITH THE BRANCH TO A AND A PLACED LAST, AND A SWITCH'S `default:` BODY EXACTLY WHERE THE LABEL SITS - so retail's order [cases][rotation path][case-0 path][shared tail] means the case-0 body was NOT the switch's default arm but a label after the rotation code, which only a `goto` shape reproduces** (round 431, field/main/misc8 func_80083288, 78.75 -> 83.18, 448 insns / 1792 bytes vs retail's 451 / 1804). Probed first: a plain `switch (x & 3) { case 1..3 default }` puts the default body BEFORE the code that follows the switch (the dispatch chain is retail's, so the switch form is right and only the body order was wrong). Writing `case 3:` to break into a `rotate:` label, `default: goto parent;` and `parent:` + a following `setMatrices:` label reproduces retail's layout, and the threaded-away `goto parent` is exactly what makes retail's compare chain end in `j <case-0 block>`. The mirror lever on the tail: retail's `beq` onto the `-1` block means the source is `if (minHeight == NONE) { free; return -1; } ...return 0;` - the negated `if` emits `bne` and puts the two blocks the other way round (74.01 -> 75.91).
- id: g-case-label-that-does-nothing-sets-the-table-span | keywords: switch, jtbl, sltiu, table, span, case, empty, fallthrough
  **A RETAIL TABLE WIDER THAN THE HIGHEST DISTINCT ARM MEANS THE SOURCE CARRIES AN EMPTY `case <max>: break;`, AND AN ARM WHOSE `state++` RETAIL JUMPS TO A SHARED STORE MEANS THAT ARM DOES NOT FALL INTO ITS NEIGHBOUR** (round 431, world_map/main/misc11 func_8008D678, 445 insns, XenoWorldMap preset, parked 99.96% on a table-alignment pad only). Two measured halves, both visible in one diff each: (a) the state switch's highest distinct body is case 50, so the natural spelling gives `sltiu v1,51` and a 51-word table where retail tests `sltiu v1,65` - state 0x40 is a live case whose body IS the switch exit, so `case 64: break;` restores the 65-word table (14 words / 56 bytes, and every later table in the unit with it); (b) retail's `lhu v0,0x20(s1) / j <shared`sh v0,0x20(s1)`> / addiu v0,v0,1` is the arm BREAKING, not falling through, while the arm above it keeps the store inline - so copy the twin's `/* falls through */` only where retail's next block is the neighbour's body. The one-line check is to count `sh v0,0x20(s1)` in both objects (9 vs 8 here) instead of reading it as a cross-jump residue; that single statement was the last 4 bytes of the function.
- id: g-owned-jtbl-at-4-mod-8-can-never-be-emitted | keywords: jtbl, align, pad, layout, rodata, shift, overlay, table
  **A FUNCTION'S SWITCH TABLES ARE `.align 3`-PADDED RELATIVE TO THE UNIT'S `.rodata` RANGE START, SO TABLES THAT RETAIL PACKS AT 4 MOD 8 COST A 4-BYTE PAD AND SHIFT THE WHOLE OVERLAY - measure the offset from the range start before blaming the body** (round 431, world_map/main/misc11 func_8008D678: the body is retail's instruction-for-instruction at retail's exact 1780 bytes / 445 insns and objdiff 99.96% - only the two `lw v0,<jtbl>` operands differ - yet `check_bin.sh world_map` reports the overlay 4 bytes long). The two tables (jtbl_800708D4, jtbl_800708F4) sit 0x3BC and 0x3DC bytes into the range - base 0x800708D4-0x3BC = 0x80070518, which is 0xA28 + 0x8006FAF0, i.e. the yaml's `[0xA28, .rodata, main/misc11]` - and BOTH are 4 mod 8. Proof it is the pad and not the body: with the stub parked (tables supplied by the asm stub, splat places them exactly) the object's `.rodata` is 0x4E0 = the yaml range and `check_bin.sh world_map` is OK; with the C live cc1's `.align 3` at offset 0x3BC pads to 0x3C0, the section comes out 0x4E4, every later byte of the overlay is +4 and the binary is 4 bytes long. Read it off with `mips-linux-gnu-objdump -h -r -j .rodata build/src/<unit>.c.o` (the last relocation run is the function's tables, and its start offset is the one to compare against `% 8`). Unlike i-jtbl-offset-follows-file-position the file position here is already right (the C definition is in address order), and unlike i-trailing-table-word-null-carve the 4 bytes are a pad BEFORE the tables, so neither the position nor a splat carve at the unit's end can move it: park it and say JTBL_LAYOUT. Third such unit after world_map/misc12 and menu/misc10.
- id: g-parity-4-split-is-the-route-for-a-4-mod-8-tail-table | keywords: jtbl, align, pad, parity, split, rodata, yaml, check_bin
  **THE FIX FOR THE `g-owned-jtbl-at-4-mod-8` CLASS IS A SPLIT THAT GIVES THE TAIL ITS OWN `.rodata` RANGE OF PARITY 4, AND THE ARITHMETIC THAT SAYS WHETHER IT WORKS IS `(retail_table_file_offset % 8)`: the new object's section start supplies that parity, so every table the new file emits lands at `start + 8k` and the pad disappears** (round 444, world_map/main/misc11 func_8008D678, re-confirmed with a direct byte comparison: `cmp` shows the FIRST differing byte of `build/out/world_map.bin` is file 0xDE4 - four zero pad bytes exactly where jtbl_800708D4 belongs - and every later word that holds a `.text` address, including misc1's rodata words at file 0x4, reads +4; rodata is this overlay's first section, so one pad in a late unit shifts the whole file). The recipe for that function, in case a later round wants a 445-insn match for two yaml lines: misc11's range is `[0xA28, .rodata, main/misc11]` and the tables are its last ones at 0xDE4/0xE04 (both 4 mod 8 from 0xA28, which is 0 mod 8), so cut the unit at the function's file offset - `[0xA28, .rodata, main/misc11]` + `[0xDE4, .rodata, main/misc11_b]` and `[0x1AC3C, c, main/misc11]` + `[0x1DB88, c, main/misc11_b]`, moving func_8008D678 and the stubs after it into `src/world_map/main/misc11_b.c` (plus a `paths` key for the new file, never a directory key). The new object's `.rodata` then starts at file 0xDE4 (parity 4), the two C tables sit at internal 0 and 0x20 with no pad, and the tail rodata 0xEA8..0xF08 rides along as asm from the moved stubs. Same shape as the misc12 tail split this lever family already recommends; a worker cannot do it (new .c file + yaml + gears.toml), so report SPLIT_JTBL_PARITY4 with the two offsets instead of parking silently. ROUND 452 APPLIED IT: misc11's c range now ends at file 0x1C874 and `[0xCBC, .rodata, main/misc11_c]` starts the tail at parity 4, so misc11_c's first table (jtbl_800707AC) sits at internal +0 - func_8008C364 closed with `check_bin.sh world_map` OK on the first try.

- id: i-a-volatile-lvalue-keeps-a-load-in-the-merged-tail | keywords: switch, case, cross-jump, duplicate, load, volatile, merged, tail
  **WHEN TWO CASE ARMS ARE CROSS-JUMPED AND gcc COPIES THE SHARED TAIL'S GLOBAL LOAD INTO BOTH ARMS, MAKING THAT LOAD A `volatile` LVALUE PINS IT INSIDE THE MERGED BLOCK - it pays one instruction (`lui+addiu+lw` instead of the `lw $r,sym` macro's `lui+lw`) and saves the duplicate copy, so the body gets SHORTER** (round 436, world_map/main/misc6 func_8007EE34, XenoWorldMapDiv preset: 98.17% / 2692 bytes -> 98.42% / 2684, retail 2680). Retail's case 3 arm is only `lw v1,0x38(s3); j; addiu v0,1` and the merged tail owns the `g_WorldMapPlayerPosition` load; our body emitted that load in BOTH arms (2 extra instructions) because the volatile stores to `command`/`state` around it were not enough of a barrier. `*(volatile u32 *)g_WorldMapPlayerPosition` in both arms moved it into the tail, and the merged tail then costs 3 instructions where retail's copy costs 2 - i.e. only worth it when the duplicate exists (count the copies in the diff per case, not per tail). Measured dead on the same body: making the plain x store volatile or not (identical either way), and reading the position into a named local before the two stores (`s32 nDirX = pActor->dirX; nPosX = *(u32 *)g_WorldMapPlayerPosition;`), which gcc folds/schedules back to the same object.

- id: i-default-grouped-with-a-shared-arm-retargets-the-range-check | keywords: switch, default, jtbl, out-of-range, target, beqz, check_bin, park
  **A SWITCH WHOSE TABLE COVERS EVERY VALUE THE INDEX CAN TAKE NEEDS NO `default:` AT ALL; WRITING `default:` ON A SHARED CASE BODY RETARGETS cc1's OUT-OF-RANGE GUARD AT THAT BODY INSTEAD OF AT THE SWITCH EXIT - one branch offset wrong, objdiff still reads 99.87% at retail's exact byte count, and only `check_bin.sh` sees it (one byte: `beqz v0,+7` against retail's `+0x4B`)** (round 452, world_map/main/misc11_c func_8008C364, XenoWorldMap, 460 bytes / 115 insns, closed byte-identical apart from the `jtbl_` operand).
