- id: d-a-symbol-address-live-across-a-call-is-rematerialised-not-shared | keywords: remat, address, callee-saved, call, pseudo, fold, return, constant
  **A SYMBOL ADDRESS USED AS A CALL ARGUMENT AND AGAIN AFTER THE CALL IS REMATERIALISED INTO BOTH REGISTERS, never shared in one callee-saved register, so a retail sequence `lui s0 / addiu s0 / move a2,s0 (jal slot) / lbu v1,0(s0)` is unreachable from any C in gcc 2.6.0** — and the twin fold: a local's constant is propagated into `return local` inside a STRAIGHT-LINE block but NOT when the return sits at a merge label, so a park one instruction short with a missing `move s0,zero` (store) beside a returned copy is a cse fold, not a source shape. Measured round 450, menu/main/misc12 func_801E93A0 (98.39% / 760 bytes / 190 insns against retail 772 / 193): spelling the 0x15 query's status pointer as the literal `&g_MenuCdStatus` at both uses gives 98.23 / 768 / 192 with `lui a2; addiu a2; ... lui v1; lbu v1,0(v1)` (fresh `u_char* pStatus = &g_MenuCdStatus;` measures identically), where reusing the already-live pointer local gives no remat at all; and moving the success path's `result = 0;` to after its two calls is byte-identical, i.e. position inside the block is not the lever. Both residuals are needed for MATCH, so neither alone can close such a park.

## struct / address folding (appended out of order by round 447)

- id: writing-the-guard-on-the-OFFSET-not-the-counter-lets-cc1-fold-it-to-zero | keywords: constant, fold, guard, index, address, addu, offset, accumulator
  **WHEN AN ARM IS GUARDED BY `if (i == 0)` BUT THE ARM'S ARRAYS ARE INDEXED BY THE LOOP'S OFFSET ACCUMULATOR, EVERY ADDRESS IN THAT ARM PAYS AN `addu at,at,s0`; WRITING THE GUARD ON THE OFFSET ITSELF (`if (off == 0)`, the same test, since off == i * 0x60) LETS cc1 CONSTANT-FOLD THE INDEX TO 0 AND THE ARM EMITS RETAIL'S BARE `lui v0 / lbu v0,%lo(sym)(v0)`, WHICH IS WORTH 1.7 POINTS AND THE WHOLE first-arm residual** (round 481, battle/main/misc2 func_8007500C, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0, 88.07 -> 89.74%). Retail's first arm reads `g_BattleTextSlotFlags` twice with a per-use `lui` and no index add while the else arm uses `lui at / addu at,at,s0`; the same source with `if (i == 0)` cannot fold `off` (it is a separate variable), and spelling the read as a literal `g_BattleTextSlotFlags[0]` is WORSE (83.48: the constant address is loop-invariant, so cse hoists it into a callee-saved register that retail does not have). So when an arm's index is provably 0 but written as a variable, move the test onto that variable - the fold is free and it changes no semantics.


symptoms: cast view struct hoists a global base, per-load %lo addends, two locals swapped in s0/s1
try: cast view struct array member fields regalloc swapped
- id: a-cast-view-struct-hoists-the-array-base | keywords: struct, cast, array, member, cse, hoist, lui, addend, regalloc
  **A CAST VIEW STRUCT OVER A STRUCT MEMBER ARRAY (`((View *)g_State.rows)[id].unk4`) MAKES gcc CSE `&g_State+0x16BC` INTO A REGISTER, WHILE THE HEADER'S OWN NAMED FIELDS (`g_State.rows[id].commandMask`) KEEP RETAIL'S PER-LOAD `lui $at,%hi(g_State)` + `addu` + `lhu %lo+0x16C0/0x16C2` - the two loads carry different %lo addends so retail's never CSE, and the cast ruins that** (round 447, battle/main/misc1 func_80070F40, XenoBattle260; that change alone took the park 96.03 -> 97.05% and removed 28 diff lines). Before writing a view struct for sign/wideness, check whether the header already types the field the way the access needs: here `commandMask`/`characterConditionMask` were u16 all along, so the "unsigned view" existed only because an old note said the header was s16. Companion find on the same body, worth 97.24 -> 97.52% and 32 diff lines: two heap blocks used at two different sites want their OWN locals (`skinBlock1/skinBlock2` for the first pair, `block1/block2` for the later D_800D2D3C/D_800D2F60 pair, the first pair declared first) - sharing one pair made gcc hand them out mirrored ($s1/$s0 against retail's $s0/$s1) and added a `move s1,v0` copy in the later site.

  **Round 448 re-measured the same body (unparked, live: 67.82% / 3700 bytes / 925 insns against retail's 3708 / 927) and closed the last two source-side doors on it, so a later lane should not re-unpark it.** Retail's saved set is s0-s6+ra and its `$s6` is `frames` (the `addiu s6,zero,1` at 0x517F8 is the `if (frames == 0) frames = 1` clamp, NOT a hoisted constant), so the single surplus register really is only the const-1 group - there is no second hoisted value to remove. And retail's 0x9D arm stores element `[0]` inline in EACH branch (`sh v1,%lo(A)(v0)` off the `lui`'s hi word, `addiu v0,v0,%lo(A)` in the `j`'s delay slot) and cross-jumps only `[1]`,`[2]`, where the compile cross-jumps all three off a callee-saved base; that arm's missing 2 insns are not source-order reachable because in cdk `-fschedule-insns` the delay slot after the `bne` holds the OTHER symbol's `lui`, i.e. the branch bodies are already reordered by the scheduler. Its `g_BattleSlotVectors` is an `SVECTOR`, so the typed spelling (`pSlotVec->vx = ...`) is available but changes no byte: the offsets are the same.
- id: a-nonzero-field-offset-off-a-symbol-never-uses-the-base-register | keywords: address, fold, displacement, offset, symbol, la, probe, preset

What does move this function: the movstr source is `&g_WorldMapSaveBlock + 0x3C` (not the block base) - 86.75 -> 88.71 - and blocks that re-read the volatile `g_FieldActors` once must go through one element-pointer local re-assigned per block, which is what closes 88.71 -> 91.47; `g_WorldMapSaveCursor += N` must follow a memory store or gcc folds it into the preceding store and loses both the store and the reload.

- id: a-modified-parameter-gets-retails-prologue-copies-a-local-does-not | keywords: regalloc, prologue, parameter, assign_parms, callee-saved, copy, live-range, tie
  **WHEN RETAIL'S PROLOGUE IS ONE `sw $sN,off($sp)` + `move $sN,$aM` PAIR PER PARAMETER, THE BODY'S COORDINATE LOCALS ARE THE PARAMETERS THEMSELVES (named `x`/`z` and assigned in the branch), NOT LOCALS ASSIGNED AT THE TOP: that spelling reproduces the whole 4-copy prologue, where the local version puts one copy in the prologue and the other at the END of the entry block** (round 483, field/main/misc11 func_80092894, Default = gcc-2.7.2; still parked, 91.82% at 904 bytes / 226 insns against retail's 908 / 227, and the named-parameter body measures 91.42% / 896 / 224). It does NOT fix the register map: the pair then mirrors (`x` takes `$s1`, the incoming `arg3`'s home `$s0`, retail the other way) because the parameter whose only use is in the else arm keeps a SHORT live range and wins the lower register, and merging the if-arm/branch-arm values into retail's caller-saved join register (`$a3`) does not happen for a parameter that already owns a callee-saved home. So use this lever to repro the prologue and then read the residual as the `a-global-allocno-priority-is` contest, not to hunt statement order. Presets screened on the same body: gcc-2.7.2-cdk 91.36, gcc-2.6.0 92.88 - and 2.6.0 cannot be adopted for the unit (it drops 13 already-matched functions in field/main/misc11 below 100).

- round 484 EXTENDS this one with the reachable side: the sll 16 / sra 15 pair IS
  reachable when ONE `s16` scratch local holds both a call return and the index -
  `s16 v; v = func(...); if (v == 0) {...} ... v = prox; if (tbl[v])` - because the
  HImode pseudo then has a definition of unknown sign, and cc1 keeps the widening.
  Measured on world_map/main/misc11 func_8008A72C (XenoWorldMap, gcc-2.7.2): a
  separate `s16 moved` for the return and `s16 zone` for the index is 2956 bytes /
  99.34%, the single shared scratch is retail's exact 2960 / 99.48%. So when retail
  sign-extends an index that arrives from an lbu, look for the value's OTHER
  definition in the same function before concluding it is unreachable.

## appendix: narrow copy + a divide on its own line, round 485

- id: s-a-narrow-copy-and-a-split-divide-give-the-second-load | keywords: lbu, narrow, u8, copy, reload, s16, divide, mflo, truncation, mov
  **A NARROW COPY THAT ONLY FEEDS A MULTIPLY MAKES gcc EMIT RETAIL'S SECOND `lbu` OF THE SAME BYTE, AND A DIVIDE WRITTEN AS ITS OWN STATEMENT IS WHAT PUTS THE `mflo` SEQUENCE BEFORE THAT RELOAD - the pair together produce a body one instruction short of retail, and the s16 on the value that a `sh` stores supplies the last truncation copy** (round 485, slus_006.64/system/sound func_8003E1F8, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0, 86.18% / 148 bytes -> MATCH 100.00% / retail's 152 bytes / 38 insns). Retail is `lbu v0,0(s1) / mult v0,v0` ... `lhu v0,0xCC(a2)` (the envelope index, which clobbers v0) ... `mflo v1 / bgez v1 / addu s2,a2,v0` (the envelope address in the delay slot) `/ addiu v1,v1,0x3F / sra v0,v1,6 / lbu a1,0(s1)` - the byte is loaded a second time because the first pseudo died at the `mult`. Three spellings, each measured alone: (1) `u8 level = pScript[0]; s32 pitch = level * level;` then the sum reading `pScript[0]` again gives the reload (a single s32 local instead makes cse keep the value in a register and the body is 4 bytes short - the failure this class usually shows); (2) `s32 quotient = pitch / 64;` as its own statement before the sum, because `pScript[0] + pitch / 64` as one initialiser emits the `lbu` first and then has nothing to fill the `bgez` slot (39 insns, 78.16%, and a `nop` where retail has the `addu`); (3) `s16 volume = pScript[0] + quotient;` - with `s32 volume` the same body is 96.84% and the `addu s0,a1,zero` copy-out to the callee-saved register lands two instructions late, while the truncating assignment puts it exactly where retail has it. Not transferable to the sibling whose retail keeps ONE load (func_8003E04C `addu a1,s2,a1`): there the narrow copy would add the missing instruction retail does not have.
## abs on a struct field, and a bare array extern's `+=` (appended by round 485)

- id: d-abs-on-a-memory-field-is-an-rvalue | keywords: abs, builtin, negu, field, struct, lvalue, reload, store, move
  **`__builtin_abs(delta.stepX)` ON THE STRUCT FIELD ITSELF IS THE SPELLING WHEN RETAIL SHIFTS A FIELD, STORES IT UN-NEGATED AND THEN NEGATES THE REGISTER IN PLACE: the in-place `if (x < 0) x = -x;` on that field makes gcc store the NEGATED value back (`negu v0,a0` + `sw v0,32(sp)`) and reload it at the use, and an abs on a separate local costs an extra `move`** (round 485, world_map/main/misc12 func_800914D0, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2-psx; the field form 90.31 -> 93.69% and it closed a FOUR-long deficit to retail's exact 1664 bytes / 416 insns; in-place on the field 90.31 / 1660, abs on a local 89.71 / 1668). Retail is `sra a0,a0,0x3 / sw a0,32(sp) / bgez a0 / nop / negu a0,a0 / slti a0,a0,64`, i.e. no `move` and no write-back - the value read back later in the else arm is the un-negated field. So when a diff shows an `abs`-style `bgez`/`negu` WITHOUT the `move` half of the pair (see d-sign-known-ternary-folds and d-an-abs-needs-one-local-per-site, both of which describe the `move`/`negu` half), the operand is a memory lvalue and the builtin belongs directly on it, not on a copy.

- id: a-bare-array-extern-gives-a-global-rmw-a-base-register | keywords: struct, array, extern, address, register, lui, at, read-modify-write, cast
  **A GLOBAL READ-MODIFY-WRITE THAT RETAIL DOES THROUGH ONE BASE REGISTER (`lui a0,%hi / addiu a0,%lo / lw v0,0(a0) / ... / sw v0,0(a0)`) NEEDS NOTHING MORE THAN DECLARING THAT GLOBAL AS AN ARRAY: `extern s32 g_X[];` + `g_X[0] += delta;` reproduces it, where the scalar `extern s32 g_X;` + `g_X += delta;` gives the `lui v0` load / `lui $at` store macro pair** (round 485, world_map/main/misc12 func_800914D0, XenoWorldMap; 93.69 -> 96.66% and -8 bytes, at all three sites of the walk). No `__asm__` alias is needed when the file has no other declaration of that global, so this is the cheap first try before the round-474 `extern T g_X[] __asm__("g_X")` form. That retail really has one member of a global triple array-shaped and the others scalar (`g_WorldMapScrollX` base register at every site, `g_WorldMapScrollY/Z` always symbol macros) is itself the evidence: read which of the three keeps a register across a call before assuming the declaration should be uniform.

## appendix: folded displacement vs base derivation, and a top-of-function counter, round 486

- id: j-a-pointer-local-for-a-folded-displacement-re-derives-the-base | keywords: store, fold, displacement, addiu, pointer, local, base, addiu, regalloc, addu
  **A STORE WHOSE NEGATIVE OFFSET gcc FOLDED INTO THE DISPLACEMENT (`sh a1,-10(a0)` where retail has `addiu t2,a1,-10` + `sh a1,0(a0)`) IS NOT FIXED BY NAMING THAT DISPLACED POINTER: the separate local does emit retail's `addiu`, but the ring base then gets re-derived from the symbol into a fresh `$a2` and pActor's live copy moves `$t0` -> `$t1`, so the fold and the base derivation are ONE allocno decision** (round 486, field/main/misc8 func_80081C54, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8; baseline park 92.75% / 768 bytes / 192 insns, `u8* pRingTriIds = pRingStep - 0xA;` before the loop 92.76% / 768 with 98 differing lines against 64, and the same pointer declared inside the loop body 92.45% / 768). Read the diff before trying this class: if the `addiu` you are buying is worth one instruction but the base under it changes register, the trade is even at best.

- id: j-a-top-of-function-counter-does-not-fill-the-second-branch-delay-slot | keywords: delay-slot, move, zero, counter, init, declaration, prologue, bnez, loop, t1
  **RETAIL'S `move a3,zero` IN A GUARD BRANCH'S DELAY SLOT IS NOT A TOP-OF-FUNCTION COUNTER INITIALISER IN A DEFAULT-PRESET UNIT: `int i = 0;` among the declarations makes cc1 emit `move t1,zero` as the second instruction of the function (before the frame's own `addiu sp`), gives the counter `$t1` and pushes the sprite-copy to `$a3`** (round 486, field/main/misc8 func_80081C54, same unit and body as above: 92.45% / 772 bytes / 193 insns, against the park's 92.75 / 768 / 192). With no scheduler in the preset, an initialiser above the guard is simply live from the top; the delay-slot fill retail has comes from reorg pulling the counter's `for` init up from the fall-through block, so keep `for (i = 0; ...)` and attack the register pair instead.

- id: s-a-three-store-per-component-local-is-three-statements | keywords: struct, local, store, compound, assign, divide, magic, slot
  **A STACK-SLOT LOCAL WRITTEN THREE TIMES PER COMPONENT (`lw pTarget->pos.x` / `sw 0x10(sp)`, then `sw` of the raw difference, then `sw` of the quotient) IS THREE SEPARATE STATEMENTS, NOT ONE FOLDED EXPRESSION: `delta.x = p->pTarget->position.x;` ... `delta.x -= p->position.x;` ... `delta.x /= 48;`** (round 486, battling/main/misc3 func_80078194, Default = gcc-2.7.2, 89.19 -> 100.00% at retail's 1392 bytes / 348 insns). Folding it into `delta.x = (p->pTarget->position.x - p->position.x) / 48;` drops 8 instructions and every one of them is a store. The `sra` on the `mfhi` tells you the divisor exactly: magic 0x2AAAAAAB with shift 1 is /12, shift 3 is /48 - the parked body had 12, the only semantic mismatch in it.

## appendix: a call-crossing narrow value cannot be steered onto an already-saved register, round 487

- id: j-a-call-crossing-narrow-delta-always-costs-a-new-saved-register | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, spill, reload, s16, conversion, call, delay-slot, tie
  **A HALFWORD VALUE THAT MUST SURVIVE A CALL CANNOT BE PUT IN THE CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER RETAIL REUSED FROM A DEAD LOCAL, SO THE ONLY BODY THAT DOES NOT PAY AN EXTRA SAVED WORD IS THE ONE THAT RELOADS IT FROM ITS OWN STACK SLOT** (round 487, field/main/misc8 func_80082620, Default = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8; parked 96.38% / 1436 bytes / 359 insns against retail's 1424 / 358, the surplus instruction being `lh v0,82(sp)`). Retail computes `delta.vy`, stores it `sh` into its own slot, keeps the SImode in `$a0` and does `sll a0,a0,16` early plus `sra s0,a0,16` in the `bnez` delay slot - i.e. ONE (s16) conversion whose result lands in `$s0`, which was stepX and already saved, so the `sra` is free. Measured on the same body: keeping the raw SImode in a local and casting at the use (`s32 dy; dy = <rot.y - track->rotationY>; delta.vy = dy;` then `... - (s16)dy - 0x800`) is 94.86 / 1448 / 362 with the value in `$23` (s7) across the call and `actorIndex` pushed out of s7 into `$fp`; writing the same value into `stepX` itself (the dead zero-init local retail put in `$s0`) is 94.59 / 1448 / 362 with the same `$fp`; a `s16` local at the top is 95.34 / 362. The allocator hands the call-crossing allocno the next free callee-saved in priority order whatever the source variable is, and reusing the dead variable changes nothing because the two live ranges are one allocno only when they are adjacent. So on this class the reload body is the best reachable shape: count the learned-first lever as `lw`/`lh` at the use and stop.

## appendix: a +4 array field folded into the load, and a two-read volatile flag pointer, round 487

- id: a-nonzero-array-field-offset-folds-into-the-load-unless-a-pointer-local-holds-it | keywords: address, fold, displacement, offset, array, pointer, local, struct, load
  **A SUBSCRIPT INTO A STRUCT-ARRAY MEMBER AT A NON-ZERO OFFSET (`p->offsets[base + n]`, offsets at +4) FOLDS THE +4 INTO THE `lw` DISPLACEMENT AND SAVES AN `addiu`, WHERE RETAIL'S SEPARATE `sll / addiu 4 / addu / addu / lw 0(reg)` COMES FROM A POINTER LOCAL TO THE FIRST ELEMENT (`pOffsets = &p->offsets[base];` then `pOffsets[n]`)** (round 487, field/main/misc6 func_800A08B8, Default preset, 95.32 -> 95.69% and the byte count to retail's exact 916 / 229). Retail's index is `base*4 + 4` in one register and `n*4` in another, summed before the load; the single-sum subscript has only one scaled term, so cc1 folds the constant field offset into the load and the body comes out 2 bytes short. The pointer local restores both the split and the `addu` order. Same round, same body, two companion spellings worth 0.7 points: `((u8*)g_pGameState + partyId)[0x22B1]` for a memory-loaded base (lever c-pointer-from-memory-paren-sum-is-base-first) and the offset-first cast sum `indices[i] * sizeof(T) + (u32)g_FieldActors` for a two-use `lui/addiu` under -G8 (c-cast-sum-with-the-offset-term-first).
- id: a-volatile-pointer-plus-a-value-local-reproduces-a-two-read-global | keywords: volatile, pointer, local, read, load, cse, cse-two-reads, flag, global
  **WHEN RETAIL READS THE SAME GLOBAL TWICE BUT REUSES ITS VALUE ONCE (a test and an index share load 1, a later argument re-reads it), the C is a `volatile T*` LOCAL plus a plain value local for the shared use: a non-volatile read CSEs both into ONE load (2 insns short), and re-dereferencing the volatile pointer for the later use is what puts the second `lw` back** (round 487, field/main/misc6 func_800A08B8, Default preset, 95.32 -> 95.69% at retail's exact 916 / 229 insns; `nReloadFlags = *pReloadFlags;` for the test and the offsets index, `*pReloadFlags` again in the 6th call argument). The address-form half of retail's shape (`lui t2 / addiu t2` once, both reads `lw X,0(t2)`) is NOT reachable under -G8: this cc1 folds the address into each load, and the same body measures 98.01% under `--gp -G0` against 95.69 here. Read the unit's other matched functions before believing -G0 is available: in field/main/misc6 three drop (99.96, 99.75, 99.78).

  Round 487 confirms it on a third body (field/main/misc4 func_8007D3D4, Default gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8, parked 86.66%): retail's frame is 0x80 with vars 0x40 = eight 8-byte slots, of which 0x50..0x57 is referenced by nothing, and the six spill slots below it (nSetIndex 0x20, pY 0x28, pNormal 0x30, pVerts 0x38, nFlagMask 0x40, nPos 0x48) plus the 5th/6th parameters at 0x90/0x94 are all at frame 0x80 + 0x10. A dead `u_long unusedFrame[2]` closes the frame to 0x80 and puts the saves and the 0x90/0x94 reads on retail's exact offsets, but it lands in the FIRST var slot (0x20) and pushes all six spills +8, so the score does not move (86.66% either way, 160 differing lines) - the hole is above the spills and unreachable, exactly as the round-428 entry says.

## appendix: an eighth loop IV costs a saved register, round 488

- id: j-an-eighth-loop-iv-costs-a-callee-saved-register | keywords: loop, iv, giv, addiu, callee-saved, frame, strength-reduction, at, byte-offset
  **WHEN RETAIL HAS ONE MORE LOOP-BOTTOM `addiu` THAN YOU (`addiu t5,t5,0x8` feeding an `$at`-relative `lbu`), SPELLING THE MISSING IV OUT COSTS MORE THAN IT BUYS: the body grows a callee-saved register and every constant moves** (round 488, battle/main/misc2 func_80075938, XenoLibrary = gcc-2.6.0; 94.12% / 2780 bytes / 695 insns against retail's 696 with 159 differing lines). Retail walks `g_BattleSlotFlags` through `$t5` (+= 8) and keeps `$t8` for the 0x68DB8BAD magic, `$t9` for 0xCE; the seven-IV body derives the byte offset with an inline `sll` and uses `$t5` for the magic. Adding `s32 flagsOff` with `flagsOff += 8` in the for-clause and `g_BattleSlotFlags[flagsOff]` gives 93.85% / 2792 bytes / 698 insns, 190 lines: the loop-live value takes `$s3`, the frame goes 0x30 -> 0x38, the constants become `$s0`=0x14, `$s1`=0x1A, `$s2`=0x1E, `$s3`=0xC. Eight IVs and seven are not both affordable, so count the loop's live IVs before chasing a missing increment: if the source also has explicit offset IVs (`actorOff += 0x1C`, `slotB8 += 0xB8`), the compiler is already at its limit and the extra `addiu` is not source-reachable.
- id: j-a-for-clause-pointer-init-only-renames-the-loop | keywords: move, copy, la, order, preheader, pointer, init, for-clause, regalloc
  **MOVING TWO PRE-LOOP POINTER ASSIGNMENTS INTO THE for-CLAUSE INIT RESTORES RETAIL'S EMISSION ORDER BUT NOT ITS `move`** (same round, same function): retail is `lui v0,%hi(timers) / addiu v0,%lo / move t4,v0` then `addiu t7,t4,-22`; a body with `pTimer = g_Sym; pLimit = pTimer - 0xB;` as statements emits `lui t4 / addiu t4` FIRST (before the `move t1,zero` IV inits) and one instruction short, and the for-clause form (`for (slot = 0, actorOff = 0, pTimer = g_Sym, pLimit = pTimer - 0xB; ...)`) measures 94.10% / 163 lines with pLimit in `$t6` and actorOff in `$t7` (retail `$t7`/`$t6`) - it fixes the emission order and still coalesces the address into the pointer. `la` straight into the variable's register is what cc1 2.6.0 does; the copy needs the address to be live in a second allocno, which the loop body has no use for.

- id: b-a-store-address-is-never-substituted-from-a-register | keywords: lui, addiu, store, symbol, address, register, cse, constant, fold
  **THE CONSTANT-FOLD ASYMMETRY THAT BLOCKS A WHOLE CLASS OF PARKS: cc1 NEVER SUBSTITUTES A REGISTER FOR A CONSTANT SYMBOL ADDRESS IN A *STORE*, EVEN WHEN A LIVE REGISTER ALREADY HOLDS EXACTLY THAT ADDRESS, WHERE A RETAIL BODY SHOWS `sh v0,0(s0)` FOR A STATIC GLOBAL** (round 488, menu/main/misc12 func_801E78C8, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0; `cc1_probe.sh menu/main/misc12` on `pRect = &D_801EA8E4; pRect->x = index * 4; D_801EA8E4.w = 4; LoadImage(pRect, ...)` emits `sh $2,D_801EA8E4` and `sh $2,D_801EA8E4+4` - the symbol form, one `$at` expansion - and adding a second live use of the same address only makes the `la` appear, the stores still name the symbol; the same snippet under gcc-2.7.2-psx is identical). So retail's `sh v0,0(s0)` (with `s0 = la D_801EA8E4`) proves its source address expression was NOT a compile-time constant, and no spelling of the static global - plain field, `RECT*` local, decl-init pointer, cast sum - reaches offset 0 through that register. When a park's diff is "retail stores through a live base register, ours re-forms every `D_` address with `lui $at`", check for this with a probe before spending the lane: if the probe matches retail's symbol form and the real body does not, the register is being kept alive by something else in the body (a loop-invariant pointer, an argument), so count instructions and move on rather than hunting spellings.

## appendix: a global-cast pointer local hoists the loop's compare constants, and per-loop locals flip the saved set, round 488

- id: i-a-local-cast-of-the-global-hoists-the-loop-s-compare-constants | keywords: loop, hoist, li, local, cast, global, callee-saved, preheader, frame
  **A POINTER LOCAL THAT ONLY MIRRORS THE GLOBAL BASE (`pOwned = (T *)g_X;` then `pOwned->array[i]`) MAKES `loop.c` HOIST THE LOOP'S COMPARE CONSTANTS INTO THE PREHEADER, WHICH COSTS TWO CALLEE-SAVED REGISTERS AND EIGHT BYTES; SPELLING THE ACCESS THROUGH THE GLOBAL CAST ONCE PER USE (`((T *)g_X)->array[i]`) REMOVES BOTH HOISTS** (round 488, battle/main/misc29 func_800B853C, XenoBattleTailCdk0 = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -O2 -G0; 88.41% / 576 bytes -> 96.45 / 576 and then 100.00 with the levers below). Retail materialises the state test and the bound inside the iteration (`beqz s0,L / li v0,21` in the delay slot, `li v0,3` before the bottom `bne`) and runs both sprite loops on `$s0`-`$s3`; the local's version emits `move s1,zero / li s3,0x8c8c / li s4,21 / li s3,3 / lui+addiu base` and spills to `$s4`, frame 0x38. This is the round-457 `pVerts = g_QuadCorners` lever (a mirroring local buys the MASK hoist) seen on `li` constants in a battle unit: the knob is the number of hoistable invariants the preheader has, not the loop form - for/while/do-while, `i < 3`, two `continue`s instead of the `&&`, nested `if`s, `u32 i`, every declaration order, the `-G8`, `-O3`, `gcc-2.7.2-psx` and `gcc-2.6.0` variants and isolated `cc1_probe` replicas of the loop all measured the same hoist while the local existed.

- id: regalloc-a-second-identical-loop-wants-its-own-pointer-and-its-own-counter | keywords: regalloc, callee-saved, rotation, loop, counter, split, local, allocno, mirror
  **WHEN TWO CASE ARMS CONTAIN THE SAME THREE-ITERATION LOOP AND THE WHOLE BODY IS INSTRUCTION-IDENTICAL EXCEPT A THREE-WAY `$s0`/`$s1`/`$s2` ROTATION, THE ORIGINAL GAVE EACH ARM ITS OWN POINTER LOCAL AND ITS OWN COUNTER - the allocno COUNT and identity decide the hand-out, the names do not** (round 488, battle/main/misc29 func_800B853C; one shared `SpriteData *pSprite` and one shared `s32 i` over both arms measured 96.45% / 576 bytes against retail's 568, one shared sprite local with two counters 96.73 / 576, and two sprite locals plus two counters (arm 1 `pSprite`+`j`, arm 2 `pFadeSprite`+`i`) `MATCH` / 100.00 / 568 / 142 insns). Both distinctions are load-bearing: dropping either one brings back the rotation or an extra `sw`/`lw` pair. Measured on the matching body: swapping which arm owns which counter (`i` for the first loop) is 99.26% / 568 with 34 differing lines, i.e. the pairing is pinned by allocno creation order and renaming is not free - keep the version that scores. Reading the retail diff first is what suggests it: retail's first loop counter lives in `$s2` while the second loop's, the wait loop's and the release loop's all reuse `$s0`, which a single source variable does not produce.

- id: struct-a-base-local-keeps-a-large-offset-unfolded | keywords: address, fold, lui, addiu, li, addu, offset, local, cast, struct
  **`pWork = (T *)((u8 *)g_X + 0x8000); pWork->unkDA8 = 0;` FOLDS THE WHOLE 0x8DA8 INTO THE SYMBOL'S `%hi`/`%lo` (`lui v0,0x1` + `sb zero,-29272(v0)`), WHERE RETAIL MATERIALISES THE BASE AND THEN ADDS THE BLOCK OFFSET AT RUNTIME (`lui/addiu %lo(g_X)`, `li v1,0x8000`, `addu v0,v0,v1`, `sb zero,0xDA8(v0)`); WRITING THE BASE AS A LOCAL FIRST (`pBase = (u8 *)g_X; pWork = (T *)(pBase + BATTLE_RENDER_STATE_OFFSET);`) REPRODUCES RETAIL** (round 488, battle/main/misc29 func_800B853C, XenoBattleTailCdk0; the two-step form took the function 88.41 -> 90.56% on its own, the single-expression form staying 2 instructions short). The same unit's matched BattleInitFrameRenderState pins it: retail there is `ori v0,zero,0x8000 / addu s1,s0,v0` off a base local, never a folded displacement.

## appendix: a two-sided guard folds to a range test and hands you retail's `index - 1` giv, round 489

symptoms: one index register short, sltiu where you have a beqz, symbol+1 operand, second induction variable missing
try: giv range test fold index symbol two-sided guard sltiu

- id: a-two-sided-guard-is-what-creates-the-index-minus-one-giv | keywords: giv, loop, index, range, test, fold, symbol, sltiu
  **`if (f != 0 && i > 0 && i < MAX)` FOLDS THROUGH `fold_range_test` INTO `sltiu v0,s2,2` ON A REGISTER HOLDING `i - 1`, AND THAT REGISTER IS THEN THE ARRAY INDEX TOO - THE +1 OF `array[i]` FOLDS INTO THE SYMBOL (`%hi(sym+1)`, immediate 0), SO THE WHOLE SECOND INDUCTION VARIABLE, THE MISSING SAVED REGISTER AND THE FRAME SIZE OF A PARK COME BACK FROM ONE GUARD SPELLING** (round 489, battle/main/misc3 func_80078310, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0: `i != 0` measured 86.57% / 480 bytes / 120 insns against retail's 504 / 126, and `i > 0 && i < MAX_PARTY_MEMBERS` measured 99.92% / retail's exact 504 / 126, `check_bin.sh battle` OK - the last 0.08% is only the reloc spelling `lbu v1,0(at)`+`%lo(D_800D2D25)` vs `lbu v1,1(at)`+`%lo(g_BattleActorCharIds)`, i.e. the same address, a MATCH/RELOC). Retail's loop carries two counters (`$s2` = i-1, incremented in the latch, and `$s3` = i, tested `slti $s3,3`) and the spare giv is what spills the sixth out-parameter to the stack: the frame 0xC8 and the 126 instructions both follow from it, so a park that is "one induction variable and one stack slot short" is a comparison-shape question, not a loop.c one. Also measured on the same body: `(s32)(i - 1) < 2` written literally gives the identical 99.92 (it is the same RTL the fold produces), and the earlier `i > 0` alone measured 86.13 - the fold needs BOTH sides of the range for cc1 to rewrite the test.

## appendix: a word store read back as a halfword is one spilled pseudo, round 489

- id: spill-a-word-store-read-back-with-lhu-is-one-spilled-si-pseudo | keywords: spill, frame, lhu, subreg, halfword, sw, truncation, local
  **A `sw $s7,0x70($sp)` FOLLOWED BY `lhu $t1,0x70($sp)` IN THE SAME SLOT IS ONE SImode LOCAL, NOT TWO: cc1 2.6.0 loads only the LOW HALF of a spilled SImode pseudo whose use is a u16 rvalue, so retail's `sw`/`lhu` pair is `s32 y = textY;` used as `rect.y = y`, and reading it as "a u16 variable stored with a sw" sends you hunting for two variables that do not exist** (round 489, battle/main/misc17 func_80093B08, XenoBattle260 = gcc-2.6.0, 397 insns, parked at 92.06%). The same function pins the other half of the pair: `sw`/`lw` on 0x78 is the same construct with an s32 use (a byte offset), and both slots hold COPIES of live scalars, so count the outer loop's live values before blaming the allocator - retail keeps seven across the inner loop's calls ($s0-$s7+fp) and homes three copies, which is only reachable when the loop is at its register limit.
- id: spill-a-copy-whose-only-uses-are-in-the-inner-loop-is-strength-reduced-away | keywords: spill, copy, propagation, strength-reduction, giv, frame, register, pressure
  **`s32 ofs = countOfs;` BEFORE THE INNER LOOP AND USING `ofs` THERE SURVIVES AS A MEMORY SLOT ONLY WHEN THE LOOP HAS NO SPARE CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER; OTHERWISE cc1 COPY-PROPAGATES IT INTO ITS SOURCE AND STRENGTH-REDUCES counts+ofs INTO ONE WALKING POINTER, WHICH REPLACES A DIFFERENT SPILL (rowY) AND LEAVES THE FRAME 8 SHORT** (round 489, same function, measured both ways on one body). Adding the copy plus an `s32 digitY = textY;` copy and reading the post-loop digit through `ofs` measured 90.20% / 1600 bytes / 400 insns / frame 0xB8 with five spills (the three intended plus two slots holding &counts itself); changing only that one post-loop read to the source variable, `countOfs`, measured 92.06% / 1560 / 390 / 0xA0, where the two &counts slots and `ofs` vanish and the walking pointer lands in fp. So in this function retail's data flow is `ofs` inside the digit loop and `countOfs` after it - the split is load-bearing, and a copy variable is worth trying only after the loop's live set is already full.

## appendix: the signed-div-by-4 dividend copy is placed by cc1, not reorg, round 490

symptoms: one move short, delay slot holds the store, loop head copy missing, div-by-power-of-two, j target one instruction early
try: loop div copy move delay slot reorg preheader invariant short

- id: loop-a-signed-div-by-power-of-two-copies-the-dividend-at-the-loop-head-only | keywords: loop, div, move, copy, delay-slot, reorg, preheader, invariant
  **`i < n / 4` COMPILES TO cc1'S OWN `move dst,src / bgez dst,0f / addiu dst,dst,3 / 0: sra dst,dst,2` WITH THE DIVIDEND COPY INSIDE THE LOOP HEAD BLOCK, SO A RETAIL BODY THAT HAS IT ONCE IN THE PREHEADER (OUTSIDE ITS LOOP LABEL) *AND* ONCE IN THE `j` DELAY SLOT IS 184 INSTRUCTIONS AGAINST 183 AND NO STATEMENT ORDER REACHES IT** (round 490, slus_006.64/psyq/libgpu_c func_8004668C, PSY-Q = gcc-2.7.2 `-O3 -G0`: parked 99.10% / 183 insns / 732 bytes against retail's 184 / 736). Before blaming reorg, read `build/src/<unit>.c.s`: this body's cc1 output already ends the loop with `j $L14 / sw $5,0($4)` and already opens `$L14` with `move $2,$17`, i.e. both halves of the diff (the store in the delay slot, the loop-head copy) are cc1's, and maspsx is not involved. The signature that identifies the copy as the division's dividend and not an invariant reload: it feeds a `bgez` + `addiu +3` + `sra 2` triple whose destination the test then clobbers, which is why gcc cannot hoist it (a genuinely hoistable invariant, like this loop's `move a3,p`, does land in the preheader). Measured byte-identical to the `for` form (99.10, 15 differing lines): `i = 0; while (i < n / 4) { ...; i++; }` and the swapped-operand `n / 4 > i`, and a permuter run found nothing (1243 iterations, base=163 best=163). Parking is correct for this shape.

## appendix: four identical `base + offset` adds are not reachable from any C spelling

- id: b-a-repeated-base-plus-offset-sum-always-collapses-to-one-addu | keywords: addu, cse, giv, loop, offset, fold, reassociate, duplicated
  **RETAIL SHOWING FOUR `addu $vN,$base,$off` WITH THE SAME TWO REGISTERS AND THE CONSTANT IN EACH LOAD'S DISPLACEMENT IS NOT SOURCE-REACHABLE: cc1's `fold` REASSOCIATES `pB + (off + K)` INTO `(pB + off) + K` BEFORE `cse`, SO EVERY PARENTHESISATION OF THE SAME SUM COLLAPSES TO ONE `addu` AND THE OTHER THREE USES JUST LOAD ITS RESULT** (probe-measured after round 476, field/main/main `FieldLoadUITextures`; the park is 87.32% / 432 bytes against retail's 428 with the three extra adds being the whole gap). `cc1_probe.sh field/main/main` on an isolated copy of the loop reproduces the parked body exactly (`addu $2,$19,$21` once, then `lh 2/4/6/8($2)`), and six re-spellings measure the same single add: `pB + (off + K)`, `(K + off) + pB`, `off + pB + K`, `&pB[off + K]`, a `Row*` subscripted `pRow[i].field`, and a flat `s16*` subscripted `pT[i * 6 + K]` (that one becomes a single walking base with displacements 0..10, no add at all). `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop` changes nothing, so the add is not a post-loop cse merge either - the tree is already shared at cse1. Two by-products worth keeping: `off + pB + K` is the spelling that produces retail's BASE-FIRST operand order (`addu v0,base,off`; `pB + off + K` gives `addu v0,off,base`), and subscripting a struct array through the SYMBOL (`D_800ADC44[i].clutX`) makes each field form `lui $at,%hi(<the field's own symbol>)` so the base never gets a register at all (73.11% vs 87.32%). Count the addus before spending a lane: if retail repeats one register pair four times in one block, no offset/pointer spelling of that one value will reproduce it, and the source must have had something the C cannot express.

## appendix: retail re-forms a base+scaled sum, and the other-of-two-contexts index, round 490

- id: cse-a-base-plus-scaled-index-sum-that-retail-refolds-is-not-a-preset | keywords: cse, addu, array, subscript, index, sum, hoist, preset
  **FIVE `arr[index].field` READS IN ONE BLOCK WHOSE RETAIL REBUILDS `addu reg,base,scaled` FIVE TIMES ARE NOT REACHABLE FROM SOURCE, AND THE PRESET IS NOT THE QUESTION: every compiler in the tree cse-s `base + index * size` into ONE register** (round 490, field/main/misc9 func_800ABA98, parked 87.23% / 612 bytes / 153 insns against retail's 668 / 160). Retail keeps the table base in `$s2` and `index << 5` in `$s1` live across the whole body and re-forms the sum at each of the five field reads AND at a sixth read after a `HeapFree`, i.e. five separate sums and one MORE callee-saved register (frame 0x40 vs 0x38, pImage in `$s3` vs `$s2`); this cc1 keeps the sum and needs one fewer. Measured on the live body: gcc-2.6.0 87.23, gcc-2.7.2 87.23, gcc-2.7.2-cdk 87.08, `-G0` 87.23, and a full `-O`/`-G`/`-mcpu` sweep on the earlier body peaked at 82.61, so do not spend a second preset screen on this shape. Note retail DID common the shift (`sll s1,s0,5` once) - only the sum is missing - so the wall is cse's treatment of the address sum, not of the index chain.
- id: c-the-other-of-two-contexts-index-is-addiu-plus-andi-not-xor | keywords: addu, andi, xori, index, context, two, spelling, table
  **FOR AN INDEX THAT SELECTS "THE OTHER OF TWO" RENDER CONTEXTS, RETAIL'S `addiu v1,ctx,1 / andi v1,v1,1` MEANS THE SOURCE WAS `(ctx + 1) & 1`; WRITING THE EQUIVALENT `ctx ^ 1` COMPILES TO `xori` AND COSTS 6 POINTS** (round 490, field/main/misc9 func_800AC99C, 80.34% -> 74.50% on the same body, the xor also moving the whole `$s0`/`$s1` hand-out). Nothing else changed, so read a two-way context selector off the retail opcodes before optimising the expression by hand.

## appendix: a narrow callee return type, and a per-arm local's argument-copy order, round 492

symptoms: andi 0xff on the assignment instead of the test, u_char return, move copy in the wrong slot, argument decrement order
try: andi narrow extension return type copy order delay slot arm local

- id: b-a-qI-callee-return-type-decides-where-the-zero-extend-lands | keywords: andi, return, type, u_char, narrow, extension, copy, move
  **WHEN RETAIL HAS `addu a1,v0,zero / andi v0,a1,0xff / beqz / addiu a1,a1,-1` AND YOUR COMPILE HAS `andi a1,v0,0xff / beqz a1` PLUS ONE INSTRUCTION FEWER, THE CALLEE'S DECLARED RETURN TYPE IS THE KNOB: declare it SI and cast at the test** (round 492, slus_006.64/system/temp2 func_800248D4, XenoGraphicsDiv = gcc-2.7.2-cdk, 97.22 -> 97.50% and 1592 -> 1596 bytes, the arm then exact). `AnimScriptStackPopU8` really returns `u_char` in animation_scripts.c, but with `extern u_char` the width change is emitted at the ASSIGNMENT (the value is copied through a masked pseudo) and `if (count != 0)` has nothing to mask, while retail keeps the copied value unmasked in `$a1` and masks a separate `$v0` for the test - i.e. the original TU's declaration was SI (or unprototyped, which defaults to `int`) and the source wrote `if ((u8)count != 0)`. A QI-to-SI conversion is a conversion insn; an SI declaration plus an explicit `(u8)` cast is one too, so this is not a byte-neutral respelling - check the width before blaming the allocator for a missing move.
- id: b-an-arm-local-plus-its-own-decrement-statement-orders-the-argument-copies | keywords: regalloc, arm, local, argument, copy, order, decrement, delay-slot
  **IN A SWITCH INTERPRETER, GIVING AN ARM ITS OWN LOCAL AND WRITING THE PARAMETER'S DECREMENT AS A SEPARATE STATEMENT PUTS THE DECREMENT BEFORE THE FIRST ARGUMENT COPY, WHICH IS RETAIL'S `beqz $v0 / addiu a1,a1,-1` (SLOT) / `addu a0,s0,zero`; SHARED WITH OTHER ARMS THE SAME CODE EMITS `beqz / addu a0 / addiu a1` AND READS ONE INSTRUCTION SHORT** (round 492, same function, 97.50 -> 97.74%). The arm was `AnimScriptStackPushU8(pSpriteData, count - 1);` on a function-level `count`; `s32 loopCount = PopU8(); if ((u8)loopCount != 0) { loopCount--; PushU8(pSpriteData, loopCount); }` fixes both the copy order and the pseudo (a shared local that crosses a call takes a callee-saved register). Two more arm locals on the same body paid the same way: the 0xA7 arm's own frame count made its division-by-256 keep the result in the `mflo` register (retail's `nop` bgez slot instead of a duplicated `sra`), 97.74 -> 98.01%, and block-scoping `count`/`flags`/`mask` into 0xBE measured byte-identical, so the win is per-arm ownership, not per-arm naming.

## appendix: a struct's callback return type decides the entry copy, round 492

- id: h-a-narrow-callback-pointer-truncates-the-call-result-in-place | keywords: callback, return, prototype, header, s16, s32, copy, truncate
  **WHEN RETAIL'S ENTRY IS `move s2,v0 / sll v0,s2,16 / sra s1,v0,16` (RAW RETURN VALUE COPIED OUT, THEN THE NARROW ONE DERIVED FROM IT) AND OURS IS `sll v0,v0,16 / sra s2,v0,16 / move s1,s2`, THE STRUCT FIELD'S FUNCTION-POINTER RETURN TYPE IS WRONG: an `s16 (*pInterpolate)(...)` field makes cc1 convert the call result in place, a `s32 (*)(...)` field gives retail's raw copy and puts the `sll/sra` on the `s16 local = level;` assignment** (round 492, lib_gear/main/main func_801E1258, XenoLibraryDiv = gcc-2.6.0; `include/libgear/main.h` `Temp8::pInterpolate` s16 -> s32 measured 89.35 -> 92.35% / 1036 -> 1032 bytes / 259 -> 258 insns, and it also restored retail's four tail exits, which truncate the raw `$s2` in the branch delay slots). The evidence to look for first: the same function in another unit that declares its own copy of the struct with `s32 (*)(...)` already (`src/battle/main/misc22.c` `BattleMisc22Image`), i.e. a sibling's park note saying "the callback returns something wider than s16" is a HEADER-TYPE statement, not a body statement. Check the blast radius before keeping it: a field type change only alters code at the CALL SITES, so grep for the pointer's name across `src/` and re-run `check_bin.sh` on the binary that owns the header.

## appendix: a repeated absolute-symbol access in one block forces an address register, round 492

- id: cse-a-repeated-absolute-symbol-access-in-one-block-becomes-la-plus-a-register-load | keywords: cse, address, la, lui, lw, symbol, absolute, repeat, gp
  **RETAIL RE-FORMING AN ABSOLUTE SYMBOL ADDRESS AT EVERY ONE OF FOUR ACCESSES IN ONE BASIC BLOCK (`lui v0,%hi(g); lw v0,%lo(g)(v0)` FOUR TIMES, THE STORE VIA `$at`) IS NOT SOURCE-REACHABLE WHEN TWO OF THOSE ACCESSES ARE NEAR-ADJACENT: cc1 MATERIALISES THE ADDRESS IN A REGISTER AT THE THIRD USE (`la $4,g` + `lw $2,0($4)` + `lw $2,0($4)` + `sw $2,0($4)`) AND NOTHING IN THE SPELLING MOVES IT** (round 492, field/main/misc6 func_800A1364, Default = 2.7.2 `-O2 -G8`; park 92.58% / 396 bytes / 99 insns = retail's exact size, ALL 32 differing lines being this shape plus the knock-on placement of the `lui a1,0xFFFF`/`ori a1,a1,0x1FFF` mask). `cc1_probe.sh field/main/misc6` on the tail alone (four reads of an unbounded `extern s32 g_C[]` feeding two array stores, a bitfield store and `g_C[0]++`) reproduces the `la` exactly, and it is measured IDENTICAL under gcc-2.6.0-psx, under `-G0`, with `extern volatile s32 g_C[]`, with an `s32 nSlot` local carrying uses 3 and 4, with the bitfield store moved before the second array store, with `%8`, and with `g_C[0] = g_C[0] + 1`. Two diagnostics worth reading before spending the lane: the first two accesses stay SYMBOLIC (`lw $2,g_C`), so the trigger is a second address use that survives an intervening store, not the count of uses; and `-O1` scores 61.07 / `-O3` 41.91 on this function, so the preset screen is empty. A `-G0` unit removes the whole shape (both forms become `la`), which is why this class only shows up in `-G8` units.

- id: cse-a-return-zero-in-an-entry-branch-delay-slot-is-a-second-copy-not-a-hoist | keywords: regalloc, return, delay-slot, reorg, v0, allocator, tie, join
  **TWO `addu $v0,$zero,$zero` IN RETAIL - ONE IN THE ENTRY `bne`'s DELAY SLOT AND ONE AFTER THE LAST JOIN BEFORE THE TRAILING STORES - MEAN THE RETURN-VALUE INSN SITS BEFORE THOSE STORES, AND THAT IS WHAT KEEPS `$v0` OUT OF THE ALLOCATOR'S HANDS FOR THE POINTER LOAD IN BETWEEN; A BODY WHOSE `move v0,zero` LANDS AFTER THE STORES HAS THE POINTER IN `$v0` INSTEAD AND IS TWO INSTRUCTIONS SHORT** (round 492, field/main/misc6 func_8009FA54, Default = 2.7.2 `-O2 -G8`; park 90.86% / 316 bytes / 79 insns against retail's 324 / 81, the two missing being the `sll a0,a1,0x10` + `sra v0,a0,0x10` pair that only appears once the angle is out of `$v0`). The reorg fill is free on both paths exactly because the value is constant, so the entry delay slot is a *symptom* of the RTL position, not the knob: `return 0;`, an early `return 0` first, and a `s32 nResult = 0;` local all leave the copy at the end. Read the retail tail before typing: if the trailing sequence is `move vN,aX` then three stores through one pointer, retail's sum temp and pointer are the two registers the return value is not using.

## appendix: an element-unit offset giv, and the frame word it buys, round 492

- id: giv-a-pointer-add-scaled-offset-folds-to-a-byte-giv | keywords: giv, loop, strength-reduce, sll, addiu, offset, frame, mfhi
  **FIVE `pBase + (y * STRIDE + 1)` ADDS FROM ONE SHARED OFFSET COMPILE TO A BYTE-UNIT GIV, SO RETAIL'S `addiu $sN,$giv,1` + `sll $v0,$sN,1` PAIR IS A `loop.c` DECISION AND NOT A SOURCE SHAPE - AND THAT MISSING GIV IS WHAT BUYS RETAIL'S EXTRA CALLEE-SAVED WORD, WHICH IS WHY AN `mfhi` DESTINATION IN `$sN` INSTEAD OF `$tN` MUST NOT BE COUNTED AS A SECOND RESIDUAL** (round 492, battling/main/misc17 func_8008E120, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8, parked 89.31% / 392 bytes / 98 insns against retail's 408 / 102). Retail hoists five tap bases out of the loop, keeps `y * 0x70` in a giv in ELEMENT units (`li t4,0x1490` / `addiu t4,t4,-0x70` at the tail) and forms the shared scaled offset in the head (`addiu s1,t4,1` / `sll v0,s1,1`); this cc1 folds the whole `2 * (y * 0x70 + 1)` into a byte giv (`li t3,0x2922` / `addiu t3,t3,-0xE0`), which is exactly 2 instructions less. The four-instruction gap is therefore `[addiu + sll]` plus `[sw $s5,0x24(sp) + lw $s5,0x24(sp)]`: the extra live value pushes retail's `mfhi` copy into `$s5`, so a diff that shows `mfhi $t9` against retail's `mfhi $s5` in a function whose frame is one word short is ONE residual, not two - count the frame words before parking them separately. Measured dead on this body: spelling `pOut` off the shared element offset (`&pGridB[off - 0x70]`) is 90.28% / 388 / 97 (it keeps the `t5` giv as `li 0x2842` and folds the `addu`+`addiu` pair into one `addu`); a hand-maintained element counter, `row = y * 0x70` plus `row + 1`, and the `+1` per tap (that one gives retail's 102 insns at 79.52%) are all in the park note; and a `cc1 -fno-strength-reduce` probe (not shippable) changes the whole function's shape, so the fold is the giv pass and no spellable source reaches retail's pair.

## appendix: a run of dead stores to one word is placed by sched2, round 492

symptoms: same registers same bytes, four dead stores of the same word in the wrong slots, chained read-modify-write of a bitfield word, store motion
try: store order sched2 dead store hoist bitfield

- id: c-a-dead-store-run-is-sched2s-placement-not-the-rtl-order | keywords: store, order, sched2, dead, hoist, bitfield, chain, schedule-insns2
  **THE FIVE STORES OF A BITFIELD CHAIN ARE ONE PER STATEMENT IN RTL (ALL AT THE END OF THE BLOCK) AND sched2 HOISTS EACH ABOVE THE REST OF ITS CHAIN, SO A RETAIL BODY THAT KEEPS THE FOUR DEAD STORES TOGETHER NEAR THE BLOCK END IS A SCHEDULER PLACEMENT - read the RTL order first by compiling the unit .i with `-fno-schedule-insns2`, and park if retail sits between the two schedules** (round 492, battling/main/misc12 func_80088A40, XenoBattlingNoGp = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G0, parked 86.96% at retail's exact 184 bytes / 46 insns with every register and mask already retail's). The body is five `pFlags->field = ...` bitfield assignments on `&g_BattleOptionFlags`; the unit flags emit `lw a2 / and / ori / and a1,a2,a1 / sw a2 / andi / sll / or ...` (each store right after its chain step), `-fno-schedule-insns2` on the same `.i` puts one load and all five stores after the last `or`, and retail has the four dead ones three instructions above the block end - i.e. sched2's hoisting stopped early there for a reason no source handle reaches (a park note that read "the store positions are the source order" was wrong about this). Also measured dead on the body: `-fschedule-insns` (no change), `-O3` (does not compile it), cdk -G0 84.13, 2.6.0 -G0 86.96, and the two shapes that move the other way - five `u32` temps then five stores lets cse delete four of the stores by coalescing the chain into one register (168 bytes / 42 insns / 73.13%), and a `volatile u32*` keeps all five stores at 184 bytes but coalesces the chain (64.43%). A 3-minute permuter run scored its best candidate 406 against a base of 1815 while objdiff was unchanged at 86.96 (its winning edit was a constant-1 local), so its number is not a workable proxy here.

## appendix: a `+ 0xFF` uv edge fills the load slot, and an s32 flag word shifts `sra`, round 493

- id: d-a-plus-0xff-edge-fills-the-lbu-slot-and-a-s32-flags-word-shifts-sra | keywords: delay-slot, nop, lbu, edge, uv, sra, srl, unsigned, cast
  **A PERIMETER EDGE SPELLED `u + 0xFF + w` INSTEAD OF `u + w - 1` IS THE SAME STORED BYTE IN A u8 FIELD AND FILLS THE `lbu` LOAD-DELAY SLOT, because the constant only depends on the first load: `addiu v0,v0,255 / addu v1,v1,v0` replaces `addu / addiu v0,v0,-1` plus a nop, which was FOUR instructions and four nops over four sites** (round 493, slus_006.64/system/rendering_atfree func_8001E9BC, XenoRenderingAtfree = gcc-2.7.2-cdk -O2 -G0: 91.68% / 1176 bytes from 82.74 / 1172; gcc then attaches the 0xFF to whichever operand it loads second, so retail's `lbu texX` first vs this body's `lbu width` first stays 8 differing lines with no size change). Same round, same function: `SpriteFlagWord.flags` is `s32`, so `flags >> 8 & 0x1F` emits `sra` where retail has `srl` - `((u32)flags >> 8) & 0x1F` is the one-line fix (91.72 -> 91.95). Companion: the round-457 `pVerts = g_QuadCorners` lever also flips the SAVED SET to retail's exact s0-s8 on a 299-instruction loop (86.39 -> 82.74 as a raw score while the body is six short), so read the saved set, not the percentage, before judging that edit.

## appendix: block splits pin a store group, and one extra use of a halfword temp flips the `li` register, round 494

symptoms: stores in another order, hoisted store, do-while, split block, regalloc swapped, li register, same size permutation
try: store order do-while split block swapped register

- id: a-field-rmw-through-a-pointer-split-into-read-stores-write-pins-retail-interleaving | keywords: store, order, pointer, rmw, increment, ip, do-while, schedule
  **A `p->ip += N` WRITTEN AS `pIp = &p->ip; ip = *pIp; <the stores retail puts in the gap>; *pIp = ip + N;` EMITS RETAIL'S INTERLEAVED TAIL INSTEAD OF A LOAD/USE/STORE RUN, because the pointer local keeps the address in place and the explicit read gives sched2 a value whose use the middle stores can sit between** (round 494, field/main/misc func_8008EE14, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8). Retail is `lhu v0,0xCC(a0) / li v1,1 / lui at / sw v1,SceneActive / addiu v0,v0,0x13 / sh v0,0xCC(a0)`; the park's `pIp = &actor->ip; *pIp += 0x13; SceneActive = 1;` gave `lhu / nop / addiu / sh / li / sw` (332 bytes, 93.54%), and the read/stores/write split closes it at 328 bytes / 100.00%. Same file, func_8008EA58 uses the same shape with three stores in the gap (`g_FieldMode`, SceneActive, StopFlag) and needed it too.

- id: a-run-of-stores-and-a-global-rmw-each-wrapped-in-do-while-0-land-in-retail-order | keywords: store, order, do-while, block, split, hoist, constant, scheduler
  **WHEN sched2 HOISTS A LATER STORE UP TO REUSE A CONSTANT (or hoists an `andi` above a store), wrapping the run of stores in `do { } while (0)` creates the block boundary that stops it: three `ImageX2/Y1/X1 = 0` stores wrapped in one do-while stopped gcc grouping the two `0x100` stores that straddle them, and wrapping the `G = type & 0xF` store in its own do-while stopped its `andi` moving above the preceding store** (round 494, field/main/misc func_8008EA58, 92.37 -> 96.19 -> 99.70%, retail's exact 472 bytes). The file already used the same idiom to pin the per-call read/store order in the head of that function; a store group is the second place it pays. Prefer this over `volatile`, which pins the whole group and costs bytes.

- id: one-early-use-of-a-halfword-temp-rematerialises-it-at-the-use-site-and-flips-the-li-register | keywords: regalloc, swapped, li, register, halfword, u16, rematerialise, permuter
  **A HALFWORD LOCAL THAT IS READ ONCE RE-MATERIALISES AT THAT READ (so a spelling that assigns it early and uses it once is byte-identical to reading the field there), AND GIVING THE INCREMENT TEMP THAT ONE EXTRA EARLY USE FLIPS ITS REGISTER AGAINST THE `li 1` CONSTANT THAT FOLLOWS IT** (round 494, field/main/misc func_8008EA58, 99.70 -> 100.00%, 472 bytes). Retail is `lhu v0,0xCC(a0) / li v1,0x1 / sw v1,...`; the honest body had `lhu v1,204(a0) / li v0,0x1`, and the permuter's only winning edit was `ip = pActor->scriptInstructionPointer;` before the second continuation read with `SCRIPT_READ_U8(ip + 0xB)` there - the load still reloads from the actor (one use = rematerialised), so the bytes are retail's and the source stays semantically equal. Using the same local at TWO or more sites is wrong for this purpose: gcc then keeps it in a callee-saved register across the calls (444 bytes, 89.48%).

## appendix: an if/else that retail re-tests at the join is two sequential ifs, round 494

symptoms: join re-tests the flag retail just tested, extra load+branch at a join, if/else vs two ifs, 2 instructions short
try: exit shape join retest if else two guards reload

- id: d-an-if-else-that-retests-its-own-condition-at-the-join-is-two-sequential-ifs | keywords: exit, shape, join, retest, if, else, reload, guard
  **WHEN RETAIL'S JOIN RELOADS AND RE-TESTS THE VERY FLAG THE GUARD JUST TESTED, THE SOURCE WAS TWO SEQUENTIAL `if`s, NOT an `if/else` - and the first `if`'s false edge is redirected straight into the second one's body, which is what makes it LOOK like an else** (round 494, battle/main/misc22 func_800A4DB8, XenoBattle260Div = gcc-2.6.0; 85.22 -> 90.62%, 614 -> 617 insns, 2480 -> 2492 bytes against retail 2500). Retail has `bltz v0,.L50C8` at 0x501C sending the false edge to the ZEROING block that sits after the arm, then at the join `lh v0,0x7A(sp) / addu a0,v0 / bgez v0,.L50D8` - i.e. the same test twice, because the flag lives in memory and each `if` must re-read it. The `if (y >= 0) { ... } else { y = 0; }` spelling emits ONE test and a `j` over the zeroing (and is 3 instructions short); `if (y >= 0) { ... }` followed by `if (y < 0) { y = 0; }` reproduces retail exactly. Read it as: a duplicated test at a join is never the allocator, it is one guard too few in the source.
  Companion on the same body (three spellings, one measurement each): (1) `& (pArg->texPeriod - 1)` written inline at both mask sites CSEs the `-1` into ONE `addiu t1` as retail has it, where a `s32 texMask = pArg->texPeriod - 1;` local computed before the divisions earns a stray `andi` (a `u16` local earns it too); (2) a `u_short` field read with a `(s16)` cast is the `lh` retail uses in an expression where the same field read plain is `lhu` - the two loads differ, so cast per site, not per field; (3) the 8-byte gap at the frame bottom (retail `vars=0xB0` where the same slot set gives ours 0xA8, and NOTHING in retail's asm touches 0x10..0x17) is the phantom-slot case of `j-a-phantom-slot-below-the-saves-is-a-sixth-reload-spill`, one spill slot BELOW the expand-era locals instead of above: do not hunt it, every `$sp` offset stays 8 low and the function cannot reach 100.

## appendix: swapping a compare's operands buys one register, not the first one, round 495

symptoms: closing compare in a0/v1 vs v0/v1, regalloc swapped tie, third register, dead base reuse
try: regalloc swapped tie compare operand a0 dead base reuse

- id: b-swapping-a-compare-buys-the-second-register-and-the-first-reuses-the-dead-base | keywords: regalloc, tie, compare, swapped, operand, dead, base, reuse
  **A BLOCK THAT ENDS IN `a != b` ALLOCATES ASCENDING FROM $v0 WITH THE ADDRESS REGISTER STILL LIVE, SO SWAPPING THE C OPERANDS MOVES WHICH VALUE GETS $v1 BUT THE OTHER ONE ALWAYS REUSES THE DEAD BASE REGISTER - to reach retail's third register ($a0) the base would have to stay live past the second load, which no spelling of the same two reads produces** (round 495, battling/main/misc14 func_8008B730, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8). Retail's close is `lw v0,0(s4) / lh a0,0x12(s4) / lh v1,0(v0) / nop / bne a0,v1`; `if (pAnim->position != pAnim->config->length)` gives position->$v1 and length->$v0 (the `lh` tying the dying base), and the swapped `if (pAnim->config->length != pAnim->position)` gives length->$v1 as retail has it but position->$v0 off the dead base, one extra `nop` and 192 insns against retail's 191 (93.45 -> 92.86%). So an $a0/$v1 tie is not a spelling question; leave it with the allocator group, not the C.

## appendix: pooling an 11th constant address trades bytes for percentage, round 495

symptoms: one instruction over, 4 bytes long, 4 bytes short, frame 8 too small, callee-saved rotation, scratchpad pointers
try: regalloc swapped pool constant address spill scratchpad size

- id: e-one-extra-constant-address-pseudo-flips-five-registers-and-the-frame-size | keywords: regalloc, swapped, pool, constant, address, spill, frame, size
  **A REGION THAT BODIES A HAND-ROLLED CLIP TEST AGAINST FIVE FIXED SCRATCHPAD ADDRESSES CANNOT HAVE BOTH RETAIL'S SIZE AND RETAIL'S ALLOCATION: each extra constant address you pool as a pointer local buys percentage and costs the frame, and a body 4 bytes short or 4 over never links, so the percentage is a dead number until the size is exact** (round 495, world_map/main/misc16 func_800983A0, XenoWorldMapDiv = gcc-2.7.2 -O2 -G8 --dont-expand-li; retail 1036 bytes / 259 insns / frame 0x70 with two spilled point pointers, the park 1040 / 260 / 0x68 at 88.71%). Measured on one body, one edit each: pooling `D_1F8000C8` into a `Point* pC8` local at the loop head (the 11th live value) gives 89.27% (the best percentage seen) at 1032 bytes / 258 insns - one instruction SHORT, base s2 -> s1, pTex s3 -> s2, every slot shifts; pooling `pC0` and `pC8` together gives 86.83 / 1012 / 253; dropping a CSE-artifact local (`pA0`, used once right after its assignment) is byte-identical, so it is worth removing for looks and never worth counting as a lever. The two exact-1036 spellings already recorded in that park are 81.45 (fourth corner spelled `pScratch + 0xB8`) and 78.47 / 74.88 (the five inner points as named symbols, pooled / unpooled). Conclusion to reuse: when a park measures 88-89% at +4 or -4 bytes against retail and every pooled-address variant moves the whole saved set, the residual is the reload/rematerialisation decision, not the C, and another pooled local is not the answer.

## appendix: where a shared switch-arm tail lands is arm polarity plus an empty statement, round 496

symptoms: retail keeps the later copy of a shared tail, ours the earlier, one instruction short, extra or missing `j` to the merged block, block order in the switch region
try: cross-jump shared tail switch block do-while polarity site

- id: b-the-copy-site-of-a-shared-switch-tail-follows-the-arm-polarity-not-the-copy-count | keywords: cross-jump, shared, tail, switch, block, polarity, do-while, site
  **WHEN TWO SWITCH ARMS END IN THE SAME `{store; break}` AND RETAIL SHOWS THE MERGED BLOCK AT THE LATER ARM (with the earlier arm's block ending in a `j` to it, i.e. one instruction MORE), THE LEVER IS THE LATER ARM'S TEST POLARITY PLUS A BLOCK-NUMBERING STATEMENT, NOT THE NUMBER OF SOURCE COPIES** (round 496, menu/main/misc9 func_801DBE54, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0: 94.26% / 892 bytes / 223 insns -> 95.69% / 896 / 224 = retail's exact size, in two edits). Retail's case-4 tail `j .L801DC054 / prevCol = 0xFF` (= block B) is followed by case-5's text and the merged `{selectedSlot = 0xFF}` block C sits AFTER case 5 at 0x70, so B's `j .L801DC070` is retail's extra instruction; the park's body put C immediately after B (case 5 branching backwards to it) and was one instruction short. Writing case 5 as `if (selectedSlot == 0xFF) { active = 0; } else { selectedSlot = 0xFF; }` (the polarity retail's `bne s3,v0,.L801DC070` shows) AND moving the park's empty `do { } while (0)` block-numbering probe from case 2's arm to the end of case 5's arm is what flips it; measured on the same body: case-5 do-while with the ORIGINAL polarity 94.89 / 896, the polarity swap alone 93.81 / 888 / 222, both together 95.69 / 896. Two positions measured inert (a do-while at the end of case 0's or case 3's arm: identical, 95.69 / 896 / 107 differing lines). The residue after the flip was a SECOND, independent merge site in the same switch (case 1 and case 0 share a `col = v1` store; retail keeps the later copy after case 0, this cc1 the earlier after case 1) that no other probed position moved - so expect one such block per switch to be out of reach and count the instructions before blaming the C.

## appendix: a scaled-global access's SPELLING re-ranks sched2 for the whole block, round 496

symptoms: one store six slots late, two stores swapped inside an identical instruction stream, same size, cast vs typed pointer
try: store order spelling cast pointer scaled global schedule

- id: a-byte-pointer-scaled-global-re-ranks-sched2-where-a-typed-index-does-not | keywords: store, order, spelling, cast, pointer, schedule, sched2, struct
  **WHEN A STRAIGHT-LINE BODY IS INSTRUCTION-FOR-INSTRUCTION RETAIL'S BUT ONE STORE IS SIX SLOTS LATE, THE SPELLING OF A SCALED GLOBAL ACCESS IS THE KNOB: `u8 *p = (u8 *)G + (i << 7);` with cast offsets re-ranks sched2's ready list and a TYPED pointer or typed index on the same arithmetic does not** (round 496, world_map/main/misc3 func_8007756C, XenoWorldMap = gcc-2.7.2-psx -O2 -G8 `--dont-expand-li`; 93.22 -> 97.57% at retail's exact 93 insns / 372 bytes, 10 differing lines -> 2). `WorldMapPlayer *pPlayer = &((WorldMapPlayer *)g_WorldMapSlots)[arg0];` and `(WorldMapPlayer *)((u8 *)g_WorldMapSlots + (arg0 << 7))` both emit the same `sll a0,a0,7 / lw a1,g_WorldMapSlots / addu a1,a1,a0`, yet both leave retail's `sh $zero,%lo(g_WorldMapViewRotationZ)` five or six slots below its slot (just before the FadeLevel store) at 93.22; spelling it `u8 *pSlot = (u8 *)g_WorldMapSlots + (arg0 << 7); *(s32 *)(pSlot + 0x28) = ...;` puts the store back between `li v1,120` and `addu` and the body jumps to 97.57. So this is not the arithmetic (identical) and not the field types (identical) - the typed form's index RTL re-ranks the ready list. Two probes bound the class: the unit's own `.i` compiled with `-fno-schedule-insns -fno-schedule-insns2` prints the source order, `-fno-schedule-insns` alone still leaves the store after the FadeLevel store, and `-fno-schedule-insns2` is what keeps it beside the CameraHeight store - so sched2 owns the move, and an empty-statement barrier between the two stores (the usual sched2 lever) costs 5 points here (88.04, it drags the pathFrame `la` up and sinks the Height store). Reaching for the byte-pointer spelling FIRST is the cheap move on any store-placement residual over a scaled global.
  What it did not fix on the same body: the last residual is a two-store swap inside the camera-target triple (retail stores x, Z, Y through one `a1` store and two symbol stores; every source order measured emits the LAST source statement's symbol store first with the `a1` store between, 92.09-97.57), i.e. the same class the old note called unreachable, now down to one pair.

## appendix: a named VALUE keeps retail's index IV where the inline address scales it, round 496

symptoms: loop index vs byte offset, missing sll addu sll multiply, induction variable stride 800 instead of 20, eighth callee-saved IV
try: giv biv index byte-offset scale induction variable value invariant

- id: f-a-named-value-local-keeps-the-index-iv-the-inline-address-form-scales-away | keywords: giv, biv, index, byte-offset, scale, induction, variable, invariant, callee-saved
  **AN INDEX EXPRESSION THAT RETAIL KEEPS AS A VALUE WITH THE MULTIPLY AT THE USE IS REPRODUCED BY A NAMED `s32` LOCAL ASSIGNED IN THE OUTER LOOP BODY, NOT BY THE SAME EXPRESSION WRITTEN INLINE AS AN ARRAY SUBSCRIPT - naming the value makes it a non-address giv (unscaled, stride = the outer step, `sll/addu/sll` at each use), while `&Base[row * STRIDE + K]` puts the multiply in the address tree and `loop.c` folds it into a SCALED byte-offset IV instead** (round 496, field/effects/distortion FieldDistortionDraw, Default = 2.7.2 -O2 -G8, retail 2060 bytes / 515 insns). Retail's col==19 arms index `&pPrim[row*20+19]` through an IV initialised `li 0x12B` (= 299 = 14*20+19) and bumped by 20 in the outer tail, spilled to a stack slot, with `sll v0,sX,2 / addu v0,v0,sX / sll v0,v0,3` doing the *40 at each use; the inline subscript form gives a byte-offset IV (`li 0x2EB8`, stride 800) and three instructions fewer. `s32 lastIndex = row * DISTORTION_GRID_ROWS + DISTORTION_GRID_ROWS - 1;` as the first statement of each outer body reproduces retail's IV exactly (505 -> 511 of retail's 515 insns), and BLOCK-SCOPING that same declaration inside the body loses it again - it has to be a function-scope local assigned per outer iteration. Read the other side of the trade before shipping it: the new value is loop-live and takes a callee-saved register, and on this body the register retail gives a long-lived value (its `offsetY`, `$s6`) so the allocation shifts: 84.72% / 2020 bytes inline vs 81.05% / 2044 with the index IV. Use it when the multiply's presence in retail is the evidence you are chasing and the register map is already close; the percentage alone will prefer the scaled form.

- id: a-ring-scan-step-belongs-in-the-wrap-test-not-the-for-clause | keywords: loop, increment, wrap, rotate, clamp, preheader, hoist, delay-slot, block-order, park
  **A "STEP ONE SLOT, WRAP AT THE END, BREAK WHEN THE ENTRY IS SET" SCAN CLOSES ONLY WHEN THE STEP IS WRITTEN INSIDE THE WRAP TEST (`if (++slot >= N) slot = 0;` / `if (--slot < 0) slot = N - 1;`): AS A `for (slot++; 1; slot++)` FOR-INIT IT EMITS THE SAME 65/65 INSTRUCTIONS BUT 84.26%, AND AS THE TEST IT IS MATCH / 100.00%** (round 497, menu/main/misc8 func_801D9704, XenoMenu260 = gcc-2.6.0, 260 bytes / 65 insns). Three separate residuals all came from the one spelling: (a) the for-init is emitted BEFORE loop.c hoists the invariants, so the block read `addiu a0,a0,1 / andi a2,a2,0xff / lui g_Menu / li 0xFF` where retail has the hoisted group first and the step LAST; with the step in the wrap test the preheader is `[invariants][addiu a0,a0,1][slti v0,a0,3]`, i.e. retail's exact order. (b) the back edge then carries the step in its DELAY SLOT (`j top` + `addiu a0,a0,1`, and `beqz v0, top` + `addiu a0,a0,1`), which no for-clause spelling produces: dbr moves the step out of the top block into both back edges and compensates the exit path, so the arm's exit reads `beqz v0, top / addiu a0,a0,+1 / j ret / addiu a0,a0,-1` - a `+1/-1` pair that looks like a source `arg0--; break;` and is NOT one. Read that pair as dbr's fill+compensation before writing a decrement into the C: the honest source has a plain `break` in the arm and the compensations appear on their own. (c) the mode test's arm order follows for free. Corollary: two `+1` and `-1` pairs inside a 60-instruction function are usually delay-slot fill, not source arithmetic, and a park that keeps re-deriving them by hand (`arg0--; break;` measured 88.20 and 89.68 on the two earlier shapes) is one control-flow move away. Companion: the same "early `break`/`continue` from an if-arm lays that arm's block out first" move closed func_801D9808 in the same unit (99.67 -> 100.00) by writing `if (choice != 0) choice--; else choice = n - 1;` instead of `if (choice == 0) choice = n - 1; else choice--;`.
